This is the coding for Ntuzuma :SAPS Overview:25/05 Social media reports began circulating about children being kidnapped and they mentioned the involvement of foreign nationals. These went viral.  29/05  Further reports circulated that children were being kidnapped and parents marched to schools to take their children out. Roads began being blocked. 2 marches took place, 1 in Ntuzuma , and looting of foreign shops began. 30/05 Protestors marched from school to school taking their children out. 1 container looted – live rounds fired by security company and 1 child shot in the leg. 4 security officers arrested. At time of meeting the looting was still continuing. There are fears that  this may spread to Quarry Heights and Inanda tonight. There are no registered cases of kidnapping at this stage. Update from our partner organisation 06/02: This morning, the team assembled in Durban at 8 am for our 1st briefing. We managed to meet with our partner organisations as well as other colleagues. Of note from the or briefing is: LHR had not been approached by any PoCs seeking legal assistance as a result of the attacks; One POC approached RSS seeking assistance. She had a injury on her leg and a cast (unsure if it is related to the attacks). She indicated that her husband had a shop which was looted. We managed to obtain her details and will schedule a meeting with her. The team thereafter left for the KZN Social Cohesion MRM summit that is going on at the Kwa Mashu Christian Centre. We met with M.M. of Zoe Life and held a further de-brief. Of note is: The summit had been more political with majority of participants being Mayors and Councillors who took tike to discuss election matters. The KZN premier had condemned the attacks on foreign nationals and called for extra vigilance and support from the Security clusters. The MEC for Human settlements informed the participants that there were messages circulating on social media calling the residents to "rise up and March against the Nigerians due to allegations of drug peddling and kidnappings. The MEC warned against any attacks on foreign nationals. - We will continue to monitor this development.

records.name: Public hospitals deny migrants health care services.
records.description:
Due to their nationality or legal status, migrants are denied health care services at Gauteng public hospitals as revealed by a human rights organisation. There have been instances where immigrants in Gauteng have been denied access to health care services because of their nationality, because they had the necessary paperwork, or because they lacked the cash up front to cover the cost of the service. The organisation states that foreign nationals were denied access to anti-retroviral therapy as well as their entitlement to quality health care in general by South African public hospitals and clinics. The organisation cited an incidence from June 2017 in which a pregnant immigrant was forced to give birth at the Gautrain Park Station after being turned away from three regional government hospitals for medical attention. 
Source: https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2018-03-29-medical-xenophobia-public-hospitals-deny-migrants-health-care-services-sahrc/

records.description: On the 15th of February 2018 in white river, the victim, originally from Zimbabwe was working as a manager for a wifi company. They used to get paid every fourth night or every two weeks so as a manager he was also responsible for payments for other staff members so since they were also foreign nationals most of them didn't have bank accounts so he would pay them hand in cash so that day was pay day in the morning he went to the bank and withdrew R40 000 to pay other staff members. On his way back he passed by his room or place to get the envelops to package the money. While inside, he heard someone knocking so he tried to hide the money so that he could attend the people knocking before he knew it, the perpetrators broke the door and forced themselves inside, he shouted for help but as it was during the day, and when people tried to help him the perpetrators pointed at them with their guns and shouted that he owed them money. The perpetrators were were four guys. They beat the victim severely, injured him and  took all the money.

records.name: A Xenophobic Incident - email had attached press statement of incident.  A University of Johannesburg PhD student ...
records.description: A Xenophobic Incident - email had attached press statement of incident.  A University of Johannesburg PhD student was killed by a taxi driver outside his Sophiatown residence, colleagues said this week. The police have confirmed a case of culpable homicide was under investigation; while the university said it would issue a statement later on Friday. Colleagues of the deceased, a Tanzanian national, say he was killed in the early hours of Friday, February 23. His colleagues and friends issued a joint media statement about his death. They say CCTV footage shows Nafari and a fellow UJ student running for their lives while two men in a taxi pursue them. “As Baraka and his friend run for safety‚ they flee toward the UJ Sophiatown residency‚ however the taxi violently pursues them‚ such that the taxi deliberately struck Baraka against the fence of the UJ Sophiatown residence‚ and [this] marks the death of the victim‚” the colleagues said in a statement‚ which was distributed by the African Diaspora Forum. They said UJ prided itself on being a pan-African institution‚ a home for students from across the continent. “The deceased was a Tanzanian citizen and we welcomed him here. We are disturbed that the university‚ so proud of its international students‚ has not yet issued a public statement condemning this appalling murder.” The university said it would comment later on Friday about the allegations levelled by the colleagues. The African Diaspora Forum said it planned a meeting at the university’s Sophiatown residence on Monday to understand why it had taken long for the university to respond.

records.name: Mahikeng and surrounding areas were affected by violent protests from the 18-21st of April 2018. Community members ...
records.description: Mahikeng and surrounding areas were affected by violent protests from the 18-21st of April 2018. Community members were protesting against the removal and/or resignation of Premier Supra Mahumapelo from his position. According to media reports, several complaints and allegations of corruption and poor service delivery have been lodged against him. As a result, roads were blocked and barricaded; shops and several tuck shops in the area belonging to both foreign nationals and South African citizens were looted. Some buildings, cars and buses were burnt down including Mmabana Arts Centre. It is reported that police fired rubber bullets at protestors to control the situation. Media reports confirmed that 23 people were arrested and one person is confirmed to have died. Police were reported to be on standby to monitor the situation and ensure calm in the area. Whilst it is maintained that foreign nationals were not directly targeted, they were also affected by the consequences of the protest. No further attacks have been reported but the situation still remains tense and unresolved to date. A further update from the daily Maverick is that 350 community shops were looted and It’s unclear how many foreigners were displaced during the protests in Mahikeng, but it’s estimated that almost 1,000 people were forced out of communities as looters targeted foreign-owned stores. Most are stuck in temporary accommodation, relying on community donations. Their future is uncertain.

records.name: Following reports circulating in the media concerning the death of a Nigerian man burnt to death by a mob, Xenowatch ...
records.description: Following reports circulating in the media concerning the death of a Nigerian man burnt to death by a mob, Xenowatch conducted verification follow ups with the Rustenburg Police Station and the Nigerian Union in South Africa. Both parties confirmed the occurrence of the incident but provided conflicting reports on what actually transpired and the response taken by the police. Incident: According to reports, the victim was approached by a mob that easily identified him as a Nigerian and demanded to know if he had drugs. The victim informed them that he owns a shop that makes furniture but the mob descendant on him, attacked and burnt him to death. According to a statement provided to Xenowatch by Sergeant Ofentse Mokgadi, police on the scene tried to assist the victim and fight off the mob but he ran away without the police noticing which led to some mob members who had seen him run, chase him and set him ablaze. However, the Nigerian Union in South Africa states otherwise. According to a source from the organization, eye witnesses reported that the police did not intervene when the victim requested assistance. He further stated that it was the eye witnesses who called for help and not the police. Unfortunately the victim succumbed to his injuries and died in the early hours of the 22nd of April 2018. The deceased was aged 31 years old. He was customarily married to a South African woman and they had two children.

records.name: On 26th May 2018, 43 foreign nationals from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi, seeking asylum in South ...
records.description: On 26th May 2018, 43 foreign nationals from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi, seeking asylum in South Africa were violently expelled by rogue community members of Mapoteng in Kathu, Northern Cape. Kathu had been their place of business and residence for the past 8-15 years. The community members, with weapons in hand, threatened the foreign nationals with violence and demanded that they leave Kathu or they will be killed. The foreign nationals then sought protection from the Kathu police, but their cries for help were only answered by the Kimberley SAPS. They were assisted to pack their belongings and transported to the police station in Kathu were they sought refuge for a period of 8 days. With the urgent intervention of South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) and our partner organisation, the local municipality in Kathu (Gamagara Municipality) decided to accommodate the 43 foreign nationals at an old library in the town of Kathu – with little to no access to basic services. The conditions were harsh and not suitable for human habitation. On 7th June 2018, a meeting was convened with various stakeholders at the Gamagara municipality where a long term solution was meant to be forged. One of the conclusions of the meeting was to convene a meeting with the community leaders so as to start a process of re-integration and peace-keeping within the community. Unfortunately, the process was unsuccessful and the community maintained its position that should the foreign nationals be allowed back into the community they will be killed one at a time, as the police cannot provide 24 hour protection. On the 14th June 2018, 16 of the displaced fled to Upington and arrived at the offices of the SAHRC with their belongings seeking protection. The rest of the displaced fled to other parts of the country or moved to a different township in Kathu. The difference between the 16 who fled to Upington and the ones who did not is that the former are self-employed business men and could not return to their jobs as the salons are located in Mapoteng. While a majority of the rest are security guards in town and managed to settle elsewhere in Kathu. An urgent meeting was then convened with various stakeholders in Upington (Local and District municipality, Immigration office, Crime Intelligence, Police, Social development, SASSA, National Defence Force). The following was resolved: The Municipality would provide them with emergency shelter at the Toll Spelman Hall for a period of 5 days and are open to making extensions were necessary; DSD offered to provide meals for the displaced, three (3) times a day; Immigration would verify the documentation of the displaced; SAPS agreed to patrol the area every hour on the hour for the duration of their stay in the Hall; and The stakeholders will meet regularly to discuss a long term solution. On the 25th June 2018 another meeting was convened where the local municipality delegation stated that they were no longer prepared to accommodate the displaced anymore – this is despite undertaking to do so. The municipality justified its position by stating on record that it is not in their mandate to assist the foreign nationals any further; The delegation from the municipality and the office of the Mayor added that it was their intention to evict the displaced from their place of safety in the community hall; When asked whether the municipality would provide alternative accommodation, the response was that the displaced would be forcibly removed without a court order and would be transported back to Kathu; The delegation maintained its position even though we informed them that there had been recent confirmation by the Gamagara Municipality officials that the situation in Kathu was still hostile and that the lives of the foreign nationals would be at risk, should they return; It was on the basis of these views by the municipality officials that Xenowatch partner organisation together with the SAHRC requested to see the Mayor of Upington to further engage on the matter. The Mayor suggested that the meeting with her be convened the next day; and Indeed the next day, 26th June 2018, a meeting was convened only without the mayor who instead sent the speaker of the municipal council to attend on her behalf. On this occasion the Speaker reiterated their unwavering intention to unlawfully evict the victims from the premises. It was then necessary to urgently send a letter of demand to the local municipality, the mayor as well as the provincial department of Co-operative Governance, Human Settlements and Traditional Affairs (COGTHA). The letter stated clearly that should the municipality seek to evict the displaced from their place of safety, an urgent application would be launched to prevent them from doing so. We are happy to report that no eviction took place. In and around 28 June 2018, the non-xenophobic community members in Kathu began to fight back against the perpetrators of the xenophobic attack. The community was led by the employees of the displaced, who had become unemployed because of their employers being unjustly expelled from their homes and businesses. The confrontation between the community members was violent, leading to the perpetrators of the xenophobic attack to flee from the town or otherwise succumbing to the threats laid against them. The local police intervened to restore peace and were generally in agreement with the community members who fought for the return of the 16 displaced. The clients then informed our partner organisation that they intended to return to Kathu as a result of the latest developments. However, they were not willing to return to the same township – Mapoteng. On Friday, 29 June 2018, our partner organisation  travelled to Kathu in order for the leader of the group, Hamza, to look for accommodation and to see for himself whether it was safe to return. The following day, he confirmed that it was safe to return. With the assistance of the funds raised by Africa Awake, our partner organisation was able to assist the displaced to return to Kathu and re-start their lives. The amount raised covered one month’s rent and travelling costs to return to Kathu. We are happy to report that the 16 displaced left for Kathu on 3 July 2018 and some have immediately returned to working at their hair salons in Mapoteng. On 3 July 2018, our partner organisation wrote a letter to the police in Kathu, as well as to the Mayor and Municipal manger, informing that the 16 displaced have returned to Kathu. Our partner organisation further requested that the police monitor the situation in Mapoteng to ward off any more conflicts. Additionally, we invited both municipalities from Kathu and Upington to work on their contingency plans in cases of emergency and should they need assistance, our partner organisation is willing to come to the table. There has been no response from either municipality.  Report by Our partner organisation.

records.name: Residents tore down a shack belonging to an immigrant from the Democratic Republic of Congo and his wife in Siyahlala ...
records.description:
Residents tore down a shack belonging to an immigrant from the Democratic Republic of Congo and his wife in Siyahlala informal settlement‚ Khayelitsha‚ on Saturday. The Community leader tried to restrain some residents who took away corrugated iron sheets‚ poles and wooden planks. She told them to leave the couple’s belongings beside the place where their shack stood. But after the community leaders left the scene‚ residents looted two beds‚ a table‚ blankets‚ plywoods‚ and corrugated iron sheets and left the spot where the shack stood empty. A witness‚ said: “People destroyed my shack and took everything. They say they don’t want a kwere kwere [derogatory word for a foreigner] to stay here‚” he said. The witness said he still wanted to stay in Siyahlala. “The committee [of community leaders] says I’m not safe because residents may burn my shack while I’m asleep‚ but I’m not scared to return and stay here‚” said the witness. Currently‚ he said‚ he rents a house for R2‚500 a month in‚ Khayelitsha. “I also want to have my own land where I won’t have to pay rent‚” said the witness‚ who works for Uber. His wife‚ said: “The residents say I must not stay here because I’m trying to get a place for a kwere kwere. The shack belongs to me‚ and I want to stay with him because he is my husband.” The witness has a South African identity document. She said her husband owns an Audi A4 station wagon and Corsa bakkie‚ and so residents suspect he wants to set up a business. “Because they see his cars‚ they think that we have money and we come here merely to set up a business venture”‚” said the wife. She said she opened a case against the residents at Khayelitsha police station on Saturday evening. “I want the police to help us get our building materials back‚” she said. Before they destroyed the shack on Saturday‚  another community leader  told the residents at a community meeting that a foreigner and his girlfriend had built the shack even though they had told them not to. “We told him that if he values his building material‚ he must not build a shack because residents don’t want foreigners to stay here‚” he said. “The informal settlement is already full and people who are desperate for places to stay struggle to find vacant land. Foreigners will just want a place to kick-start business ventures‚” he told GroundUp. On Sunday‚ the victims met the community leaders to ask them about the destroyed shack in Siyahlala. They told them that he and other leaders would help them find another spot to put up their shack. “We want the residents who stole his belongings to return them to him‚” he said. On Monday the victims said the community leaders and the residents searched for their belongings in Siyahlala and found a mattress‚ corrugated iron zinc sheets‚ sofas‚ ceiling boards and wooden planks. “The leaders who incited the residents to destroy our shack and other residents helped us find our belongings and building materials‚ but we didn’t find all of them‚” she said.

- This article was published by GroundUp Source :TimesLive

records.name: Somali trader has been killed and another one wound in Cape town in latest xenophobic violence against Foreigners ...
records.description: Somali trader has been killed and another one wound in Cape town in latest xenophobic violence against Foreigners in South Africa. An unidentified gunman stormed a Somali-owned shop in the port city on South Africa's Southwest coast leading the death of the victim. In the recent years, dozens of Somalis have been killed in what seems to be orchestrated gang violence . A businessman who survived from the attack said another businessman was wounded in the attack. "Several men armed with pistols accosted and opened fire at close range. We escaped from the shop (but) unfortunately the bullet hit two businessmen,  the deceased succumbed to injuries he sustained from the attack and another trader escaped with injuries," said the witness. He noted that the assailants managed to escape from the crime scene before law enforcement agencies arrived. The attack comes barely two days after another Somali businessman  were killed in a heinous attack. The renewed attacks are reminiscent of January xenophobic attacks carried out by armed men from the hosting community in the country. Early this year, Amnesty International accused the South African government of lacking the political will to avert xenophobic attacks. "There is a lack of political will on the part of the government to deal with issues of violence and xenophobia in a sustainable way," said, Executive Director of Amnesty International South Africa, "and the consequence of this inertia has resulted in continuing sporadic bursts of violence which often end in deaths, injuries and damage to property."

records.name: About 63 South African haulage truck drivers have been arrested after staging a ‘xenophobic’ protest targeting foreign ...
records.description: About 63 South African haulage truck drivers have been arrested after staging a ‘xenophobic’ protest targeting foreign drivers, including Zimbabweans in Harrismith along the Johannesburg-Durban (N3) Highway. South African drivers alleged that foreigners, particularly Zimbabweans were taking away their jobs, and were the main cause for low salaries they are receiving. The protesters were demanding that all foreign drivers dump their trucks at the pass and leave their country with immediate effect. Armed police teams were engaged to disperse the protesters and some arrests were made. The protest started early in the morning on Wednesday. Local haulage trucks drivers blocked the road from both directions and traffic only started clearing after 9PM after police intervened. Zimbabwe’s Consul-General to South Africa, Mr Batiraishe Mukonoweshuro said about 63 protestors were arrested and were set to appear in court soon. “I can confirm there was a massive protest yesterday (Wednesday), by haulage truck drivers as South Africans claimed that foreign drivers were taking away their jobs. The protest was also done for a number of other reasons which include little salaries, hard working conditions for them, with foreign drivers being pointed as the sole problem causers. “About 63 people were arrested and will appear in court. The protesters took advantage and decided to make their statement in a mountainous area — Van Reneen Pass in Harrismith between Johannesburg and Durban,” he said. Mr Mukonoweshuro said police had managed to clear the road and were closely monitoring the situation.

records.name: Shopkeeper attacked for failure to pay protection fees
records.description: A refugee from Somalia currently living in Verulam/eThekwini municipality reported that while he was still living and running his business in Nyanga/Cape Town between 2015 and 2019 he experienced xenophobic attacks. One of the incidents that he reported was of a time when he was running a shop in Nyanga. In 2017 a group of people came and asked him to pay a protection fee of R2000/week or else close his shop and leave the area, otherwise he would be killed. The refugee victim then decided to close his shop and moved to another area of Nyanga. When the perpetrators out found where he moved, they went after him at night (around 22h00) of July 2018, broke into his shop where he was sleeping, and shot him four times, in the head, neck and in the left hand. They then left with an undisclosed amount of money. He subsequently opened a case (no. 52/07/2018) and got 2 of his attackers arrested. Thereafter, he continued receiving threats saying that if he does not withdraw the case, he will be killed, so he went and withdrew the case, only to be attacked again. That is when he decided to leave the Western Cape altogether and came to Durban/Hammarsdale. He tried to open a shop there but was told that he could not because he was a foreigner and that only locals could open shops in Hammarsdale. This happened while he had already completed the construction of the building that was to be used as his shop. Now he is unemployed, doing nothing but staying with a friend who is running his business (shop) in Verulam. He wants to be repatriated to Somalia where his wife is at the moment. It must be noted that he still has the bullet in his neck; he went up to Albert Luthuli but was told that it is risky to remove it.

records.name: The ordeal began on the 26th of July 2018 when community members protested and demanded service delivery from the ...
records.description: The ordeal began on the 26th of July 2018 when community members protested and demanded service delivery from the local municipality. They marched to the municipal offices demanding houses and basic services. Some started looting the shops belonging to foreign nationals and stealing fridges in the process. 56 shops belonging to Ethiopians were looted and vandalised. Shoprite U-save and funeral Parlour were also looted and burnt to ashes and they still closed as we speak.  A total of 227 Ethiopians including women and children were displaced since July 2018. Most of them have been and are still living in the church and some are renting houses in town. They are concerned that the money for rent is getting depleted as there is no source of income. Most are using their savings and they fear that they won’t have any money to buy stock should the community allow them back.

records.name: Xenowatch received an email from a partner organisation  regarding xenophobic attacks in Zeerust which read as follows: ...
records.description:
Xenowatch received an email from a partner organisation  regarding xenophobic attacks in Zeerust which read as follows: " I hope you are well! Not sure if you guys have heard but there has been some terrible trouble up in the NW in the Zeerust area over the past week. Below I have copied the report  we received a from a local pastor in the area. I have also included some comments. As you can see this is not a good situation. You can count this as verified as  my colleague got this info through a local Pastor with a first hand account. Xenowtch then conducted several verifications and were able to get in touch with the Congolese Solidarity President who was in Zeerust following the attacks and was also in communication with the victims . The following is the detailed report of the incidents he shared with Xenowatch: I was on the phone with the refugee community in Zeerust around 12:52pm on Friday -03/08/2018. According to our correspondence, there were attacks in Zeerust since the beginning of last week. People who came to attack the foreign nationals claimed that foreigners are selling drugs to their kids and the same drugs are destroying their children. Because of this, all foreigners in the area must pack up and go back to their countries by September otherwise they were going to kill them. According to the victims, the early warning message started on Monday 30/07/2018 afternoon. They saw a large number of local people with sticks and stones in their hands saying they were looking for drug dealers. On the same day, the victims heard that one guy from Malawi was attacked and this is how Xenophobia started in Zeerust. The following day Tuesday 31/07/2018, the attacks were still undergoing. In the afternoon around 5:30 pm, many cars came to park in front of a salon.  Locals came out caring sticks, stones and even guns. According to the salon owner, the people came when it was about time to close up the salon. They arrived at the salon and found people seating outside because they normally wait for each other to finish off with clients so that they can leave together. 
The locals then allowed everyone outside to enter the salon and started to ask them where the drugs were. The salon owner then asked one of the locals why there were looking for drugs in his salon? He replied by telling the salon owner to shut up. They then took one foreign boy who was still new in the community and shouted that there were drugs in his pockets. Then they started beating him up and took him to the salon where he works. They then searched the salon but could not find any drugs. The locals even took the boy to his residential place and according to them, they found some drugs. The boy was beaten up, and police were even escorting the community in this attack. Locals surrounded the young man with a tire and sent someone to buy Petrol so that they could burn him alive. A young white guy realized what was going on and took the victim and put him in the police van. The same day they heard that another guy was caught with drugs but few hours later he was released. Same Tuesday night, they went to a pastor’s house around 11pm. After knocking at his door, the pastor asked who they were and one of them replied, “We are the police man”. Before the pastor opened, he heard people saying you must enter first if it’s your pastor’s house point him to us. The pastor heard a voice of one of his church member saying I know him he is my spiritual father and I cannot enter his house and betray him. They entered the house and asked him were the drugs where. After they found no drugs in the house, they intimidated him and this traumatized the pastor’s wife and kids. The local community that attacked the foreign nationals was led by a lady who was driving a white Mercedes and her husband. On Wednesday, the following day at 5pm, the locals went to two other salons in the area belonging to foreign nationals. They found one of the owners working on his last two last customers. They entered and ordered the customers to get out and the owner of the salon asked them to give him time, about 20minute to finish. The same lady with the Mercedes came and started beating him in front of other people and his customers and told the salon owner that his salon could not be open around 5pm. This led to other people around being afraid to respond after seeing how the owner of the salon had been terrorized by the lady, her husband and locals. The owner of the salon then went to open a case at the police station with other guys from Tanzania and Congo who had escorted him. At the police station they found a white police officer who refused to open a case for him questioning why he is only coming after being beaten. They asked the police officer what the right time for opening a case was, and he just told them to come back the following day. This series of attacks has made foreign nationals afraid and in addition, community members started saying they will involve people from locations around to attack foreigners and make sure end of September they leave the place and go back to their home countries. At night, some locals came into some foreign nationals’ homes, asking them to open up because they were looking for drugs. When they let them in, they entered and took their belongings such as money, cell phones, and even their computers. They asked for receipts and if they failed to show them, they took anything they wanted. On Thursday around the same time, 5pm one of the police officers entered into another salon. The owner explained to the police officer about the attacks and how local community members are saying they must close all salons at 5pm. The Police officer negotiated with the owner, saying this was a good time for him to come and cut his hair. While the salon owner was cutting the police officers’ hair, some locals, accompanied by the lady with the white Mercedes came into the salon and started shouting at the owner. They rudely asked the police officer to remove the protective cap used when cutting hair but he refused. The police officer asked them why they were trespassing in someone’s business. 
The lady who was leading the mass took her cell phone and phoned someone. After a few minutes, the former municipality manager came. The former manager used some intimidation on the police officer trying to undress him by force. When the police officer refused, the former manager slapped the police officer and that is when the police officer stood up and asked the former manager if he knows who he is dealing with! Without wasting time the police officer started to heat the former manager and took his knife pointing at the former manager and saying if you resist me, I will poke you with this knife on your neck. The police brigadier then came and tried to stop the police man. 
I left Durban on Saturday 4/8/2018 after receiving a call from my fellow refugee community who were attacked in Zeerust. In connection with our church branch in Zeerust, I decided to go there. I arrived in Johannesburg Sunday and the same day I took transport to Zeerust for about 280km. I arrived safely in Zeerust. The same day I had a meeting with more than 40 people of mostly Congolese nationals and they narrated to me how the attacks started on 30/07/2018. I conducted trauma counselling the same night and gave them strategies on how to deal with this kind of situation from my previous experience in Durban and in Kathu. 
The next morning on Monday 06/08/2018 I went to the municipality office and made an appointment to see the person in charged with safety or if possible to speak to the Mayor. Unfortunately they were all in a meeting and they asked me to come the following day. On the same day I went to Zeerust police station and was referred to Dinogana about 20km to meet with Commander and brigadier and other police officers. I went and our meeting was successful, they promised me that they would conduct patrols from that day on but also asked me to tell our fellow members not to open salons after 5pm.

records.name: Immigrants running hair salons in Pietermaritzburg say they were assaulted even though they are operating legally. ...
records.description: Immigrants running hair salons in Pietermaritzburg say they were assaulted even though they are operating legally. “Go back to your country! That’s an order,” a Msunduzi Municipality law enforcement officer reportedly told immigrants. On Monday police raided the hair salons of immigrants in Church Street, Pietermaritzburg. The salon owners say the municipal police “forcefully removed” them, pointed guns at them, used teargas, broke mirrors, and confiscated their hair clippers and chairs. Spokesperson for the municipality Thobeka Mafumbatha advised any business owner who was assaulted to open a case with the police. “I’m in this country legally and I don’t deserve such torture,” said one victim from Malawi. The victim said he had paid his business fee at the municipal offices. He has been operating his salon for 15 years at the same spot. “I was busy shaving a customer’s hair at the time. The customer was forced to leave with his hair half-shaved,” said the victim. “The first thing they did was to call us names. They told us they don’t want amakwerekwere … We asked them why they are doing this because we are not doing anything wrong.”When GroundUp arrived at the scene about 30 immigrants were standing on the roadside, picking up the pieces. Another victim, originally from Ivory Coast, came to South Africa in 1994. In 2005, he started operating his salon business. “I don’t owe the municipality anything. I pay the business fee every month. Not even once have I missed the payment. The municipality has delayed giving us business permits. They have promised to sort it out for years. We are law abiding citizens … I don’t know why foreign nationals are treated like animals … We are human beings working hard for our children,” said the victim. A South African street vendor who operates across the road said she has seen a lot of assaults on immigrants. “They call them names which is sad. At the end of the day they are human. We cannot say much because police always come here armed. We are scared. We just watch. Last month, they came more than five times. Every time they take their stuff,” said the vendor. Another witness said there is a fee paid by foreign nationals who are in the country legally. She confirmed the Monday operation. “The operation is done by the municipal police to finish illegal businesses. If there was anything that was offensive or assault done by the municipal police, the victims should open a case,” said Mafumbatha.  Story by groundup:

records.name: Xenowatch received a forwarded email from a partner orgasation. The email was with regards to a meeting that called ...
records.description: Xenowatch received a forwarded email from a partner orgasation. The email was with regards to a meeting that called on foreigners to leave the country. Email reads as follows: "Hi all! Just had a call from a journalist a yesterday. This ABM called a meeting in Umlazi on Sunday- they are demanding that all foreign nationals leave by December! Apparently there were a 100 or so people at the meeting... Xenowatch followed up with the source who informed us that she received a call from a Journalist from the Daily News in Durban on Sunday, 05 August 2018. He wanted to find out if she had heard of any attacks on foreign nationals or about the meeting that was held in Umlazi earlier in the day. Xenowatch then called the journalist to get more information on this. He stated that the meeting was called by a party called Africa Basic Movement (ABM) on Saturday via WhatsApp and announcements using a speaker throughout the township. According to the journalist a sizeable crowd had arrived to attend the meeting and from his estimation it could have been a 100 or so people present. The meeting took place on Sunday at around 10 am. The journalist was also present at the meeting and stated that he suspects that the meeting was part of the party’s campaign given the upcoming elections. The aim of the meeting was to remove foreign nationals out of the community. He further stated that the party representatives claimed that they had written an open letter to the president stating that they want foreigners to leave the country. According to the journalist, there were polarized views among the people in attendance on their opinions regarding the matter. He reported that some people in the crowd wanted foreigners to go but emphasized that they did not want violence to occur. On the other hand some defended foreigners stating that even though some engaged in criminal activities, South African citizens were also not innocent of this as well. Others stated that foreigners were adding value to the community. One person stated that she was employed by a Pakistan shop owner who has helped her more than the government, while another stated that she had foreign nationals renting in her home. No violence was reported on the day and Xenowatch will continue to monitor the situation.

records.name: On the afternoon of Monday 6 August, about fifty people danced and sang their way to Winchester Court, a block of ...
records.description: On the afternoon of Monday 6 August, about fifty people danced and sang their way to Winchester Court, a block of flats on Yeoville’s edge. The songs told of land that would be reclaimed, South African land back in authentically South African hands. A few ringleaders asked to be let into the building but were denied access by the security guard on the basis that they were not tenants or had been invited by tenants. Over the road, a spaza shop snapped shut. The mob broke down the Winchester fence and beat the guard. A bystander started videoing the incident and was promptly beaten bloody, though the guard got a chance to sprint off towards the spiffy new Yeoville police station four blocks away. Most residents were away at work, but a Zimbabwean beautician who works in Cresta, was dozing in her Winchester flat on her day off. She woke up to the sounds of doors being bashed down, security gates being ripped off their hinges, and a curious argument. “I want this room!” “No no, I said I’m taking that one first, you take that one.” “You two sort yourselves, I’m going for that one over there”. When the beautician's door was broken open, she screamed for mercy. A few rooms down, a young boy heard the same sounds and when his own door began caving in under blows from the other side, he ran for the window. He was alone. He wanted to jump, a 3m fall seeming safer than whatever was coming. People on the street shouted, ‘No, stay! You won’t be hurt.’ So he went back in and buried the family TV under blankets before hiding in the closet. In another room, a nine-year-old girl was screaming, also alone at home, clutching her family’s most valuable possession, a computer. She was slapped by one of the invaders, but she would not let go. Remarkably, the assailants rewarded her young courage (and possibly her ability to communicate in the vernacular) with clemency and the computer was saved. The attack quieted down. At the police station, the security guard  tried to raise the alarm. The police’s attention, I’m told, was elsewhere, and the security guard was asked to come back at a more convenient time, ‘tomorrow’, so he went to hospital instead. When he returned to the station, his bosses, of K201 Properties, were filing a complaint which he enjoined. Another wave of the attack followed a couple of hours later. More rent-paying tenants had returned from work by now and were told to pack their bags and go back to where they came from. No one objected. No one dared. Furniture was broken and valuables lost as a score of people carried their worldly goods through a human corridor of sjamboks, wooden clubs and jeers, which included the m-word (makwerekwere). A friend of mine had recently bought a property nearby and now turned it into a safe house for the violently evicted. With their tattered goods locked up, the victims made another trip to the police station, this time enmasse. The police, I’m told, were still preoccupied, so a sit-in ensued, lasting for several hours deep into the night. That night, the building’s two live-in security guards left their women and suckling children behind at Winchester, forced to accept the assurance that they would be safe, but that the men, had they stayed, would not. A large wooden table was set alight and taken into the courtyard to fuel a bonfire. A night of hard drink and dance ensued. Songs of Winchester Court’s liberation kept the women, babies and neighbors up till sunrise. The women desperately exchanged text messages through the night to assure their husbands that “we will see you again”. To their credit, the police did go to Winchester the next day and cleared out the property hijackers, making several arrests. On the Sunday before Winchester Court was invaded, the same songs of taking South Africa back chimed down Rockey Street to the marketplace where people with sjamboks beat the stalls, telling their owners to go back to where they came from. The same thing happened at the market the Sunday after Winchester Court was invaded. On the 13th of August, after closing, a start was allegedly made at burning the marketplace down. The police have been prompt in defending the market, shooting warning shots and dispelling mobs before any serious damage is done to the municipal property. So, till now, the market operators have been effectively defended. Still, all those I spoke to feel insecure.

records.name: Durban - An Inanda family whose shop was burned in the recent spate of attacks on shops run by foreigners, says ...
records.description: Durban - An Inanda family whose shop was burned in the recent spate of attacks on shops run by foreigners, says without the rent they were getting for it, they have no income. The shop owner said the shop had been in her family for decades. “My father built it from the ground up with his own hands. Over the years, different family members have run it but for the past 10 years, we have rented it out because we could not afford to stock it,” she said. She said the family received R4 000 rent from Somali national. The foreign national, was in the shop when an unknown group of people ordered him and other shopkeepers out, while pouring petrol over everything and setting it alight. “All the stock I had just bought, piled up to the ceiling, lots of money - about R25 000 - all burned. I tried to reason with them but they would not even talk to us, they just came in and told us to get out,” said the Somali national. They had been working and living in the shop so all their belongings were burned too. The Somali national said he had sought refuge among his fellow countrymen in the Durban CBD but did not have money to pay any contribution for his accommodation, food or transport to return home. “I lost everything but before I lose my life, I think it’s better I go home,” he said. He has been in South Africa since 2010, having started off working before saving enough money to start his own shop.

records.name: Many foreign business owners have closed their shops and fled from Zeerust in the North West. This is after suffering ...
records.description: Many foreign business owners have closed their shops and fled from Zeerust in the North West. This is after suffering attacks from locals who accuse them of drug dealing. The Congolese Solidarity Campaign has dismissed the allegations as unfounded. But locals insist the foreigners are responsible for a criminal element within the small town, and hosted a protest march on Friday. Fearing for their lives, some of these foreign nationals are hiding in nearby mountains, armed with only blankets and water. It follows attacks by locals over the past three weeks, who accuse them of drug dealing. The Congolese Solidarity Campaign has called on government for support. “This is a xenophobic attack. I plead with the government to work on it because we are innocent. We are pleading with the government to respond very fast before people can lose their lives,” says Congolese Community Leader. “Even the police should do their work. They shouldn’t arrest the criminal and release them before they reach the police station. Some of the foreign nationals say the issue of being attacked in their residential areas has affected their daily lives.” Another witness, says they fled from the Congo a year ago because of the on-going war. Now, they are simply disillusioned. “When I arrived here I thought here is a very peaceful country, but I found that it is still the same situation. People have been beating us every night and we decided now, every night we should come and sleep in the forest and it is not good for our health as human beings and for the kids,” says Congolese national. Locals have established the so-called ‘Enough is Enough Movement’, alleging to have found illegal substances in foreigners’ homes. “We came to realize that this issue is bigger than we thought. So, as the community, we do not want to be seen as or sound xenophobic to the foreign nationals. They are our compatriots. If they sell drugs, we will not allow and accommodate them within our society … Zeerust in particular,” says Chairperson of the Movement Crosby Maeema. Officials from the municipality, National Prosecuting Authority and police accepted their memorandum, and undertook to respond within seven days- SABC News

records.name: Xenowatch received a message from a partner organisation regarding notices that were given to foreign nationals ...
records.description:
Xenowatch received a message from a partner organisation regarding notices that were given to foreign nationals to evacuate the houses they are staying in otherwise they will be burnt down by community members. Xenowatch contacted Zeerust Police to inform them of these threats and to verify them. After further investigation into the issue, Canal Johnson reported back that he spoke to a few Congolese who confirmed that they had received threats to evacuate their houses in two weeks otherwise they will be  burnt down and as a result they are living in fear as to what will happen if the demands of the locals are not met by the municipality within the stipulated 7 days. Canal Johnson stated that he has informed his colleagues and they will take the necessary action to prevent this from happening. There is also a WhatsApp message circulating and it reads below as follows:

CAMPAIGN CLEAN AND SAVE SOUTH AFRICA

By End of August... Every South African who has rented their garage to Somalians for Spaza shops must chase them out or else the house and Spaza shop will be burnt on the Saturday the 8th of September. 

Forward this message to all South Africans who has Somalians in their bagyard. Their lives and kids are in danger.

records.name: Chaos has erupted in Ratanda, Heidelberg, after protesters set buildings alight and looted shops, police and locals ...
records.description:
Chaos has erupted in Ratanda, Heidelberg, after protesters set buildings alight and looted shops, police and locals say. The protests, which began on Monday and continued on Tuesday, appear to be over a lack of electricity in the area, police said. "Yesterday [Monday], there was a protest because electricity had been cut off by the local municipality. It escalated to looting. Police are on scene attempting to bring calm," police spokesperson Captain Thivhulawi Tshilate said. He said that a supermarket had also been set alight on Monday evening, but could not confirm the name of the establishment. Thus far, 54 people had been arrested, including 12 minors who were released into their parents' custody. Tshilate said those arrested faced a range of charges, from public violence to possession of stolen property. He added that there had been several clashes between police and locals. 
According to Heidelberg resident, a local U-Save in Rensburg was also set alight.
"Yesterday, on Vaal Dam Road, cars were burning and shops were being looted. The local resident further stated that there were also claims that protesters were unhappy with foreign nationals.
"Locals have been claiming that Pakistani nationals poison their food and take their jobs," he said.
Tshilate said that, while it was possible that foreign national could have been targeted, he could not immediately confirm.
Other stores, including department stores, were also closed.
The resident also described the protest as intense saying there had been clashes between police and the community.

records.name: Xenowatch received a WhatsApp text from a partner organisation with media links and a video of the incident - Hie, ...
records.description: Xenowatch received a WhatsApp text from a partner organisation with media links and a video of the incident - Hie, here are someof the recent details. What is the best response?  Please article below: One person has been shot dead during ongoing violence in White City, Soweto on Wednesday afternoon, police confirmed to News24. Lieutenant Colonel Lungelo Dlamini said shops owned by foreign nationals were being looted. "Police are there, [and] trying to deal with the situation," he said. Dlamini said he could not confirm details around the shooting. "We don't know who shot who. We are investigating." Police could also not immediately provide details on how many people were injured in the violence. More to follow. As of Monday 3 September 2018, the media now report 4 people to have died. Xenowatch conducted follow ups with the centre that temporrily housed some of the victims from the shops that were looted. The manager took us to the place were the remaining goods from the the victims' spaza shops were kept. Xenowatch was informed that the storage was keeping goods from over 100 looted shops from the families that they had assisted. Most of them were temporarily staying with family and friends in diferent areas. These attacks which are recorded in subsequent cells followed a threat that has been circulating the previous week. Poster details are as follows: Hi Fellow South African, Its final now .We tired of SOMALIANS, PAKISTANS, etc. That are killing our Families, Friends, and even our new born babies with their Imitation (fake) and expired products. They produce their own food, groceries, beverages and toiletries. Our economy is suffering because their fake products that they produced at backyard factories and they’re not taxed.  More than 50 Billion every year that they take to their countries. And We as South Africa are suffering because of their Evil deeds. Health and Food inspectors are aware of this matter but are not doing a thing. On the 29th we are striking all provinces, towns, locations. No one will be going to work. Town to town we will be marching. Please spread the word.

records.name: Looting of foreign shops in various areas in Soweto is taking place.  Xenowatch  conducted verifications after receiving ...
records.description: Looting of foreign shops in various areas in Soweto is taking place.  Xenowatch  conducted verifications after receiving notifications of the incident. At Jabulani Police station, a source confirmed that 3 shops belonging to Pakistani nationals have been looted in the North Zola area along Dendile Road, Ndaweni & Zwane Street. She stated that the looting is a result of community members complaining that Pakistani tuck shops are selling them expired products and in some cases products with poison. Police have been at the scene since 12pm to monitor the situation. She confirmed that the situation in the area is much calmer and foreign shop owners have been advised to pack up their goods and keep them in a safe area. However, she noted that even though her area is now safe, community members are spreading to other areas with no police presence. As of September 2018, the media reports 4 people to have died.

records.name: Acting National Commissioner Lieutenant General Lebeoana Tsumane has commended police for their “swift response” ...
records.description: Acting National Commissioner Lieutenant General Lebeoana Tsumane has commended police for their “swift response” and for arresting 27 people in Soweto for the recent violence and looting, which resulted in the death of three people. “By increasing deployments in the affected areas, 27 suspects were arrested for various crimes including murder, attempted murder, possession of unlicensed firearms and public violence,” he said, adding that more arrests are imminent. Earlier the City of Johannesburg's Public Safety MMC Michael Sun has confirmed that a total of 15 people have been arrested after violence erupted in Soweto, Johannesburg. Sun, who went to the Moroka police station to confirm details about killings and the arrests, said one person died after he was shot in the head and another had been stabbed to death. Sun said three people have been arrested for murder and the possession of unlicensed firearms. He said 12 others were arrested for public disorder. Violence broke out during protests in the Johannesburg suburb on Wednesday afternoon. Sun said it was believed that the violence was sparked by "accusations that shop owners within the community had allegedly been selling counterfeit and expired goods to members of the community". This came a day after the Johannesburg Metro Police Department (JMPD) conducted an operation dealing with shop owners who sold expired food to the public in another part of the city, he said. Police spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Lungelo Dlamini said the looting of foreign-owned spaza shops had spread to more parts of Soweto. Rubber bullets and teargas were fired to disperse the crowd in the afternoon. "We are trying to diffuse the situation, but it looks like it is busy spreading to other parts [of the area]," Dlamini said at the time. This, after community members cleared out almost three more spaza shops outside Margaret Gwele Primary School in Dobsonville, Soweto. Children stood on pavements and looked on as community members used metal pipes and hammers to break down the doors of the shop. They took maize meal, sugar, cooldrinks, bread and household products. Empty packets, boxes and plastic bottles lined the streets. At one stage, a car stopped at one of the shops and goods were loaded into the boot. According to a resident, who asked to remain anonymous, only one police vehicle was seen in the area, though it left later. "They broke into all the Indian shops in the area. We tried to phone the police several times, but they didn't come," the woman said. Sun urged residents not to take the law into their own hands not to resort to acts of violence and looting. "We will continue to monitor the situation as night falls. We suspect there will be more looting and violence. Both JMPD and police will be out on full force and we do urge community members to stay indoors." Speaking to retailers, he said: "I also urge all shop owners and retailers to immediately remove from their shelves any counterfeit and expired foodstuff or goods. JMPD will continue conducting an operation to rid our community of such ill business practices."

records.name: DURBAN - While looting of foreigners tuck shops was rife in Soweto this week, two foreign shop owners survived serious ...
records.description:
DURBAN - While looting of foreigners tuck shops was rife in Soweto this week, two foreign shop owners survived serious arson attacks in Durban this week. Arsonists attempted to burn them alive inside their tuck shops on Thursday. The incidents took place in KwaDabeka, near Pinetown and in Newlands West, to the north of Durban. KwaDabeka-based Ethiopian shopkeeper  victim, was sleeping in the Thursday night when his shop was attacked and set alight. He narrowly escaped and survived with minor injuries.  Four men armed with guns and petrol attacked his container and fled with R4000 after breaking in with an axe. "They broke their way through the store and pointed their firearm at me, the container was already on fire at that time. Others stood outside and kept shouting, 'Dubula inja (shoot the dog)'. I pleaded with them not to take my life, after they had already taken more than R4000 from my safe, airtime machine and cigarettes, “ the victim said. The victim's brother who is the owner of the tuck shop was already refurbishing his container that was gutted by fire, when Sunday Tribune visited the scene. He  was adamant that he would give up on his shop. He recounted the fateful incidents he had endured since he came to Durban in 2012 while he was painting his burnt container. His shop has been attacked numerous times. 
He said from time to time he had to start afresh because his shop was constantly attacked.  “We no longer fear for our lives because being attacked has become a norm in their lives. Government and police have failed us, our only hope is God,” said the brother.  
police.

records.name: Police spokesperson Colonel Thembeka Mbele said the Newlands attack happened on Friday morning. The shopkeeper was ...
records.description: Police spokesperson Colonel Thembeka Mbele said the Newlands attack happened on Friday morning. The shopkeeper was sleeping inside the shop when he noticed smoke coming in. He tried to get out, but the shop was locked. He shouted for help and people from the house in whose yard the container was located, doused the flames and released him. He suffered burns and was said to be recovering in hospital.

records.name: Two Congolese foreign nationals came to the Xenowatch offices this afternoon to report that they are still receiving ...
records.description:
Two Congolese foreign nationals came to the Xenowatch offices this afternoon to report that they are still receiving threats from community members in Zeerust. Community members are still telling them to leave the country otherwise they will burn down their houses. Both victims report that community members are still assaulting foreign nationals and forcing them to close their salons before 5pm. One of the victims reports that his wife was assaulted at his salon on Tuesday. The other says he is being falsely accused of selling drugs, assaulted and fears for his life. They report that they have lost a lot of business and are unable to sustain themselves financially since the attacks began in late July. Their children have not been able to attend school since the threats began as they have also been told to go back to their country. Both victims state that all foreigners in Zeerust fear for their lives and a possible break out of violence in the area. They mentioned that although, UNCHR and South African Human Rights Commission (Zeerust office) visited the area and had a meeting with foreign nationals, community members and representatives from the Congolese National Solidarity Campaign, nothing was really resolved as community members went back to threatening and  assaulting them after the two organisations left the area.

They are requesting for assistance and for organisations to mediate the situation and speak with community members on their behalf. Both victims stated that they were traumatized and were in need on counselling.

records.name: Xenowatch received a whatsapp message with a link to the incident :- A Brixton shop owner of Bangladeshi descent, ...
records.description: Xenowatch received a whatsapp message with a link to the incident :- A Brixton shop owner of Bangladeshi descent, and his brother, narrowly escaped death on Saturday morning when their shop was torched, Johannesburg police said. Spokesperson Captain Mavela Masondo said the owner of the Store was asleep with his brother when he heard a window shattering at 05:10. "He woke up to investigate and saw something that looks like liquid dripping next to his bed. The next thing the fire erupted," said Masondo. He and his brother fled the shop from another door and the shop was gutted. The fire department came out and people from the flats upstairs were safely evacuated.The blaze was doused and the flats upstairs appear to have been spared.Nobody was injured and police would investigate further. The owners are estimated to have lost stock worth R150 000 and cash.

records.name: Xenowatch received a whatsapp message from a partner -"Reports of burning in Klerksdorp this morning at 10.30am. ...
records.description: Xenowatch received a whatsapp message from a partner -"Reports of burning in Klerksdorp this morning at 10.30am. Allegations are that a taxi owner was Killed by a Nigerian migrant. They then burnt down a Nigerian owned shop. Please share with contacts in the area to verify." Upon further verification Xenowatch came across media articles that confirmed the incident. The incident is detailed below based on a media report. Two men have reportedly been killed in the escalating violence between taxi drivers and foreign nationals in Pienaarsdorp, Klerksdorp. According to an IOL report, police said the two men had been killed in separate incidents on Sunday in the wake of apparent clashes between taxi drivers and foreign nationals in the North West town. Police spokesperson Brigadier Sabata Mokgwabone told IOL that the body of a man was found on the street on Sunday morning. He was believed to be a taxi driver. "It is alleged that an unconfirmed number of taxi drivers grouped themselves later in a bid to avenge the death of their colleague, whom they suspect to have been killed by a foreign national." OFM reported that police further confirmed a foreign national had been stabbed to death later on Sunday. Stalls at the local taxi rank were also set on fire. Police had been deployed to restore calm to the area. No arrests have been made yet, but two separate cases of murder have been opened and investigations are ongoing.

records.name: A spaza shop and a vehicle belonging to a foreign national have been set alight in Tshamahansi village, outside ...
records.description:
A spaza shop and a vehicle belonging to a foreign national have been set alight in Tshamahansi village, outside Mokopane. This comes after the businessman shot and killed a man who allegedly tried to break into his shop on Wednesday night.
Community members now want revenge for the 24-year-old man’s killing. Police officials are investigating whether the Somali national's gun was legal.
Spokesperson Moatshe Ngoepe says: “We would like to condemn these types of acts by the local community of taking the law into their own hands. At this stage, we are still investigating.” (Edited by Shimoney Regter)

records.name: Police are yet to make any arrests after looting erupted in Coronationville‚ west of Johannesburg on Tuesday. It ...
records.description: Police are yet to make any arrests after looting erupted in Coronationville‚ west of Johannesburg on Tuesday. It was later confirmed that the shop was owned by a foreign national. "It is alleged that the shop was closed when the complainant [the shop owner] saw a crowd of approximately 200 people attacking his shop with bricks and breaking the security gates open‚" said Captain Mavela Masondo. "After gaining entry‚ the suspects started looting the shop. It is alleged that items taken include bread‚ cigarettes‚ airtime‚ deep freezer‚ meat‚ cold drinks and airtime."Police have since opened a case of public violence. No arrests have been made. The incident comes about a month after a series of foreign-owned shops were looted in Soweto‚ apparently triggered by complaints of ‘fake’ or expired foods.

records.name: Following media reports of Shangaan and Mozambican shop owners being chased out of Duduza after a 4 year old baby ...
records.description: Following media reports of Shangaan and Mozambican shop owners being chased out of Duduza after a 4 year old baby was found dead. Xenowatch contacted Duduza police station to verify the incident. Captain Harry manaka confirmed that the incident had occurred. It started late afternoon around 15pm on the 8th -10th of October. He stated that it was spiked by the discovery of a child who had been found dead. The person who was being suspected by the community for killing the baby was of Shangaan origin, that is why they explicitly tartgeted shangaans. He informed Xenowatch that the sporadic unrests turned into random acts of criminality and a mission to target Shangaan's and their belongings as people took advantage of the situation and started looting shops belonging to Shangaan shop owners, stealing food and some even going to the extent of stealing fridges with goods inside. They also caused damage to property by breaking down doors etc.. Captain Manaka noted that around 6 shops were looted in the area and three people have been arrested for public violence, malicious damage to property and theft. He also noted that the situation has since calmed down in the area after the 11th of October 2018. Captain Manana also noted that since the 2015 xenophobic attacks, all foreign nationals that owned shops moved out of the area, the only area that still has foreign owned shops is in the John Dube area.

records.name: Properties belonging to foreign nationals have been looted after a 26-year-old man was arrested for murder in Middelburg, ...
records.description: Properties belonging to foreign nationals have been looted after a 26-year-old man was arrested for murder in Middelburg, Mpumalanga, on Wednesday. Police spokesperson Brigadier Leonard Hlathi said that the protests were sparked by the discovery of the remains of a 25-year-old woman. "When police arrived at the scene they discovered that it was the body of a woman with the head covered with a plastic bag and the rest of the body wrapped in a blanket," he said. "The victim was declared dead by paramedics who were summoned to the scene and a case of murder was opened. Police then launched an investigation following all possible clues, which led them to Tshwane in Gauteng, where they arrested the suspect." Police have also discovered that the victim had been burned with a hot plate and stabbed with a sharp object. "A post-mortem will be conducted to determine the cause of death and for further investigation," Hlathi said. The suspect will appear in the Middelburg Magistrate's Court on a charge of murder. So far, the victim is still not yet identified and police urge anyone with a missing family member who could possibly be the woman in her late twenties to come forward. News 24

records.name: Tension lurks in the streets of Hillbrow in Johannesburg as residents continue to clash over drug activities in ...
records.description: Tension lurks in the streets of Hillbrow in Johannesburg as residents continue to clash over drug activities in the area. At the weekend residents allegedly attacked Nigerian nationals who are accused of selling drugs. They burnt their properties and looted shops on Sunday night. Two weeks ago the community chased away alleged drug dealers, raided flats and confiscated drugs that were later handed to MEC for community safety Sizakele Nkosi-Malobane. Angry Nigerian nationals and business operators yesterday shared their frustrations at the ongoing attacks. A bar on Fife Road was burnt down by a mob that arrived in the area at about 11pm on Sunday. "I was here earlier that night and I saw a group of people demonstrating in the street. I closed the business early because of that. At about 11pm I received a call from my security guys who told me that people were breaking everything," he said. "Everybody including my tenants ran away. I have been operating this business for 20 years and I do not have any problem with the community."  The estimated damage at the bar was about R2m. "They stole everything and burnt the place down. I had eight TVs, R200000 in liquor stock. I had just renovated the ceiling, my machines, computers and all the furniture was burnt," he said. The bar owner said no one had complained to him about drugs in his business before. "I don't know what to do. I have 15 employees, who is going to pay their salaries? I don't know where to start. This is xenophobia. If they are fighting drugs they must go after those people," he said. The bar owner has reported the incident to the police. who owns White Spice shop with his brother said he believed the attacks where xenophobic. His shop was looted and vandalised. "People were assaulted, it got worse at night. They started breaking shops at 10pm. This thing is not a drug issue. It is pure looting and xenophobic attacks. We are not safe. Two of our brothers are in a coma in hospital. We are crying out for help. Police spokesperson Captain Mavela Masondo said they were investigating cases of public violence and malicious damage to property. He said no one was arrested for the attacks." Sowetan live

records.name: The victim is one of dozens of immigrant shopkeepers from Ethiopia, Somalia, Bangladesh and Pakistan who are living ...
records.description:
The victim is one of dozens of immigrant shopkeepers from Ethiopia, Somalia, Bangladesh and Pakistan who are living in fear in Osizweni, Newcastle. A spate of violent robbery attacks on immigrant-owned shops has claimed the lives of two Bangladeshi businessmen in the past week, GroundUp reports. The victims  who worked as partners in a rented store in Osizweni Section C were stabbed to death during a robbery in the early hours of Thursday, October 25. "We are foreign businessmen in a foreign country, and we are all now living in fear because we don't know what will happen next," said a witness. "We don't know when the attacks will stop, but we have no choice but to keep the business running, because this is our livelihood and our only source of income." Police have arrested two men, aged 25 and 28, for the murders. A 61-year-old woman — a landlady of a rented store — was arrested for defeating the ends of justice. She was found by the police washing blood-stained clothes belonging to the alleged murder suspects. Money, stolen cigarette boxes, airtime vouchers to the total value of R9 200 as well as blood-stained knives were found in the possession of one of the suspects, according to Osizweni police spokesperson Captain Sipho Nkosi. The suspects will appear at Madadeni Regional Court on November 2. Shops closed said  an individual from Hosaena, Ethiopia. He has lived in Newcastle for almost three years. He arrived in South Africa with his elder brother, A, in 2016.  His elder brother runs a shop in Johannesburg. Another individual , who co-owns a container-housed shop in Osizweni Section C, said: "There have been many attacks targeted at us the foreign shop owners in this township, and this year it has even been worse. I'm also one of those shop owners who have been at the mercy of violent robbers in recent months as I was attacked in September." About three robbers used crowbars to force my shop's door open in the  early hours at about 03:00. "I was awakened by a loud bang on the door and I quickly realised that the robbers had arrived. In just about two minutes the door had been forced open and the robbers were upon me, and I pleaded for mercy as they demanded money, cigarettes and airtime. "I was very frightened that they would kill me as they were carrying crowbars and knives, so at that moment I was pleading for my dear life, as they were helping themselves to the valuables.
"Just after they had just left, that's when I screamed for help and the neighbours came out for help, though the robbers had already fled the scene," said the victim.Some shops run by Bangladeshi and Pakistani businessmen have closed down in recent months due to the constant robberies.

records.name: Durban - Two refugee brothers were burnt to death allegedly by members of a local community in the Adams Mission ...
records.description: Durban - Two refugee brothers were burnt to death allegedly by members of a local community in the Adams Mission area of Durban on Tuesday last week. The police on Monday confirmed that two men had been killed, but said the identities of the victims remained unknown subject to DNA testing. “Charges of murder are being investigated by KwaMakhutha South African Police Services. It is alleged on 11 December at 6am, two bodies of unknown men were found burnt at Nkangala area, Adams Mission,” one of KwaZulu-Natal’s police spokespersons, captain Nqobile Gwala, told African News Agency (ANA). A representative of the Africa Solidarity Network (Asonet) said the brothers were from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The men’s names are known to ANA. One was a fridge mechanic and the other a barber. One of the brothers is survived by a girlfriend and two young children, who were both born in South Africa. Both men were in their early 30s. The representative said the murders took place when the brothers were collecting a fridge for repairs from the Adams Mission area. “Other than that we are unable to get any other information,” he said. “The silence of the local police on repeated attacks and blatant disregard for lives was clear in the assault and ultimate brutal murder of [the brothers]” ANA representative said. “We call on the president of the country to deal with tribalist vigilante groups and bring justice to the deaths of African people. He also called on the minister of Justice to act against xenophobia and for the Department of International Relations and Cooperation to protect African refugees. "We ask all human rights groups to stand with the victims and survivors in keeping refugees safe in this country and hold the national government to account for not dealing with this phenomena which has become a violent reality of many African people,” Byamungu said. Human rights activist Vanessa Burger said she received reports that the incident was first reported to the 10111 Crime Stop number “but police failed to respond”. “Relatives and representatives of the refugee community have also alleged that the police have proved unhelpful or even refused to provide information to them regarding the incident,” adding that she had written to the SAPS acting provincial commissioner in KwaZulu-Natal for assistance with the case.

Dear Colleagues,
We  have just been alerted of this development in Alexandra  Township Ext. 7 in Johannesburg. At this point, we are unsure whether those affected are PoCs but it is reported that a group of 70 odd men from an organization calling itself "Bonafide
