Eye Witness News (EWN) reports that  SAPS officials have been accused of failing to protect the foreign nationals. The group has threatened that " From January we will be taking them all out in Alexandra and not just in extension 7." Unconfirmed death

records.name: Xenowatch conducted verifications on the housing situation in Alex: According to sources, people are still being ...
records.description:
Xenowatch conducted verifications on the housing situation in Alex: According to sources, people are still being chased out of their houses although the incidents are now happening sporadically and mostly on weekends than during weekdays. On Wednesday (16th Jan), the day Xenowatch made follow ups, sources reported that there had been no forced removals since Monday.
•         The removals are taking place in Alex Ext 7,9 & 10. According to one of Xenowatch sources’ ext 10 is the most affected as it has more foreign nationals living there.
•         The group that is chasing people out of their homes claims to have a list of names of people on the waiting list to receive RDP houses. The group claim to have been granted permission by the MEC to remove those not on the list and give the houses to those who had registered for them a long time ago but are still on the waiting. One of the sources reported that this is not true as the group evicting people take most of the houses for themselves.
•         According to all sources, police made arrests and intervened when this incident first started last year, but currently they are not doing anything. Xenowatch called Alex Police station on Tuesday this week to report the incident. According to the police, they received reports of the incidents last year and arrested individuals on charges of property damage, assault and other charges related to the incident. Currently, police report that the situation is under control as they have engaged with the Department of Housing and Home Affairs to intervene and will not make any arrests.

records.name: Following up on the email received from our partner organisation on the 25th of February 2019, Xenowatch conducted ...
records.description:
Following up on the email received from our partner organisation on the 25th of February 2019, Xenowatch conducted further verifications with the Witback Police station and this is the information gathered: Following previous emails regarding the looting of shops in Witbank, Vosman area. Xenowatch managed to conduct further verifications and spoke to Brigadier Mota. She confirmed that she was heading the operation but denied that foreign shops were looted. According to Brigadier Mota, it was operation Fiela which started on the 13th of Feb 2019 when 7 women from Lesotho came to the police station to report that the Ethiopian tuck shop owners they were working for underpay them (R1200) and constantly monitor and search their suitcases to make sure they have not stolen any goods. Following this, Brigadier Mota contacted DHA, Health, Labour, environmental affairs and other government departments and together they embarked on an operation to check if tuck shop owners in the area where in compliance according to South African laws of running a business and had the correct documentation to do so. Those who were found  to be non complaint had their shops shut and their goods taken for exhibition. She maintains that foreigners were not explicitly targeted during this process but because 90% of them own tuck shops, they were the most affected. Moreover, she maintains that as the police, they did nothing wrong and followed all the regulations of South African law for every action they took. As far as she is concerned foreign nationals must ensure that they comply with South African Laws. Our partner organisation then followed up with this information a few weeks later on the 1st of April 2019: This email serves to provide a brief summary of reports of violence towards non-nationals residing in Witbank Mpumalanga. We have also received a new report today of an attack in Pretoria West. 
Witbank, Mpumalanga (Feb – March 2019)

•         Last week 142 affected non-nationals approached our offices seeking to report incidences of violence 
•         It appears that in February 2019, Operation Fiela was initiated and most people we consulted with confirmed that it was coordinated by different government departments eg: Labour and DHA. 
•         Most shop owners state that in February 2019, the police under the instruction of Brigadier Mota who referred to them as “kwerekweres” told them to shut down their stores and leave the country. A few of their goods were looted at this point in time by the police. They have confirmed that the DHA did not harass them in anyway. 
•         They subsequently got a Court order  which interdicted the conduct of the police and permitted the shop owners to make applications for temporary trading licences within 7days. The manner in  which the Operation was conducted was also declared to be unlawful
•         Some shop owners who already have trading licences report that their shops were still looted and they were still told to shut down and leave the country 
•         On 20 March 2019 the police began raiding foreign owned shops. The following nationalities were affected– Pakistan, Bangladesh, Somali and Ethiopian. 
•         All of the people we consulted with were male. Most of the men were single and the minority have wives and children residing with them in SA
•         Most people live where they trade and have become homeless as a result of the lootings 
•         They have now fled to nearby churches and mosques for shelter
•         Many have reported being hungry and in need of social assistance and have been left with nothing except the clothes on their back
•         Majority of the people we saw were documented. 
•         Some reported having had their refugee or asylum seeker permits burnt, torn or lost during the lootings. 
•         Majority of the people we consulted with were asylum seekers and refugees with valid permits.
•         Some individuals were physically assaulted by the police. Some received medical assistance and got stiches. 
•         We also received many reports of Vosman Police station refusing to open police cases and telling individuals to go back to their country and leave South Africa 

Please note, this is a very general account of the reports we received, but it appears from the information we have this initially started off as Operation Fiela but took a xenophobic turn.

records.name: Xenowatch conducted further verifications and this is an email responding to the nformation we gathered. Dear .......I ...
records.description: Xenowatch conducted further verifications and this is an email responding to the nformation we gathered. Dear .......I managed to conduct follow-ups on the possible planned Xenophobic attacks in Hermanus with various sources on the ground. This is the information I have been able to gather so far: Two sources have confirmed to receiving a WhatsApp audio clip detailing plans to close down foreign national shops in Zwelihle area on the 7th. The WhatsApp audio which is in isiXhosa seems to have been recorded in a community meeting that took place two weeks ago. The speaker in the audio clip can be heard telling those in attendance that after his last court case on the 6th. He is going to call on local community members to help him close down foreign-owned shops in the area on the 7th. He will target around 20 shops in the area. The audio clip was forwarded to the Xenowatch WhatsApp number and the source who forwarded it states that he also sent it to the UNHCR office in Cape Town. One of the sources living in Zwelihle confirmed that foreign nationals in the area are living in fear for their lives and are afraid to report the matter to the police as they fear intimidation by local community members. Another source from, an organization that works with a network of undocumented migrants in Cape Town, informed Xenowatch that he had not heard about the threats but would share the information with his network including those who live in Zwelihle and a contact in the provincial government office. If he receives new information he will inform Xenowatch. Xenowatch also contacted Hermanus police station to find out if they had received information on the plans to close down foreign-owned shops on the 7th. Kennel Africa confirmed that they had not yet heard of the threats but are aware of an organization called Zwelihle Renewal (ZR) which instigates toyi toyis in the area almost every day with constant threats to close down foreign-owned shops. Kennel Africa stated that the police have tried to speak to the leaders of this organization on several occasions and have warned them several times not to take the law into their own hands but they are arrogant and very aggressive. Kennel Africa further informed Xenowatch that ZR also goes to the extent of intimidating South African locals who refuse to be involved in their activities and threaten to burn their houses down.  Xenowatch has forwarded Kennel Africa the WhatsApp audio clip and he has informed us that he will pass it to the crime intelligence unit to conduct further verifications and investigations in Zwelihle. His office will revert to Xenowatch with any information they are able to gather. At the same time, Kennel Africa will inform his colleagues about the threats so that if an incident occurs they are prepared with enough manpower to take action. Xenowatch will continue to monitor and follow up on this case with the sources identified on the ground, in the next coming days. Updates on any new information will be provided or in the likelihood, an intervention is required.

records.name: On the night of the 17th of March several houses belonging to Zimbabwean immigrants were burnt in Vumani, Limpopo. ...
records.description: On the night of the 17th of March several houses belonging to Zimbabwean immigrants were burnt in Vumani, Limpopo. Victims are reported to have fled from their homes because of xenophobic attacks. Reports mention that there is an immigrant who lost his car  and house that he has been renting for over years. He has moved to Duthuni, 20km from Tshino village. It is also mentioned in the article that Limpopo is one of the fewer provinces that have few xenophobic incidents but 2 of the suspects are expected to appear in court on the 25th of April 2019.

records.name: During protests in Kwathema, last week, immigrants were terrorised and their shops looted. Some immigrant shops ...
records.description: During protests in Kwathema, last week, immigrants were terrorised and their shops looted. Some immigrant shops have remained closed. A Somali shop owner told GroundUp that he pays for "protection" during protests by giving cash, cool drinks and paraffin to protesters. "Those who do not contribute do not have protection during the protest and their shops get broken into," says the source, who is 29 years old and came to the area in November 2018. "They broke into my shop four times before l started contributing cold drinks and paraffin for the protests. I always give them two litres of paraffin for burning tyres during protests. On top of that l give them a crate of 18 cold drinks and another crate of energy drinks." The source says he also pays a total of R4000 a month to two men who "protect" and give him information whenever looting is planned."I can say that l am a lucky man. No one touches me or my stock now," he says. The community of Extension 3 is planning a protest next week. The source says he already has some paraffin and drinks to give to the planners of the protest. Last week, a mob torched the shop of a Somali shopkeeper. The victim had a nine-year lease with a local community member , agreed to in 2016. The victim said that last week he was awoken at night by stones smashing his windows and landing on top of the roof of his shack in Extension 3, Kwathema. "Everyone knows that when stones are thrown on top of the roof … a mob has come knocking," said  the owner. "It was terrifying. Voices were shouting that they had come for the Somali man, who was running a shop on my yard. Some were chanting, demanding that l open my gate. Luckily, police had taken " the Somali" to safety earlier that day. The owner said the mob broke into the shop and looted what they could. They stripped the metal shelves and doors. Then they poured paraffin and set a match to what remained. The fire department extinguished the fire, but much of the stock had already been incinerated. "I do not not know if he will come back because he is no longer answering my calls. The money which l got from renting the shop to him was my only source of livelihood as l am unemployed," he said. "The sad thing about the Somali is that his family back home sold their house in Somalia to pay for his business,"  says a source. "He had been paying rent for his family back home monthly with proceeds from his shop. Now that his stock has been destroyed life has become difficult for not only him but his family in Somalia." The source says the Somali community is putting money together to try and help the victim. Immigrant shop owners are caught up in the middle because people are trying to catch the attention of the government," said resident Nurse Mota. We have been living in shacks since 2007. Although we now have electricity and toilets, we still do not have houses," said a resident. The community has held protests every two weeks for the past three months. "The most frustrating thing is that the municipality switches off our electricity and water asking us to pay rent. When we go to the office to pay rent they give us utility bills which are under other people's names. We want our houses to be registered in our names. How can l pay rent for a stand that does not belong to me?" asked a resident. Mota said: "My stand is registered under Mphahleli. I don't know who that is." A resident says he does not know why people loot when the protests are not about immigrant shop owners. "I feel sorry for the Somalis," says South African fruit and vegetable vendor Smangaloso Mbaso, "because if they do not give the planners what they want their shops are looted." "No one will dare loot my vegetables," he says. "We do not even know who plans the protests. The protests start anytime and we are not even told."

records.name: In the afternoon of March 25, a group of South African truck drivers and other locals protesting the employment ...
records.description: In the afternoon of March 25, a group of South African truck drivers and other locals protesting the employment of foreign truck drivers blocked the South Coast Road near Durban’s dock yards, and then moved along the lines of stopped traffic, forcing truck drivers out of their vehicles and demanding their driver’s licenses to identify foreign nationals. The group then took the keys from many drivers they identified as foreign nationals, left the trucks on the road, then beat the drivers. One of the victims, a driver, told Human Rights Watch he was stabbed as the police looked on, without apprehending the attackers or helping him get medical care. He said that six protesters approached his truck and told him to get out. Once he showed them his driver’s license, which revealed his nationality, one of the assailants lurched out of the group and stabbed him in the stomach once with a knife.  “As I fell down bleeding, I saw [the assailants] casually walk away while the police [monitoring the protest] watched,” Takawira said. “I called out to the police to ask for help, but they ignored me and continued to watch as other protesters ransacked my truck, stealing my shoes and food.”  The victim said that the police at the protest at the time said their mandate was to monitor the protest and not to arrest people. They did not arrest his attackers or write a report about the assault. The victim was able to reach help over his mobile phone, and an ambulance arrived to transport him to hospital more than half an hour after he had been stabbed. The victim’s uncle, who responded to his phone call for help, told Human Rights Watch the police refused to write a report about the assault on Takawira and to arrest the assailants, saying they feared the protestors might attack the police if they intervened. Human Rights Watch was unable to independently corroborate this information. Source: Human Rights Watch

records.name: The protests began in the early hours where foreign nationals who were attacked include Malawians, few Mozambicans, ...
records.description: The protests began in the early hours where foreign nationals who were attacked include Malawians, few Mozambicans, Zimbabweans, Somalis and Ethiopians. 1 South African national who was looting  was shot by a Somali shop owner. While other people allegedly died during a stampede. During this, 5 Somali and 1 Ethiopian shops were looted while several peoplewere assaulted but numbers were not specified. 250 people were displaced to Sherwood although it is now closed and it may be said that these protests were started by NORBA, Northen Region Business Association who used the President's speech as a way to gain support. There was repose through humanitarian support where the displaced where provided with shelter.

records.name: Main nationalities targetted were Malawians and ethiopian shop owners. According to eyewitnesses, many were assaulted/beaten ...
records.description: Main nationalities targetted were Malawians and ethiopian shop owners. According to eyewitnesses, many were assaulted/beaten but no exact number. 11 ethiopian shops looted. 1 Somali shop not looted but was closed. Owner paid protection fees, according to respodents. Malawians fled to Overport Mosque.

records.name: Malawian and Mozambique shop owners were attacked and their shops looted. In order  to protect themselves they had ...
records.description: Malawian and Mozambique shop owners were attacked and their shops looted. In order  to protect themselves they had to seek shelter in neighbouring areas and with friends and family. According to eye witnesses 3 shops that belonged to Ethiopians were looted whilst one continued working because they had paid for protection. Also according to eye witnesses many were injured/ assaulted but there was no exact number mentioned.

records.name: The multiple-stabbing in the back of Malawian national on Saturday in Diepsloot, north of Joburg, was a message ...
records.description:
The multiple-stabbing in the back of Malawian national on Saturday in Diepsloot, north of Joburg, was a message to the country that crime targeted specifically at foreign nationals was xenophobia. The victim merely asked two men sitting on a street corner for directions as he was unfamiliar with the area. The Mamelodi resident was visiting his niece. The men refused to answer, but as the victim turned away to cross the street they went after him, stabbing him multiple times in the lower back near the spinal cord and also in the upper arm. They never stole his money nor any of his possessions he had in the bag he was carrying. The vicious stabbing was a hate crime targeted at someone who clearly did not come from South Africa. “It was a xenophobic attack as the men I approached could hear from my accent that I was not from South Africa and they were looking at each other strangely,” the victim said. “All I heard was people screaming on the other side of the road, and as I looked down I saw they had stabbed me and blood was pouring out all over the road. “No one came to my rescue, and this happened very close to the Diepsloot police station,” the victim told Independent Media. “An ambulance came and took me to Tembisa hospital. Once I regained consciousness, I told a SAPS officer at the hospital what had happened, hoping he would take a statement from me, but he just told me he couldn’t help as he only works in Tembisa, not Diepsloot,” the victim said. Tembisa hospital discharged the victim 48 hours after his admission, saying they needed to make space for other emergency cases. He was discharged with only painkillers and antibiotics and forced to return by public transport to Mamelodi with no access to medical care for his wounds. Independent Media informed Minister of Police Bheki Cele’s office of the incident and of the fact that no statement was taken by the police, and was told that the provincial police commissioner would be alerted. Despite having provided the minister’s office with Kanyemba’s contact details, by Monday afternoon Kanyemba had still not been contacted by the police for a statement. “This is a clear example of hatred against a foreign national, and cannot be categorised as criminality. It is obviously xenophobia,” Fulu Sinthumule, the director of the Consortium for Refugees and Migrants in South Africa (CoRMSA) said. “When we have seen attacks against foreign nationals in 2008, 2015, and currently, we hear political leaders say it is criminal elements, but these attacks are pure hatred, and it is time they are recognised as xenophobic,” Sinthumule said. “It is time to make the National Action Plan Against Racial Intolerance and Xenophobia, which was launched last week by Deputy 
Minister of Justice John Jeffrey, a living document. The National Action Plan was launched on March 25, but a day later the xenophobic attacks against Malawian nationals broke out in Durban. Pope Francis has added his voice, issuing a plea for host countries to treat migrants and refugees with humanity.

records.name: Somali Shops looted. 4 Ethiopian shops looted. Police responded quickly to stop and prevent the spread ...
records.description: Somali Shops looted. 4 Ethiopian shops looted. Police responded quickly to stop and prevent the spread of the violence

records.name: At least 8 sustained serious injuries, taken to hospital, now recovering. 5 kidnapped by perpetrators and rescued ...
records.description: At least 8 sustained serious injuries, taken to hospital, now recovering. 5 kidnapped by perpetrators and rescued by the police. Kinappers were not arrested.  All hair saloons belonging to foreign nationals were looted in the area although the number is not disclosed.  51 Congolese, Ethopians and Burundis were displaced and are currently acommodated at a shelter in Durban Town. They spend the day at RSS and slept at a shelter. African Basic movement provided most of the information. Police rescued the kidnapped and there was some humanitarian aid in terms of shelter.

records.name:
Pretoria West (31 March 2019)

•         A man together with his wife and 3 young children approached our office ...
records.description:
Pretoria West (31 March 2019)

•         A man together with his wife and 3 young children approached our office today (asylum seekers from the DRC )
•         The man’s clothes were covered in  blood and he had a large bandage on his forehead. Visible wounds on his chest were also present. 
•         The man stated that he had been attacked on 31 March 2019 by a mob of people who were wearing ANC t-shirts
•         They had raided his home together with the homes of 2 other people who are from Zimbabwe and Mozambique 
•         The individuals told him and his family that “foreigners were taking land and should leave. Land must go to South Africans first and the kwerekweres must go.”
•         His wife and children were slapped. 
•         The mob told him that they were going to kill him and he managed to run away to the Pretoria West police station where they followed him throwing rocks and chanting that he should leave the country. 
•         At the police station , members of the crowd openly called him a kwerekwere and demanded that he leave the country. 
•         The police did not make any arrests or open any cases. Instead they informed the man that the problem was beyond their control and bigger than them. They also told him that it was a national problem that will not get resolved anytime soon and it may be best that he goes back to DRC 
•         Since the crowd was angry and he was bleeding profusely, the police agreed to drop him off at a friend’s house. He subsequently got medical assistance at a Hospital

records.name: Cofimvaba  immigrant shop owners are forced to pay for protection
records.description: Immigrant shop owners in the Eastern Cape town of Cofimvaba claim that the South African National Civic Organization (SANCO) and the Intsika Yethu Business Forum are extorting money from them under the guise of "protecting" their shops from xenophobic attacks. On Wednesday, April 3, 2019, a group led by SANCO closed down all immigrant-owned shops in Cofimvaba, alleging various labor abuses and claiming sexual harassment of employees. They then marched to the Ntsika Yethu Municipality offices. Prior to this, shop owners received text messages from the Managing Director of the Intsika Yethu Business Forum, informing them that their employees had joined SANCO and requesting their release for a "labor desk meeting" on Wednesday, April 10. Following the meeting, SANCO accused immigrant shop owners of mistreating their local employees and subjecting them to slave-like working conditions. Immigrant shop owners reported being pressured to close their shops to force them into paying protection money. They claimed they were coerced into joining the Intsika Yethu Business Forum and paying a joining fee of R300, followed by a monthly subscription of R100, whether they agreed or not. While some complied, many resisted, leading to their shops being forcibly closed. They were told that joining the business forum would guarantee protection against xenophobic attacks, despite no such attacks ever occurring in the area. A spokesperson for the immigrant shop owners stated that they had never felt threatened and were unaware of any impending attacks. Another noted that only immigrants were targeted, as larger stores like Spar and Boxer were never approached to join the business forum and continued operating while immigrant shops were forced to close.
records.duration: Few weeks but continued sporadically for several months after.
records.response: Insika yethu local municipality organised meetings with various stakeholders. But it was Groundup media that exposed the incident to the rest of the country, including the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC). Subsequently, the SAHRC went to investigate few years later after more incidents were reported.

records.name: Congolese street vendor who has been in South Africa since 2001, “The victim” told Human Rights Watch that on April ...
records.description: Congolese street vendor who has been in South Africa since 2001, “The victim” told Human Rights Watch that on April 12, 2019, he was selling clothing on the street in Johannesburg when nine South Africans carrying sjamboks, heavy leather or synthetic whips, approached him. The victim said he first attempted to engage with them in English, but when they rejected his efforts, he tried to run away but was caught and beaten. They stole all the clothing he intended to sell, losing his income for his family for which he is the sole breadwinner. His wife had previously sold second-hand clothing at flea markets in Johannesburg but told Human Rights Watch that she quit because of excessive harassment from South African locals.

records.name: On April 27 at around 2 a.m., a Zimbabwean driver was asleep in his truck at the Durban port when a gasoline bomb ...
records.description: On April 27 at around 2 a.m., a Zimbabwean driver was asleep in his truck at the Durban port when a gasoline bomb was thrown at his truck, setting it on fire. The driver managed to escape but suffered severe burns and the loss of movement in his left arm, where his shirt became stuck to his body in the fire. Human Rights Watch spoke to the driver on June 29 in a Durban hospital, where he had been for the two months since the attack. The driver said that he was unable to speak for three days after the attack, and that the police came to take his statement the following week. The man had not heard anything from the police since then. Because of his injuries, the driver most likely will not be able to work again. He also said that his papers, including his asylum documents, driver’s permit, and passport, were all burned in the truck.

records.name: Around 11 p.m. on May 18, at Mooi river on the N3 Highway about 140 kilometers from Durban on the road to Johannesburg, ...
records.description: Around 11 p.m. on May 18, at Mooi river on the N3 Highway about 140 kilometers from Durban on the road to Johannesburg, a group of unidentified men threw stones at a Zimbabwean driver’s truck, shattering the windshield, injuring the driver, and forcing him to stop the vehicle. The driver said that one of the men ran to the truck and shouted that they attacked the truck because the owner of the company employed foreign drivers. The driver sustained serious facial injuries, including a broken jaw, split lips, and a broken nose. His company dismissed him after the incident, saying he had been negligent.

records.name: Another Victim told Human Rights Watch that while standing outside his shop in Johannesburg in June 2019, several ...
records.description: Another Victim told Human Rights Watch that while standing outside his shop in Johannesburg in June 2019, several men who he believed were South African approached him with guns. He ran and they followed for some distance, firing six bullets at him but thankfully missing him.

records.name: In the early hours of June 1, men in a white sedan shot at a Zimbabwean driver en route to Durban from Johannesburg. ...
records.description: In the early hours of June 1, men in a white sedan shot at a Zimbabwean driver en route to Durban from Johannesburg. One of the men in the car was holding a gasoline container while three others had handguns. Human Rights Watch saw six bullet holes in his truck during an interview on June 30. One of the bullets hit the radiator, causing the driver to stop the truck and flee. Although he was not injured, when he reported the incident to his company, they did nothing but give him another cargo load to transport that day using a different truck. The driver believed he was targeted because his company employs foreign drivers, and his company’s logo is clearly displayed on the driver’s side of the truck. The driver said he was afraid to keep driving but had to because he must pay his daughter’s school fees and look after his family.

records.name: Lack of documentation leads to the death of a two-year-old Zimbabwean boy.
records.description:
A boy aged 2, passed away from poisoning in December 2019 after being denied medical attention at Charlotte Maxeke Academic Hospital because his Zimbabwean mother was unable to provide his birth certificate right away or pay R5,000.

Source: https://www.groundup.org.za/article/court-application-aims-to-stop-refugees-from-dying-because-they-are-refused-free-health-care/
records.response: Local public interest  NGO.

records.name: On June 16, three ATDF men stopped a Malawian truck driver as he drove on the N3 highway, about 150 kilometers from ...
records.description: On June 16, three ATDF men stopped a Malawian truck driver as he drove on the N3 highway, about 150 kilometers from Durban on the road to Johannesburg. The driver said the men ordered him to call his employer to say he was resigning and that the company shouldn’t employ any foreign nationals. He complied. One of the three men then spoke on the phone with the employer, telling him to stop employing foreign nationals regardless of whether they had a work permit. After that, the driver said, he was told to leave the truck on the road and go back to his country. The driver abandoned the truck but was able to keep his job in South Africa with the same company.

records.name: On June 16 and 17, assailants carried out several coordinated attacks at truck rest stops on the road between Durban ...
records.description: On June 16 and 17, assailants carried out several coordinated attacks at truck rest stops on the road between Durban and Johannesburg. At least 10 trucks were attacked and vandalized at the Estcourt Truck Inn, Tugela Plaza Truck Stop on the N3 Highway, and at Mooi River near Durban.

records.name: Six truck drivers interviewed said that on June 22 in Witbank town, a group of approximately 60 people claiming ...
records.description:
Six truck drivers interviewed said that on June 22 in Witbank town, a group of approximately 60 people claiming to be ATDF members blocked the R544 road near the Legend Trucks company and stopped all trucks passing through Witbank, ordering the drivers to show their drivers’ licenses, but did not ask for work permits. They ordered those with foreign licenses to abandon their trucks or to empty the contents of their trucks onto the road and then leave the trucks on the road. The truck drivers were not asked for work permits.
A Zimbabwean truck driver said: A group of men, about 20, stood in the middle of the road in Witbank and forced [me to stop my truck]. They demanded to see my license, shouting that all foreign drivers must fall. When I showed them my Zimbabwean driver’s license, they accused me of being an illegal truck driver although I have a valid work permit. One of them, who had a pistol in his hand, ordered me to tip all the coal in my truck onto the road and to leave the truck and go back to Zimbabwe. I tipped over the coal and ran away, leaving the group with the truck. I later phoned my company, who sent a manager to get the truck the following day, but without the coal, which had been looted.
A  Zambian truck driver said: When I got to Witbank, the road was blocked. Three trucks were parked on the road. Three men approached my truck and ordered me out of the truck. I didn’t know who they were. But I was too afraid, so I got out of the truck, and left the truck. I called my company after 20 minutes to tell them what happened. When the men stopped me, there were police trucks parked nearby, and the police officers watched, but they did not come to my assistance.
Source: Human Rights Watch

records.name: On the night of June 23, a group of 8 men claiming to be ATDF members, 3 of them armed with pistols, targeted truck ...
records.description: On the night of June 23, a group of 8 men claiming to be ATDF members, 3 of them armed with pistols, targeted truck drivers in the town of Ermelo in Mpumalanga, about 125 kilometers southeast of Witbank, threatening to kill 5 drivers and forcing them to flee and abandon their trucks. Human Rights Watch interviewed four of the drivers. One of them, a Malawi national, said that the men stopped him and demanded that he hand over the truck keys or die on the spot, telling him: “No foreigners on our trucks. All foreign truck drivers must fall!” The driver called the truck owner to make him aware that he was in danger and hid, watching the truck from a distance. He said the owner sent a local driver to retrieve the truck after about two hours but did not offer him any assistance.

records.name: On the 10th of July around 3pm, a group of Sebokeng locals who seemed to be part of a group of protestors  for shortage ...
records.description: On the 10th of July around 3pm, a group of Sebokeng locals who seemed to be part of a group of protestors  for shortage of electricity in Sebokeng, threatened Congolese shop owners with sticks and bottles and told them to leave the country and go back where they belong. Due to the fear of being attacked the victim says they closed their saloons and went back home only to be told later in the evening that the the protesters were pouring petrol on and around  Congolese owed shops and setting them alight. The victim says because they feared for their lives they were scared to go there immediately and only went back the following morning to find their saloons on fire. The police were present after having being called in by fellow shop owners. The victim stated that the police were called in by fellow shop owners and there were also fire man attending to the fire . No arrests were made..

records.name: Looting of shops in Ivory Park resulted in looting of foreign national shops. Residents were protesting against ...
records.description: Looting of shops in Ivory Park resulted in looting of foreign national shops. Residents were protesting against lack of electricity for almost a month. The protests started at night around 10.30pm and they started looting foreign shops including the victim who reported the incident. The victim stated that he was also beat up and choked. Goods worth R60 0000 were destroyed and looted. The victim stated that he was still traumatized by the incident.

records.name: On the 24th of July 2019 foreign nationals were attacked in Richards's bay  after a man identified as a taxi driver ...
records.description: On the 24th of July 2019 foreign nationals were attacked in Richards's bay  after a man identified as a taxi driver was found dead behind the taxi rank around 6.30am. The taxi rank was tense that day with people accusing Paras for killing the man. Taxi drivers then went to the scene and started beating up all Paras or anyone they thought looked like one. Later on they were rumors that foreign nationals were also responsible for selling drugs. The foreigners at the rank denied this. The mob then started beating more people including foreign nationals at a Richard's Bay taxi rank. According to a partner organization, the number of deaths is 3 and the victims were Tanzanian nationals. It is claimed that a building was burnt. Containers belonging to Burundians and Congolese were destroyed and shops belonging to migrants were affected. Charges of murder and attempted murder were laid. A spokesman for the foreigners, said the biggest danger was for foreigners living in the Richards Bay CBD and also said 12 containers used to run their businesses were set alight and two restaurants were looted last week. It was also mentioned that some people had their asylum papers stolen by attackers who accused them of drug dealing. Many stayed in their homes over the weekend out of fear. One witness states that, the following day after the incident, they tried to open a case at the police station but the police refused and told them that they had already opened a case of public violence against the people responsible for the violence. Approximately 113 people were displaced, including 50 children, with little access to shelter and food, having lost their livelihoods.

records.name: Xenowatch received a call from a victim who stated that he had received our number from a partner organisation. ...
records.description: Xenowatch received a call from a victim who stated that he had received our number from a partner organisation. The victim stated that he is Ethiopian and has been living in South Africa for a while now. He stated that on the 26th of July this year,  he was in his shop when a customer came and told him to leave because people where heading his direction and were looting foreign shops. He ran to the nearest police station which was 3km away. He found other foreign nationals there as well and they slept at the police station. The following day he found that they had looted his whole shop and lost goods that cost him a lot of money. He states that this is not the first his shop has been looted resulting in him startting afresh.

records.name: A Zambian artist, told Human Rights Watch that in August 2019, South Africans looted his metal workshop in Alberton, ...
records.description: A Zambian artist, told Human Rights Watch that in August 2019, South Africans looted his metal workshop in Alberton, Ekurhuleni. Among those involved were his South African employees. He said: “...I thought they were loyal to me. I thought they were more than employees, that they were my friends, so this was very sad for me.” The victim has been in South Africa since 2008 as an artist on a valid visa and was attacked in 2008 when there was xenophobic violence. He said, “Attacks after attacks...I asked, ‘how can I take your job if I employ your guys?’”

records.name: After receiving WhatsApp warnings in September 2019 that an armed mob was heading towards the school, a foreign ...
records.description: After receiving WhatsApp warnings in September 2019 that an armed mob was heading towards the school, a foreign school teacher and the three other foreign teachers at his public school requested permission to leave the school grounds, but the director, a South African, did not believe the threats and refused. The teacher showed Human Rights Watch a window at the back side on the second floor of the building through which he escaped as the mob entered through the front of the building. He said that two of the other teachers safely shut themselves in a room, but the other foreign teacher was caught and beaten by the mob. According to Teacher, the police came to stop the attack, but no arrests were made.

records.name: A group of men armed with crude weapons made their way through the inner city, breaking and looting, in the wake ...
records.description: A group of men armed with crude weapons made their way through the inner city, breaking and looting, in the wake of police raids in which refugees and other migrants were rounded up and their goods confiscated at gun point. “Sizobabamba ngezandla uhulumeni usiphoxelani (We’ll get our hands on them. Why has the government failed/disappointed us),” sang a group of men in isiZulu as they marched down Margaret Mcingana Street in Jeppestown, Johannesburg, on the afternoon of Wednesday 7 August. Armed with knives, hammers, scissors, knobkerries and pieces of wood picked up along the way, the mob had gone to the Wolhuter Men’s Hostel to mobilise more support. Their message was clear. “We are going to go deal with these foreigners.” One of the men in the group, carrying a stick, said: “The foreigners, they kill our police. They must go.” Another man, encouraged by his comments, added: “We are going to go remove the Nigerians and take their stuff.” The mob had formed earlier near the Noord Taxi Rank and Fashion District in the central business district of Joburg and made its way towards Jeppestown. Along the way, they smashed the windows of shops and cars believed to belong to migrants and robbed street traders of their goods and food. As the procession gathered momentum, individuals became more brazen. Some started chasing after anyone they perceived to be a migrant. The rest of the group stood and watched, jeering and banging their crude weapons against shut roller security doors and cars parked on the side of the road. Marching towards the hostel in Jeppestown, the group of men stormed a supermarket and a small liquor store on Commissioner Street, smashing windows and stealing food, meat and alcohol.  The police were aware of the group, but provincial police spokesperson Brigadier Mathapelo Peters said she was hesitant to link the mob attack and looting to the police operations taking place in the Fashion District. The looters had formed near the cordoned-off area of the police operation. Incident derived from New Frame

records.name: On the 8th of August an Ethiopian victim from the Soweto looting also reported that he was arrested during the Johannesburg ...
records.description: On the 8th of August an Ethiopian victim from the Soweto looting also reported that he was arrested during the Johannesburg raid. He heard from someone that police were conducting raids in Johannesburg. He then closed his tuckshop and rushed to Johannesburg town where his wife and kids live to make sure they were okay. He was with his family when the police came knocking on his door. He states that the police pointed at him with a gun and  told him to seat down and started beating him. They asked his wife if she earns a government grant, when she confirmed it they started accusing them of benefiting from state resources and should go back to their country.Despite informing the police that he had legal papers to stay in the country they arrested him took him to Johannesburg central police station. He states that he was in cell with other foreign nationals. According to his estimation there were around 40 people in his cell from Malawi and Bangladesh. The conditions in the cell were horrible. They slept on the floor. He said he was lucky because a police officer from Orlando in Soweto identified him and knew that he was legal. The following day the police officer he knew released him.

records.name: Some foreign nationals in Orange Grove in Johannesburg have told Eyewitness News they've been forced to leave the ...
records.description: Some foreign nationals in Orange Grove in Johannesburg have told Eyewitness News they've been forced to leave the area after locals illegally invaded their homes and vandalised their belongings. A group of residents went on the rampage on Sunday, evicting foreign nationals and accusing them of illegally occupying the houses and of dealing in drugs. At least 20 coffins were discovered at one of the properties and were dragged to the streets along with the furniture. About 12 people were arrested last week in the same area for public violence. A community gripped by fear after a group of locals targeted homes occupied by foreign nationals. One man said: “I am scared to even stay in this place, I don’t know what I am going to do. I am scared, I am afraid of those guys.” One man said he's been forced to move his family to Pretoria to seek refuge. “I am scared, I have to send my family to Pretoria to my big brother," he said. A caretaker at a property where at least 20 coffins were found and thrown out on the streets by locals claims the owner is a businessman who re-sells new coffins to funeral parlours. Police have confiscated the coffins while investigations continue, and they're searching for those behind the illegal evictions.

records.name: A KwaZulu-Natal truck driver was killed in yet another brutal attack in the province on Monday. The driver, identified ...
records.description: A KwaZulu-Natal truck driver was killed in yet another brutal attack in the province on Monday. The driver, identified victim, who is believed to be a foreign national, was found dead next to his burning truck on the N2 Main Harding road in Paddock, in southern KZN. Provincial police spokesperson Col Thembeka Mbele confirmed the incident and said a provincial task team would be investigating. "On August 19 2019 at 12:10, police received a call regarding a truck which was on fire on the N2 Main Harding road in Paddock. Upon arrival at the scene, police found the driver lying on the road near the driver’s door. He had bullet wounds in the left arm and chest and had burn injuries to his body. The 37-year-old driver was declared dead on the scene." Mbele said the motive was unknown and the task team would investigate further. Meanwhile, South African Long-distance Truckers (SALT) posted a tribute for Ntini on Facebook which has been shared close to 2,000 times. SNB Freight were approach for comment but declined, saying the matter was sensitive. In June the Sunday Times reported on the onslaught against companies employing foreign truck drivers which had left dozens dead or injured and caused R1.2bn in damage to trucks and cargo, according to the Road Freight Association (RFA). The RFA said 213 truck drivers were killed in the past year. However, it is still unclear how many of these deaths were linked to the protests. However, it confirmed that 12 foreigners had been killed in the violence as well as at least three South Africans.

records.name: Chaos descended on parts of the Pretoria CBD on Wednesday as foreign-owned shops were looted and burned by a mob ...
records.description:
Chaos descended on parts of the Pretoria CBD on Wednesday as foreign-owned shops were looted and burned by a mob that was on a mission to rid the city of drug dealers. The morning started with taxi drivers blocking several roads in the CBD, protesting against the shooting of one of their own on Tuesday. After the shops were looted, they were set alight. At one point, police officers from the flying squad, wielding R5 rifles, attempted to gain access to Lilian Ngoyi Street to allow the fire department through to attend to the burning buildings. Police officers and firefighters were eventually forced to retreat as the looting continued. A large police contingent finally moved into the area firing rubber bullets, tear gas and stun grenades in an attempt to disperse the crowd. As the police started firing, looters ran away, some with large flat screen TVs that were stolen from an electronics store on the same street. The police kept clearing streets as the looting continued. News24 also observed that while the police formed a line on Lilian Ngoyi Street, a group of people moved around the corner and looted shops on Bloed Street, including a tavern. By this time, firefighters were able to enter the area and attended to the fires that had already spread to previously unaffected buildings. Dozens of looters ran away clutching Castle Lite six-packs as the police eventually caught wind of the looting on Bloed Street. No arrests Despite several people being caught inside looted shops by the police, they were later released. Gauteng police commissioner Lieutenant General Elias Mawela confirmed no arrests had been made during the mayhem that unfolded on Wednesday. "For now, we are concentrating on putting the fires out, and then once that is stabilised, it will allow forensic investigators to come in and do their work," Mawela said.He added once all the evidence was collected, the case would then be taken forward, saying the police were also going to sit down with the taxi industry to listen to their grievances. In the meantime, additional police officers have been deployed in the CBD, Marabastad and Sunnyside. "We have also observed that there are some criminal elements who are exploiting the situation; the ones who are looting, once they get an opportunity to break into a shop and loot.
"The instruction is clear to our police officers, to say that they must deal with those criminal elements and treat them like criminals. But those who are having a serious and genuine concern like the taxi industry, we are going to sit down with them and discuss the way forward," Mawela added.
Taxi drivers. Taxi drivers said they had taken to the streets on Wednesday to rid the CBD of drug dealers - targeting mostly foreign nationals. This came after a taxi driver was shot and killed on Tuesday after taxi operators allegedly found the police were involved in drug dealing, News24 previously reported. News24 spoke to several taxi drivers on condition of anonymity. They said they were forced to do the work of the police, accusing law enforcement of being corrupt and complacent when arresting alleged dealers in Pretoria. "The reason why we are doing this is because the law enforcement agencies are failing us, due to the guys who are selling drugs," one taxi driver said. "One of our brothers was killed yesterday, that is why we are so angry," another added. The regional chairperson of the SA National Taxi Council in Tshwane, Xolly Tshabalala, said the taxi driver who was killed had a family and was fighting for residents in Pretoria. "We are fighting for our youth. They are using drugs and no one cares. Where is [Police Minister] Bheki Cele? He has to come and tell us what will become of this case." Tshabalala said they do not have a problem with foreigners, but rather with criminal activities. By Wednesday afternoon, the police managed to take control of the situation in the Pretoria CBD and crowds dispersed. However, taxi drivers promised this would not be the end of it. Mayor calls for calm. Tshwane Mayor Stevens Mokgalapa condemned the outbreak of violence and called for calm."There is no grievance that should result in death, irrespective of the circumstances between the individuals involved," Mokgalapa said in a statement."This confrontation has led to the looting of shops as well as the destruction of city and business infrastructure. Commuters have also been left stranded as the riots led to the suspension of the Tshwane bus services including the Gautrain.
"I appeal for calm and urge Tshwane residents, the taxi industry, informal traders and all other stakeholders to exercise restraint."The mayor added that retaliatory crimes were intolerable.

records.name: A week prior to the violence, a letter inviting South African Citizens to join Sisonke People's forum to come together ...
records.description: A week prior to the violence, a letter inviting South African Citizens to join Sisonke People's forum to come together and get rid of foreigners. Xenowatch conducted verifications and the threats were confirmed. The person we spoke to confirmed that they are planning  a shutdown on the 2nd of September. They plan to protest in Tembisa and other areas. They will be protesting against Nigerians selling drugs to youth and for taking jobs away from them. He stated that as representatives of South Africans, they want the government to be pro-active in helping them get work instead of constantly prioritizing foreigners. They plan to meet in the morning of the 2nd and march to different areas. Meetings were conducted and on the 1st of September 2019, violence began. Shops were looted and a local panel beater workshop was damaged in Jeppestown following the death of three people in a fire in the area, police have said. Police spokesperson Captain Mavela Masondo on Sunday said police responded to a call of a building that was gutted in Jeppestown at around 05:00, where two men and a woman died. The three deceased people... were burnt to death. While at the scene, a group of criminals then took advantage of the situation and started attacking nearby shops," he said. Nearby shops were broken into and then looted, Masondo said. "They then moved into a nearby panel beater workshop where they damaged two cars and set alight one vehicle. At the moment, we don't know who owns those shops and are calling for owners to come and open cases," he said. Police have arrested four suspects and have deployed additional personnel into the area. Masondo said they have opened an inquest docket regarding the death of three people and are investigating cases of public violence. The following day violence the violence erupted to other areas over a number of days as coded in cells in the subsequent It is reported that the violence resulted in 12 deaths. 10 of which were South African citizens and the other 2 Zimbabwean nationals. 865 people were displaced due to the violence. However, a recent report from Human Rights Watch placed the number of deaths to 18 in KZN, JHB & CPT between the 2nd  - 9th Septermber 2019. https://www.hrw.org/sites/default/files/media_2020/09/southafrica0920_web_4.pdf

records.name: Several foreign owned shops have been looted in Tembisa over night. Residents of the township on the East Rand said ...
records.description: Several foreign owned shops have been looted in Tembisa over night. Residents of the township on the East Rand said they were avenging the killing of a Pretoria taxi driver allegedly by a foreign national. The looting spree started before midnight on Sunday. Residents  also said they wanted to rid townships of foreigners. One of the residents Nhlanhla Nkambule told SowetanLIVE that they were fed up with foreign nationals in their community. “They come here and sell drugs to our children. They also killed a taxi driver in Pretoria because they want to sell drugs,” Nkambule said.  But other residents said they did not know what had triggered the looting of shops. Ekurhuleni MMC for Community Safety Frans Mmoko said  the situation was contained before it spread to other parts of the township. “We have managed to keep the situation localised in one area. We don’t want it to spill over to other parts (of Tembisa) and we will be camping here to make sure of that,” he said. Mmoko said he suspected that the lootings are a result of messages that were circulated on social media about a possible shutdown in the township. “We have unconfirmed information that people wanted to hijack trucks and block the highways and freeways with them. We didn’t take chances so we placed members at spots we thought would be targeted,” he said. Meanwhile 41 people have been arrested following incidents of looting and torching of buildings and vehicles in Jeppestown and surrounding areas. Police spokeswoman Brig Mathapelo Peters said includes the initial four who were arrested on Sunday for public violence, whilst the rest were arrested after they were found in some of the shops busy looting and being in possession of stolen items, 22 in Malvern. Eight suspects were arrested inside one shop in Vusimuzi informal settlement in Tembisa.

records.description: The pillaging started in Jeppestown on Sunday 1 September and by Monday morning had spread to other areas of Johannesburg, including Germiston and Malvern, where dozens of businesses and cars were set alight. A number of incidents of public violence and criminal activity have been reported in the Germiston area today (September 2). In the first incident the Primrose police responded to a report of public unrest at 1.30am at Rainbow Restaurant on Rietfontein Road, Primrose where people had gathered and were burning tyres in the road. “They forcefully broke into the restaurant and looted liquor and a TV set. “No arrests were made and a public violence docket has been opened at the Primrose Police Station,” said Capt André de Jager, the spokesperson for Ekurhuleni District Zone Four. In another incident later in the morning, the Public Order Police and Primrose SAPS were called to a protected wage strike at Waltons at Pencil Park. “Police officers negotiated with the protest leaders as they had stopped traffic by burning tyres. “They were told not to do this and reminded that they were only allowed to be at the entrance to the office park,” said de Jager.“The protestors then walked to the gate and closed it stopping personnel from other companies entering the premises. A Somali national called Xenowatch to report that he was attacked. His shop was looted and set on fire. He has lost everything and ran to Mayfair to live with friends.

records.name: “I don’t think I can stay here anymore. It is not safe and this happens every year” says Bangladeshi shop owner ...
records.description: “I don’t think I can stay here anymore. It is not safe and this happens every year” says Bangladeshi shop owner On Tuesday morning, immigrant shop owners in Alexandra were salvaging what was left of their stock after a group of unidentified people looted and burnt their shops overnight. The streets were covered in rubbish and rubble when GroundUp visited the area. 2nd Street and West Street were cordoned off by police who were letting only shop owners through to assess the damage and collect leftover stock. Emergency water services were dispatched to the area to put out the fires that were still burning. The xenophobic violence in Alexandra followed similar attacks on mostly immigrant-owned shops across Johannesburg. The attacks started in Jeppestown on Sunday and had spread to Alexandra, Tembisa, Germiston, Kempton Park, Coronation Park, Turffontein and Malvern by Tuesday. The wave of xenophobic violence that spread across South Africa in May 2008 started in Alexandra. On Tuesday, one of the Bangladeshi shop owners in Alexandra, was carrying salvageable stock like speakers, radios, sweets and other goods out of his uncle’s shop and loading it into a van. The pavement outside the shop was strewn with burnt fruit, vegetables, tables, trolleys and chairs which belonged to street vendors who usually leave their stock there overnight. The victim told GroundUp that the attacks on the shops along West Street and 2nd Street started at about 8pm on Monday evening. His shop, which is on the street adjacent to his uncle’s, was also looted and set alight. Liquor City, which is on the corner of the same street as the immigrant shops, was also looted. The victim moved to South Africa three years ago because his uncle and other family members owned shops and said he could make a living in the country. He first lived in Marlboro, next to Alexandra, but he said he did not enjoy travelling to and from Alexandra every day so he made himself a bedroom in his shop. He has been living in his shop for the past six months. The vicrim said he was in his bedroom when the group tried to break the doors and set it alight. He said they did not know he was in the building at the time. He managed to escape through a window and jumped onto another building next door which was also set alight by the group. “Those things that were burnt are just material things. At least I am alive and safe,” said the victim “But I don’t think I can stay here anymore. It is not safe and this happens every year. What’s the point if it gets burnt to the ground every year and we have to start again? I think I will go back to Bangladesh and work in a clothing factory or something. At least there I can make some money and be safe. But here, my life is in danger.”

Construction materials have been provided to residents, who are rebuilding their homes. records.name: A man lay dead, covered by a silver wrapper, while his relatives wept in the White City section of Kwathema township ...
records.description:
A man lay dead, covered by a silver wrapper, while his relatives wept in the White City section of Kwathema township in Springs on Wednesday. Police and residents gathered around the marked area. Witnesses say the shooting happened at about 3pm when a landlord tried to protect his tenant, a foreign shop owner. The victim lived about 3km away and was apparently coming from a shop when he was shot. Kwathema police later said that he was 24 years old. A 45-year-old woman was shot during the same incident and taken to hospital, according to police.  “It is alleged that a group of people wanted to attack a shop owned by a foreign national. The landlord came out to rescue the shop owner. He warned and threatened the group of people that were outside his yard. A fight ensued. When he saw that he was overpowered he took out his licensed firearm and started shooting randomly,” said a police statement. The suspect has been arrested, the police said. A relative of the arrested man, said: “This violence against foreigners is getting out of hand. Innocent people are being shot. Our brother fired the gun in self defence. He was trying to defend our home.” She further said that after the shooting they received warnings that their house would be burnt down. Vans were witnessed dropping groups of men who had come to loot shops in the area. Residents say looters were not from their area; they had not seen them before. ‘Welcome to South Africa, a place where foreign nationals are tormented’ In Kwathema’s Deep Level section GroundUp saw looters take the remaining stock out of a foreign national's shop. The non-national was still shaken, he sat on the ground holding his asylum permit. He had not yet called the police. Looters had not only taken his stock, but also his money. “They said I must go back to my country because l am an illegal foreigner. I showed them my asylum permit but they laughed at me,” he said. The victim said he had closed his shop earlier when people told him that looters were coming. However, he said they managed to break the security door of his rented room and forced him at gunpoint to open the shop. “While some looted my shop others turned my sleeping quarters upside down. They took all my money.”
 He had operated his shop for five years. It had never been looted before. “Now reality has been knocked into my senses,” he said. “When I called my friends and told them that my shop had finally been looted, they said: ‘Welcome to South Africa, a place where foreign nationals are tormented’.”

records.name: Violence linked to xenophobic tensions has engulfed parts of Johannesburg for the second weekend in a row, as hundreds ...
records.description: Violence linked to xenophobic tensions has engulfed parts of Johannesburg for the second weekend in a row, as hundreds of protesters ran riot across the city on Sunday. Two stabbings have been reported, and the damage to stores and public institutions has proved to be devastating in the light of day. The troubles began in Jeppestown, during a speech made by outgoing IFP President Mangosuthu Buthelezi. In trying to bring peace to the area, a splinter group rebelled and ran amok in the CBD. Protests eventually spilled over into Malvern, where shops – many owned by foreigners – were burned to the ground. Sadly, the thugs orchestrating this wave of violence didn’t spare religious venues, either. The Masjid Himayatul Islam Mosque on Nugget Street was petrol-bombed late in the evening. Thankfully, law enforcement arrived on the scene rapidly to extinguish the fire. Two suspects were arrested during this incident: This fresh round of xenophobic protesting has apparently been a deadly one: EWN are reporting that two people died on Sunday, with the second victim succumbing to gunshot wounds sustained during the nighttime violence. David Tembe, the chief of police in Johannesburg, has been monitoring the situation. Further reports for a Human Rights Watch Report state that: A Bangladeshi shop owner, showed Human Rights Watch a row of shops in Johannesburg Central Business District that were looted during the September 2019 riots, pointing to mangled metal that was cut and bent to force entry. He said that within the Bangladeshi business community, 1,000 shops were looted and a mob of 300-500 people tried to break into his family’s shops. The row of shop owners, including the victim's, called the police. However, the police did not come for three days, so he and other shop owners did not sleep for three nights, as they guarded their shops as rioters threw stones at them for three days.

records.name: The victim lost merchandise worth over R150,000 from vandalism and looting during xenophobic attacks in Johannesburg. ...
records.description: The victim lost merchandise worth over R150,000 from vandalism and looting during xenophobic attacks in Johannesburg. Her clothing store, located in the Maboneng Precinct, was one of the many outlets in the region that were broken into and looted on Sunday. The victim''s high-profile clientele includes her mother-in-law. Protesters smashed the window, trashed the store, broke equipment and stole clothing. "They managed to break a lot of stores there, but others had strong windows so they couldn't go through. With my store, they managed to go through and they took everything - the whole stock," the victim said. "Within five minutes they were done. When I got there a few guys were still around, walking up and down and doing as they please. "We tried to reason with them that we are the owners and we are your fellow South Africans. They said 'we don't care, we want to show you what vandalism is'. These are angry people," the victim said. She has been forced to temporarily close her other store located in the Fashion District in the CBD out of fear that she will lose more stock.

records.name: Unrest in Johannesburg which has already resulted in one fatality on Sunday has spread to Malvern where a building ...
records.description: Unrest in Johannesburg which has already resulted in one fatality on Sunday has spread to Malvern where a building was on fire, Gauteng police confirmed on Sunday night. “There is a group that is looting and attacking people,” spokesperson Captain Kay Makhubele said. Police were on scene. Earlier on Sunday, one person was killed in violence in the Johannesburg city centre, with  Makhubele confirming that the victim had been stabbed with a sharp object at the corner of Bree and Plein Streets. He was unable to confirm the identity or nationality of the deceased. Five others had been injured. A group of men, some of them wielding sticks, pangas and tree branches, marched through the city centre after disrupting a meeting in which IFP President Emeritus Mangosuthu Buthelezi spoke to hostel residents following a week of deadly xenophobic violence. Makhubele said 16 people were arrested for public violence and possession of stolen property before the situation in the CBD, Jeppestown and Hillbrow was reportedly “under control”.

records.name: Police are investigating the deaths of a 32-year-old woman and an unidentified man after chaos broke out in the ...
records.description: Police are investigating the deaths of a 32-year-old woman and an unidentified man after chaos broke out in the Samora Machel informal settlement in Cape Town at the weekend. The bodies were discovered in the remains of a looted foreign-owned shop. Shop owners packed up their wares and and left as the looting of stores started. Police joined in the task of stabilising the area by the military and arrested 30 people in connection with the crimes, but have not yet identified suspects in the killings of the two people. "During the protest action, two fatalities were reported," said SAPS spokesperson Lt-Col Andre Traut. "The bodies of a 32-year-old female and an unknown male were recovered on the premises of the looted store. The circumstances surrounding their deaths are under investigation," he said. "Operation Lockdown and additional police deployments will remain on high alert in the area to prevent any further incidents of violence." He said a sweep of the settlement garnered a further five arrests. "An additional five people were arrested for being in possession of groceries and a deep freezer when houses were searched in the area," he said.

records.name: Joburg Metro Police Department chief David Tembe has confirmed to Eyewitness News that a second person has been ...
records.description: Joburg Metro Police Department chief David Tembe has confirmed to Eyewitness News that a second person has been killed during clashes in the city and that four people had been arrested. Tembe said the latest victim was shot in Malvern on Sunday night the other person was stabbed earlier in Hillbrow. The trouble started early Sunday when a group of men, apparently from nearby hostels, made their way into the CBD demanding that foreign nationals leave the area. Areas including Malvern, Jeppe and Hillbow were under lockdown for hours. Tembe said that several cars and buildings had been set alight overnight while businesses had been looted.  "I think this is pure criminality because some of the shops that were burned did not belong to the foreigners, it belonged to South Africans." At least 20 people have been arrested after another night of violence in the Joburg CBD. A person who identified himself as a shop owner said he and other foreign shop owners were warned to evacuate their premises. The arrested suspects are due to appear in the Athlone magistrate's court soon.

records.name: The Elsburg SAPS were out in Buhle Park last Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, between 11pm and 2am, combating ...
records.description:
The Elsburg SAPS were out in Buhle Park last Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, between 11pm and 2am, combating crime in their area after residents started to loot stores owned by foreign nationals.
The shops looted were:
• Buhle Park Discount Supermarket in Nitrogen Street was looted and the door was burnt.
• Yellow Spaza Shop in Nitrogen Street.
• White container in Obita Street.
• New tuck shop on the corner of Mutandi and Lex streets.
• Blessing tuck shop in Prima Fasie Street.
• Ashaan Mini-Market in Niemann Street.
• White spaza shop in Dragon Street was vandalised. “Fifteen suspects were arrested during the violence and were due to appear in the Germiston Magistrate’s Court on a charge of public violence,” said Const Daphney Phooko, communications officer for the Elsburg SAPS.

records.name: Several shops were plundered and destroyed when violence broke out in Witbank, Mpumalanga, but some “looters” were ...
records.description: Several shops were plundered and destroyed when violence broke out in Witbank, Mpumalanga, but some “looters” were caught and allegedly beaten by store owners. Looters were captured in video footage making off with various items, including audio speakers, suitcases and bicycles on Wednesday. In the footage, a shop owner can be seen allegedly grabbing a man, who slipped and fell, then delivering a sharp blow to his head with a flat hand. Two other shop owners allegedly join in and beat up a second man. A police officer had to intervene and break up the scuffle. Police spokesperson Brig Leonard Hlathi said three people were arrested for looting. Hlathi said police also recovered some of the stolen items.“We also had a meeting with the shop owners and business people to try to put a plan in place. We are also going to do patrols.” He said calm had been restored on Thursday.

records.name: An Alexandra couple, have for months been victims of attacks by a group of armed men who have threatened to occupy ...
records.description: An Alexandra couple, have for months been victims of attacks by a group of armed men who have threatened to occupy their home, culminating in the husband suffering a serious head injury over the weekend after being beaten with a sharp object. Despite the SA Police Service (SAPS) being aware of the incidents and knowledge of those behind the attacks, those implicated get released at the Alexandra Police Station, according to Joburg Metro Police chief David Tembe. While having gathered their belongings, strewn in the street by the “occupiers” and gone back to their home yesterday, the family told The Citizen that they were “unsafe and scared” that the group could return in the evening. The victim is a Zimbabwean-born naturalised South African, with a barcoded identity document and his wife is in possession of a work permit. This has not spared them from regular attacks by the gang, masquerading as “fighting illegal immigrants” and believed to be part of a rampant scam in Alexandra to take over and sell houses to unsuspecting residents. According to the victim, the men would swoop on their home twice in a month, “making our life a living hell”. “This is very scary and traumatic, especially for my two daughters who are in Grade eight and R. They can no longer concentrate at school. “Armed with an assortment of weapons, they came in large numbers yesterday, beat my husband up and stayed in the house until 6.45am – just minutes before the police came. They broke the gate and kitchen windows to gain entry into the house,” said the victim, whose daughters are aged four and 13. The victim has worked for energy expert as a domestic worker for over 10 years. His employer, who has reported the incident to Alexandra Station commander Colonel Johannes Tau, left messages for Tembe and Joburg mayor Herman Mashaba. “My conversation with Tau confirmed my suspicion that the armed group worked with some members of the police in this housing scam.” Calls by The Citizen to Tau went unanswered. Source: https://citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/news-xenophobia/2182569/cops-ignore-xenophobic-attacks-in-alexandra/

records.name: President Cyril Ramaphosa has once more weighed in on the ongoing xenophobic attacks and called on law enforcement ...
records.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa has once more weighed in on the ongoing xenophobic attacks and called on law enforcement agencies to act firmly in dealing with those who take the law into their own hands. The president spoke for the third time on the violence following his recent public statement and a tweet he sent earlier. His latest statement was sparked by another wave of violence that broke out in Johannesburg, leaving at least two people dead. Ramaphosa expressed his condolences to the families of the two who were reportedly stabbed and shot during attacks in Johannesburg on Sunday. Emerging reports were that the violence was being sponsored in order to cause a conflict between South African and fellow African countries so that the international community could impose sanctions against South Africa. The African Transformation Movement (ATM) party said the violence was being engineered so that locals were pitted against African foreign nationals.The party holds a strong view that this manufactured conflict is aimed at driving a wedge between South Africa and her neighbours so that South Africa is isolated by its peers on the continent. “The isolation of South Africa engenders fertile ground for irrational economic sanctions by the west to further distract South Africa from its developmental agenda and programmes of inclusion [transformation],” ATM said in a statement. The president called on law enforcement agencies to maintain vigilance and firmness in dealing with individuals or groups who take the law into their own hands and violate the rights of people. He praised the police for arresting 16 people during Sunday’s violence in Johannesburg. “Government will not allow sporadic lawlessness and violence to disrupt the safety and livelihoods of millions of South Africans and the majority of foreign nationals in our country who are law-abiding and have the right to conduct their lives and businesses in peace,” he said. “Lawlessness, injury and death inflict a great psychological and economic cost that lasts long after victims are buried, arrests are made and streets are cleared. “This cost holds back our country and undermines all the efforts we are making to grow a South Africa that offers opportunity to all who live in it.” The ATM said the party viewed the perpetuation of violence against foreign nationals as “distractions” and as “part of a veiled strategy to formally recolonise South Africa”. “Humanity must prevail and be underpinned by peace and ubuntu. All communities should be engaged with a view to finding lasting solutions,” it said. Source: Times Live: https://citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/news-xenophobia/2177089/ramaphosa-speaks-after-atm-says-violence-engineered/

records.name: Asylum seeker from Burundi attacked by local taxi drivers
records.description: On 20th October 2019, 3 months after the violent xenophobic attacks in Richards Bay on 25th July 2019,  an Asylum seeker from Burundi tried to reopen his gazebo (street barber) to get money for food. That is when he was attacked by 5 taxi drivers together with some taxi rank security guards. Things were still a bit tense and foreigners were still not yet allowed to restart trading. Since the victim was unable to fluently speak English and isiZulu, He was wrongly mistaken for someone coming from little Burundi. He was severely beaten up and left for dead lying in a pool of his own blood. He was later rushed to hospital by a family member and to police station where a case of attempted murder was opened against the perpetrators.
