records.name: A Cameroon national was killed, and his home both vandalised and set alight, in the Western Cape Province
records.description:
As reported by credible sources on the ground in Vrygrond/Capricorn community, around Muizenberg, the City of Cape Town, in the Western Cape Province, the killing of a Cameroon national in question took place sometime towards the end of the year in 2019, and was a result of a series of a number of attempts and stalking. Reportedly, the Cameroon national who was killed and his property (a double story house) was burnt down. The victim had been involved with a drug addicted female partner, a South African citizen, and they had children together.

According to local witnesses, the Social Department or social workers had given custodianship of children and ownership of the plot (RDP House) to the victim, for the sake of the children, as the mother lived on the street, under constant drugs influence. Reportedly, the Cameroonian gentle man had improved the property and developed it into a   double story house. As he was completing the 2nd floor part, he had divided the first floor into four units, and rented them out to different business operators. Allegedly one section was for a take away restaurant; another one for a tyre mending workshop; another one for “Green World Chinese Natural Medicine” products; and the last one for groceries, meat, and fruit & vegetables raw food items.

The fact that all these four businesses as located within the Cameroonian RDP house premises, were owned and operated by foreign nationals, who was doing well could have triggered and increased some envy and anti-foreign sentiments, to the point that both locals and some criminals decided to loot the shops, vandalise the home of the victim, and then burnt the whole house down. The “carbonised” remains have now become a hazardous dumping place, that anyone can come and see in Capricorn.

According to local witnesses, some day in 2019, people armed with guns arrived at the Cameroonian house, and knocked at the gate to see the Cameroonian, who luckily was not present by that specific moment. Reportedly, the assailants found his Rwandan friend on the premises, and they shot him, and he died on the spot. Allegedly, when the Cameroonian came back, he heard about the incident and ran away to hide. However, according to local witnesses, the Cameroonian guy used to come from time to time to collect the monthly rent fees, from the four business operators. 

Apparently, some interested criminals had been stalking him, watching and monitoring his whereabouts, as one year later or so, after his Rwandan friend was killed, he was also shot dead in 2019, by unknown people, and his corpse was found dumped far from Capricorn. To date, no arrest was ever made in relation the killing of this Cameroon national.

Surprisingly, after his copse was found, some locals, common South African citizens, mixed with local gangsters and criminals attacked the four shops, looted them, taking away everything in those shops, including vandalising the house, as they took doors, windows,  and zincs, then finally, they set the empty building on fire, before they left the demolished premises.
.
As commonly shared among locals, not only this looting directly affected the four business owners, but also six families comprising of thirty shop workers were also directly affected, including local suppliers in the value chains. Different foreign nationalities of which Angolans; Cameroonians; Congolese (DRC); Malawians; Rwandans; and Zimbabweans were affected. The four business owners were particularly affected, as they lost all they assets (business items), and had to start from square one, searching for new business venues and setting up their business activities again.

As stated by local witnesses, there were no intervention whatsoever, besides the SAPS along their routine patrols, just collecting information around deaths statistics. Apparently, the violence stopped itself as soon as the looting and vandalising activities were over, and then the whole building was set alight.

records.name: A Somali national shop owner was petrol bombed in Katlehong (Tsolo Section) near the Caltex garage on the 5th of ...
records.description: A Somali national shop owner was petrol bombed in Katlehong (Tsolo Section) near the Caltex garage on the 5th of January 2020. Community members in Tsolo section had called a meeting concerning foreign nationals in December 2019. Some wanted all foreign nationals owning shops to leave the area because they did not want them to sell anymore, while others wanted them to stay. Following the meeting, in December 2019, most foreign shop owners left the area but came back in January 2020. The Somali victim is one of the shop owners that returned. On the day of the incident, about 5-10 people noticed that his shop was open and tried to get in the yard but it was impossible because of the wall. They tried to destroy the wall but did not succeed. They then threw a petrol bomb at him which burnt him and destroyed his shop. The owner of the property, a South African national was beaten by the group for allowing the Somali victim to open a shop in his property. The perpetrators did not allow by passers/witnesses to take pictures. The police and the ambulance were called. Both the victim and the owner of the property were rushed to the hospital by witnesses. The property owner sustained injuries while the Somali victim died in hospital. No arrests were made. After the incident most Somali and Ethiopian shop owners packed their belongings and left the area out of fear of being attacked.

records.name: Residents of Rosedale, a community in Upington in the Northern Cape, have taken matters into their own hands and ...
records.description: Residents of Rosedale, a community in Upington in the Northern Cape, have taken matters into their own hands and declared war against foreign nationals in reaction to the murder of a police officer. SABC News reporter Ulrich Hendricks has been following the riots that have gripped the Upington community. Disgruntled residents have accused a foreign national of the murder of a local police officer whose identity has not been revealed. This, the community cried, was the last straw in tolerating the alleged criminal activities and unrest brought by foreign nationals. What started out as an outcry for the murder, has escalated into a full-scale confrontation between residents and foreign nationals. Rosedale police had to intervene when residents ransacked homes and businesses belonging to foreign nationals, threatening them with violence if they refused to leave the community. Consequently, 20 rioters were placed under arrest and charged with various crimes. On Thursday, the Rosedale community gathered in numbers outside the Upington Magistrates Court, calling for the immediate release of the rioters. Of course, the prescripts of the law suggest that the arrested rioters will have to go through the judicial process. Their court appearance was still ongoing at the time of publishing this article. Thus, it is not known if they were granted bail or not. Community members who have spoken to the media have remained adamant on the fact that their actions are not xenophobic. They claim that they have put up with enough and the murder of the officer, allegedly by a foreign national, was the last straw. One of the residents charged that the murder of a police officer is the murder of a nation, and as proud South Africans, the community will not accept foreign nationals. No reports have surfaced on the condition of the affected foreign nationals. Coincidentally, the ongoing unrest in Upington erupted at the same time leaders of the African National Congress (ANC) were in the province, drumming up an emotive 108th anniversary campaign.

records.name: A spaza shop owner from Burundi is under police protection after residents of Paballelo in Upington broke into and ...
records.description:
A spaza shop owner from Burundi is under police protection after residents of Paballelo in Upington broke into and looted his shop in the latest round of violence against immigrant shop owners in the area. The victim, who came to South Africa three months ago via Zambia, runs a spaza shop in a shack in Groblershoop, about 110km from Upington. But on Tuesday he was looking after his brother's shop in Paballello while his brother travelled to Musina in Limpopo to renew documents. He says about 200 people came to his shop in the morning, banged on the walls and told him to leave. He locked the front door. But while he was taking a nap in the bedroom behind the shop, at about noon, he says, a smaller group of people forced their way in through the back door and looted the shop. When GroundUp arrived at about 3pm, police were there. Station commander Lieutenant Colonel Elizabeth Bacela said the victim would be taken to a place of safety. The police helped to lock the back door of the shack but could not store his merchandise.
A spokesperson for about 25 Swahili-speaking spaza shop owners from Burundi, Congo, Rwanda and Tanzania spread around the townships of Upington, said a pregnant woman was hurt in Dakotaweg in looting yesterday. A man was also hurt in the looting of another spaza shop in Paballelo, he said. Attempts to loot a shop in Bakhwethaville had not succeeded, The spokesperson said. About the looters, he said: "When they have problems like bad public service why do they hurt other people?"
The convenor of the Paballelo Youth Movement, said the movement targeted drug dealers. He said: "We identify where the drugs are. We don't encourage looting."He denied the movement was xenophobic. About a week ago, immigrant spaza shop owners were chased from Rosedale in Upington after the killing of police constable Steff Visagie. Visagie was stabbed to death while asleep in Keimoes, 30km from Upington. He was a resident of Rosedale. Nigerian immigrant has appeared in court in connection with the murder. His next court appearance will be on 23 March.

records.name: A similar attack happened in apparent retaliation for an incident involving a non-national who allegedly killed ...
records.description: A similar attack happened in apparent retaliation for an incident involving a non-national who allegedly killed a police officer. Oupa Matjie, a police captain in Diepsloot, a township in Johannesburg, was fatally shot on January 17, 2020 while pursuing a Zimbabwean national alleged to be involved in an attempted murder and home robbery. Six days later, on January 23, violence against foreigners erupted when the police refused to hand over the Zimbabwean suspect to an angry mob. A journalist who witnessed the violence told Human Rights Watch that the rioters barricaded roads with burning tires, cow skulls, and furniture. They set bushes on fire and shut down shopping malls and schools while the homes and shops of non-nationals were looted and attacked for several days.

records.name: Locals threatened Nigerian national to leave the area of Keimoes
records.description: Locals threatened Nigerian national to leave the area of Keimoes because they claim that the foreign nationals were dealing with illegal substances and prostituting young women. The locals warned that if  foreign nationals do not leave, they will kill them. On the morning of the 23rd of January 2020, a large group of locals came together and all the Nigerians in the area were forced to leave the area. The Nigerians and had to leave as they feared for their lives.

records.name: A local community member went to buy mealie from a Somali/Ethiopian shop owner (nationality not clear). When he ...
records.description: A local community member went to buy mealie from a Somali/Ethiopian shop owner (nationality not clear). When he got home, he found that the mealie-mealie was expired. He took it back to the shop owner and demanded that he either give him another packet of mealie-mealie or refund his money. The shop owner refused and subsequently an argument ensued. It is alleged that the shop owner then shot the client which resulted in the client’s death. When local community members caught wind of this, they approached the shop owner and were aggressive towards him. Police were called to the scene and tried to calm the situation. During the commotion, a young boy was accidentally hit and died. This further angered local community members who then demanded all Ethiopian and Somali shop owners operating in that area of to leave. Local community members are refusing to let the shop owners return to the community despite their pleas to let them back. Apparently, the shop owners affected are less than 10. The foreign shop owner who shot the client was arrested.

records.name: Thugs have torched a shop belonging to Chinese nationals, who they apparently blamed for bringing the coronavirus ...
records.description:
Thugs have torched a shop belonging to Chinese nationals, who they apparently blamed for bringing the coronavirus to South Africa. The container shop in Leiden was set alight on Monday. Shops on either side of the Chinese winkel were not damaged. When the Daily Voice arrived on the scene yesterday, residents were going through the debris and salvaging items. “It is stupid,” says a resident. “This shop hired people from the community and now these domkoppe burnt it down because of the coronavirus they (the Chinese nationals) know nothing about.” The owner of a shop in the area who didn’t want to give his name says the Chinese owners have fled the area fearing for their lives. “They are in Durbanville and they are not coming back. They were clearly targeted because other shops were not torched,” he says. But another resident believes it is a pure criminal act: “If they were scared of the virus, they would not have looted the food or even come close to the Chinese.” Local councillor, Michelle Adonis, says she is investigating the matter: 
“I still need to find out what really happened (but) it is quite shameful that people would do such a thing.”

records.name: Xenowatch received a report that an Ethiopian man was beaten to death by a group of policemen on (1 April 2020) ...
records.description: Xenowatch received a report that an Ethiopian man was beaten to death by a group of policemen on (1 April 2020) in Isipingo beach. Xenowatch contacted a witness on the ground who informed us that he witnessed the incident from afar. According to the witness, a group of police officials approached a Spaza shop in the area and demanded that the shop keeper open the shop and let them in. The shop keeper refused because the previous day the police had demanded the same and left the shop with some money and food from the shop. The shop keeper informed the police to wait for the shop owner to arrive so that they deal directly with him. According to the witness, the police refused and began cutting the shop gate with a heavy metal cutter to get into the shop.  The shop keeper phoned the shop owner to inform him of the situation. Together with his cousin, the shop owner rushed to the store to find out what was going on. Upon arrival, the shop owner and his cousin found the police outside the store while the shop keeper was hiding inside the shop. According to the witness, around 7-8 police officials started beating up the shop owner and his cousin. The cousin of the shop owner was beaten on the head and fell to the ground. The witness states that two policemen were holding the deceased (cousin of the shop owner) while others were beating him. The shop owner was also thoroughly beaten but was fortunate to survive.  When some community members heard about the incident, they tried to defend the two men and fight off the police. The witness states that more police vans arrived at the scene. One of the vans allegedly at the scene had the following plate number: BVF292B and BVJ977B. The deceased was put into a police van and the shop owner was taken to the police station. The witness states that he followed the police to the police station. The shop owner was arrested and released on a R2000 bail the following morning. Moreover, the witness confirmed that he received news from the hospital that the shop owner’s cousin had died. The witness also noted that the community in Isipingo beach is not happy with the events that took place. The family of the deceased has opened a case against the police officers involved.

records.name: On the eve of the 13th of April, around the Port Elizabeth’s Northern area, residents began looting the supermarkets ...
records.description: On the eve of the 13th of April, around the Port Elizabeth’s Northern area, residents began looting the supermarkets mainly situated in Gelvandale, specifically, the Barcelona supermarket, which was denounced for price hikes, and consequently became the first target of looting. The South African Police Services (SAPS), Community Peace Forum (CPF) and the South African National Defense Force (SANDF) managed to be at the scene on time and obviated the fuming community members, from unlawfully accessing the supermarket. Furthermore, the victim who serves as a shop keeper at the mentioned supermarket, was successfully protected and continued to sell essentials, through the security gate.

records.name: Looting of Spaza shops in Soweto and Veeplaas areas in Northern parts of Port Elizabeth took place at night. The ...
records.description: Looting of Spaza shops in Soweto and Veeplaas areas in Northern parts of Port Elizabeth took place at night. The looting displaced about 140 people, about 40 shops were directly affected, and 100 shop owners have closed their shops as a preventative measure. All the displaced were accommodated by friends and families so none at this point have been reported to be staying in a public facility. The Disaster management in Port Elizabeth provided 100 mattresses and blankets for the displaced persons. The nationalities of those affected include Ethiopians, Somalians and Bangladesh and Malawians and Burundians. Upon follow up on the looting, it was confirmed that our partner, Disaster Management Department, SAHRC, community structures, CPF and SAPS speedily responded to the incident and its aftermath. The community as direct beneficiaries to the services rendered by spaza shops,  directly protected the foreign shops from looting. SAPS managed to make arrests on the matter and the quick response by all relevant parties, avoided further lootings. Criminality and gangsterism are elements that were identified as causes the incidents.

records.name: Received reports that foreign shop owners were threatened by a group of gangsters to pay a protection fee. The gangsters ...
records.description: Received reports that foreign shop owners were threatened by a group of gangsters to pay a protection fee. The gangsters are well known in the area by the police and community for committing crimes. It is alleged that shops owners have been receiving threats via texts from the gangsters. The gangsters have also circulated a letter with their demands. The letter was forwarded to the police and crime intelligence. records.description:
Att: all media houses
We note with concern/s on the Forceful Takeover of Spaza Shops but as Young people who are members of the ANC Youth  League, stand by our call for Foreign Nationals to hand over the keys to Local Youth and Women to participate in the Local Economy.
We are raising an emotive issue which will spark robust engagement which needs to be attended immediately. We strongly believe that the Youth of this Country must share in the wealth of this country and it must start with the local economy.
We also note the concerns raised by members of ANC and the Youth League. Our main aim is to remove all illegal spaza shops and those who do not comply with our health & safety standards including those who are not paying tax and registered with our government. 
Legal foreign shops are welcome in our communities but those who break the law will be forcefully removed. It is our right to be wrong and be corrected as young people.
We still hold the view of the Economic Freedom in Our Lifetime as a resolution of the young people of our movement in 2010 at Gallagher Estates.
The economy should be should be shared amongst the people who live in it including the young generation as per our freedom charter. It is not a criminal offense to want to participate in the economic chain of our land.
South African Youth must stop being a substitute in the economy. 
We call upon our government to regulate this sector, implement rules aimed at curbing illegal, non compliant and unregistered spaza shops. A budget should be allocated and given to a South African bank to make easy access for young people to gain financial services particularly for Funding spaza shops. Because our people come from a background of sleeping without food.
The following demands are a need to be addressed:
1. We demand Local Youth, Women and people with disabilities to be beneficiaries of the spaza shops in our communities.  2. All unregistered and illegal owned spaza shops (white, black, Indian, Chinese) must close down and hand over keys to Local Youth people, Women and persons with disabilities.

3.Government must assist in registering businesses and compliance.

4. All beneficiaries must attend workshop.

5. Funding must be made available for beneficiaries.

6. Youth unemployment should be an agenda of all progressive Youth of the Country. People living with disabilities are no exception in that regard.

7. We call for practical lecture on radical economic transformation for South African Youth.

Forceful does not mean violence but a means to advocate for our demands to be heard and addressed by our government and business society at large!

records.description: A Somali business owner in his early 50s is reported to have died after allegedly being beaten by the police. The business man denied these allegations but the police persisted with their accusations. The police then beat up the businessman including in his abdomen area which resulted in him falling. The African Disapora Forum (ADF) is aware of the situation and plans to engage the family of the deceased to take legal action against the Minister of police. ADF reports that Lawyers for Human Rights and Human Rights Watch are aware of the case and have reached out to also assist.

records.name: According to a press release by the Mayor of Saldanha condemning the violence, details on the incidents were presented ...
records.description:
According to a press release by the Mayor of Saldanha condemning the violence, details on the incidents were presented as follows: on Monday, 6th of July 2020, the Saldanha Bay Municipality's Disaster Management received an early warning indicating that the All Truck Drivers Foundation (ATDF) is allegedly organising a protest action (national shutdown of truck operations). This planning to engage in a protest action is against what they call, “the exploitation of drivers” by the Road Freight Industries in South Africa and the employment of foreign drivers in the industry.
On Tuesday, 07th of July 2020, a group of people started to gather around the area of George Kerridge and the South African Police Service (SAPS) along with the Saldanha Bay Municipality's Law Enforcement were deployed in the area to monitor the gathering. The situation worsened around 21:00 and SAPS requested the support of the Public Order Police Service (POPS).
1 house shop has been burned to the ground.
15 container shops have been looted and vandalised of various foreign nationals.
23 shops have been vandalised and looted.
1 hardware shop has been vandalised and looted.
All foreign-owned businesses within the area of George Kerridge have been completely looted.
Foreign nationals living in informal settlements like George Kerridge, Tsitsiratsitsi, Better Life, Smartie Town and Ongegund have received direct life threats and an instruction to leave Vredenburg within the next 24-hours. Meanwhile in Middelpos, Saldanha vandalism has occured and foreign nationals been made subject to life threats.
We will not tolerate vandalism, violence and any form of hate speech against foreign nationals or even our residents. I know times are tough and that our people are struggling, but turning our emotions into anger against others is not the solution, said Koen.
Although it is difficult to enter these areas due to the volatility of the strike, the SBM's Law Enforcement, SAPS and POPS are monitoring the situation.
The Saldanha Bay Municipality's Disaster Management is currently verifying the status and the actual number of the foreign nationals affected to determine the humanitarian support that we can provide.
Cases have been opened in Vredenburg and Saldanha at the various Police stations.   

Additional information from a partner organisation : We have had an indication from a community representative in Vredenburg that roughly 11 persons are currently displaced, it is unclear if this was precautionary relocation or as a direct result of attacks. Reports on ground confirm that no further attacks were carried out over the weekend. The Saldanha Community Advice Office confirms that community members and SAPS have been going door to door to retrieve some of the stolen items (freezers, doors, structure materials) with the assistance of some local community members that have a vested interest in ending the criminal activity. Finally, there are mixed reports, but it appears South African nationals were also targeted and some generalised crime may have accompanied the targeted attacks on foreign nationals.

records.name: Two people died and several were injured as a result of a series of shootings in broad daylight on a busy Pietermaritzburg ...
records.description:
Two people died and several were injured as a result of a series of shootings in broad daylight on a busy Pietermaritzburg street on 10 July 2020. Families of the victims say the shooters were police disguised as bandits. Footage of the fatal shooting recorded on various closed circuit television cameras (CCTV) paints a vivid picture of the events of 10 July 2020 when migrant traders were hit in what they say was violent police extortion. The South African Police Service (SAPS) will say nothing more than that the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (Ipid) is probing the matter. Traders who witnessed the shooting claim their attempts to help identify the killers were spurned by police who told them to “fuck off”. An Ethiopian migrant and fellow traders interviewed by New Frame at the scene tell a terrifying story of brutality and xenophobia. The shootings occurred in a block bordered by West and Pietermaritz streets in an area with a radius of about 650 metres. West Street is home to formal high street businesses: supermarkets, petrol stations, a butchery, a motor repair shop and the like. West intersects with Pietermaritz, a road lined with Jacaranda trees and old colonial houses mostly used for informal businesses: tuckshops and wholesale suppliers to spaza shops. The street typifies the neglect of basic service provision in Pietermaritzburg: mangy dogs hop across gutters choked with litter, animal bones and other waste. The area is dominated by migrant traders, mostly Ethiopian. Three of the men who were shot were Ethiopian. A fourth is Malawian. According to eyewitnesses and footage from some of the road-facing shops, masked shooters arrived at 8.20am. One eyewitness says there was a gang of eight. CCTV footage shows six people getting out of a double cab bakkie, registration number NVH574b, with a cage at the back. The footage shows five men and a woman, some wearing distinctive workwear trousers with reflective bands on the legs. Traders described their gear as “municipal” overalls. Some wore caps and hoodies. The woman is seen adjusting a holstered gun. They walked down from West Street towards Pietermaritz Street. A staffer at a tuck-shop in Pietermaritz Street, one of the first targets of the gang, says when they arrived they demanded that everyone lie down. The commotion attracted the attention of neighboring traders. Eyewitnesses say it looked like a police raid, but there were no police uniforms or badges, just armed men in “municipal” workwear and civvies. They were obviously masked because of Covid-19. The noise of the raid emboldened neighboring traders to draw closer, shouting at the gang, demanding they identify themselves. This appears to have thrown the group off, and they broke up, running in different directions, chased at a distance by angry traders who say they are often harassed by police. One shooter ran about 80m east and outside 29 Pietermaritz Street encountered a trader from Edendale who had just parked his van to collect supplies. Mamush Fune says the person shot Tesfay in the head. The young man fell down and lay bleeding on the pavement. The witness says he pursued the shooter at a distance. A police car came down the road, and the witness frantically flagged it down, jumping into the van and urging cops to race towards Boom Street where the shooter had fled. Within minutes they came upon him. Fune shouted: “That’s him!” The police van pulled up beside the gunman who opened the back door and got in. Fune says he was aghast. “He pointed the gun at me and told me to get out.” Horrified, the witness fled. Meanwhile, the commotion ramped up on Pietermaritz Street. CCTV footage from a trader shows men dressed in workwear with reflectors on the trousers and armed with guns chasing people. People can be seen diving for cover behind trees and vehicles. Some threw rocks at the shooters. Up the road in West Street, another drama unfolded. A gunman had been chased by traders into a motor mechanic’s workshop. He was holed up in the toilet there. The workshop has road access through a roller shutter door. There is a small office reception area to the right and the rest of the workshop is chockablock with cars on ramps. At the back, another roller shutter door leads to a courtyard with a toilet. It is surrounded by high walls topped with barbed wire fencing.Another witness, a mechanic and the owner of the garage. He says he was outside because of the disturbance in the road and one of the shooters dashed in, past the cars and hid in the toilet. The second witness says: “It all happened quickly.” He didn’t see the gunman. He only ran into his workshop when he heard cries for help from staff. They told him a man had been holed up in the toilet shouting into a radio or cellphone that he was being chased. “He said he was going to shoot himself out.” And he did. A migrant trader, who had chased the shooter in from the road, was badly injured from a gunshot wound in the thigh. When New Frame visited, the bloodstained workshop floor and splintered toilet door bore testimony to the shooting.
Soon afterwards, an ambulance arrived and parked at the petrol station diagonally across the road from the workshop. CCTV footage from there shows police cordoned the area off. In addition to the traders who were shot, who both later died in hospital, two others were shot and injured, an Ethiopian trader and a migrant from Malawi. The Malawian says he was making his way home from working night shift at another petrol station nearby when he found himself amid the commotion. “I was on the corner of Pietermaritz and Loop streets, and I heard shooting. People started running past me. I didn’t know what was happening. I realised I was shot in the arm.” A migrant trader told New Frame cops frequently bullied traders, including himself, demanding cash and cigarettes. “We are scared. The police take a chance. They ask for [business] licences. Then they search the store. They ask to see cigarettes in the back storeroom. I ask why. The cigarettes are in my stock, not on the shelf. We hope we will get justice. This is not right. This is not the legal way. They want to finish us one by one. We are foreigners, but we know the rule of law,” the man said. An Ethiopian elder who has been in South Africa for 14 years, spoke to New Frame at the wake held for the two victims who had died. The silence of the ceremony was punctuated by the wailing of young men who slapped their heads in anguish. Hands outstretched, an impassioned the leader said through an interpreter: “The police often come in groups to search our shops, especially since lockdown. They use force. They intimidate. They disconnect the CCTV then they take stock and money. When we try to open a case, the police treat us like guilty people and refuse to act. They follow us to our houses and victimise us. I come from Africa. This is Africa. They call us makwerekwere, but I have a right to live in Africa.” A week after the shooting, police and army hit the Pietermaritzburg central business district again in a show of force. According to the Weekend Witness, police arrived with troops and home affairs officials, rounding up migrant traders and arresting 57 people. Cartons of cigarettes were seized. Witness reporter Clive Ndou wrote that the bustling business precinct resembled “a war zone, with heavily armed soldiers”, one of whom was overheard screaming: “You came to my country to commit crime. We won’t allow you to do as you like.” Police, he wrote, used crowbars to break stores open and army nyalas blocked roads and cut off escape routes. “The shop owners, some of whom were visibly terrified, were made to stand in the middle of the road from where they were loaded into police vans.” Ndou quoted Economic Development, Tourism and Environmental Affairs MEC Nomusa Dube-Ncube saying her department’s consumer complaints unit had “a responsibility to protect businesses conducting their operations according to the book against bogus business owners who have no respect for the law.” Attacks on migrants in South Africa have escalated dramatically since Covid-19 and continue in spite of widespread condemnation by organisations demanding an urgent end to the xenophobia. The KwaZulu-Natal Christian Council has expressed concern over attacks on migrants and raised the issue at a recent meeting with KwaZulu-Natal premier Sihle Zikalala. Ipid spokesperson Ndileka Cola failed to respond to questions.
Source: New Frame -https://www.newframe.com/mystery-of-maritzburgs-masked-murderers/

records.name: Xenowatch received reports of xenophobic violence in parts of the East Rand, Ekurhuleni Municipality at 12 mid day ...
records.description: Xenowatch received reports of xenophobic violence in parts of the East Rand, Ekurhuleni Municipality at 12 mid day on Wednesday. Reports were informed by verification partners on the ground who reported that there was a meeting last weekend - Friday and Saturday to address issues of unemployment within the Ekurhuleni area. The outcome of the meeting was that rising unemployment was resultant on foreign nationals living and residing in the area. These attacks were the outcome of a considered decision to rid the community of foreign nationals. It was reported that on the night of the 28th July 2020- foreign shop owners were targeted and on the 29th July large groups of young people went door to door chasing out foreign nationals renting backyard rooms and shacks. Police were immediately alerted by Xenowatch and various stakeholders. There was police visibility but by Wednesday evening the situation had become worse. Police were informed and stated that a team would be sent out to address and monitor the situation. By Thursday morning the situation was still tense. Reports were that people were burning migrants belongings and migrants were fleeing the area. Reports estimate that that 124 spaza shops, stalls and other businesses in the area were either damaged or looted. Over a 100 families and individuals left the area due to fear for their lives and are staying with family members in various parts of Gauteng. Police report that about 20 people have been arrested and charged with public violence and are due to appear in court. 1 death was reported by a partner organisation.

records.name: Two foreign nationals in Durban on Monday opened a case with the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (Ipid) ...
records.description: Two foreign nationals in Durban on Monday opened a case with the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (Ipid) after being allegedly assaulted by police for having expired asylum seeker documentation. The victims said that they were detained, beaten, and then released without charge on 16 October. The two victims who are originally from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, said that the policemen also used xenophobic insults. They said that their two-hour nightmare started when six police officers stopped their vehicle while they were walking from a relative’s house in a Durban suburb. “They asked us to take our documents out and we showed them our asylum seeker documentation, and when they saw that they started handling one of the victims in a very unpleasant way. So, they started picking him up,” the other victim said. The victims were then taken into a police vehicle. “And the one guy who was in front came with a glass bottle and started hitting us with it,” he said. One of the victim said the police took them to a room within the Durban bus station where they were further assaulted. “All of them would just come and slap us and bang our heads constantly against the wall and even against each other.” Ipid confirmed that it is investigating the matter.

records.name: A group identifying as MK veterans — some dressed in military fatigues — marched through the city centre on Monday ...
records.description: A group identifying as MK veterans — some dressed in military fatigues — marched through the city centre on Monday and Tuesday last week demanding that foreign-owned businesses be shut and their owners “go home”. The group justified its actions with the ubiquitous refrain, heard in the province and nationally during xenophobic flare-ups, that foreigners were “taking jobs” from locals and were involved in drug dealing and drug trafficking. The march soon turned violent, with several shop owners threatened or assaulted and stores looted. However, witnesses have said, “drug users” known to frequent the city centre were the ones “mostly” responsible for the looting.

Durban Central

The MKMVA-KZN, ATDF ASA, EPWP, Unemployed Graduates and Street Vendors will be holding a march from Albert Park to Open Beach, Point. The purpose of the march is to voice their dissatisfaction with Government Treatment of South Africans. According to the organizers Foreign Nationals receive better treatment then locals. They also alleged that Foreigners do not pay Tax and South Africans are only given grants such as R350 unemployment funds of which most South Africans have not qualified to receive it. Approximately 500 participants will be expected to attend. The possibility of confrontations between Foreign Nationals and participants leading to criminal elements such as looting, Malicious damage to property, Public violence cannot be ruled out, furthermore the blocking of roads and heavy traffic congestion cannot be ruled out. Monitoring is required. Thereafter two vehicles will proceed to Bayhead Transnet offices to hand over a memorandum regarding Foreign Nationals who are employed by South African owned trucking companies to enter the port.

records.name: DURBAN: 24 November 2020 – A 24-year-old shop owner is expected to appear before the Ntuzuma Magistrates Court today ...
records.description: DURBAN: 24 November 2020 – A 24-year-old shop owner is expected to appear before the Ntuzuma Magistrates Court today on charges of murder and possession illegal firearm and ammunition. It is alleged that on 22 November 2020 at 18:00, a group of residents from KwaMashu Hostel embarked on protest action. The group of protestors proceeded to a shop in B Section where they instructed the owner to vacate. The owner allegedly fired shots towards the crowd. A 17-year-old male was fatally shot and he sustained a gunshot wound to the chest. He was identified by his father. Public Order Police and KwaMashu police were alerted and they responded rapidly. On arrival, they pursued the crowd that was looting the shop and chasing the shop owner. The owner was apprehended and police recovered a 9mm firearm with 21 rounds of ammunition in his possession. He was then placed under arrest and was taken to KwaMashu police station for detention. Furthermore, police officers were able to arrest and charged a total of five suspects for public violence. They are appearing today at the Ntuzuma Magistrates Court. Further reports state that 4 shops were looted.

records.name: Further reports from Daily Maverick are as follows: Last week, foreign national traders were again attacked at the ...
records.description:
Further reports from Daily Maverick are as follows: Last week, foreign national traders were again attacked at the popular Church Walk flea market, situated next to the Workshop shopping centre and within spitting distance of city hall, despite police patrols in the area being increased. Scores of foreign traders fled the market in November following violent attacks by the veterans, who told Daily Maverick at the time that the traders had been “chased away” because they were “illegal” and had to make space for local traders, who had been ordered to sell “traditional” wares by the veterans. A foreign national who regularly trades at the market and has a permit to do so told Daily Maverick his stall was torched during the attack, that he was stabbed, and alleges that a petrol bomb was thrown — while metro police looked on. 

“We were told at a meeting with the mayor’s office that all of those who have a contract with the municipality must go back and open their stores because it won’t be a problem, there will be police guarding us,” said the man, who is known to Daily Maverick.  “On Friday [11 December] I opened my store. Maybe after 20 minutes, as I was waiting for customers, I saw a group coming from [the Steers side of the market]. I was sitting with two of my friends, talking and drinking coffee. I told [my friends] these guys are coming to us, let’s wait for them. “They stopped in front of my shop, I saw one guy pull a knife, he told us to stop talking. I told him to not bring problems here, we are here to trade, we don’t have any problems. They said I was [a foreigner] and I must ‘just fucking go’. They started swearing.“I just told them ‘guys, move from here,’ but they didn’t leave. They just started pulling the knife, they wanted to [stab us] they even [stabbed] me. Then they started with the petrol bomb. Then the police came, they told us to pack our bags and go. We told the police to just give us a chance to pack our backs and we would go. “As we were walking away, the group also [attacked] people at the [other] end of the market. [The attackers] were stealing, and they started with the petrol bomb again, they burned it [sic], in front of the police, the police were standing there. We called the police, but they were taking a long time.”The trader said he opened a case at Durban Central police station and was promised that a case number would be SMSed. “I still haven’t got it.”Last week’s attacks took place just one day after a meeting with eThekwini officials and police, where the traders were assured it was safe to return to the market. Another victim reported to Xenowatch that while he was selling his stuff on the streets, a mob came to his work place and started beating him. They took all his products and told him to go back to his country because they did not want any foreigners. He reported the case to the police but nothing was done. Victim reports that the police told him to go to court. Victim is traumatised and is not certain about the future.. He lives in constant fear of death and is ready to be relocated else where.

records.name: Poster circulating on WhatsApp telling foreign nationals not to come back to SA. "To all illegal migrants in South ...
records.description: Poster circulating on WhatsApp telling foreign nationals not to come back to SA. "To all illegal migrants in South Africa. Go and enjoy festive season in your country and don’t come back!! Respect Immigration Act 13 of 2002 and employment services act . South Africa is not a refugee camp for all desparate foreigners. Many South Africans are desparate and poor too, in their country. Stop coming here to sell your cheap labour, pushing poor South Africans out of work. Be resilient and find solutions in your countries. Stay in your countries and deal with your corrupt politicians . Stop running away to SA. We cannot save you!!! Don't come to SA to give birth in our public hospitals. You are a burdern and are taking space meant for South Africans. Don't come to SA to steal our cars, cables, sell drugs and destroy our cities. SA belongs to South Africans, not politicians and political parties. Don't buy fake South African ID's, work permits, permanant residence and citizen documents from corrupt officials. It will end in tears!!! Many Patriotic South Africans are tired of the influx of illegal migrants!! Sikhathele."

records.name: Spaza Shop Owners Accuse Police of Stealing Their Cash
records.description:
In March under Operation Okae Molao immigrant-owned spaza shops in Diepsloot were targeted by police. Police say they confiscated R63,000 in cash and it is held in a state account. Shop owners say it was more than double that amount. The shop owners also claim they had to each pay police R5,000 to be released. Immigrant spaza shop owners in Diepsloot say they have been struggling to recover tens (if not hundreds) of thousands of rands confiscated by police during Operation Okae Molao two months ago. The shop owners GroundUp spoke to all tell a similar story. They say their shops were raided, they were handcuffed, and their cash was taken. They spent a day in police cells and were released after paying the police R5,000 "bail". They were never charged or taken to court. The "bail" money was not officially recorded. Police subsequently issued them receipts for the money confiscated, but it is usually 50% of the actual amount taken according to the shop owners. They say they have tried to open cases for the missing money, but police refuse to open any dockets.
https://allafrica.com/stories/202105311145.html

Further investigations from Xenowatch revealed that police forcibly seized and stripped shop owners of large sums of cash during security operations in the area during the month of March, with some shop owners and their employees even being brutally beaten by the police.These victims said after the violent encounter at the hands of the police, they attempted to file a complaint with local authorities but their complaints were ignored. The police reported that during the time of the operations they were searching for illegal weapons that where suspected of being in the shops owned by foreign nationals.

records.name: Foreign traders were attacked in Soldiers way flea market by the so called MKMVA war veterans
records.description: On Sunday 28th February, foreign traders were attacked in Soldiers way flea market by the so called MKMVA war veterans. All their goods were looted, money and valuables taken by attackers. Since then , they were not able to trade and earn a living. After a lot of pressure to the municipality to provide police guards for the market, it was only on Sunday 09th May that this was seemingly organised and foreign traders were promised SAPS and Metro Police presence in the market. Unfortunately these came early in the morning for a short time and then went elsewhere leaving the market to MKMVA thugs who came into the market when the police left. They then  started extorting money, R50 per foreign trader (only these were paying) and others had to hide winter clothing from them. This is illegal, criminal and xenophobic because only foreign traders were paying this money and these are permit holders who pay regularly to the municipality. The matter was reported to eThekwini municipality but so far no action taken.. The majority of victims are Congolese and Burundians but there were also few Zimbabweans, Malawians, Cameroonians and women from Mozambique.

records.name: Eswatini Truck drivers Beaten up in Richards Bay Port Harbour
records.description: On Friday 14th May 2021, we received videos of people beating truck drivers who happen to be from eSwatini. The people in the video could be heard saying that South Africans want their jobs and they do not want South African trucks to be driven by foreigners. They then proceeded to beat the victims (eSwatini truck drivers) with sjamboks, warned them never to come back with trucks to South Africa. These perpetrators happen to be members of ATDF, the same group that was responsible for burning trucks on N3 and that joined forces with MKMVA and unemployed graduates to cause mayhem among migrant informal traders here in Durban. We received another call from another Swazi truck driver who reported that the ATDF people are there again attacking and beating up foreign truck drivers without any law enforcement agency being aware of it.

records.name: 11 people were shot and killed on Saturday 15 May 2021 in Khayelitsha and surrounding areas.

This incident is part of several incidents that took place in different parts of Khayelitsha and surrounding areas. These include Khayelitsha, Philippi and Kraaifontein. It is reported that one of the persons killed was Ethiopian and 5 were Somalian and another was Malawian, the remaining 6 were South African. Confirmation from the ground is that it is as a result of extortion - protection fees. It is reported that after the initial shooting of some of the foreign nationals that rival gangs also had a shoot out as the one was trying to take over the other gangs turf. The shootings sent a shockwave through the neighborhoods and families of the deceased were severely traumatized. Locals were also very concerned with what happened.

records.name: Foreign Shop Owners Shot in Gqeberha (Booysen Park)
records.description: On 18/05/2021 at 19:00 a white Toyota Quantum stopped in front of Top 10 shop, William Slammert Drive, Booysen Park, Gqeberha, in the Eastern Cape but no one got out of the vehicle which then drove away from the shop, and parked away from the shop. The occupants got out of the vehicle and went back to the shop. The first victim stood at the gate of the shop on the inside when 4 Xhosa guys entered the shop and without saying anything, started shooting at the second victim whom out of shock ran into the room where they sleep. At that stage, he was preparing to sleep with no knowledge of what was going on. The 1st victim ran into the room where the 2nd victim was but he was followed by the criminals who forcefully opened the gate. The moment  the criminals entered the room, they found  the 2nd victim on the bed where he was shot twice on the upper right leg by the criminals. Afterwards, the criminals went back into the shop and took what ever they wanted. Whilst they were still busy in the shop, the neighbors fired 2 warning shots in an effort to scare the criminals off. After hearing the shots, the criminals ran to their vehicle and drove away. According to a source, the neighbor never went to the front of his house because he did not want to be seen by these criminals. Community members contacted one of the shop keepers who was not present at the scene to inform him about the incident at the shop. Accordingly, he rushed to the shop at Booysens Park, Gqeberha and on arrival, found the 2 victims in the bedroom, shot by these criminals and left for dead. Without waiting on the police he rushed with the 2nd victim to Livingstone Hospital for treatment and returned to the shop. On his arrival he found the police on the scene whom informed him that 8 shots were fired at the first victim but he was struck by 4 bullets which caused him to die, according to the Medical practitioner who was assisting on the scene.

records.name: Two Shop-owners attacked in Booysen Park
records.description:
On 18 May 2021 the two victims working at Top 10 shop saw a White Toyota
 Quantum parked in front of the shop. The quantum owners went into the shop and decided to get back in vehicle and drove off. They parked further down the road and walked back to shop whilst one of the victims stood at the counter behind locked gate. Four unknown Xhosa guys entered the shop and shot at the victim. Out of shock the victim ran to a room where the second victim was sleeping oblivious to what was happening. The gate was forced open, and the four men came across the second victim who was sleeping and shot at him twice on his upper right leg and went back into shop and helped themselves to the goods in the store. Neighbors heard shots being fired and called the police and also fired two warning shots to scare the men off. When the men heard the shots, they to their vehicle and sped off.  The shop owner  was contacted by community leaders and informed about incident. On arrival, the shop owner took the first victim to Livingstone Hospital for medical treatment.  When the shop-owner returned to his shop, he found the police at the scene who informed him the second victim had died of 4 bullet wounds that struck his body.

records.name: Mobs loot 50 shops of Bangladeshis
records.description: A mob looted and vandalised around 50 shops and malls owned by Bangladeshis in Brandfort of Free State province in South Africa on Tuesday. The attack comes after businesses of foreign nationals were vandalised and looted over a five-day period since May 16 in Bloemfontein of the same province. The mobs had been protesting poor service delivery by the local government.

records.name: Truck driver threatened and accused of taking South African Jobs
records.description: The incident took place on 31/05/2021 at the Emerlo 24/7 truck stop at around 6:00 am in the morning. The victim, a truck driver from Swaziland was stopped on a roadblock by a group of people who asked for his licence and identity document to check if he was South African. When they found out that he was a foreign national, the group told the victim to get off the truck, took his license, ID and the truck keys. The victim was held hostage for some time and was accused of coming to South Africa and settling for a less salary to take South African jobs. There was no physical damage to the victims's truck and he was not harmed. The victim was set free after some time of being held hostage and was given a verbal verbal warning. It is reported that the perpetrators were young unemployed South African young men who are members of the ATDF and are frustrated at foreign truck drivers at taking their "jobs" since foreign truck drivers agree to be paid for a lesser fee. It was also reported that the police monitored the situation in case the situation escalated.

records.name: A Somalian National Attacked in Nelspruit
records.description: A Somalian national who owns a spaza shop in down town Nelspruit, 16 Anderson street was attacked  in May 2021. The incident happened late at night after he had closed his shop and was accompanying his brother. He was hit with a brick on his head and was injured in the process. He had to go to hospital to get stitched as he was bleeding very badly on his forehead. Upon arrival at the hospital, he was refused help and was accused of wasting time, resources and lying about what happened to him. He was not stitched correctly and it was done to just stop the bleeding. When he  went to the police to report the incident the police, the police did not want to open a case or investigate. Instead they wanted to arrest him for not sanitizing his hands when he entered the police station.

records.name: Victim attacked by armed men in his Salon
records.description: The victim originally from Ghana owns a salon in Sabie Town. On the 12th of August 2014 late in the day when he was about to close his salon, a group of four guys with masks came to his salon with guns and shouted at him calling him a foreigner who came to still business opportunities from the community of Sabie. The perpetrators then demanded that the victim give them the money he made for that day. The perpetrators told the victim that he didn't deserve to make money in a foreign country.

records.name: Trucks drives attacked in Richards Bay
records.description: According to reports received, a group of black South Africans in 5 vehicles were stopping drivers who are from Eswatini, beating them up and telling them never to come back to Richards Bay anymore or drive South African trucks while black South Africans are unemployed and poor. The Consulate of Eswatini in South Africa who happened to be in Mpongolo at the time the incident occurred was contacted and immediately drove to Richards Bay to witness the incident. Upon arrival and witnessing the incident, the Consulate contacted the police for intervention.

records.name: Nigerian Asylum Seeker dies in Police Custody
records.description: A Nigerian asylum seeker was apprehended in Central Newcastle by Police who suspected him of being in possession of drugs. When he saw their intention of arresting him, he run away and they run after him. When they apprehended him, they took him in the police van and tortured him badly. It is believed that they used a plastic tube to force him to confess and that is when he passed out. He later died in the Police van on the way to the police station.

records.name: Containers belonging to foreigners were removed or demolished by Police and Municipal Officials in Greytown
records.description: It was on 07/06/2021 in the afternoon that police and official from various departments of Umvoti municipality were seen picking up small containers on Durban street and and loading them on trucks and taken to an unknown place. The operation continued up to the 09th June 2021. The problem is that only containers belonging to foreigners were removed or demolished, which is discriminatory especially considering that all of them had vending permits issued by the same municipality.

records.name: Foreign shops looted in Upington
records.description: Community members led by the local business forum attacked and looted shops of foreign nationals claiming that they are taking away opportunities as well as business ventures and are not contributing to the local economy, this was also sparked by the stabbing of local SAPS official as per their claim.

records.name: Anti-protests march led by Operation results in foreign nationals fleeing the area
records.description:
A ‘clean-up’ march - through Soweto led to sporadic looting of migrant-owned shops and the eviction of some residents. On the 16th of June 2021 dozens of people armed with sjamboks and sticks met in Diepkloof, Soweto, under the banner of Operation Dudula. A poster about it had been circulating for weeks online, warning “We will be removing all illegal foreign nationals by force!!!” Similar posters doing the rounds contained even more inflammatory language and images. 

Flyers had also been hand-delivered to migrant-owned shops in the weeks leading up to Youth Day. Despite the poster’s crude and alarming xenophobic statements as well as the messages accompanying it when it was shared online, the organisers of Operation Dudula, which claimed on the day they gathered at the Diepkloof Hall that the group was not xenophobic. Reports of evictions of foreign residents carried out on the day were reported. 

Xenowatch conducted further investigations in the weeks following the protests and the following was determined:
1.) 34 stores owned by foreign nationals where looted in Soweto. Information i received also reveals some of them where partially looted during the mayhem. 
2.) Up to 300 people fled Soweto between the 10th and 16th of June following large scale anti migrant protests in the area. Most of these individuals packed up their belongings and stored them in places such as the Salahudin Cash and Carry, Hawaash Cash & Carry & Tayo Cash and Carry. These locations stored belongings and supplies belonging foreign nationals and document the details of the individuals so that they are able to get their belongings back.
3.) The vast majority of these victims where foreign nationals/migrants that owned stores in various neighborhoods throughout Soweto. Seven families that are foreigners are reported to have fled the area due to the volatile situation that was unfolding at the time. All seven of these families lived in Diepkloof. 
4.) It is alleged that foreign nationals where attacked in Diepkloof, Mapetla and Naledi. Similar attacks where reported in Zola, Orlando East, Senaoane and Dobsonville  where foreign nationals own businesses.

records.name: Two victims at Madiba shop where shot at
records.description: On the 19th of May 2021, two victims at Madiba shop where shot at. One of the victims was shot four times and fell to the ground. According to the paramedics, he died on the scene as a result of bullet wounds.

records.name: Service delivery turns violent and results in attacks on foreign nationals
records.description: A service delivery protest started on the 23rd of June in an area that reported living 2 weeks without electricity while  another area had electricity. The following day, the protest turned violent and some protesters decided to attack foreigners (especially Ethiopians) who opened their shops after the protest. Two shops were ransacked, goods systematically looted and shop keepers beaten. 3 shop keepers sustained head injuries but no one lost his life.

records.name: Shop owners in Malmesbury warned to pay extortion fee
records.description: Shop owners in Malmesbury were handed leaflets demanding that they pay extortion fees. Some of these leaflets were found in about 10 stores owned by foreign nationals. [Dear my friend, my crew and I want to protect your shops from robbery but on one condition, you have to pay rent of R1500 per month, we will collect once a month. If you don't follow our request, they will be a problem]. Police were informed and having been monitoring the situation and are visible in the area. It is reported that some arrests were made.

records.name: Victim shot dead in KwaDwesi
records.description: Two Xhosa guys approached Discount Mini Market at 37 Asrayi Street, KwaDwesi, Gqeberha and on entering took out firearms and shot at shopkeeper no reason. He was not injured but  another victim was injured his arm when diving onto ground. It was discovered that these criminals travelled in a Silver Mazda Etude without number plates. Further reports state SAPS are reluctant to assist foreign nationals even if cases are being reported. They would at all times ask if these criminals are known and if not fail to open serious crime cases.

records.name: A called group called Enough is Enough in Zeerust is threatening and forcing salons belonging to the Congolese nationals to close early
records.description: A called group called Enough is Enough in Zeerust is threatening and forcing salons belonging to the Congolese nationals to close by 1pm on Saturday and not open Sundays and if they don’t comply, then they should go back to their country. The same group threatened them in 2018 and they reported the issue to the SAHRC. SAPS queried them then, for going the SAHRC instead of coming to them, still nothing was done. On Sunday the 27th June 2021, One of the shop owners was threatened by the two of the Enough is Enough leaders who broke bottles in his shop and telling customers to leave. The victim also fled and went to report the matter to the SAPS. He was provided with a number to call if he ever feels threatened again. The police did not take a statement.

records.name: Two Ethiopians attacked during Riots in Durban
records.description: It was late evening on Sunday the 11th July, the 3rd day of the #FreeZuma riots when a crowd of people stormed the spaza shop where 2 Ethiopians were working. They tried to run but unfortunately both fell and people trampled them over. They both sustained head injuries and were taken to hospital where they were treated.

records.name: Zimbabwean woman assaulted in Jail and told to go back to her country
records.description: A Zimbabwean woman detainee, appeared in court after her accused dropped charges against her. While in incarceration, she was harassed by SAPS officials, the female SAPS official tried to slap her saying that she must go back to her country, at one stage, she was taken to Groot Marico jail and put in a solitary cell, but then was again transferred to Mafikeng Rooigrond jail.

records.name: Land and housing protest results in looting of foreign shops
records.description: The incident happened on Tuesday, 3rd August 2021 in the early hours of the morning. There was a protest march for land and housing by locals. The incident was chaotic as tyres were burnt on the street. Police did not attend the scene. Law enforcement officers arrived but were overpowered by the protesters who started stoning the authorities resulting in them leaving the scene. At about 6pm the protestors stormed a foreign owner's spaza shop and looted everything. Looters attacked a second shop which was close by. There was some damages to the roof as a result. The shop owners were traumatized by the incident.

records.name: One Bangladesh male, a foreign shop owner was attacked and shot two times.
records.description: One Bangladesh male, a foreign shop owner was attacked and shot two times. The victim was in his shop with his worker when two guys stormed into the shop and made remarks that foreigners are taking away locals business opportunities. They shot the victim twice and took an undisclosed sum of money and vanished in a get away vehicle. The police are still looking for the suspects and the victim is critical in the Kimberley Hospital.

records.name: A Western cape farmer refused to pay his foreign employees because they are undocumented. Instead he gets immigration officers to arrest them
records.description: This incident involved 7 Burundian undocumented asylum seekers who have been working for a company for almost a year. They all came into the country few months before lockdown and where not able to get their documents before the lockdown started. The farm management knew their situation and accepted it. The victims speak Kirundi, Kiswahili and little bit of French, so on 31st of August 2021 when they were called to the office to sign some documents, they did not understand the meaning of what they were signing; about 30 minutes after, they were called back to the office by the farm Manager. When they arrived, they were asked to wait outside and after a while the manager and the owner came to meet them outside. The Manager then informed them that there were officials who were going to take them to their office to ask them some questions. They got worried and started asking questions as to why they are questioned on the farm. This led to some fighting as they were resisting to board a bakkie. That is when they realized that they were in the presence of 3 Immigration Officers.  Some of them managed to escape, leaving only one who was subsequently taken to the Bellville Police Station. He was locked up for 10 days during which he managed to get hold of a lawyer from UCT law clinic who then managed to get him released after his third court appearance at Bellville Court. He is currently following up the CCMA case with others. The CCMA case number is WECT 1273-21.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: The police was not called but one of the victim managed  to contact (a UNHCR social partner based in Cape Town) which contacted UCT law clinic which in turn managed to get them released from jail.

records.name: Shop Assistant in NU13 Motherwell shot and killed for failure to hand over Protection fees
records.description: On the 9th of September 2021, the shop assistant of Africa shop, located in NU 13, Motherwell, was attacked by criminals who came to collect protection fees. The shop assistant was shot twice and killed for failing to give them the money.

records.name: Sebokeng residents chase away foreigners after missing child is found dead
records.description: Residents of Sebokeng Zone 6 have vented their anger on African foreign nationals residing in the area after the decomposed body of a teenager was found in a storm water drain a month after she went missing. They have stated that they want them gone after accusing a foreign national of being behind her murder. Since 10 August, residents have marched house to house, demanding all foreigners, particularly African countries, vacate the township. Foreigners, except for those who own spaza shops, have been given until Monday (September 13) to leave the area. On Monday morning, groups of residents led by women marched to houses where foreigners were renting rooms calling for them to disperse.https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/sebokeng-residents-chase-away-foreigners-after-missing-child-is-found-dead-20210913

records.name: Ethiopian Shopkeeper Shot and killed in Lamontville
records.description: It was on Tuesday evening around 18h00 that a group of armed guys stormed the shop of the victim and took cash, and cellphones before shooting the shopkeeper. Investigation is still underway to verify the motive of the killing but the Ethiopian leadership believes that it is a local guy who wants to start his own spaza shop, who is responsible. This is because he threatened the Ethiopian shop keeper before the shooting to either shut off his shop or else face consequences.

records.name: Foreign Owned Shop Petrol Bombed in Zwide
records.description: Two shops belonging to foreign nationals in Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape, South Africa, have allegedly been petrol bombed. Naidu says the police are investigating if these two incidents are linked to the violence that erupted in Korsten on Wednesday afternoon between taxi operators and foreign nationals. One of the shops affected was in Zwide.https://mbaretimes.com/2021/10/xenophobic-attacks/

records.name: Foreign-owned shop petrol-bombed in Kwazakhele
records.description: On Thursday 14/10/2021 the evening of the Korsten incident, two shopkeepers were attacked in their place of work. There were asleep when they smelt smoke and realized the shop was burning.  The two shopkeepers managed to escape through the back of their room and called the shop owner for help informing him that the shop is being set alight. Residents of the area ransacked the shop by removing all the stock which was inside the shop before it was completely destroyed. The stock was worth about R 500 000 and the building was completely destroyed and burnt to the ground. The fire was put out by the fire brigade to prevent other houses from burning as well. Suspects unknown to community of the area. It seems criminals took advantage of situation in Korsten and destroyed businesses belonging to foreign nationals.

records.name: Residents of Alexandra township are angry and attacking all Nigerians in their area
records.description: According to The Daily Talk Online TV, residents of Alexandra township are angry and attacking all Nigerians in their area, following an incident whereby a Nigerian shot and killed a South African. The neighborhood was blanked with smog-like tear gas fumes, and it has been reported that the suspect was attacked by an angry mob but the police were called to the scene to intervene. Thereafter, the residents realized that law enforcement is not on their side. All Nigerians had fallen victim to the anger as the angry mob was looking for them to teach them a lesson. The police have managed to calm the residents, but Nigerians around the township are living in fear as they do not know what could happen to them when the police are not around.https://za.opera.news/za/en/justice/0cc2a72b3f9c756d51a1f40f1717a118

records.name: Truck driver attacked while enroute to Richards Bay
records.description: It is alleged that on Monday 2021-11-08 at 20:30 a truck driver for Transmec Trucking, was enroute to Richards Bay and had stopped at the N2 off ramp stop sign, when two unknown African males pulled the truck trailer brakes, so that the truck could not move. Two shots were fired at him, one shot hit the left hand side of the windscreen. He got off the truck and ran to hide. The truck driver stated that he saw petrol bombs being thrown at the truck. The suspects fled on foot and then he went back to the truck and used a fire extinguisher to put the fire out. After that, the truck driver called his supervisor to inform him of the incident and proceeded to the police station to open a case.

records.name: Truck Driver attacked in Richards Bay
records.description: It is alleged that on Monday 2021-11-08 at 20:30, a truck driver for NI-DA Trucking was at the robot between John Ross Highway and Alumina Allee in Richards Bay, when he heard gunshots, one shot hit the windscreen, other shot hit the passenger seat of the truck. He then heard a male voice instructing him to get off the truck, he got off and ran into a nearby bush. He then saw his truck burning. Later, he saw a traffic vehicle approaching, so he approached the traffic officer and related the incident. Fire Brigade and Saps responded to a call.

records.name: Somali Shopkeeper Killed by armed gunmen
records.description: The incident took place in the evening of the 14th of November 2021. Armed gunmen stormed the shop of a shop-owner and demanded protection fees. Moments later shots were heard from the shop, the owner of the shop was found in his own pool of blood according to neighbors. The Police arrived at the crime scene but the culprits had long gone. The family is very traumatized.

records.name: Local Residents in Upignton attack foreign shop owners
records.description: On the 03/11/2021, Twenty (20) local residents in the Upignton area in the Northern Cape organized themselves with weapons which included, knives, pangas and other sharp objects. The residents went to  5 different shops in the areas demanding a protection fee of R5000 (five thousand rands) from the foreign national shop owners. The shop owners refused to give them the money. On 15/11/2021 the 20 (twenty) residents came back again armed and started to vandalize the 5 (five) shops and looting the shops leaving nothing with other members of the community taking part in the looting and vandalizing. cases have been opened with the SAPS Upignton of damage to property, common assault and assault to cause grievous bodily harm, the local police states that no arrest has been made thus far.

records.name: Zimbabweans leaving in Seshego attacked and told to leave
records.description: Around the week of the 15th of November 2021 a xenophobic incident took place which was sparked by the alleged serial killer Mr Themba Prince Willard’s Dube who is 36 years old and is facing seven counts of murder and seven of kidnapping at the Seshego Magistrate court in Limpopo province. His case was postponed to the 27th of January 2022. According to media sources, it is understood that the community reacted by attacking all Zimbabwean living in Seshego and killing a number of Zimbabweans, the numbers are not known and the authorities are not providing any information. It is also alleged that information was circulating on social media during that week informing Zimbabwean living in and around Seshego to leave within fourteen days or face the consequences. The Community Advice and Law office in Seshego confirmed having received two (2) Zimbabweans running for safety, whom they accommodated. During the week of the 22nd of November 2021 social media videos were circulating with two (2) Zimbabweans who were being stoned in Seshego Township and were killed by Seshego community members. Upon contacting the Seshego Police station regarding the xenophobia incidents, they refused to comment and claimed that the case of the serial killer was still under investigation and in court therefore were not in position to share any information and despite they were not authorised to share any information.

records.name: Murder of shop keeper and theft
records.description: The Ethiopian shopkeeper was shot and killed in his shop, in Umzinto. The exact location is not known but it appears that money was taken from the till as well as airtime vouchers that he was selling. Nothing else seems to have been taken.
records.who_attacked: An Ethiopian shop keeper. Money and airtime vouchers were also taken from the shop
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: The police was called to crime scene
records.other_text: I learnt from Ethiopian community leader

records.name: Nigerian informal traders denied the right to trade in Musina
records.description: In November 2021, the Musina local municipality officials in charge of informal trading, instructed Nigerians informal traders at Musina street market, to stop trading accusing them of trading without licenses and dealing in drugs. These Nigerians have been selling clothes and cosmetics in that market for more than 10 years alongside other informal traders with no major problems. Many of them have been unsuccessfully applying for trading permits over all those years. The affected Nigerians, who have not been trading since November last year, are accusing those officials of discriminating against them simply because they are Nigerians. These accusations are based on the fact that other informal traders, both national and non nationals, whether trading with or without permits, were not subjected to the same treatment. A delegation of Nigerian Union of South Africa (NUSA), led by its President, met with Musina  Municipal manager on 2nd February 2022. In the meeting, he apologised to his guests and promised to attend to the matter as a matter of urgency, saying that anyone who is in the country legally has the right to earn a living in any way that is allowed on his or her visa.
records.who_attacked: Nigerians informal traders at Musina street market
records.response: The municipal manager promised to resolve the problem, but so far nothing has changed yet
records.other_text: The President of Nigerians Union of South Africa (NUSA)

records.name: It is a report on violent xenophobic attack on migrant shop keeper
records.description: It was on Thursday morning around 10h00, on 25 November 2021, when the victim and friends were offloading goods from their bakkie as supplies for their tuck shop, when 6 young guys stormed the place. It is when the victim wanted to start the car and flee that he was fatally shot several time while in front seat of the bakkie. The perpetrators then took an undisclosed amount of cash that was in the bakkie and fled on foot.
records.response: The matter was reported to Bhekitemba Police station but so far no arrest was made. The medico-legal team from SAPS came to pick up the body of the deceased.
records.other_text: I learnt from Ethiopian community member

records.name: Municipal Official only targets foreign traders
records.description: On 4th and 27 October 2021 morning, an officer in charge of informal trading for Msunduzi municipality, assisted by police, evicted foreign street traders from their sites as they did not have trading permits.
