According to sources he goes there at least once every week and impound goods belonging to foreign traders. Of course the municipal by-law prohibit anyone from trading on street without a license or a trading permit, but the reports received and that was verified indicate that the officer was only confiscating goods belonging to foreign traders while South African traders without permits were left alone.

records.name: Truck drivers harassed at old Durban airport
records.description:
eThekwini Metro police dispersed a crowd of about 100 illegal protesters who were stopping trucks near the old Durban airport site on Wednesday 12th January 2022, demanding to see their drivers’ licenses to check whether they are foreign employees.

Metro police responded to the scene where alleged members of ATDF (All Truck Drivers Forum) had been pulling over trucks and demanding to see their permits and dispersed the perpetrators. It is alleged that a post that circulated on an ATDF WhatsApp groups called for this action but the The ATDF secretary attributed this action to a group of job seekers called Amaphisi.
records.who_attacked: All foreign truck drivers who happened to be on that road on the day
records.duration: The whole morning, up to 10:00 AM
records.response: Yes, Metro police responded to the scene and dispersed the perpetrators.

records.name: A Tanzania in the Police custody on the 16th of January 2022
records.description:
A Tanzanian National died in the Police cells on the 16th of January 2022 who was living in District 6/Cape Town CBD.  The police raided their place looking for illegal substances and ended up arresting him and many other foreigners in the Cape Town CBD for being in the country without proper documentation.

They were then taken into police custody at Cape Town Central Police Station where he died 2 days later, on Sunday 16th January in police custody. It appears though that the deceased was diabetic and on medication, but the police did not allow him to take his medication. The Police spokesperson, Captain FC van Wyk, confirmed the death and said an inquest docket was opened following the death of the 33-year-old Tanzanian man.

The case is currently being investigated by Cape Town Central SAPS Detectives and a post-mortem will be conducted to determine the cause of death. The Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) is also investigating the matter.
records.who_attacked: Mr. Ali Garley, died in police custody. The exact cause of his death is still under investigation
records.duration: He was found dead in the morning.
records.response: An inquest docket was opened and also IPID is investigating.

records.name: Illegal crackdown of foreign run shops in Eldorado Park.
records.description: Members of Patriotic Alliance, including their chief whip, went around Eldorado Park shutting down shops operated by foreign nationals
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: So far no response, other than interviews of the leadership of the party by the mainstream media i.e. eNCA, SABC and Newsroom Africa

records.name: Operation Dudula at Bara taxi Rank
records.description:
Operation Dudula.
Some residents of Diepkloof in Soweto witnessed scenes of Operation Dudula, aimed at chasing away foreign nationals who are informal traders at Bara Taxi Rank. 
This “clean-up” operation, unsupported by any legal entity such as the police or home affairs, was allegedly aimed at ending illegal activities and removing unlawful immigrants. It is important to note that while no law enforcement official was seen on the scene yet Diepkloof has a Police station not far from where the operation took place.
Many foreign nationals who were trading at the rank lost their livelihood and had to salvage whatever they could.
records.who_attacked: Kiosks, stalls and spaza shops operated by foreign nationals at Bara Taxi Rank in Diepkloof
records.duration: The whole morning, more than 4 hours
records.response: Not that we are aware of

records.name: A refugee family attacked and told to go back home
records.description: On Monday 17 January 2022, in Rosettenville, Verona street where the victim and wife used to sell vegetables, a group of 4 boys, 3 Africans and 1 coloured approached them and told them to go back home and leave their country. They then started beating them, injuring the wife in the process; they also took his phone and R500. The victim reports that he called UNHCR as he has a file with them, for any assistance but was sent to Future Family for assistance, but unfortunately the assistance was not received. After the incident, the victim and wife were rushed to South Rand hospital and were refused treatment because they did not have R400 to pay. The hospital said that they no longer treat refugees and asylum seekers for free; from there they went to South Hills Police station but there again they were told pay bribe otherwise they will not open a case for them.
records.who_attacked: A Congolese refugee and wife as well as the vegetables they were selling
records.response: Yes, the Police and Metro Police were on the scene but they allegedly refused to open a case for the victims

records.name: Operation Dudula conduct house-to-house searches for foreigners in Turffontein, Johannesburg.
records.description: On Monday, 17th January 2022, some locals under the banner of "operation Dudula" were seen harassing and evicting people identified as foreign nationals from houses and trading sites in Turffontein township in Johannesburg where they were selling various goods. Some of the evicted people were seen being bundled into police trucks with members of operation Dudula promising to set them alight should they attempt to come back to their rented dwellings and the vegetable market. In some videos some foreign nationals were seen on rooftops attempting to flee from mobs targeting them.
records.who_attacked: Foreign nationals who were living in Turffontein, mostly Zimbabweans
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: The Police was there and only worked to load victims in police vans

records.name: ATDF members attack Seswati speaking truck driver, accusing him of being a foreign driver
records.description: On 25th January, a truck driver from Parson's trucking company based in Emalahleni reported to us and said that he is in hiding somewhere around Richards Bay after being forced to leave his truck by people identifying themselves as ATDF members. They accused him of being foreigner from eSwathini and said his South African ID is either fake or obtained fraudulently. They occupied the truck and said that he and the truck will not offload the load at Richards Bay harbour. As soon as we received the information, we immediately called Richards Bay Police station and police officers were sent on the scene, and only after their intervention did the victim managed to leave and went to offload his consignment.
records.duration: More than 4 hours, when the police intervened
records.response: Yes, we called Richards Bay Police station and they sent 2 police vans there.

records.name: Foreign nationals ordered to close shop, pack up and leave
records.description:
As part of the clean-up campaign called Operation Dudula, operators of the foreign-owned Cash & Cash wholesalers at Nandi Nice Square in Vosloorus were on January 29 commanded to close their business and vacate the area. Operation Dudula is a campaign spearheaded by local civil organisations and individuals and is aimed at removing foreign nationals who operate businesses in the townships and surrounding suburbs. The launch of the operation in Vosloorus was also attended by people dressed in regalia of the Umkhonto weSizwe Military Veterans Association (MKVA). The deputy chairperson of the operation Dan Radebe said they told the store owners to close the store because there were reports of non-compliance with the norms and prescribed health standards.
Radebe said it’s also a concern for the country because these foreign nationals are in the country illegally. The deputy chairperson of the operation Dan Radebe said they told the store owners to close the store because there were reports of non-compliance with the norms and prescribed health standards. Radebe said it’s also a concern for the country because these foreign nationals are in the country illegally. MKVA and Dudula members’ effort to shut down the Vosloorus Cash and Carry, proved futile. Vosloorus SAPS members and EMPD officers monitored the situation. The co-owner of the wholesaler, said he is disappointed and hurt because the Dudula members just want to dictate to them to close their business without genuine facts. “We have been operating this business legally for 17 years, and we are in the country legally.“If they pick up something wrong in our store they must come and notify us, instead of commanding that we must close the business. The Vosloorus Police Station acting commander, Paul Mathebula, said the members of the MKVA and Dudula operation cannot just do as they please and disregard the laws of the country. “The owners must carry on operating their stores. What we are witnessing here is unlawful. As law enforcers, we wouldn’t allow this business to operate if it was contravening the law.” Source: https://boksburgadvertiser.co.za/435346/foreign-nationals-ordered-to-close-shop-pack-up-and-leave/
records.response: Police monitored the area

records.name: Street barbers evicted and ordered to pay protection fees in Empangeni
records.description: On Tuesday 1st of February 2022, a group of about 20 guys who belong to a group known as "SKEPE" stormed all foreign-owned barber tents in Empangeni Central and closed them off, accusing them of selling drugs and taking their business opportunities. This happened on Commercial Road, opposite Spar; after that they told those foreign barbers not to attempt reopening their tents until their leaders speak to them and this was done. In the meeting with the leaders of affected migrants, they were told that whoever wants to reopen must first pay R500 each upfront and commit to pay an additional R100 every Friday. The leaders then proceeded to the police station to ask for assistance and were chased away and told to speak to the municipality; that's when they went to the Empangeni Magistrate Court to apply for a protection order, which they received the following day and reopened their businesses. It is rumored that the perpetrators are planning to go back therein full force on Friday; so people are living in fear as we speak.
records.response: They received a protection order from Empangeni Magistrate Court, but before that the police was contacted and refused to help.

records.name: DA Councilor stop Hi-tech from working in Gqeberha accusing them of employing foreign nationals
records.description: On Thursday 17/02/2022, DA Councilor told workers from Hi-Tech to stop digging trenches between Quick and Theale Str. in Gqeberha accusing the company of hiring only foreign nationals. This company was awarded a contract by Yonke installation, to dig trenches for the installation of Wi-Fi network in Gqeberha. It appears that on the day, most employees who were on the field digging trenches were non-nationals from Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Malawi. When confronted about not employing citizens, the company responded that the job required qualified people who were not available locally, but after verification, it appears that they were paying those non-nationals about 60% of what South Africans doing the same job would be paid. The employees of Hi-Tech we sent home because they are non-nationals .
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: No because the employees just packed theyr goods and left

records.name: The Police accompany members of operation Dudula to attack migrants housed at Tsietsi Mashinini Centre
records.description: On 6 February, a mob of hundreds masquerading under the flag of Operation Dudula, holding traditional Zulu leather whips and escorted by police attacked Tsietsi Mashinini Centre, claiming “Enough is enough. Put South Africans first.”, It is estimated that the community centre housed more than 100 migrant families living side by side with their South African counterparts. The group claimed that foreign nationals are stealing jobs that belong to South Africans and therefore they must leave the country and go back home.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: Not that we are aware of. The police said they are monitoring all activities of operation Dudula.

records.name: A Nigerian hairdresser beaten to death by the so-called Galeshewe crime fighting group
records.description: It was on 12/02/2022 afternoon when a group calling itself "Galeshewe crime fighting group" went to a barber shop run by a Nigerian in Kimberley and accused him and his close friend of stealing a laptop. It was later discovered that he did not steal the laptop but bought a stolen laptop rather and had already sold it also. That is when the group took the barber and his close friend to Galeshewe township to meet the owner of the laptop and offered to buy him a new one by the end of the following week. Even though she agreed to the deal, they still proceeded to beating them up with sticks and other objects while the criminal who stole the laptop and sold it to the victim was left unharmed. The police were called in and found the victim already unconscious; he was rushed to Robert Sobukwe Hospital where he was declared brain damaged and moved to Intensive Care Unite from where he died 2 days later. The police opened an attempted murder case but so far no arrest has been made.
records.who_attacked: A Nigerian hairdresser and his close friend
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: The Police was called on the crime scene but it was too little too late. They, however opened a case of murder even though no one is yet arrested.

records.name: 2 Nigerians killed in Vereeniging, near Johannesburg allegedly over drug dealing
records.description:
On 12/02/2022, Vereeniging, eMfuleni municipality near Johannesburg came to a standstill as taxi drivers closed Voortrekker and allegedly took matters in their own hands, by attacking foreign nationals believed to be drug dealers and beating two of them to death”.

When police officers arrived at the Vereeniging taxi rank, they found a Nigerian citizen dead and two males badly assaulted. The two were transferred to Kopanong hospital where one of them later passed on. The police were investigating the case and urged anyone with relevant information to contact them.
records.response: The police arrived at the Vereeniging taxi rank and found a Nigerian citizen dead and two others badly injured. The two were transferred to Kopanong hospital where one of them later passed on

records.name: Operation "Clean up" targets migrants' businesses in Durban Central
records.description: On Valentine's day, Monday 14th February 2022 around 13h00, more than 8 Metro police vehicles raided shops run by migrants who are predominantly refugees and asylum seekers from Central Africa in Park street, St. Georges street and McCarthy street. They were allegedly looking for stolen goods and illegal immigrants but ended up taking money, food, cellphones and turning things upside down in these shops. They did not enter any South African run shops even those who employ migrants. The metro police arrested 3 migrants who were accused of being in South Africa illegally even though they had left their documents at home which was not far from their businesses. The 3 migrants begged the Metro police to accompany them to their flats so that they can show them their documents but they were not interested. The 3 migrants were subsequently released from police cells when relatives brought their documents.
records.duration: About 1 hour at the reported area
records.response: No response since the raids were held by Metro Police.

records.name: Migrant informal traders at Soldiers way flea market told to pack and go
records.description: On Sunday 27th February, members of MKMVA who regularly collect what they call "protection fees" from migrant informal traders, told them to pack their goods and go back to their home countries and trade from there. They were told not to wait for their leaders to come because they may lose their goods altogether. Knowing how violent are these people, migrant traders taken by panic fled the market and some of them left their goods behind, which were subsequently looted by unknown people.
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: Metro police came late and were only busy checking trading permits. Xenowatch and RSS also sent someone there to verify what is going on and report about it.

records.name: Trucks turned away near Richards Bay Harbour by ATDF members
records.description: A group of about 30 ATDF ASA members pulled over dozens of truck drivers in Richards Bay in northern KwaZulu-Natal as police and soldiers monitored the situation. Drivers were ordered to pull over or turn around at an informal truck stop along the John Ross Highway while attempting to enter the harbour. About 30 members of the All Truck Drivers Forum and Allied SA (ATDF ASA) pulled over dozens of truck drivers in Richards Bay, northern KZN, on Monday as their national shutdown over wage increases and ongoing dispute over the hiring of foreign nationals continued. @TimesLIVE pic.twitter.com/M5CVKzYvRp. ATDF ASA organiser said they couldn't count how many trucks they pulled over. In Johannesburg, trucks blocked the M2 and M1 south as well as the N3/N12 (Geldenhuys Interchange). The industry faced a crisis caused, to some extent, by various departments, including home affairs.  “We no longer want foreigners in the bargaining council,” said the ATDF General Secretary. He said “they should just kick them out.” Truck driving “does not require a specialized skill” and SA had an oversupply of drivers.  There was a strong police and army presence on the N2. According to the media liaison for Positive Freight Solutions (PFS), a non-governmental organisation representing the interests of private logistics companies in SA, ATDF ASA “ignored opportunities” presented to them by PFS. SAPS KZN spokesperson Lt-Col Nqobile Gwala said: “We can confirm that this morning Richards Bay police arrested five suspects aged between 30 and 56 who were intimidating truck drivers”; they will appear in court soon.
records.duration: The whole morning, more than 4 hours
records.response: Yes, the police was monitoring the situation and said they have arrested 5 perpetrators

records.name: A Somali shoopkeeper robbed at gunpoint in Kwazakhele/Gqeberha
records.description: On 03/03/2022 a group of 5 criminals who only target Somali shops in the area of Kwazkhele/Gqeberha entered Tonjeni Enterprises Supermarket, in Kwazakhele/Gqeberha and wanted to buy airtime. The shopkeeper bowed down to get the airtime but when he got up, he looked into a barrel of a firearm which was pointed at him. They requested protection fees, which he did not have but instead out of shock he raised his hands, saying that the money is with the shop owner. After that they instructed him to open the door leading into the shop, which he did and after entering the shop, they beat him up with the firearm over his head; he fell down and lost consciousness. That is when they helped themselves with airtime, money, his cellphone and left, telling people outside the shop to help themselves which they did in a looting kind of way.
records.who_attacked: A Somali owned shop and its shopkeeper
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: The crime scene was visited by CPF where the community informed them that they are scared to get involved because information goes back to criminals.

records.name: Criminals target Somali shop owners and operators in Gqeberha
records.description: On 05/03/2022 Lucky Spaza Shop based in Ikamvelihle, Gqeberha, was visited by 4 criminals who were known to the shop owners of Motherwell and Ikamvelihle. The criminals asked the shopkeepers for protection fees and when they were not able to give them the money because they are not owners of the shop, they were assaulted and cigarettes, money, airtime and cell phones were taken from them in an effort to stop them from contacting the police. The shopkeepers never opened any cases out of fear of their lives.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: The Councillor together with the Swartkops SAPS visited the crime scene

records.name: Another Somali shopkeeper is beaten up and robbed for non payment of protection fees
records.description: On 05/03/2022 in Motherwell, a shopkeeper was approached by 5 criminals who bought airtime; when the shopkeeper gave them the airtime, one of the assailants grabbed his hand and requested protection fees which he could not provide at the time. He was subsequently asked to open the door leading to the shop which he did out of fear. Three of the attackers entered the shop and the other two stood at the door observing the situation outside. They took money, airtime, cigarettes, cellphone, etc.  Once outside the shop, they told people to enter the shop and serve themselves with whatever they want, which they indeed did. Out of fear the shopkeeper said nothing and allowed the people to do as they wish. After everyone was gone, he went to his neighbor to to ask for cell phone to call his brother for assistance. The shopkeeper  was beaten by criminals with firearm on their way out and left bleeding.
records.who_attacked: A Somali shop keeper in Motherwell, Gqeberha, Eastern Cape
records.response: Not really, meetings are planned but there is very little police presence in the area, which create an enabling environment for criminals

records.name: Various armed criminal groups in New Brighton force Somali shopkeepers to pay protection fees or get assaulted and robbed
records.description: On 06/03/2022, in New Brighton, Half Price Supermarket was visited by 6 unknown criminals demanding protection fees but was told by shopkeepers that they don't have any money left at the shop because the shop owner had already taken it. They were beaten by the criminals who entered the shop and helped themselves to money, cigarettes, airtime and some cool drinks and then left. After the criminals were gone, one of the shopkeepers ran to his neighbor and asked for help to contact their boss and other relatives for help.
records.duration: Unclear but not more than 1 hour
records.response: SAPS took long to get to crime scene and criminals had a lot of time to get away.

records.name: Operation Dudula members clashed with migrant street vendors in Alexendra
records.description: Tensions ran high in Alexandra on Monday afternoon as Operation Dudula members clashed with migrant street vendors. The group had been demonstrating against what they say is the employment of migrant workers over South Africans for several months now. Large groups of protestors near the Pan African Mall have been demonstrating, moving from shop to shop shutting down businesses owned by migrants. According to protestor, the call remains the same: they want South Africans to own the shops. Tensions broke out between migrant shop owners and Operation Dudula members earlier on Monday when protestors said they wanted the stalls occupied by the migrant owners to be dominated by South Africans. Police have since arrived on the scene, monitoring the situation, which has since calmed down.https://ewn.co.za/2022/03/07/migrant-shop-owners-clash-with-operation-dudula-protestors-in-alexandra
records.response: Police intervened to calm the situation

records.name: A shopkeeper left alone after being coerced to pay protection fees to criminals
records.description: On  07/03/2022 at Day & Night shop in Motherwell/Gqeberha,  3 unknown local guys entered the shop pretending to buy something from the shop. There were other customers in the shop and as soon as the customers who were inside the shop left, a firearm was produced and pointed at the shopkeeper demanding protection fees. He had no choice but to take whatever he had in the cash box and handed to them in an effort not to get hurt. After receiving the money they left without hurting shopkeeper.
records.who_attacked: A Somali shopkeeper in Motherwell/Nelson Mandela Bay
records.response: No response because the Police was not informed out of fear for their lives.
records.other_text: Message received through a Somali interpreter.

records.name: Pakistan Mthatha-based businessman in Slovo Park's Staff  Kidnapped for a Ransom
records.description: It was on Sunday 6 March around 9am, when these guys came into the store, pulled out guns and took all the staff hostage. Six of his employees were South Africans. The robbers took all the money in the till. Then they demanded the keys to his bakkie. They forced only the two employees who are Pakistani to go with them. About two kilometres away they transferred them to a waiting car. The kidnappers called in the afternoon demanding a ransom of R10-million. They told them that they did not have that money. The matter was reported to the police who advised them not to call when they receive the call from the kidnappers and not to male any settlement without their knowledge. Eventually a settlement amount was reached and paid for the two kidnapped employees.
records.response: Police assisted to negotiate ransom amount.

records.name: What started as an argument between 2 people, a South African and a Malawian end up in attack on all non-nationals
records.description: On 15/03/2022, a Malawian who was trading at the corner of Church street and Retief street, was visited by a taxi driver who sold him a cellphone. A few days later, the taxi driver came back to collect his cellphone and was prepared to the trader his money back. Unfortunately the trader claimed that he no longer had the cellphone as had already sold it. The taxi driver then called his armed friends and relatives to come and help him. Upon arrival, one of the friends threatened the trader and pointed a firearm towards him, threatening to kill him if the cellphone is not found. More Malawians joined the argument and managed to disarm the person with the firearm and he subsequently fled the scene. This led to more taxi drivers, conductors and other opportunists joining the argument with the aim of recovering the firearm. The group started attacking not only Malawians but all foreign nationals who were trading. About three non-nationals got shot and were rushed to hospital. The violence worsened and spread to other parts of the CBD and was characterized by confiscation and looting of goods belonging to foreign nationals, burning of tires and some of the goods confiscated. People were assaulted around the city using firearms and traditional weapons while singing revolutionary songs that were calling for others to join and for all foreign nationals to leave the city and the country. The CBD was inaccessible due to barricades that were erected and the huge smoke that engulfed as a result of burning tires. Some looted goods belonged to foreign nationals who were then ordered to not trade until further notice. Later on the police intervened which helped to prevent the xenophobic violence from spreading further. The following day the situation returned back to normal.
records.who_attacked: Foreign national informal traders in general and Malawians in particular
records.response: Yes, the police intervened, which helped to contain the violence

records.name: Operation Fiela take the law into their own hands and and attack migrants in Kimberley on Human Rights Day
records.description: On Human Rights Day, a group of locals calling themselves "operation fiela" have raided foreign-owned businesses in Kimberley saying they are targeting Nigerians and other foreigners who are involved in drug dealing and those who are in the country without proper documents. They said they were destroying the drugs and forcing apprehended drug dealers to go back to their home countries. However, after verification, it appears that all foreign nationals, with and without documents were victimised on the day and they said their operation will continue until they have rooted out the city of undocumented migrants and drug dealers. The police was present and monitored the situation, ensuring that no looting took place and no one was injured in the process; however they did not attempt to stop or prevent this act of people taking the law into their own hands.
records.who_attacked: Migrant traders in general and mostly Nigerians
records.response: The police was present and monitored the situation but they did not stop them to do what they were doing.

records.name: Shop keeper shot for not paying protection fees
records.description: On 03/03/2022, 5 criminals targeting foreign shops entered Ahlan Wasahlan Cash & Carry in KwaZakhele and demanded protection fees from the shop keeper. When he replied that he did not have the money but that the shop owner should know about those issues, he was shot at as a message to show how serious they are with regards to protection fees and instructions. After the shooting they left in a hurry not to be caught by community members. As soon as the shop owner was informed about the incident, he rushed to the scene to take the injured to Hospital.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: The police is still investigating the matter, no arrests made so far.

records.name: A Somali shopkeeper is robbed at gunpoint for resisting to pay protection fees
records.description: Whilst delivering stock to shops at Joe Slovo on 4th March 2022, a shop owner was approached by 6 unknown males who pointed a firearm at him for refusing to pay protection fees. They then took all the money that he collected from his shop as well as his cell phone. He was then loaded into the back of his delivery truck and dropped him off in an area unknown to him. He ran to the nearest place which he could see and asked for help to contact his brothers to fetch him from where he was. On their arrival they took him to Korsten to discuss the incident and decided not to open a criminal case out of fear for their lives .
records.who_attacked: A Somali shop owner in Joe Slovo, Gqeberha, Eastern Cape
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: Robbery, resistance to pay protection fees
records.other_text: The message was received from KwaDesi Police Station

records.name: More than thousand foreign nationals attacked and displaced and their homes destroyed in a Bredasdorp township
records.description: More than 1,000 men, women and children from Zimbabwe and Malawi have sought refuge at municipal facilities and a local mosque after they were targeted in xenophobic and afrophobic violence. Last week, residents embarked on a service delivery protest but the demonstration turned ugly when some individuals broke away and targeted homes and spaza shops owned by migrants. A community leader who's asked to remain anonymous has described the situation facing scores of foreign nationals in the Overberg town of Bredasdorp as disastrous. He said the Glaskasteel Community Hall was so full that some individuals had been forced to sleep on the grass outside the building. More than 100 people have also spent the past few nights crammed into the local mosque where they've been sleeping on a mat.https://ewn.co.za/2022/03/30/migrants-living-in-zwelitsha-scared-to-go-home-after-protests-activist
records.response: Police has responded and is patrolling the area but so far no one has been arrested

records.name: Foreign national's stall looted by protestors
records.description: A foreign shop owners stall was looted on the 26th of March 2022 during a protest march. The march was to hand over a memorandum at the Police Station in Buitenkant Street. After the memorandum was handed over to the Police, a group came in their numbers pretending to buy goods from the foreign owner but instead looted his stall. The foreign national was unable to stop what was happening  as he was outnumbered by the crowd. He called to the policemen who were on the street but they failed to assist and instead watched the looting take place.  Once the looters left, the police approached him and said that he should open a case. Case number 1132/3/22 - was opened but no arrests were made. 70% of his stock was stolen and his stall was damaged.
records.response: Police did not offer immediate assistance. They watched as his stall was looted.

records.name: Community of Kromhoek/Umzimkhulu mobilised to attack a Zimbabwean national
records.description: A South African woman lives with her Zimbabwean husband on their family farm in Kroemhoek location/Umzimkhulu. It is a rural area run by a traditional leader commonly known as headman and this family moved there in 2017 where they run a spaza shop and do small scale farming. Since some locals and the headman learnt that she is married to a foreigner, they want them out of the area and are using all sorts of hate speech, sending criminals to break in and rob their Spaza shop, to that effect. They have reported the matter several times to the police but so far no serious action has been taken. The last time they did that was on Sunday 27th March 2022 when they went to her aunty and told her to kick out this family from the area, not knowing that they are the rightful owners of that place.
records.who_attacked: A Zimbabwean man married to a South African woman
records.duration: It has been going on for more than 4 years. but getting more intense lately. This last incident lasted for more than 2 hours.
records.response: For the last incident no but in the past, the matter has been reported to SAPS and cases opened but no progress on that side. The victim advised to apply for protection order and file for defamation.

records.name: Four refugee owned shops are looted in Kwadabeka township/Durban on on the day of the failed launch of operation Dudula in Durban.
records.description:
Late in the afternoon of the 27 March 2022, groups of people stormed spaza shops in Kwadabeka and Clermont, and tried to gain access. In some cases they gained easy access but in one case, they had to threaten the shopkeeper with firearm to force him to open his shop.  After shops were opened, they called other people to come and serve themselves while the shopkeepers were looking helplessly. Before the police responded, private security came first and shot in the air to disperse looters. It is believed that some of the looters sustained injuries. When the police came, 2 shops were already completed emptied but they managed to disperse the crowd but did not take a statement from shopkeepers.

A shopkeeper of one of the looted spaza shops said that all shops in the area were looted during the July unrest and were still trying to get back on their feet and pay back loaned money to restart when this happens. Another one said that he knew about the botched plan to launch Operation Dudula in the Durban and the warning to them not to trade on the day but he thought this applied only to shops in city centre and therefore would not affect them.
records.who_attacked: 4 spaza shop operated by Ethiopian refugees and asylum seekers in Clermont and Kwadabeka
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: Yes, private security and police responded but at that time 2 shops were already completely looted.

records.name: An Organiser of Operation Dudula based in Durban is sentenced for inciting Xenophobic violence
records.description: In March 2022, a voice message went viral throughout Kwazulu Natal, threatening to attack all migrants leaving Durban. The audio, which was intended for Operation Dudula members but was widely distributed, including among the targeted migrant community, warned fellow members that "thunder and storm" would be heard in the Durban CBD. The audio eventually made its way to the police, who tracked the culprit down and summoned him, at which point he confirmed that he was the one who sent out the audio via his cellphone. This audio elicited a response from the eThekwini Mayor, who mobilised informal traders against Operation Dudula. It was also in response to this mobilisation that the Kwazulu Natal social cohesion consortium was launched in Durban in the same month. As a result, the launch of Operation Dudula in Durban did not cause any attacks on foreign-owned businesses, and they were not able to mobilise meaningfully in Durban. However, xenophobic attacks were subsequently recorded in Pietermaritzburg, where Operation Dudula violently evicted migrant informal traders of various nationalities, as well as other businesses, from their trading sites in the CBD. As a result, on August 30, 2023, the Durban regional court convicted this Operation Dudula organiser of violating Section 14 of the Cybercrime Act of 2020 by inciting violence after disseminating a WhatsApp voice note that sparked xenophobic attacks. He was sentenced to a fine of R10.000 or three years, half suspended for five years.
records.who_attacked: Migrant informal traders and businesses, particularly in Pietermaritzburg
records.duration: The impact of the audio message on the lives of migrants lasted for many months, partly because the arrest of the culprit was not reported in the media.
records.response: Yes, the sender of the audio was subsequently convicted and sentenced.

records.name: The South African driver's license of a Malawian driver confiscated by elements of ATDF
records.description: On Friday 1 April 2022 around 16h30, a group of 10 people who were in 3 different vehicles stopped a truck that has just come from delivering fresh produces to customers. They asked the driver for his driver's license, ID and/or passport and any other document that allows him to be in the country. The driver gave them all those documents which they took away. After a while, they returned other documents but kept his driver's license. He then proceeded to Umbilo police station to open a case after consulting his employer, but was only allowed to write an affidavit for reasons that he does not comprehend.
records.response: The incident was reported to Umbilo Police Station by the victim and an affidavit was issued to that effect

records.name: Persons Wearing Operation Dudula and OPESA T-shirts Attack and Kidnap an Asylum Seeker in Durban
records.description: An asylum seeker from DRC is a supervisor at a bloc of flats on Che Guevara Rd/Durban. He had a tenant that had to vacate the flat because she was unable to pay rent for two consecutive months but refused to leave. She threatened him, called him names and told him she will show him. On 1st April around 17h30, two vans full of fifty people wearing T-shirts written "Operation Dudula" and "OPESA"  stormed the flat of the victim while others were waiting outside and in the two vans. The assailants beat the victim, took his money (R63,000), his two laptops, shoes and clothes and then took him away. He was only saved by the police who intercepted the perpetrators after receiving a call from the victim's sister. Since then he is living in hiding waiting for the situation to improve or at least until the problematic tenant is fully evicted from the flat.
records.who_attacked: An asylum seeker and his sister
records.duration: More than an hour on the first day but they came back the following day as well.
records.response: The owner of the building and the body corporate responded. The police also responded and rescued the victim from these people who had already abducted him.

records.name: Pakistan man kidnapped and Tortured in Ngcobo, Eastern Cape
records.description:
A Pakistani national was kidnapped at his hardware store in a village 15km from Ngcobo on 3 April. Three men turned up at his store in the afternoon, saying they wanted to buy 1,000 bricks. While he was counting the bricks, one of the men pulled a gun and ordered him to lie down. They blindfolded him and started ransacking the shop for money. When they were not happy with what they managed to get, they started demanding that the shop owner take them to where he kept all his money. When he told them that was all the money he had, they took him into the car and drove off to the place where they kept him. 

The kidnappers held the shop owner for eight days where he was tortured. A gun was pointed to his head, he was beaten up with guns, a machete, sjambok and beer bottles. At some point, they poured boiling water and melted plastic bags on him. All this was captured on video which was sent to other Pakistan nationals that are close to the victim, so that they can find money to pay the ransom. Sometimes, the kidnappers would make phone calls and put the phone on speaker while beating the victim. He was starved and provided with slices of bread once a day. 

The kidnappers initially demanded R5-million. The victim's friends went to report the issue to the police at Ngcobo. The police only assisted in advising on how to negotiate. In the end an amount was agreed upon and paid which was a tiny fraction of what was being asked. - Source: GroundUp
records.response: Police only advised friends of the kidnapped shop owner on negotiating the ransom money

records.name: Asylum Seeker forced to pay for hospital fee to access healthcare services
records.description: On 5th April 2022, an asylum seeker from Burundi took his pregnant wife to the Tshwane clinic in Pretoria CBD. When they arrived there, they were greeted by insults from nurses who said they do not want refugees at their health facilities anymore because they make many children which burdens the health system in this country that is already struggling with its own problems. When the husband of of the pregnant wife insisted, he was told to pay R10,000 like any other foreigner because the rules have already changed. He asked them to contact UNHCR as they were asylum seekers and unemployed, surviving only on temporary jobs. The nurses  subsequently accepted to see his wife but refused to give her medication. Instead, they were given prescription to buy medicines at a private pharmacy and a referral letter to go to Tshwane District Hospital. When they arrived at the hospital, they were told to pay R220 for consultation fees, which they did not have.

records.name: A Zimbabwean National burnt to death by in Mob in Diepsloot
records.description:
One person has been killed in an apparent mob attack in Diepsloot, north of Johannesburg. Police have confirmed that one person died from injuries and more than 20 people were arrested overnight.Eyewitnesses told police that a small group of people went to the deceased's home and then attacked him with stones and apparently set him alight. By the time officers arrived on the scene, it was too late to save the man. Residents have been venting their anger and frustration over the lack of policing in Diepsloot and the large number of illegal migrants living there. https://ewn.co.za/0001/01/01/1-person-killed-in-alleged-mob-justice-attack-in-diepsloot

Since the murder of the Zimbabwean national, seven of the attackers have
been detained and are currently awaiting trial, which will begin on the
24th of August. The attackers are currently out on R3.000 bail each. The
wife of the deceased is an important witness in the case, but she fled
to Zimbabwe and she won't go back to South Africa because she doesn't
have a residence visa, which makes her safety uncertain. She is a
crucial witness in the state's case, so failing to testify runs the risk
of preventing her husband from receiving justice.
records.response: Zimbabwean consulate, police, Zimbabwe diaspora community

records.name: Two foreign nationals killed in Mozombane village in the Mahwelereng policing precinct.
records.description:
Two individuals, 38 and 41, have been detained in connection with the murder of two foreign nationals in Mozombane village, Mahwelereng policing precinct. At around 10.30 p.m., community members attacked the victims who they accused of stealing copper cables from the vicinity. The assaults on the victims were serious, and they eventually died from their injuries.

Source: https://www.iol.co.za/news/mob-justice-2-held-in-limpopo-after-foreign-nationals-are-beaten-to-death-e043059e-b509-4d8a-897a-3c740e7a43fc
records.response: Police

records.name: Brutalisation of a Club owner who refused to pay Protection fees.
records.description: An owner of a Night Club in the CBD of Cape Town was badly beaten for refusing to pay extortion fees in mid-April 2022 by a gang of five men. The gangsters stormed into his night club and demanded payment for protection fees. The night club owner informed the perpetrators that business was very slow and so he could not pay them. The perpetrators became aggressive and started beating him. When the the Club owners friend came to check what was going on, the situation escalated as the gangsters became wild. They took out their guns and used the bottom of the guns to hit the owner and his friend on their upper bodies, especially on the head. The victims were seriously wounded and disfigured as a result. The gang members stole the victims' phones, took drinks from the club and left. The victims were rushed to the hospital for treatment. The victim confirms that it was a terrible situation as he nearly died.
records.response: The incident was not reported, and the victim he is not willing to do so.

records.name: Murder of a Migrant Informal Trader
records.description: An informal trader of Zimbabwean nationality was attacked by a group of people at Soldiers Way Flea Market. The victim was beaten with Knobkerries, had stones thrown at him and then stabbed to death. The instigators then took what ever they wanted from the victim's stall and fled before the police arrived. The incident took place at 5.30 am and the deceased body was collected by the police to the mortuary at 8 am.
records.response: Police were called but arrived very late.

records.name: A refugee woman shot at Victoria Bus Rank in Central Durban
records.description: On Tuesday 26th April 2022, a woman refugee was selling her fat cooks when she was approached by a gentleman who said he wanted to buy all her fat cooks. When asked, he said he was not prepared to pay anything because this lady was taking business opportunities to the detriment of South African women. She then packed her goods, left that site and moved to another area within the same bus rank. Little after 18h00, she heard a gunshot and fell down, luckily the bullet hit her buttocks and came out without touching any bone nor sensitive nervous system. She spent 2 weeks in hospital but is out now.
records.response: The police was called but arrived at the scene very late and found the victim lying in a pool of blood

records.name: Foreign national shop robbed and his life threatened because he is a non-national
records.description: A foreign national's shop was broken into in the afternoon of the 21st of April 2022 around 3pm. He had left to go pick his kids from school. His goods were all looted. He called the Police that afternoon and they never came. So he closed his shop and went home. His CCTV camera captured the incident. The following morning he went to the Police station and was told to open a case against the perpetrators. He also showed the CCTV footages to the Police. The robbers were arrested however, the shop owner has been receiving life threatening calls against his life and that of his family. The threats are that he should withdraw the case against the robbers so that the perpetrators can be released or his family will be killed since they know he is a foreign national. His wife pleaded with him to withdraw the case. He obliged and  and the guys were released. The victim has moved his family to a different neighborhood and will soon move his shop.

records.name: Bangladeshi spaza shopkeeper kidnapped in Delft
records.description:
A 36-year-old Bangladeshi spaza shopkeeper was kidnapped three months ago in Delft. The kidnappers burnt plastic on his back, inner thighs and stomach. His big toenail was beaten off with a hammer. The victim is still receiving treatment and will go back to Bangladesh once he is fully recovered. He was released after his family paid R120,000 ransom. the victim was too scared to talk to the media.
https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2022-06-29-western-cape-extortions-and-brutal-kidnappings-prompt-foreign-nationals-to-pack-up-and-go-home/
records.response: A ransom was paid in exchange of the victims release

records.name: Asylum Seeker Unlawfully Arrested by the Police in Newcastle
records.description: On Sunday the 1st of May 2022, an asylum seeker carrying a TV set was stopped by the police around 9 am. The police inquired whether he had proof that the TV was his and not stolen. Upon producing the box and receipt, the Police asked him to produce his asylum documents. He was not in possession of the documents. The asylum seeker was taken to the Police station where his relatives where informed about his arrest. When two of his relatives arrived  at the Police station, they were asked to also produce their documents. The family members produced documents that had been renewed online but where informed that they were fake because the documents had no stamp or signature. The community leader was called but the Captain did not want to hear from him. Refugee Social Services tried to intervene but was not successful. Lawyers for Human Rights was also contacted but there could not do much until a court appearance which is scheduled for the 3rd of May.
records.duration: Victims still detained since the 1st of May since it is a long holiday.
records.response: Xenowatch Research Assistant, wrote to the station commander to explain that the documents produced are legitimate but he could not reach him. The RA also informed Lawyers for Human Rights but unfortunately nothing can be done untiled the detained asylum seekers appear in court.

records.name: Shops Belonging to Chinese Shop Owners Attacked in Khayelitsha after Operation Dudula Launch March
records.description: The launching of Operation Dudula took place on the morning of the 14th of May 2022 in Cape Town. The SAPS and Metro Police presence helped control control things. The march was peaceful although there were reports of  vulgar language used when the marchers passed businesses owned by foreigners. Later in the afternoon, some Operation Dudula members are alleged to have stormed Khayelitsha Mall where Chinese shops were mostly attacked (R5 Store, Best Fashion Store, Beautiful Fashion Store, Electronix Shop and Mojo Men's Clothing and Footwear). During the attacks, two security officers were injured while trying to stop the attacks. In the process, Chinese shop owners pressed the panic buttons and armed response came. This helped to calm the situation. Police never came. The mall manager had a brief meeting with the Operation Dudula members to address their unlawful behaviour. In the end they agreed to have a meeting on Monday 16th May 2022 ,but it never took place.
records.response: Alarmed Response arrived to help control the situation

records.name: A street barber stabbed 12 times in Isipingo but survived
records.description: On Sunday 15th May 2022, a street barber was approached by a group of young black South Africans who started threatening him before taking out knives and stabbing him at the back and around the neck 12 times. They allegedly accused him of selling drugs yet this is a known street barber for many years. He was saved by a group of other refugees who managed to grab him back from the group and run with him to the nearby Police Station. He was then rushed to Prince Mshiyeni Hospital where he is admitted.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: The police took affidavit from the other people who rushed him to police station.

records.name: Protests Over Water in Musina Results in Looting of Shops
records.description: Protests as a result of service delivery issues, with regards to water and sanitation, electricity, housing that began last week Monday have resulted in looting of shops belonging to non-nationals as some community members took advantage of the situation. Authorities are trying to contain the situation. Information received by Xenowatch is that, about four shops that belong to Ethiopians were looted around musina in a place called Nancefield.

records.name: Gang that targets foreign nationals robs and attacks Congolese men
records.description: This incident happened on Monday 16th of May 2022 at about 6pm. A  gang of colored guys attacked Congolese nationals and took their bags and possessions. The victims ran for safety towards Parow market where many foreigners trade and live. The gang broke into one car and stole goods inside. Another male was hit on the head with a brick and landed in hospital were he received 10 stitches on his head. After further investigations, it was determined that this gang targets foreign nationals, robs them of their possessions and also insults them.  In the area of business, where most shops are owned by foreign nationals, most of them have been victims of attacks and insults.
records.response: No response. Incident was not reported to the police

records.name: A number of foreign nationals and Outsiders forcibly removed from Morokweng in North West after accusations of selling drugs by local residents
records.description: Three men accused of  peddling drugs were beaten and burnt today in their place of residents by local community members. In the aftermath, foreign nationals and anyone considered an outsider were chased away from the community by locals.
records.who_attacked: Three men accused of peddling drugs
records.response: Police alleged to be monitoring the area

records.name: A Zimbabwean Truck Driver Assaulted by Alleged Members of ATDF In Richards Bay
records.description: On Friday morning around 11 am, a Zimbabwean truck driver from Johannesburg was stopped by a group of people claiming to be members of ATDF. They asked for his drivers license and passport. As soon as he produced the documents, the group started beating him with sjamboks. After beating him, they took his drivers license but gave him his passport back and warned him never to drive in South Africa again.
records.who_attacked: A Zimbabwean truck driver who works for Van Vonk Trucking Company.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: Unknown

records.name: Foreign nationals in Alexandra harassed and attacked by alleged Dudula Movement
records.description: A group of people allegedly part of the Dudula Movement targeted and harassed foreign nationals in Alexandra. The group assaulted and went house to house confiscating staff they could find in houses. It is alleged that they took laptops, fridges and TV's belonging to the victims. They also took advantage of the situation and also targeted South African locals in the area, especially those who are renting out their property to foreign nationals. The South African property owners were warned not to rent their property to foreigners. One person is reported to have been injured and hit by a harmer on the head. Foreign nationals affected had to leave the area. Some where put up in shelters while others went to stay with relatives.
records.response: Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia members were on the ground to assist the victims

records.name: Hankey residents force seasonal workers out of town in violent clashes
records.description:
About 400 seasonal workers were forcefully evicted from their homes in Hankey in the Eastern Cape by local residents. This followed violent clashes at an informal settlement in the town last week. Police say two South Africans and one Lesotho national were killed as a result of the violence. Several shacks at the Mountainview informal settlement, home to many migrant workers, were also burnt down. According to police, the clashes between local residents and migrant workers mostly from Lesotho was sparked by the murders of two people from Centerton, another township in Hankey.

Police spokesperson Colonel Priscilla Naidu said that community members from Centerton had marched to an area predominantly occupied by seasonal farm workers from Lesotho. “When this group tried to attack, the seasonal workers from Lesotho retaliated by throwing stones at them. “Centerton residents allege that the foreign nationals are responsible for the deaths of two people. These murders took place during the early hours of [29 May] in Centerton. In both murders, the motive and suspects are unknown.”

Naidu said several shacks were set alight and pelted police vehicles with stones during the protest. She said police escorted Mountainview residents out of the area on 1 June to a neighbouring area for their safety.

Source: https://www.groundup.org.za/article/hankey-residents-force-hundreds-of-season-workers-out-of-town-during-violent-clashes/
records.who_attacked: Foreign nationals and South Africans originating from other provinces
records.response: Police and local municipality

records.name: Two Somali business men shot and killed
records.description: Two Somalis shot and killed by suspected extortionists in Langa.
records.response: Uknown

records.name: A Congolese Permanent Resident woman is attacked by members of Operation Dudula in Pietermaritzburg
records.description: After mourning two of her daughters for 8 weeks and burying one of them on Tuesday the 6th, A single mother decided to go to Home Affairs to sort out documentation issues regarding the death of her daughters. While leaving the office of Home Affairs at around 13h00, she met with members of Operation Dudula who were busy checking documents of migrants and arresting people, in collaboration with SAPS. When they approached her, they asked for her documents so that they could verify whether she was in the country legally. She produced her green ID (for permanent residents) and showed them. When they saw that she had a green ID, they questioned the validity of her ID and said her document was fraudulent. They refused to listen to her plea for verification of her ID with the department of Home Affairs. She found them doing the same with 5 other migrant males from Nigeria and Ethiopia. As soon as they started attacking them, the police took all of them into their vehicle and went with them to a near by Home Affairs office for verification of their documents. After verification, it was confirmed that the documents of all of them were valid. That is when they were released at around 17h00.
records.other_text: The video of the incident first appeared on a WhatsApp group of refugee community leaders that I am part of.

records.name: Two Somali Business Killed in Nomzamo
records.description: Police reported that two victims, aged between 38 and 32, were shot and killed in Nomzamo on Friday evening just hours after Police Minister Bheki revealed that 6 083 people had been murdered in South Africa during the first three months of the year. Police Warrant Officer Joseph Swartbooi said the two others, between the ages of 39 and 33, were taken to hospital. No one had been arrested yet.
records.response: Unknown

records.name: Two Somali business men shot and killed in Lwandle, Strand
records.description: The chairperson of the Community Police Forum in Lwandle, said according to residents three men burst into a shop called Thandabantu on the corner of Michael and Lonja streets, where they opened fire. The Chairperson said although the motive was not known yet, attacks on shops owned by foreigners were largely associated with extortion.
records.response: Unknown

records.name: Xenophobic violence in Limpopo village divides police
records.description: Amid strong allegations of police complicity, the fresh outbreak of xenophobic violence against Zimbabwean foreign nationals in a usually tranquil rural My Darling village in Limpopo has pitted a Hawks captain against an South African Police Service (Saps) station commander, with the local Saps most senior officer supporting villagers. A a group of patrolling villagers – recognised by Maleboho police station commander as having “done a good job in fighting theft in the area” – besieged the homestead of a Hawks Captain, demanding that his traumatised domestic worker return to Zimbabwe. The Hawks Captain who has opened a case of intimidation and trespassing, has relived his employee’s horror when a group of men surrounded the homestead, with some scaling the wall. “Over the past two weekends, a large number of local men, operating like a vigilante group, arrived at my homestead when I was not there, demanding that my worker return to Zimbabwe. “Due to the fact that I have a high wall, the two managed to scale over into my yard during the first incident, telling him he should return to Zimbabwe. “Despite the employee showing them documents from home affairs to prove his legal status in South Africa, they would not listen. “He gave the group leader, the phone to talk to me. The leader told me they did not want Zimbabweans in the area. “We then argued over his legal status, which they would not recognise – threatening that hell would break loose if I failed to comply. They then left my home.” When the group returned to the homestead for the second time the following weekend, The Hawks Captain advised his domestic worker “not to run away because they could kill him”. - Source: https://www.citizen.co.za/news/south-africa/local-news/3116944/xenophobic-violence-in-limpopo-village-divides-police/

records.name: Four shopkeepers murdered in Khayelitsha
records.description: In the latest shooting in Khayelitsha on Tuesday night, gunmen opened fire inside a shop in Site B. Three people died at the scene, and a fourth died in hospital. They were foreign nationals.
records.response: Police attended crime scene

records.name: Operation Dudula Orange Grove illegal eviction letters to foreign-owned businesses.
records.description:
Over the past few weeks, members of Operation Dudula have been issuing illegitimate eviction orders to nearby foreign-owned or operated businesses. They have claimed that the foreigners are to blame for the neighborhood's problems, such as prostitution and drug use. The letters, marked "Attention Non-South African Business Operator," gave the owners seven days to quit their premises. Businesses on Louis Botha Avenue are frequent targets. The business owners were requested to sign the letters. In response , foreign business owners were encouraged to file intimidation cases against Operation Dudula members and the case was opened at the Norwood Police Station. However, the case was dropped as Operation Dudula members apologized and agreed to work in harmony with the Orange Grove Foreign Shop Committee. 
Source: https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2022-06-20-operation-dudula-agrees-to-stop-illegal-eviction-letters-shopkeepers-agree-to-withdraw-charges/


21-July-2022
Nigeria’s Consul-General steps in as Operation Dudula truce falls apart in Orange Grove


Representatives of the Nigerian Orange Grove community went to the Nigerian Consulate General, where they received advice to file criminal charges against Operation Dudula members who had allegedly started an intimidation campaign against them in recent weeks. The issue is that Operation Dudula have not offered an apology as agreed during the initial settlement. 
Source: https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2022-06-28-nigerias-consul-general-steps-in-as-operation-dudula-truce-falls-apart-in-orange-grove/
records.response: Police; local NGO, Nigerian Authories

records.name: Yeoville Market Unrest
records.description:
On the 11th of June 2022 at around 10AM a group of about 20 Operation Dudula members gathered  in front of the Yeoville Market place along Rocky St, Yeoville. Seeing this, traders (largely foreigners) in the market  and surrounding areas quickly mobilized themselves and their numbers were soon over those of Operation Dudula members. A few minutes later, a few of Operation Dudula members  tried to force themselves into the market and a door of the market was damaged during the squabble. Realizing that they were being out numbered by traders, Operation Dudula members retreated and threatened to come back on Monday to take over the market. On this day there was no police intervention. On the 12 June 2022, these threats spread via social media and a letter communicating the planned activities of Operation Dudula around Yeoville (attached below) against foreigners, prompting civil society organization, The Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia (KAAX) ) and the EFF to mobilise for  Monday 13 June 2022 to protect the market and support the traders. The SAPS were also put on high alert regarding these threats from Operation Dudula.

Indeed, on the 12th of June 2022 at around 10AM approximately 50 Operation Dudula members arrived and gathered at the market. This time they sang and used abusive language against traders along Rocky St, just opposite the market. There was a heavy presence of police and ward 67 ANC councillor David Modupi arrived and addressed Operation Dudula crowd promising that the government is in the process of formulating new trading  regulations that will solve trading issues form  01 October 2022. On the other hand the EFF used a sound system to speak against xenophobia and Afrophobia.  No arrests were made.
records.response: Police, local leaders, local CSO.

records.name: Tensions between Locals and Foreign Nationals after reports of multiple deaths in Qhumanco
records.description: Qhumanco village in Cofimvaba experienced tensions between South Africans and foreigners in the area after reports of violence resulting in multiple deaths in the area. Reports had also alluded to allegations of xenophobia which had emanated from criminal conduct and distrust between members of the community with calls for foreign nationals to leave the area. https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2022-06-20-sahrc-to-visit-eastern-cape-village-after-xenophobic-violence/
records.response: SAHRC reported to conduct visit to the area

records.name: Kidnapping of Three Bangladesh Nationals in Samora Machel
records.description:
According to a witness, three Bangladesh nationals were kidnapped in Samora Machel on the 17th of June 2022. The kidnappers initially demanded a ransom of R5-million, but the negotiators managed to bring down the figure to R500,000. The family couldn't afford the amount. Residents of Samora Machel came on aboard and made donations to help pay the amount. The kidnappers came back and threatened the negotiators that if the ransom was not paid within five days they would kill Bangladeshi spaza shopkeepers. Since this threat, spaza shop owners are scared to go back to Samora Machel. Police spokesperson Captain FC van Wyk said, The circumstances of this kidnapping are under investigation. 
https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2022-06-29-western-cape-extortions-and-brutal-kidnappings-prompt-foreign-nationals-to-pack-up-and-go-home/
records.response: Police still investigating the case

records.name: Parts of the Yeoville African Market set on fire
records.description: Parts of the Yeoville African Market was gutted by fire in the early hours of 21 June 2022. The cause of the fire have so far not been ascertained. However, foreign and South African shop owners operating in the market concurred that Operation Dudula vigilantes, who have been threatening migrants around the nation, were responsible for starting the fire. On June 13, members of Operation Dudula marched on Yeoville Market to intimidate business owners and demand that their businesses be handed over to South Africans. One of the victims,  a South Africa lamented the loss caused by the fire and was quoted pointing that " “I’ve been here since the beginning of the market in 1998,.. Two weeks now we have problems with [Operation] Dudula. They came and said they want the market. If they can’t get the market, they will set fire.” Source: https://www.newframe.com/yeoville-market-fire-devastates-traders-livelihoods/?fbclid=IwAR3A-cO88_NTCkb0dfLiQiaVy15Prhg3Ba4bLbhgEKFoD7f8VG6hC3wMe4A
records.who_attacked: Market and shops in the market.
records.response: Police, fire fighters, local NGOs, local leaders,

records.name: Operation Dudula demands that Prasa evict foreign traders operating in and around the Johannesburg Park Station.
records.description: On Tuesday 21 June 2022 members of Operation Dudula marched to Johannesburg Park Station, demanding that Prasa only allow South African vendors to operate there. The group threatened to close the busy station. Source: https://ewn.co.za/2022/06/24/one-voice-of-all-hawkers-association-criticises-attacks-on-foreign-nationals
records.response: No

records.name: Hotel Manager called Kwerekwere by an employee
records.description: The incident took place during the morning shift at the Pepper club hotel in Cape Town on the 23/06/22. The victim is a foreign national from Cameroon and is also a Manager at the Hotel. She has been working there for more than 5 years and has assisted in training new staff members both locals and non-locals. One of her junior staff members called her amakwerekwere and told her she was lucky that she was working in SA. The issue was escalated to HR and the junior employee was informed that her statement was xenophobic and that such behaviour was not allowed in the hotel as it deals with people of all nationalities. The junior employee was given a formal warning for unethical behaviour.
records.who_attacked: Hotel Manager with a foreign background
records.response: HR of the hotel warned employee that discriminatory behaviour will not be tolerated

records.name: A Zimbabwean woman forced to sign an acknowledgement of debt for child's emergency surgery.
records.description:
A Zimbabwean mother who needed emergency surgery for her child was forced to sign an acknowledgement of debt for more than R34,000 in order to receive care. Then, when he required additional surgery  at the same hospital, the request was turned down due to the pending debt. Additionally, it was explained to the woman that she would be required to pay R5,000 for admittance and R50,000 for the second procedure. At this point a  local public interest organisation stepped in. However, in March, when the mother returned with him for a checkup, a nurse addressed patients on the que and informed them that foreign nationals would not receive care if they lacked the funds to pay. The mother, child and other patients left the health facility without assistance.


Source: https://www.groundup.org.za/article/court-application-aims-to-stop-refugees-from-dying-because-they-are-refused-free-health-care/
records.response: Local public interest NGO.

records.name: Pregnant asylum-seeker denied treatment and loses baby.
records.description:
A pregnant asylum seeker was refused medical attention after being injured in a robbery. She was told she needed to pay R2,000 before a "file could be opened" at Steve Biko Academic Hospital. When she went to Charlotte Maxeke Academic Hospital at eight months pregnant, she was told she had to pay R20,000 if she wanted treatment and to give birth at the hospital. Only after a a local public interest organisation  intervened was she given an appointment, but she lost her baby the night before.

Source: https://www.groundup.org.za/article/court-application-aims-to-stop-refugees-from-dying-because-they-are-refused-free-health-care/
records.response: Local public interest NGO.

records.name: Operation Dudula members burn two trucks in a protest against truck drivers.
records.description: In the third week of March, Operation Dudula members engaged in a protest and marched to private companies in Rosslyn Pretoria North Industrial area demanding that employers dismiss all foreign truck drivers and employ South African drivers.  The main targeted company on the day of the march operates in the automotive industry and employs approximately 700 employees. However, only about 15 of these employees are foreigners, some of these are holders of the Zimbabwe Exemption Permit.  Operation Dudula members handed in their memorandum and continued with the march in the area harassingly and threatening truck drivers. In the process two trucks were burnt and the group immediately dispersed as police arrived.
records.who_attacked: Factories, Truck drivers and two trucks set alight .
records.response: Police

records.name: THREE ZIMBABWEANS KILLED IN EDENDALE IN A TARGETED ATTACK ON ZIMBABWEANS
records.description: On Saturday night around 21h00-22h00 an unidentified group of locals attacked two Zimbabwean nationals who were sitting in their car. They shot both of them dead and set the car alight, and then proceeded to the next house where they shot and killed a seven years old girl. They also burnt another house when they realised that its Zimbabwean national occupants were not in. The situation is still very tense as Zimbabwean nationals are threatening to retaliate which may spark a widespread violence against all foreign nationals in Edendale, which is one of few areas that integrated a significant number of migrants in their midst.
records.who_attacked: 2 Males and 1 female, all from Zimbabwe were shot and killed
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: Yes, the police was deployed to the crime scene but so far no arrests yet.

records.name: Foreign nationals fear for their lives following the killing of a suspected thief
records.description:
A 39 year old alleged drug addict was beaten to death between the hours of Sunday night and Monday morning (3-4 July 2022). The victim was revealed to be local resident, who was allegedly killed by 2 foreign nationals who were renting a property in Manyaleni informal settlement in Chatsworth. It is alleged that the victim and 2 other accomplices had broken into the property rented by these foreign nationals and stole some goods. The other accomplices managed to flee but the victim was caught and beaten to death by these foreign nationals. 
Now the residents of Manyaleni informal settlement are baying for the blood of those, who killed the victim saying that what has been done has to be repaid in blood. They are also calling for all foreign nationals to be removed from the area while conveying their dismay at the response time of local police, In that process, one Malawian living in the neighborhood but who is not related to perpetrators, was attacked and shot; his situation is said to be critical at the hospital.
records.who_attacked: All foreign national are being told to leave the area and one Malawian has sustained gunshot wounds and is critical at the hospital
records.response: Yes the police has responded and are monitoring the situation in the area

records.name: Operation Dudula chant xenophobic songs and slogans during their protest march to Diakonia Centre
records.description: It was yesterday Friday, around 12h30 that the small group of members of operation Dudula and their partners of ATDF arrived at the entrance of Diakonia centre. One could read on their placards "Amakwerekwere asiwafuni" meaning foreigners must go, and chanting songs like "Dubula nesibhamu, nali kwerekwere" meaning shoot with a gun and here is a foreigner, which can be interpreted as "here is a foreigner shot him with a gun". After different speeches and reading their memorandum, they handed it over to the leadership f Diakonia Council of Churches.
records.who_attacked: They targeted tenants of Diakonia Centre that work with refugees and migrants such as RSS, LHR and others.
records.duration: It took about 2 hours, they dispersed around 14h30
records.response: There was strong police presence
records.other_text: I was there monitoring the progress of the event. The event was also covered by eNCA and other media houses

records.name: Criminals hijack and kidnap a Burundian Uber Driver
records.description: On Wednesday afternoon around 15h40 a Burundian Uber driver was approached by criminals in Glenwood, a vibrant suburb of Durban, abducted him and put him in the boot of his car before driving off with him. He was harassed, intimidated and beaten, he was called names and asked why he came here and why does he lives with a South African girlfriend. Around 19h45 he was dumped at one of Durban taxi rank in another car. They took not only the car but everything else that he had at that time.
records.response: A case of hijacking was opened at Umbilo Police station but so far no arrest made.
records.other_text: The incident was first reported to the KZN Refugee Community leadership that the victim and I are part of

records.name: An injured migrant verbally abused and denied services at a state hospital in Durban
records.description: On Saturday 16th July 2022, a migrant from Burundi was attacked by 3 robbers who took his money, cellphone and other belonging, injuring him in the process. He was picked up by a community leaders who took him to King Edward VIII Hospital. When they arrived at the hospital, around 21h00, the hospital Clark refused to open a file for the victim alleging that Burundians are fighting between 2 ethnic groups and killing each other. He then said that they are bringing their criminality to South Africa which this country does not need. Among things that were taken from the victim is his document, which was in his wallet; since he could not produce that, this clerk found an additional reason not to help him arguing that how will he be sure that the victim is in the country legally. It took the  intervention of the matron in charge for the file to be opened.
records.duration: The incident lasted for more than an hour or so
records.response: The Matron in charge at Casualty intervened and the victim was given his file and treated.

records.name: Husband and wife lose possessions in an attack.
records.description: Members of the Capricorn community in Cape Town attack husband and wife. Although the wife is a South African citizen, the husband is from Burundi and has been constantly harassed because he is deemed too dark to be  a South African citizen. One day, on the second week of July while they were coming from work, they found their shack or dwelling ransacked. The metal sheets making up the shack were stolen together with their identity documents. On the fateful day, the wife was threatened with a screwdriver and banged on a nearby tank, surviving a few bruises.  However, they managed to escape and sought refugee from the wife's employer in the nearby suburb. The employer provided the with shelter, and food while the employer's children gave them clothes and some money to get by. The wife has managed to reapply for her South African identity document.
records.response: Employer and her family

records.name: A young Somali businessman Shot and killed in Westbank
records.description: On the 23rd of June 2022 at 10 am. A young businessman in his twenties was killed while delivering bread in Wesbank by armed gunmen. The perpetrators never took anything from the van when they left the victim. According to sources, the killing was extortion related. Police came to the scene, as well as ambulance services but the victim was declared dead.
records.response: Police attended crime scene
