records.name: Operation Dudula gives ultimatum to Witsand factories to remove 'illegal immigrants'
records.description: On the 27th of July 2022 Operation Dudula led a protest march in the Witsand factories in Atlantis  some 38.3km  from the Cape town CBD. The protest was giving the factories 7 days ultimatum to remove all 'illegal immigrants in their factories and employ locals. It was about 150 protesters  from Operation Dudula handing in a memorandum of demands to remove all 'illegal immigrants employees. It is reported that one of Operation Dudula members stated that they wanted to reclaim back jobs. Failing to do so they would have to rope in the services of Law Enforcement or Home Affairs department to enforced their immigration policy. The PC Revalidation Managing Director (MD) was horrified with their approach but explained to them that they have 42 staff members including 6 foreign nationals properly documented to be employed by the company. The MD stated that the foreigners employed by their company are of good standing and are doing positive things in their community. The company stated that they welcome any government department for audit.https://www.iol.co.za/capetimes/news/operation-dudula-gives-ultimatum-to-witsand-factories-to-remove-illegal-immigrants-93795ced-5528-4235-af4d-4977a1b4484f
records.who_attacked: The protest march was in the Witsand factories in Atlantis.
records.duration: It was for more than an hour.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: A Taxi association is forcing Ethiopian shop owners to hire its security services in Durban downtown
records.description: An Ethiopian leader who runs a shoe and clothes shop on Bertha Mkhize street, received a message from a certain Taxi Association in late June 2022 informing of their willingness and plan to provide security services to Ethiopian shops and businesses in downtown Durban in general but starting with Bertha Mkhize street as a pilot for now. The said leader then discussed this proposal with other Ethiopian shop owners who turned down the offer on the basis that they are already using the services of another security company and also their businesses are not doing well since the unrest of last year. However, they offered to donate some money to the taxi association as a gesture of willingness to work with them in future. When he communicated that decision to the taxi association, he was told that, if that is the case then that once off payment should be at least  R350,000 which the Ethiopian shop owners said they could not afford. Now this Ethiopian leader is receiving threats from unknown individuals and messages telling him that he better come to an agreement with the guys from the taxi association because they have big guns, they are ruthless and do not hesitate to shoot but they don't want him to leave his wife and children. It should be noted that there are South African and Chinese shops on that street, but this taxi association is only targeting Ethiopian shop owners.
records.who_attacked: An Ethiopian community leader and shop owner
records.duration: The threats have been going on for 1 week now
records.response: Not yet, the victim is scared to report the matter as these guys know him and the location of his shop.

records.name: Protesters in Kagiso break into homes of alleged foreign nationals, beat men and one dies.
records.description:
Violence broke out in Kagiso when locals attacked mine dumps looking for illegal mine workers (also known as zama-zama's) they suspect of criminal activities, resulting in the death of one person. The violent attacks follow instructions contained in a brochure distributed on Monday encouraging residents of Mogale City, the municipality that includes Kagiso, to take part in a shutdown on August 4, hence violence broke out on this day, with a multitude of residents participating in this demonstration. Some of the demonstrators broke into the homes of foreign nationals. There have been images showing hands of about 13  illegal miners tied behind their backs as they laid on the ground. They were encircled by locals brandishing machetes, pangas, and sticks after being brutally assaulted and stripped naked.The Kagiso demonstrations are a direct response to the theft of equipment from a film crew and the gang rape of eight of the crew members a week ago in Krugersdorp (also in Mogale City). 

Source 1: https://mg.co.za/news/2022-08-05-kagiso-residents-turn-violent-assault-people-accused-of-illegal-mining-crime/
Source 2: https://www.enca.com/news/kagiso-protesters-breaking-homes-alleged-foreign-nationals
records.response: Police

records.name: Operation Dudula Longbeach Protest.
records.description: On Friday 5th of August 2022 Operation Dudula held a protest at Long beach mall. The protestors were mostly harassing and verbally abusing foreigners chanting foreigners must go back to their countries. The Mall was chaotic with many locals joining the protest making it tough for foreigners that had to run for their lives as they did not know what would happen to them. This incident took place around 1pm - 2.30pm. Operation Dudula demands were that they do not want to see foreigners working in the malls and in the area at large. If they see any foreigners they will kill them. Most of the foreigners ran into the storerooms to protect themselves. The security officers could not do anything. Police only came later. This incident has stirred a lot of fear in the victims, most of them had to take Ubers to go home for safety reasons.
records.duration: For about 30mins though the protest took about an hours 30 minutes.
records.response: The Police came afterward.

records.name: Operation Dudula takes fight to Cape Town employers who hire foreign staff.
records.description: The protest march of Operation Dudula took place on Wednesday 10th of August 2022 in the neighbourhood of Kraaifontein. The protesters and sympathizes of Operation Dudula were estimated to be about 200. They focused on Petrol stations and any businesses that employed foreigners. The group demanded that employers should get rid of immigrants and employ locals in their memorandum. They handed CVs of unemployed South Africans to the companies they visited. A 7 days ultimatum was given to the employers, upon replying and gathering from the ground, nothing has been done as per firing the foreigners to employ locals. One of the company that received CVs was Shell petrol station in Belmont Park who are considering to hire locals.
records.who_attacked: They protest in businesses that employed foreigners.
records.response: There was Police patrol in those areas.

records.name: Joint operation to clean up Durban CBD targets nn-nationals indiscriminately
records.description: On 11/08/2022 from 10h00 onwards, a group of marchers from Umkhonto Wesizwe, OPESA, ATDF, ASA and Operation Dudula marched throughout downtown Durban chanting anti-immigrant slogans and calling non-national names such as "Amakwerekwere". They threatened to close and to take over foreign owned stores and forced all foreigners not to operate their businesses on the day. After marching throughout town, they then headed to Home Affairs offices in Umgeni Road where the march dispersed around 14h00.
records.who_attacked: The marchers harasser and intimidated non-nationals operating businesses in Central Durban
records.duration: In Central Durban, it lasted for more than 2hours
records.response: The police escorted the march, so no major physical incident so far.

records.name: A refugee street barber robbed and seriously assaulted by people who refused to pay for service rendered
records.description: On Saturday 13 August 2022, a Congolese refugee street barber opened his tent at his usual address on Alexandra street in Estcourt. Around 08h00, 2 guys entered the tent and asked to have their hair clipped. They then refused to pay and walked out with their machete wrapped in newspapers. This is reported to be a practice that is targeted towards foreign nationals only. After a short while the guys came back and started beating the barber with the back of the machete and stabbing him with knife until he fell down. That is when they beat him on his head and took 2 cellphones and barber equipment from him when they realized that he has lost consciousness. He was then picked up by people who knew him and rushed him to hospital where he was treated for his injuries.
records.response: A case was opened with Estcourt Police station

records.name: Migrant informal traders forcibly removed from their trading sites by their South African counterparts
records.description: Most refugee and migrant informal traders in Pietermaritzburg are trading without trading licences because Msunduzi municipality refuses to give trading permits/licences to non-national informal traders. In fact some of those from Malawi and Mozambique are also undocumented. For a while now the municipality has been sending metro police to evict them and confiscate their goods and after a while they would come back because they have no other option. Then came the time when it was Operation Dudula that was evicting them, which they did for a couple of times. However, what happened this time is that it is neither metro police nor operation Dudula but rather young and women South African informal traders who took upon themselves to evict other informal traders who happen to be migrants. This happened on Church street and Retief street which are the 2 busiest streets as far as informal or street trading is concerned. It is said that they were moving from one table or site to another, asking them for documents to be in the country as well as their trading permits. Our sources indicate that most informal traders in that area, South Africans included, do not have trading licences or permits. Since most of them did not have trading licences or permits, they were subsequently asked to pack their goods quickly and leave, failing which goods were thrown on the floor and crushed. The victims were then asked not to put their foot there until and unless they have been issued with trading permits by Msunduzi municipality. It is important to note that no South African informal trader was asked to produce a trading permit or worried in any way during this operation.
records.who_attacked: Migrant informal traders mostly from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Burundi, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and Malawi
records.response: No. Some of the victims are undocumented, so they are scared to report to the Police

records.name: Shops owned by foreign nationals looted in Jane Furse, Limpopo.
records.description:
Residents of Schoonoord, outside of Jane Furse in Limpopo, looted a number of foreign-owned businesses and the looting spread to surrounding areas. The looting was sparked by the assault and murder of a teenage boy allegedly by a spaza shop owner who is a foreign national on Friday, 19 August 2022.  Police were called in to calm the tension down. 

Source (1) : https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/shops-owned-by-foreign-national-looted-in-limpopo/  
Source (2) : https://briefly.co.za/south-africa/136149-death-teenage-boy-sparks-looting-spree-spaza-shops-owned-by-foreign-national-jane-furse-limpopo/ 
Sources (3) : https://www.vocfm.co.za/foreign-nationals-shops-looted-in-jane-furse-after-the-death-of-a-15-year-old-boy/
records.response: Local government authorities, and police.

records.name: The MEC for health in Limpopo province humiliates a Zimbabwean woman patient in public
records.description: On 23 August 2022 during her visit to Bela Bela provincial hospital, the MEC for health in Limpopo verbally abused and harassed a Zimbabwean patient who had just been operated at that hospital saying that the Zimbabwean President does not give her funding to run Limpopo healthcare systems. She even ordered the hospital management to ensure the patient pays for the operation which is free to South Africans, accusing her of being an "illegal" immigrant without proof and accusing her and other so called "illegal" immigrants of benefiting from specialised healthcare that should be reserved for Citizens and therefore putting a heavy burden to Limpopo's healthcare system. This incident has fueled xenophobic reaction on social media.
records.response: Yes, the news were widely discussed in the mainstream media. Also EFF (Economic Freedom Fighters), KAAX (Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia) and LHR (Lawyers for Human Rights reacted to the video which went viral on social media.

records.name: Victim alleges that Police extorted money in exchange for her release
records.description: A woman from Mozambique said she was handcuffed three weeks ago and taken to the central police station. She was asked to pay R500 for her release. The R500 they took was all the money she had to send home to her children. According to the woman, it’s not easy to make that amount, because if it is not the police chasing them, it’s the metro cops confiscating their goods.
records.response: SAPS

records.name: Operation Dudula  harrass foreign nationals/patients and employees outside Kalafong  Academic Hospital
records.description:
Foreign patients, staff members, and individuals suspected of being foreign nationals have been prohibited from entering Kalafong Academic Hospital in Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, for the previous three weeks. Since August 4, members of Operation Dudula in Greater Tshwane have been demonstrating in front of the provincial tertiary facility, requesting that it stop providing services to foreign nationals and expelling foreign nationals who work there. The source contacted  to verify this incident pointed a medical humanitarian organization had also noted that some of the people were turned away based on their accent and appearance or skin tone. Hence this criteria affected both local citizens and foreign nationals. The demonstration began two weeks before Phophi Ramathuba, the health MEC for Limpopo, launched into a tirade about how foreigners were exerting pressure to the province's healthcare system. To prevent the demonstrators from turning away patients and staff they thought to be foreign nationals, the Gauteng MEC for Health  obtained a court interdict on Friday 26 August 2022. Operation Dudula, however, did not stop the demonstrations and has threatened to escalate the protests. EFF members engaged in demonstrations against the actions of Operation Dudula while the South African government also condemned Operation Dudula  denying patients access to healthcare facilities at the Tshwane health facility. 
Source 1: https://www.groundup.org.za/article/operation-dudula-harasses-immigrants-outside-kalafong-hospital/
records.response: Police, political party, international NGO, local  and national government.

records.name: Operation Dudula demands foreign nationals to pay for healthcare services received from Hillbrow Community Health Centre.
records.description:
On Tuesday, August 30, members of Operation Dudula protested outside the Hillbrow Community Health Centre. Operation Dudula is claiming that foreigners are exploiting the nation's healthcare services, which they contend are already degraded and over flooded. They demanded that foreign nationals pay for the services they received at the health facility.  During the protest, foreign nationals seeking medical assistance at the Hillbrow Community Health Centre were scolded and reprimanded by Operation Dudula.
The protests at the Hillbrow health facility are came after Operation Dudula members set up a checkpoint at Kalafong on Monday, 29 August, 2022 to decide which patients should be let to enter based on nationality, how dark they seemed, and if they could show their SA IDs. A court order had earlier been issued to the hospital to compel police to stop the group from threatening and harassing's patients. However, Operation Dudula members defied this court order. The Operation Dudula group at Hillbrow clinic was dispersed by the police without violent incidents. 

Source 1: https://briefly.co.za/south-africa/137084-operation-dudula-protests-hillbrow-clinic-foreign-nationals-home/
records.response: Police, local authorities, local NGO. Opposition party

records.name: Local informal traders join operation Dudula to evict foreigners from Pietermaritzburg streets
records.description: On 1st September 2022, street vendors operating under the banner of PMB Informal trade Chamber and supported by some community members and Operation Dudula (OD) marched through the streets of Pietermaritzburg calling for illegal foreigners to go back to their home countries. During the march, they were removing remaining migrant informal traders from their trading sites regardless of whether they have documents to be in the country or not. Operation Dudula said that South Africans should receive priority in terms of entrepreneurial spaces to sell their goods and appealed for support from the army and police. One of the OD members told a journalist who interviewed him that “We are here in Pietermaritzburg as Operation Dudula, we are removing foreigners from the streets and we are demanding that law enforcement agencies help us to ensure foreign nationals go back to their home countries because 90 percent of foreigners that are here in South Africa are illegal. It should be noted that this is the second time in one month that migrant traders have been forcefully removed from their trading space. The first time it was informal traders who are allegedly members of PMB Informal Trade Chamber, 3 weeks back and since then those who were evicted have not been allowed to go back to trade and are living in a very precarious situation.
records.duration: The whole morning, more than 4 hours
records.response: Operation was escorted by Police

records.name: Joburg police accused of extorting bribes from immigrants during raids and roadblocks
records.description: A woman from Bulawayo says she hid in a ditch in Johannesburg with her child last Friday when she saw a police van stopping nearby, so that she wouldn’t have to pay a bribe. She lost her asylum document five years ago. When police previously arrested her in Pretoria, she paid a bribe of R100 to be released. The woman told Daily Maverick that police are making a business of these arrests, taking anything between R100 and R3,000, depending on your luck. She said she had to pay bribes of R700 each for two relatives who were arrested on their way to church two weeks ago. According to the woman, the police also accept e-wallets and can even accompany you to the ATM machine.
records.response: None

records.name: A man from Bangladesh reported that he and three men from Malawi were arrested and Police tried to Extort money
records.description: A man from Bangladesh reported that he and three men from Malawi were placed in a police van and told to “make a plan” if they wanted to be released. The Bangladesh victim informed the police that he was not illegal but was struggling to renew his asylum permit which expired during the lockdown. However, the police demanded that the pay R500 each. He said he refused and demanded to be arrested instead. He also threatened to report the police. He was released, but the three Malawians with him paid up since they had no papers at all.
records.response: No response reported

records.name: Man pays extortion to Police for the release of his undocumented brother
records.description: A man from Malawi said he paid R2,000 for the release of his undocumented brother. The man stated that when the apply for documentation, they are not getting it and now police are using the opportunity to make money out of them.
records.response: No response reported

records.name: 4 Burundian barbers robbed at gunpoin in Umlazi E section because they are foreign nationals
records.description: On 9th September, 2 boys entered the barber shop wanting haircut at half the price. When barbers refused, they were told you will see. Two days later, on Sunday 11 September 2022 at 11h00 am, three armed boys jumped out of a white car, leaving the driver inside. They held the barbers at gunpoint, took their money, cellphones and hair clippers while calling them names and telling them if they do not leave Umlazi, next time they will lose their lives.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: Yes, The police responded quickly and managed to find the car they were driving. Perpetrators have fled the scene but left an ID for one of them and a Cellphone.

records.name: Immigrants forced out of their homes in Plettenberg Bay
records.description:
Dozens of immigrants were forced out of their homes by residents of Kwanokuthula, Plettenberg Bay.
About 30 people had to sleep in a community hall overnight. The desperate immigrants say the police have completely failed to protect their rights and their homes. South African community members also arrived, accompanied by two police vans and one law enforcement vehicle that had earlier been seen patrolling alongside the community as locals searched door-to-door for immigrants. They carried sticks and sharp objects. The immigrants started to pick up stones. A conflict was imminent. After refusing to leave, at around 9:30pm, police used stun grenades and rubber bullets to disperse the South Africans.
records.response: Victims went to seek refugee at the Police Station

records.name: Foreigners Flee Xenophobic Attacks after three Zimbabweans are killed in Chavani Village
records.description: Attacks on foreign nationals took place in some of the villages in Elim. The incident was sparked by a cable theft incident in Chavani Village which saw the suspects, 3 Zimbabweans being burnt. The situation escalated and migrants (from Zimbabwe mostly) have been driven out of their homes. Reports estimate the number to be 200. The situation worsened in a village called Shirley and most migrants were reported to be at the police station.
records.response: SAPS and civil society organisations intervened and called a meeting with all stakeholders concerned

records.name: A 21 year old Zimbabwean woman dies after giving birth to a 4kg baby at Yusuf Dadoo Hospital in Krugersdorp
records.description: On 21 September 2022, a 21 old Zimbabwean woman died at Yusuf Dadoo hospital in Krugersdorp, after giving birth to a 4kg old baby. It is alleged that she received poor treatment was and neglect by health caregivers at the hospital because she was an undocumented Zimbabwean migrant. Despite complaining of pain and excessive bleeding, the medical staff in the maternity ward did not pay attention to her. Her lifeless body covered with blood was found by nurses hours after giving birth. The family of the deceased was concerned that the statements uttered by Limpopo Health MEC, Phophi Ramathuba, could have caused the staff at the hospital to have a negative attitude towards illegal immigrants seeking medical attention in South Africa. The hospital failed to explain what happened to Luyanda but acknowledged the death.
records.duration: Unknown. But messages found in the deceased phone indicate that she went through a lot of pain and bleeding before her death
records.response: The Gauteng department of health promised to investigate the incident.

records.name: Refugees and other International migrants arrested without warrant of arrest in Greytown
records.description: On Friday 23 September 2022 morning around 04h30, refugees, asylum seekers and other immigrants were woken up by the police and asked to produce their documents. 11 refugees and asylum seekers and a significant number of immigrants from Malawi in particular, were arrested including 3 asylum seekers who had their documents. The group were taken to the main police station in Greytown for verification, yet the Minister Motsoaledi said this kind of verification can be done on the site of arrest. After verification, 3 were released around 10h00, but the rest of them are still in jail and are expecting to appear in court this Monday morning. Most undocumented refugees are newcomers who arrived in the country in 2020 and 2021 during lockdown. They said they don't have papers because they tried several times to apply for documents but were unsuccessful as a result of the department of Home Affairs implementing the process of online application and renewal of documents. Some of those arrested have expired documents because, although they have submitted their online application for extension of their documents, Home Affairs have not sent those documents to them.
records.who_attacked: Refugees, asylum seekers and other international migrants from neighboring countries
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: 2 Somali shopkeepers doused with paraffine and set alight in their shop near Queenstown
records.description: In a village called "Lower Didimana", 60 km from Queenstown in Eastern Cape, two Somali shopkeepers were burnt to death inside their shop. The incident happened on Sunday 2/10/2022 night when an unknown group of people entered the shop, tied both shopkeepers, doused them with paraffin, which was being sold in the shop and set them alight. It is unclear whether anything was taken from the shop since it also got burnt as a result. The bodies were only discovered by a neighbour the following day who then called the police and went to Queenstown to inform the Somali community the following day.
records.duration: The burnt bodies were discovered the following morning
records.response: A case was opened with the local police station, case n 3/10/2022 but so far no arrests.
records.other_text: The incident was reported to us by the keader of the Somali community in Eastern Cape.

records.name: A Burundi National Woman, asylum seeker, with one-month born baby, delivered via C-Section, was denied medical care at Delft Community Health Centre.
records.description:
On Monday the 03rd October 2022, at Delft Community Health Centre, in the City of Cape, the Western Cape Province, between 8:00 am – 13:00, a Burundian woman national, asylum seeker in the Republic, mother of two, with one month old new born baby, born by Section – C, was denied medical care services. The mother needed further medical care and a follow up as she was healing from a C-Section. The mother had been referred by Karl Bremer Hospital (where she had delivered her new born baby) to Delft Public Health facility, as the nearest public health facility, for further medical care and further follow ups in relation to her condition. She claims that once at Delft Community Health Centre, on Monday morning, on the 03rd October, 2022, she was abused, both physically & psychologically by medical staff. She argued that she was victim of unfair discrimination at Delft Community Health Centre, as she was not allowed to see the Doctor nor receive any medical care at all, and she was not given any valid explanation, as to why she could not be helped. She further argued that she had been at the same Delft health facility on Friday the 30th September 2022, but she was told by medical staff that she arrived too late for the day to be attended to. She was then advised by the same medical staff to come back the following Monday morning, on the 03rd October 2022. 

Once back to Delft Community Health Centre on Monday morning, she first was referred to the “wounds” services for her Section – C check-up, then she was referred to see the Doctor on site that same day, for further medical care and Doctor’s opinion. The victim stated that she was asked to be in the waiting room, expecting to see the Doctor sometime during the day. Meanwhile, her name was not written down on the Doctor’s appointment list for the day. This is because by 13:00 pm or so, when she was advised to go back home, her name had not been called in to meet the Doctor. Additionally, her folder was not found among those that were brought to the Doctor’s desk, to be called in to meet the Doctor. Between the times from the “wounds” section to the doctor’s room, both her medical card and folder had been returned back to the reception/administration section shelves, instead of being taken in to the Doctor’s desk. This was confirmed when she complained of having been waiting too long since morning, without any indication that she would be called in to see the Doctor soon. That was around 13:00. She said that they had to go and check in her folder at the administration section shelves, to find her medical card inside the folder. 

Tired, stressed, despondent the  mother went back home without medical care, and without any clear and satisfactory explanation as to why she could not be helped, when she needed medical care the most. She feels that she was refused medical care because she was a foreigner. Allegedly, since day one, the medical staff she interacted with at Delft Community Health Centre tended to be rude and questioned her papers, also threatened her about not receiving any medical care, if she had not paid money (around R800) she owed to the Department of Health (DoH), from her previous maternity medical care received at Karl Bremer Hospital.
records.who_attacked: A Burundi national woman, asylum seeker, with one month new born baby
records.response: No

records.name: Many documented refugees and asylum seekers arrested by police in Vryheid
records.description:
Early in the morning of Friday 7th October 2022, refugees and asylum seekers were woken up by  police boots. More than 20 police vans were involved in the operation of arresting "undocumented immigrants". They arrested everyone they came across; men, women and even children, including those who had their documents with them and others who claimed to kept their documents elsewhere. They were taken to a SAPS compound where they waited for immigration officers to verify the validity of documents for those who were arrested while having their documents.
Some of the documented ones who did not have documents on them when they were arrested, saw their relatives and friends also arrested when they brought those documents to them where they were held.
After verification of documents by immigration and home affairs officers, all those who had documents were released around 15h00 in the afternoon.
This kind of raid is unfortunate considering what was said by the Minister of Home Affairs when he declared that police has the ability of verifying documents on the spot.
records.who_attacked: Refugees and Asylum seekers in Vryheid
records.duration: The whole morning, more than 1 hours
records.response: Following verification of the department of Home Affairs, all those who have documents were released late in the afternoon.

records.name: Around hundred foreign nationals owned businesses looted in Vrygrond/Capricorn community
records.description:
A three-day armed fight left the community of Vrygond traumatised. According to the community, nine people were killed during these shootings. The SAPS suggested that seven people were killed, while a reliable source indicated that twelve people were killed, of them five associated with JFK, while six of the killed were associated with the Taxi industry in the area, and then one of the twelve killed persons was a Malawi national. According to reliable sources, this incident resulted in looting of foreign shops several days later. 

The looting incident took place after the burial of the deceased gangs. It is reported that the new JFK boss ordered his boys to loot all foreign owned businesses on Drury and Philemon Streets, for two hours, and take away whatever items they wanted. The items stolen from the foreign owned businesses included [but are not limited to] IT devices (mobile phones, laptops and accessories); electrical appliances; money; clothing; raw food; and alike. It was observed that businesses along Drury and Philemon streets had been dominantly owned by foreign nationals, but there were also some few businesses operated by local South African citizens, which were left untouched during the incident. Foreign nationals whose businesses were looted this time included Malawi, Congo, Rwanda, Burundi, Zimbabwe nationals, few mistaken local South African citizens.

According to one local non-government organisation (NGO), working in Vrygrond community, an estimate of 100 foreign owned businesses along Drury and Philemon Streets were looted. Reports further state that both local South Africa citizens and foreign nationals operate businesses on the same street across Vrygrond community, however, when there is an opportunity for looting, only foreign owned businesses are selectively targeted. To date, residents of Vrygrond community live under constant fear and they feel that the SAPS cannot help. So far, there has been no assistance (material, financial, psychological) provided to the victims of the looting in question.  The affected foreign nationals and the few local South Africa citizens whose businesses were looted on the 22nd October 2022 in Vrygrond, on both Drury and Philemon Streets, do need emergency financial assistance to rebuild their businesses.
records.who_attacked: Businesses along Drury and Philemon Streets
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Barber equipment of street barbers confiscated allegedly by members of Operation Dudula and war veterans
records.description:
On Monday morning of the 24th of October 2022, two Congolese street barbers went to collect their equipment at the storage facility where they usually keep them. Upon arrival, they found that their trolley and all its content were held by three known people who often passed their sites collecting protection fees of R10-20 per day from each from the people they extorted the money from. However, the previous week, the two street barbers had decided not to pay their fees anymore because it became strangely very quiet and they were no longer making enough money anymore. The two street barbers were subsequently warned and told that should they not pay, they would see what would happen to them very soon. 
It is important to mention that the victims were initially evicted violently from their trading sites at Soldiers' way bus rank in March 2020 and only managed to find an alternative site that they are paying a monthly fee in addition to paying for trading permit at the municipality.
records.who_attacked: They took all their barber equipment and trolley.
records.response: The victims opened a case with Central Police station but no arrest made and no single item has been returned to the barbers.

records.name: A barber asylum seeker evicted from his trading site and his container confiscated in Kranskop
records.description: An asylum seeker from DRC was operating in a makeshift kiosk near the kranskop taxi rank as a barber since 2015. In April this year, he moved in a container in the same area with his 4 associates, after buying it. In June 2022, he was informed by the taxi rank manager and associates that he must pay R200 each month for him to continue operating in the area, which he did together with others. However on 24 October 2022, the extortionists said to him that the money he is giving them is not enough and for that reason they have decided to take over the business and from that day his employees will be reporting and giving money to them. They assaulted him and ordered him to leave Kranskop immediately if he wants to remain alive. The victim then reported the case to police and managed to secure a protection order from a local magistrate court, which was delivered to the extortionists by him and the police officers. However, the extortionists refused to sign the protection order and instead assaulted him again in front of the police who could not protect him because the extortionists had automatic AK47 while the police only had pistols. Soon after that the victim was forced to leave the area and came to Durban where he is sheltered under very difficult conditions until now, The victim reported that since he left Kranskop, it is the extortionists who have taken over his business and the container and are the ones collecting money from his employees.
records.response: The latest incident occurred in front of police officers who accompanied him to hand over the protection order to perpetrators, which they refused to sign anyway.

records.name: A Foreign Pregnant Woman Forced to Give Birth at Home Due to Denied Health Care Services
records.description: A woman from Zimbabwe whose asylum permit had expired five years ago was forced to give birth at home after was denied access to prenatal care at Jeppe, Hillbrow and Coronation clinics in August and October 2022. She reported that her 4-month-old baby was born prematurely, while she was alone at home in December 2022 and the little boy is still underweight.
records.who_attacked: Foreign pregnant woman denied prenatal health care
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Women informal nail therapist evicted by members of MKMVA in downtown Durban
records.description: Today, Tuesday 22 November 2022 around 08h00 morning, a group of 10 males who claimed to be members of war veterans namely MKMVA, forced women migrants informal traders to leave their trading sites. These women were informal nail therapists located in a passage off Dr. Pixley Kaseme street in Durban central and most of them have paid up trading permits issued by eThekwini municipality. These guys who were armed with knobkerries and knives put their own people on those sites and instructed them to pay daily to them. More than 30 evicted migrant informal trader women, reported that those guys who claim to be MKMVA members stood on the sides threatening migrant women with their weapons and told them  not to dare put their foot there. After the eviction, the migrant women approached the relevant authorities, i.e. the Business Support Unit of Ethekwini municipality and reported the matter. They were then promised that Metro Police will be sent to the site to sort these people out, but these Metro Police never arrived.
records.who_attacked: Migrant women informal nail therapists operating on street
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: The matter was reported to Municipal Authorities but so far no action has been taken against perpetrators

records.name: Pietermaritzburg migrant informal traders evicted again violently
records.description: More than 100 informal traders, many of whom are women refugees and asylum seekers from Burundi and DRC, were forcibly removed from their trading spots early in September of this year 2022 by a structure called "Pietermaritzburg Informal Trade Chamber" supported by Operation Dudula and other community members. Not having anything else to do to put food on the table, some of them started coming back slowly to regain their trading sites, only to find that some of those sites are already occupied by new local traders, placed on those sites by the same PMB Informal Trade Chamber. On Monday 21 November, the PMB Chamber called a meeting with local informal traders where they agreed to evict again all migrant informal traders from the streets of Pietermaritzburg. That operation started timidly on Tuesday the 22 November but was intensified on Wednesday 23 November resulting in injuries on both sides following a resistance by some migrant informal traders where sharp objects were used. The police had to intervene and used rubber bullets to disperse the crowd. As things stand, migrants have warned all migrant informal traders not to ever think of returning on streets anywhere in Pietermaritzburg if they want to remain alive.
records.duration: The whole morning, more than 2 hours
records.response: Yes, the police responded and had to use rubber bullets to disperse the crowd.

records.name: A Congolese Bottle sotre owner assassinated in Waterloo few months after his brother was killed the same way
records.description: On Sunday morning, 27 November 2022, around 04h00 am, a Congolese owner of Lovisa Sport Bar and Bottle Store and an unknown male believed to be his plumber, were assassinated  while seated in a bakkie outside his bar in Waterloo, North of Durban/Kwazulu Natal. The relatives of the deceased believe that, it is the same people who killed his younger brother earlier this year, who did this to him. Reaction Unit South Africa (RUSA) received multiple calls for assistance after high-calibre gunfire was heard in the parking lot of a bar. On arrival, Reaction Officers discovered the bloodied remains of two men in a white Hyundai H100 bakkie. The 45-year driver was identified as the owner of Lovisa Sports Bar. The identity of the passenger was not immediately confirmed. Both men were declared deceased on arrival of Medics. The motive for the murders is not yet clearly established but he already reported to police that there are 2 groups of gangsters who are threatening him. The first group was forcing him to let them sell drugs at his bar, and another one was asking him to pay up to R15000/month of protection fees or leave the area, which he was unable or unwilling to pay.
records.who_attacked: A Congolese owner of a bar
records.response: Yes, Reaction Unit South Africa (RUSA), were the first one to respond to the crime scene and the police arrived later on.

records.name: A young male queer Zimbabwean who was suspected to be undcumented, was strangled to death on Saturday night in Mayville/Durban
records.description: On Sunday 17 December 2022 in Mayville/Durban, a lifeless body of a young and known Zimbabwean gay was found in the room that he was renting in Mayville. On the body there was no gunshot nor stab wound found but the deceased appeared to have been strangled to death. He was already living in fear because he was constantly receiving death threats from two groups of locals, one group believed that he did not have proper the documents to be in the country, while the other one did not tolerate his sexual orientation. When family members and LGBTQI+ community members came to gather at his place for some prayers, they were stopped, chased away and accused of making noise by neighbours and a group of local youth. A case of murder was opened at Mayville local police station but so far no arrest. The witnesses who saw the perpetrators leaving his room the previous night are not willing or scared to come forward and cooperate with the police detectives. The Zimbabwean LGBTQI+ community is trying to raise funds for the repatriation of the body back to Zimbabwe where his entire family is and where funerals are hoped to take place.
records.duration: Unknown as the body was fund the following morning
records.response: A case of murder was opened at Cato Manor Police station but so far they yet to arrest anyone
records.other_text: I was informed by the leader of the Zimbabwean LGBTQI+ community in Durban who lives in another area.

records.name: Operation Dudula evicts vulnerable dwellers of Joburg’s ‘building of darkness
records.description: A group supposedly posing as members of Operation Dudula has evicted more than 300 people from a privately owned derelict building, which has been home to over 400 occupants-mostly migrants. The eviction comes after months of ongoing threats directed at the occupants of the building by Operation Dudula.
records.response: Several NGO's assisted victims with shelter and provision of services

records.name: Victim forced to pay R5000 to be discharged
records.description:
Pregnant foreign nationals in need of healthcare services - Another victim stated that she had to fork out money to ensure she got assistance. She said that, when she was pregnant and went to the hospital in December, healthcare workers and nurses took advantage of her and other women who were foreign nationals by extorting money from them. The victim said she had to pay anything between R400 and R600 each time she went for a check-up. She also alleged to have paid R5000 to two nurses who were on shift the weekend she gave birth, but she was given no birth record because they threatened that the police would arrest her, as her passport was expired and she ended up leaving without her baby’s birth record. The victim partner alleges that he paid the nurses in the ward so that he could take his partner and their child home. He stated that the nurses initially wanted R15 000, but he negotiated for R5 000, which was all he could afford as he waits tables in a restaurant for tips. He managed to to raise the money over the two days his partner was in the hospital and begged the nurses to accept what he had. Even after paying, they discovered that the expectant mother had not been registered in the hospital records and struggled with birth records.
Source - https://www.news24.com/citypress/news/foreign-mothers-forced-to-pay-nurses-to-take-their-babies-home-20230604#:~:text=Pregnant%20foreign%20nationals%20in%20need,to%20birthing%20facilities%20and%20assistance.
records.who_attacked: Foreign national mothers of new born babies
records.response: Gauteng Health Department is allegedly investigating the incident

records.name: Selective eviction of migranT informal traders in Melmoth/Kwazulu Natal
records.description: On Tuesday 3rd January 2023, started an operation of evicting all migrant informal traders in Melmoth, a small municipality base in North of Kwazulu Natal, accusing them of trading on municipal property without trading permit. In total 15 migrant informal traders and heads of households were evicted including 8 street barbers. When asked why they are trading without permits, the victims argue that the municipality has refused categorically to provide those permits to them on the basis that they are not South Africans. As a result, all migrant informal traders in Melmoth did not have trading permits regardless of whether they are documented or not and whether their documents allow them to work in South Africa or not.
records.who_attacked: All migrant informal traders operating in Melmoth, including refugees and asylum seekers
records.duration: The eviction is continuous. Even now they are still evicting those who try to go back and trade.
records.response: UNHCR planned to refer affected victims to partner organisations for assistance

records.name: Operation Dudula chases immigrants away from Joburg clinic
records.description: Members of Operation Dudula have been chasing away immigrants from the Jeppe Clinic in central Johannesburg. On Monday GroundUp saw people in Operation Dudula T-shirts protesting inside and outside the clinic, telling immigrants to leave and get health care in their countries of origin.
records.response: Around 30 Civil Society Organisations have released a statement condemning the health xenophobia

records.name: Operation Dudula chases immigrants away from a Cosmo City Clinic
records.description: On 18th January, a group of people claiming to be members of Operation Dudula, stormed a local clinic situated at extension 6 around an informal settlement called "Cosmo City". They forcibly chased away immigrants who were seated waiting to be attended to by healthcare practitioners at the clinic, including a pregnant woman. They were telling them to either go to private Doctors or go back to their home countries and get healthcare service there. This was 2 days after doing the samething at jeppe Clinic in Central Johannesburg where immigrants on chronic medication were unable to collect those, putting their lives in danger. However, soon after, organisations such as Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia and Africa Simunye intervened and the following day those evicted immigrants were back at the clinic where they received the needed healthcare service.
records.duration: Less than an hour or so
records.response: Yes, organisations such as Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia (KAAX) and Africa Simunye, with support from the police, intervened and the following day those evicted immigrants were back at the clinic where they received the needed healthcare service.

records.name: Pastors harassed and falsely accused of peddling drugs
records.description: Operation Dudula members forcibly entered New Life Fellowship Church in Springs searching for drugs and accusing the pastors of peddling drugs. They took some money and stole one of the pastors phone which was returned after the intervention of the police. After, searching the perpetrators did not find anything. One of the pastors was forced to eat some white powder which was brought by the perpetrators. The pastor was later taken to the hospital and provided with medication.
records.response: Police intervened at some point during the incident

records.name: Bottle Store belonging to a foreign national attacked by alleged Operation Dudula
records.description: A bottle store belonging to a Nigerian national was allegedly attacked by operation dudula members who were chasing away foreigners and accusing them of peddling drugs. The store was looted and it is estimated that the owner lost more than 1 million in money and goods.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Operation Dudula denying immigrant patients access to Mayfair Clinic
records.description: In the morning of 25th January, a group of people wearing t-shirt on which it was written "Operation Dudula" stood at the gate of Mayfair Clinic situated on 22 Somerset street/Mayfair in Johannesburg and were controlling entry of anyone entering the clinic. They were asking people to produce their documents before entering the clinic. They continued to do that until about 14h30 when Metro Police intervened and urged them to picket outside the clinic if they want but not to stop patients from entering the clinic.
records.response: Yes, Metro police responded and convinced them to disperse in the afternoon
records.other_text: I first learnt about it on KAAX (Kopanang African Against Xenophobia) WhatsApp group.

records.name: Foreigners barred from clinic leave without life-saving medicine
records.description: An Incident of two individuals hiding behind masks barring foreign nations from accessing health care services were reported at Zandspruit Clinic. According to Sowetan Live, the pair stopped one victim along with other patients they believed were foreigners. The duo would only allow SA patients to proceed into the facility after they inspected their IDs. Members of the so-called Combat Movement said their illegal campaign to bar foreign nationals from the clinic was not xenophobia, but to protect the health facility.
records.response: Unknown

records.name: Operation Dudula members reported to be chasing foreign nationals
records.description: Reports of Operation Dudula chasing away foreign nationals from accessing health care services at Orchard Clinic in Orange Grove Johannesburg were received. According to reports, Simunye members were called to intervene.
records.response: Simunye members were called to intervene

records.name: Operation Dudula reportedly planning to chase children of illegal immigrants out of classrooms
records.description: Operation Dudula has been accused of targeting immigrant children in Diepsloot, Johannesburg, running a campaign to pull them out of school. According to a WhatsApp message quoted by activist organisation Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia, Operation Dudula says places in schools must be kept for South African children. In a statement on 30 January, KAAX quoted a WhatsApp message signed by Che Serobedi from Operation Dudula Diepsloot, calling on members and parents of school-going children to attend a mass meeting on 26 January. “All leaners/children who did not get space at all local schools will be put in classes and foreigners who are learners will be removed from classes,” the message read. “As Operation Dudula Diepsloot branch and parents we can’t allow South African children to be out of school this year. Foreigners are accommodated and learning in our public schools … No retreat no surrender.”
records.response: The Foundation for Education and Social Justice Africa has called on police to protect the children of illegal immigrants.

records.name: A Bus and a Truck from Mozambique are torched near Mbazwana
records.description:
On 26 January 2023, angry communities in Mbazwana torched a Mozambican truck on the R22 highway between Hluhluwe and Mbazwana. A few minutes later they stopped a Mozambican luxury bus from Maputo headed for Durban, forced (Mozambican and South African) tourists out and torched it. Travellers had to walk for more than three kilometres to find help. Days later the torching of Mozambican-owned vehicles continue on the R22 road between Hluhluwe and Mbazwana on the South African side. totalling a number of seven vehicles, that have been torched in the area since last week.

This follows brazen activities of cross-border crime syndicates where everything from vehicles and drugs – cocaine, heroin, meth – to counterfeit cigarettes and other goods are smuggled through the porous fence separating South Africa and Mozambique. For years now the border communities of Umkhanyakude District, including Manguzi, Jozini, Mbazwana, Hluhluwe and others, have been under siege from armed cross-border syndicates who attack them in their homes especially at night, rob, abduct them, take them in their own vehicles and dump them there while syndicate members smuggle their (the victims’) vehicles through the porous fence into the Mozambique wilderness. This cross-border crime became prevalent in the 2000s and various government efforts to root it out had failed to produce results. 

In recent weeks, communities have been protesting in frustration and some have been taking the law into their own hands - with opportunistic criminal elements creeping in, evidenced by the torching of a Mozambican truck and a bus late in January, and further incidents in February. Unfortunately the victims in this case have only one thing in common with cross-border criminals, is that they are all from Mozambique.
records.who_attacked: Mozambican vehicles, including a truck and a luxury bus
records.response: No. The police arrived when the vehicles were already completely burnt.

records.name: IFP Ward 67 Branch accused of  preventing people from accessing health services at Yeoville Community Clinic
records.description: IFP Ward 67 Branch accused of preventing people from accessing health services at  Yeoville Community Clinic. According to reports received, they were stopping people to check for documentation and only those with valid documentation were permitted to enter.
records.who_attacked: Prevention of foreign nationals seeking to access to health care facilities
records.response: A member of the KAAX attended the scene to reason with the perpetrators

records.name: Delmas township: over 200 Ethiopia Nationals Forcibly Displaced and their Businesses Completely Looted and Destroyed to Ashes
records.description:
Over 200 Ethiopian nationals forcibly displaced in Delmas had their businesses completely looted and destroyed to ashes from Saturday the 18th of February 2023 to Monday the 20th of February 2023. Around 157 businesses owned by Ethiopian nationals were completely looted, and most of the inside structures were completely destroyed. According to reports, the instigators behind the unrest in Delmas area were allegedly unemployed youth demanding work at local mines and were apparently furious about the hiring of foreign nationals instead of RSA citizens. The looting and ransacking of the hundreds of Ethiopian owned businesses around Delmas township stemmed from weeks of unrest and protesting that had started in early February 2023. Most unemployed community members (predominantly youth) from Mimosa, Botleng and Delmas communities marched complaining about a variety of issues. These issues included poor public service delivery, public safety issues and demands that potential employment opportunities such as those in the mining industry be prioritised for local citizens. 

These protests progressively scaled into riots over the weekend of Saturday the 18th - to Monday evening, on the 20th of February 2023, and consequently over 200 businesses, owned and operated by Ethiopia nationals (mostly Oromos) were completed looted and destroyed. By the end of February 2023, two of the looted business owners (Ethiopian nationals/Oromos) were still missing, they could not be physically located, nor reached via their respective mobile contact numbers.   
As stated by Oromos community leadership sources, neither the SAPS- Delmas, nor any other Local Government leadership structures in Delmas provided any help nor assistance to the affected business owners in question. Until the end of February 2023, there had been no assistance and/or intervention, that has come to the rescue of these affected business owners, from civil society organisations, or non-government organisations (NGOs), including those that are directly or indirectly involved with international “forced” migration matters in the Republic. According to same Oromos leadership sources in both Gauteng and Mpumalanga Provinces, during the peak time of the present xenophobic looting of foreign nationals owned businesses in Delmas township, more particularly during the weekend of Saturday the 18th - to Monday the 20th of February 2023, the Oromos Community Leadership in South Africa had to hire private gangs to rescue their members from the looting mobs,  and transfer them from Delmas township to Delmas town/city and to Johannesburg and other relatively safer areas around Gauteng Province, for temporary safer shelters (among other Oromo families/households). 

The estimated 200 affected foreign business owners (dominantly Oromos) are in urgent need of financial, material and psychological assistance. Reportedly, the looting/violence stopped itself after concerned local community members handed over their memorandum of concerns and requests to the relevant “Mining Management” & Municipality, and were promised further follow up engagements with their representatives. As maintained among Oromos leadership circles in Johannesburg, it is alleged that when looting victims indicated to the SAPS-Delmas their intention to lay charges /making a Court case, allegedly the SAPS discouraged them, saying that the violence/looting were public, hence no one is specifically to be charged or held responsible. The victims were not convinced by such remarks from the SAPS. Subsequently, these victims gathered at the Delmas – SAPS Station, in attempt to meet physically with Delmas SAPS-Station Commander, with intention to voice out their physical security concerns, and request more effective and efficient protection mechanisms to be put in place but their efforts were in vain as they were not able to be granted an audience with the Station Commander.
records.who_attacked: Businesses owned & operated by Ethiopia Nationals (Oromos)
records.duration: The whole weekend of Saturday the 18th  - to Monday the 20th of February 2023
records.response: Not at all. Victims of this xenophobic violence were left alone to themselves. There was no intervention (assistance/help) from Delmas-SAPS, or Delmas Local Government Structures, or any other Stakeholders involved with refugees & migrants matters in Delmas area. It was reported that UNHCR and LHR plan to visit the victims and assess the situation in the area.
records.other_text: Oromos Community Leadership sources in South Africa

records.name: Taxi operators forcibly remove refugee traders from their workplaces after burning foreigners' shacks in Burgersfort
records.description: Pretending to want to get rid of nyaope addicts, sex workers and drug dealers in the Burgersfort, taxi operators, burnt several shacks in Ext 10. It all started on Wednesday 22 February 2023, when taxi operators petrol-bombed several shacks in the area, mostly inhabited by foreign nationals. accusing them of being sex workers, nyaope addicts and dealers who are allegedly robbing commuters and shoppers and thus destroying the town and its good image. From there, they moved to the main taxi rank in CBD where they confiscated keys of shops, containers and kiosks operated by foreign nationals and accusing them of supplying drugs to local youth in the area. None of the more than 50 migrants, mostly refugees and asylum seekers from DRC, Nigeria and Burundi have been allowed to regain access to their trading kiosks or containers. If anything, the perpetrators put locals in those shops who are using equipment and infrastructure left by migrants as they were not allowed to take anything from those shops when they were evicted. The police and local municipality were approached for assistance but refused to help, saying those taxi operators are more powerful than the police, so victims should go and negotiate with them.
records.duration: Several days, until now the situation has not yet improved
records.response: No response so far

records.name: A DRC Refugee pushed out of his property in Amaoti/Inanda township
records.description: On Sunday 19 March 2023 around 09h45, members of one of the opposition parties in the area informed the victim that he had to vacate his property because he is a foreigner national and has a big plot that South Africans do not have. The victim was also informed that his plot made it difficult for community members to move around the area. The members of the political party also accused him of using fake documents issued by the ANC. They then proceeded to destroy the victim's bamboo fence while giving him one month to vacate the plot and leave the area. The victim then went to the Amaoti satellite of Inanda police station to report the matter. Unfortunately for the victim, the area has been occupied unlawfully, which means no one has any documentation to prove ownership of any of the plots in that area. The political party members who sold him the land did so unlawfully hence it was a challenge for the police to assist him with the matter because he could not prove who sold him the plot, the value of the damage as well as proof of ownership.  The victim alleges that one policewoman went as far as telling him to go build his house back in DRC. The victim then reported the case to the Ward Councillor who indicated that she was very concerned about the incident and promised to organise a meeting to address the issue. The victim is living in fear on the same plot because he does not have money to pay for rent somewhere else. He accuses members of a Pan Africanist political party for selling him the plot unlawfully and then extorting money from him as a condition for ownership. When the victim stopped paying the extortion fees, that is when he was informed that the plot belongs to another member of the political party and he is not able to join the party because he is a foreign national.
records.who_attacked: A family of refugees from DRC
records.response: Not yet. The matter was reported to SAPS and Ward Councillor. The Councillor has planned a meeting to address the matter but this is still pending.

records.name: Hillbrow Community Health Centre: Foreign Nationals Prevented from Accessing Medical Care Services by Dudula Operation Movement and its Allies
records.description:
On Tuesday morning, the 04th of April 2023, dozens of Operation Dudula Movement’s members, together with a group of local women, which was identified by some commentators as “ILAWU”, and by other as “ULAWU”, raided Hillbrow Community Health Centre, and started threatening foreign national patients. As reported by witnesses that were physically present on the scene, members of Operation Dudula Movement, as well members of ULAWU/ILAWU, forcibly took control of all the queues, and started asking identification documents (IDs), and Visas/Permits to foreign national patients. Reportedly, the assailants were chanting, sending clear messages, telling all foreign nationals that they must leave South Africa and must go back to their countries with immediate effect, and also foreign national patients, who held expired papers, or who did not have papers with them on the scene, were forcibly and immediately removed from the queue, and forcibly chased away from the health centre’s premises. 

To intensify the threats, the assailants engaged in burning tyres, overthrowing solid waste on the streets and hospital premises, and increasing verbal abuse and violent statements, selectively addressed towards foreign nationals in general and those present at the clinic. An eye-witnesses stated that the South African Police Services (SAPS)’ physical presence was noticeable on the scene. Eventually, the assailants dismissed themselves, and the event lasted just for the day. As from then until now, life has gone back to normal at Hillbrow Community Health Centre, and foreign nationals resumed accessing medical care services as usual.
records.who_attacked: Foreign national patients on queues, at Hillbrow Health Community Centre Premises
records.response: Not sure. But the SAPS were physically present on the premises when the incident took place

records.name: City of Johannesburg evicts Migrant Informal Traders selectively
records.description:
At around 10h00 of Thursday, 13/04/2023, while they less expected it, migrant informal traders, trading on Delvers street and Jeppe street were approached by a crowd of city officials led by the MMC for security and safety. Among them were the City MMC for Safety and Security, JMPD, City Street Patrollers of the City of Johannesburg and some Councillors. This happened on the same date and time that was on the poster sent by CoJ inviting the public to a cleaning and crime prevention operation. Unfortunately the operation only targeted streets where the vast majority of informal traders are non-South Africans. And even on those streets, only the goods of non-South Africans were confiscated or destroyed regardless of whether they operate with a licenses or not. 
Those who tried to resist on the basis that they operate their trading in accordance with the laws of the country and the municipal by-laws, were simply arrested. It appears that confiscated stalls of  traders on Delvers streets were returned to their owners but their stocks were nowhere to be found. 
This operation is premised on the assumption that informal traders are the ones that are littering the streets of Johannesburg and are also harbouring criminals.
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: Not that I am aware of so far

records.name: Refugees and asylum seekers attacked again in Burgersfort
records.description: After 6 weeks of relative calm, refugees and asylum seekers who were surviving on selling goods and services in and around the main taxi rank situated in Extension 10, Burgersfort, got attacked again. Initially, it is alleged that they were attacked based on wrong accusations that they were selling drugs but the accusations could not be substantiated. After 2 weeks, when the accusers (a group of locals under the leadership of long distance taxi drivers) realised that the accusations were not true, they allowed the refugee and asylum seeker traders back to trade again. Few weeks later the traders were surprised by a mob of about 30 people, moving from one gazebo to another, from one container to the next destroying all what was inside and telling refugees to go back to their respective home countries as they are taking business opportunities from locals. The matter was subsequently reported to Burgersfort Police station but the police allegedly refused to open a case or offer any other assistance.
records.who_attacked: Refugees and asylum seekers and their informal businesses
records.duration: The whole morning, more than 4 hours
records.response: Not that we are aware of

records.name: Pregnant Woman Turned Away from Accessing Prenatal Care from Jeppe and Hillbrow Clinics
records.description: A Zimbabwean pregnant woman who suspects she is eight months pregnant was turned away from Jeppe and Hillbrow clinics because of a lack of documentation. She has not received any prenatal medical attention as a result, and nurses declined to sign her up for prenatal care. The nurses told her that South Africans no longer have medical resources, and she must go back and give birth in her country of origin. This denied service is taking place despite the Gauteng High Court ruling in April that pregnant women and children under 6 years must have access to free public health services irrespective of nationality and document status.
records.who_attacked: Foreign pregnant woman denied prenatal health care
records.response: Section 27 is considering launching a hotline to track such cases for intervention.

records.name: Extortion of migrant shops is rife in Cato Crest
records.description:
In April 2023, two migrant barbers and one local customer were shot while at work in their barber container. The investigating officer later advised the owner to withdraw the case for his own safety after he filed a criminal complaint against the perpetrators at the Cato Crest police station.
Later on, he started receiving messages of threats telling him to either pay at least R1000 per month as protection fees or they would attack him, his workers, and anyone who tried to get his hair done in the shop. Since May 2023, the barber shop owner has decided to start paying and is continuing to pay even now. There are two businesses right next to his two containers: an Ethiopian spaza shop and a Pakistani-owned cellphone repairer. These two refused to pay and are constantly attacked, to the extent that the cellphone repairer has decided to close his shop and the Ethiopian is considering doing the same. Shops run or owned by South Africans in the same area are not required to pay these protection fees and are not doing so. When one of the shop owners went to report to the local police station, he was told to either cooperate or leave the area for his own safety because the perpetrators are very dangerous and do not hesitate to hurt anyone who stands in their way. The police officer also added that, after all, the extortionists were also trying to survive.
records.who_attacked: Migrant barbers, cellphone repairers and shop operators
records.response: No response. The police says there is nothing they can do and encouraged the victims to cooperate with perpetrators

records.name: Foreign mothers forced to pay nurses to take their babies home
records.description:
According to online news articles, pregnant foreign nationals in need of healthcare services have been forced to pay certain amounts of fees by nurses at Tambo Memorial Hospital on the East Rand, Johannesburg, who have allegedly demanded payments from the mothers-to-be in exchange for access to birthing facilities and assistance. This is despite a high court decision last month to uphold a ruling on free healthcare for women and young children who are foreign nationals. The women said they were held hostage in the hospital for hours and even days until someone from outside arrived with cash to pay the nurses so that they and their newborn babies could leave. The victims allege that the nurses have this power over them because they are undocumented. If they don’t pay up, the nurses threaten to call the authorities. One such woman who gave birth at the hospital a week ago informed the media that, after her baby was born, the nurses had refused to release her until they received R700, an amount she simply did not have. The woman informed the media that she had been attending antenatal care at Boksburg North Clinic before being referred to the hospital because there were some complications with her pregnancy. She didn’t expect to be held hostage there until someone came to bail her out. She alleged that nurses have to be paid directly in order for a patient to be discharged from the maternity ward. The amount depends on how wealthy one looks to them. The victim claimed that she paid R700 because that’s all the money she could raise from friends.
Source - https://www.news24.com/citypress/news/foreign-mothers-forced-to-pay-nurses-to-take-their-babies-home-20230604#:~:text=Pregnant%20foreign%20nationals%20in%20need,to%20birthing%20facilities%20and%20assistance.
records.who_attacked: Foreign national mothers of new born babies
records.response: Gauteng health department alleged to be investigating the allegations of bribery of mothers with newborns at the facility.

records.name: Another Xenophobic attack against foreign traders at Bara Taxi Rank again.
records.description: It was on Sunday, May 4, 2023, a bit before 17h00, that a crowd of a few hundred people, allegedly belonging to "Operation Dudula", stormed the rank and started attacking foreign traders there and looting their stock. They accuse them of being illegal immigrants who cannot be allowed to run any income-generating activity in South Africa. More than 50 foreigners, predominantly Mozambicans, Malawians, and Zimbabweans, were trading at Bara taxi rank, including only 2 Nigerians. They were paying monthly protection fees to the rank's management, who promised to intervene in case they got attacked. However, victims reported that no one intervened when they were being attacked. The police came later on, but instead of helping the victims, they instead chased them, telling them that they were illegal immigrants and were not supposed to trade there in the first place.
records.duration: More than an hour or so
records.response: The police came but instead of helping the victims, they were busy chasing foreigners away from the rank. The matter has been reported to KAAX (KOpanang Africa Against Xenophobia) and arre considering legal assistance to victims.

records.name: Masiphumelele: Foreign national business owners under deadly threats by a new syndicate of protection fees extortioners
records.description:
In Masiphumelele township, there are reports that members of a new gang of protection fees extortioners has been entering tuck-shops, and instructing foreign shop owners that the monthly protection fee must be paid to them (the new syndicate) and no longer to the old collectors (the old syndicate).  The new syndicates made their first appearance and introduction to foreign national business owners in Masiphumelele community by middle of May 2023. Reportedly, there is an estimate of 65 – 70 tuck-shops/spazas across the whole Masiphumelele township, and all of them are exclusively operated by foreign nationals. According to comments from local SA citizens, residents of Masiphumelele community, there was a community consensus following the nationwide first waves of xenophobia in 2008, whereby local residents of Masiphumelele community decided to hand over tuck-shops and spazas related business exclusively to foreign nationals, and opted to develop properties (their plots) into additional flats/units and rent them out to foreign nationals, for business and residential purposes. Since then, it seems that local citizens, owners of properties/houses across Masiphumelele community have been enjoying monthly renting fees from foreign nationals, as the latter struggle with the “forced consent”, related to the famous monthly protection fee, imposed to them by a deadly syndicate of “easy-money” makers (extortioners).

In June 2016 there were reports that 16 shops belonging to mostly Ethiopians were looted by the new gang in attempt to prove the old guy was not as effective as they (new gang are). The looted shops are reported to have recovered and resumed normal business. The looting is said was a perceived warning to shop owners Both gangs have had violent confrontations among each other which has resulted in loss of life. Community members for the shop owners to consider switching to the new gang from the old one, or pay monthly protection  fees to both. Masiphumelele foreign shop owners are said to have reached a consensus should the two gangs fail to reach an agreement, they would rather pay protection fees to both gangs, than to risk their lives.
   
The shop operators have substantial evidence (video clips from surveillance cameras) of every human movement that transpires inside their shops, but they indicated that they cannot even report these situations to the South African Police Services (SAPS), because they were warned by members of the gangs, that should anything about their (gang members) activities or personal particulars leak to the SAPS and/or any other law enforcement services, they would come back and shoot them. Hence, foreign national business owners, across Masiphumelele community have unanimously taken a decision “not to report” anything related to protection fees and/or any other form of extortion exerted on them.
records.who_attacked: Businesses owned & operated by Ethiopia Nationals (Oromos)
records.response: No

records.name: Informal traders attacked at Jabulani mall
records.description: On June 6, 2023, reports were received that informal traders operating at Jabulani Mall in Soweto were attacked. It is alleged that local residents were responsible for the removal of foreign nationals trading outside Jabulani Mall. Residents claimed they were fighting the undocumented foreign nationals as some of them allegedly sold drugs to young people ekasi. The traders watched from a distance as fuming community members looted and destroyed their goods. It is alleged that some traders were beaten up, punched, and kicked. https://www.snl24.com/dailysun/news/street-traders-at-jabulani-mall-forced-to-pack-and-go-20230608
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: On Saturday, the 17th of June, 2023, Somali business owners in Philippi forced to close their shops
records.description:
On Saturday, June 17th of June, 2023, Somali tuck shop operators in Philippi were forced to close up for the day by a new extortion syndicate. The shopkeepers say they are already paying protection money to another gang and are caught in the middle. Somali shopkeepers closed their shops for almost 12 hours on Saturday. They say a new criminal syndicate turned up demanding that they pay a “protection fee” if they wished to continue trading. A group of men in a white Avanza visited numerous shops, demanding protection money – between R1,000 and R2,000 a month – according to GroundUp. Besides the inconvenience of the closure of the shops on Saturday, which left residents struggling to find basic groceries, people fear that a turf war will erupt between the criminal syndicates. A Somali shop owner told GroundUp the new gang told them to close for the day and they complied. Somali shop keepers are now caught in the middle of two gangs and feel their lives are at risk unless they pay fees to both gangs. Such extortion rackets are seldom reported to police as shopkeepers fear retaliation.
https://www.groundup.org.za/article/somali-shop-owners-fear-turf-war-between-extortion-gangs/
records.who_attacked: Businesses owned and operated by Somali Nationals
records.response: Local Government authorities;  community leaders (foreign nationals & locals); and public safety authorities/Law enforcement services intervened.

records.name: Local community at Marabastad  resists Dudula march against Migrants
records.description: The march in Marabastad was unsuccessful for protesters who wanted to get rid of foreign nationals. The first march took place at the June 2023. The first incident started at around 10 am and lasted until 11 am. Protesters wearing green uniforms and accompanied by police chanted, "Foreigners must go, foreigners must go!"
