According to a Malawian salesperson in a clothing shop in Marabastad, the protestors were checking documents of foreign nationals. The Malawian salesperson lives in Pretoria west and he shared that foreigners who own businesses in the area panicked and closed their shops. The witness stated that the protestors were armed and the incident took place around  Boom street and Jerusalem street. A week later, a Congolese victim who owns a barbar shop near the taxi rank said that he was terrorised by the protestors, they (protestors) complained about his tent and he was subsequently arrested by the police for being accused of  using'' weapons'' (scissors and razors)... which  are kits for cutting techniques in a salon. The Congolese victim was taken to the police and was kept for many hours  and only released around 3pm. The protestors went to different shops harassing people and giving them an ultimatum to vacate the place, using a Megaphone and promising to come back said another witness from Mozambique selling fruits and vegetables on the same street the incident took place. The incident left migrants living in fear as every morning when they come to sale, they are scared and expect the worst to happen. Fortunately,  a group of residents, Marshalls and taxi drivers who did not support the protest came to the defense of the foreign business owners and told the protestors"Dudula", to never come back again to disturb their businesses.
records.who_attacked: Migrants who are  traders and street vendors at Marabastad
records.duration: It lasted over a period of two weeks
records.response: Local residents, Marshalls and taxi drivers  came to the defense of the foreign business owners and told the protestors"Dudula", to never come back again.
records.other_text: the incident was shared in the work group

records.name: Ethiopian shop owners in Diepsloot  targeted by the criminals and  police officers.
records.description:
The protest started  weeks ago. The community members in Diepsloot were accusing migrants who are mostly business owners originally from Ethiopia, Bangladesh and Somalia of causing criminal activities.  Shop owners contribute R 300 per month to pay for protection services. The money is collected every month in all the shops. Around 300 shops are owned by migrants in the area. Shop owners stated that they contribute when there are funerals, give food parcels to vulnerable families but the community members still complain about them not being involved in protests. Many shops were still closed at the time of investigation.  Around 4 shops were looted. Some restaurants were also closed  by authorities. Migrants are not feeling safe in the area said one witness. The witness also added that they (foreign nationals) are not criminals and they contribute in creating jobs but they face challenges of documentation. The Department of Home Affairs is not renewing their asylum seeker permits on time. The issue of documentation has affected them and their businesses, the witness said. As a result, the police are targeting and arresting them and will release them only when they pay plus or minus R5000.  Business owners  looked miserable, and powerless in this community. Foreign shop owners have also reported that some of their brothers were killed in this community during robberies that took place, and no one will get arrested for the crime, instead they will come back and ask them for documents.
https://www.groundup.org.za/article/immigrants-in-diepsloot-say-they-are-made-scapegoats-for-crime/
records.duration: The violence lasted several days, but the harassment still  ongoing.
records.response: Police visibility is there day and night, not to protect the migrants mostly (Ethiopians , Bangladesh , and Somalians ),but to arrest them, knowing that 80% have expired documents not because they want but because home affairs is not renewing their asylum.

records.name: Hermanus residents turn on foreigners after body of woman found dumped along road
records.description: The lifeless and mutilated body of a South African young woman was discovered wrapped in a plastic bag in Still Street, which connects the Zwelihle informal settlement to Hermanus, on the morning of June 27, 2023. The police reported that the body was dumped after the deceased was raped and mutilated. At first, reports received alleged that a Zimbabwean truck driver was responsible for the heinous act, but the blame was shifted to a Malawian who was living in the community. The Malawian national was taken in for questioning by the police, which resulted in angry community members (young people) burning his (the accused's) house after suspecting him of committing the crime. This, in turn, resulted in community members turning on foreign nationals living in the area and demanding that they leave the area. With the assistance of the Mayor, approximately 600 migrants were evacuated to safe locations in the Overstrand area. Six weeks after the incident took place, foreign nationals still living and operating businesses in the area have not dared to open up for trading as they live in fear of being attacked.
records.response: Mayor assisted the displaced and police visibility to ensure stability in the area.

records.name: Refugee Flea Market Traders taken hostage by Mandeni taxi association
records.description: On Friday, June 30, 2023, at around 05:30, individuals identifying themselves as Mandeni Taxi Association members stopped a bakkie carrying three refugee market vendors just past the Tongaat toll gate. They compelled the three refugees and their vehicle to return to Durban, where they were held captive for several hours until the rank manager was able to negotiate their release. The three refugees were accused of disobeying the directive to transport goods to the Mandeni and eSikhaleni markets in taxis rather than private vehicles. The victims attempted to persuade the perpetrators that their vehicle was their own and that they were transporting their own goods, but they were instead accused of undermining the taxi association and transporting goods without licences. They were also informed that they are not alone, as others slept in Mandeni yesterday to avoid taking taxis. They (the refugees) were subsequently released by the rank manager on warning that should they continue to undermine the association by using their private cars to go to the market, they would be hurt in the days to come. It is reported that locals are not subject to the same conditions. The Association focuses on Durban because that is where most migrants who go to Mandeni Market live.
records.who_attacked: Refufgee informal market traders en route to Mandeni market
records.response: Many community leaders were informed and when they asked to alert the police, the victims refused saying that it will only worsen the situation

records.name: A Swazi citizen harassed by a police officer at Maydon Wharf terminal in Durban
records.description: A  54 years old truck driver from Swaziland was stopped by a police officer on the 2nd of July while driving along Maydon Wharf in Durban. The police officer asked him to provide his driving licence and passport which he presented to him. The driver's passport has a valid stamp which was expire at the end of July 2023. The police officer told him to pay R3500 otherwise he will arrest him. The truck driver and police then drove to Sidney Road where they stopped and called the truck driver's boss as the driver did not have money. The boss negotiated the fee and they settled on R1500.  The money was paid  via  e-wallet using the police officer's number said the victim.  The victim has records of the exchange of messages and proof of payment.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: The'' Bree Operation" by Violence turned into attacks on migrants
records.description: The John Foster policeman are alleged tp have entered Bree taxi rank on July 5, 2023, looking for illicit cigarettes, fire arms, and illegal goods. The policeman targeted only migrant shops. The violence occurred while police officers were breaking into people's homes, demanding money, and taking inventory of the goods. According to one of the victims, a Nigerian who owns a shop inside the Bree taxi rank, the policeman were aggressive, and were pushing stuff around. As a result, the police broke his pool table. Another victim said that he was arrested for no reason , he added that he did not have any illegal good in his shop, he only sells groceries, but was still was taken to the police station and was released the second day. The foreign shop owners in Bree taxi rank are still traumatized by this incident and looked very confused as they did not understand why they were treated like that by the policeman.
records.who_attacked: Foreigner  shop owners were targeted and attacked by Police
records.response: No response reported as law enforcement was responsible for the attacks

records.name: Foreigner  street vendors in Malvern allegedly intimidated by ''Operation Dudula ''members
records.description: On the 20th of July 2023, after days of intimidation, the street vendors who are mostly foreigners from Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia, and DRC received a letter from Operation Dudula Jules branch, giving the street vendors an ultimatum to vacate and stop selling outside Shoprite in Jules street in Malvern otherwise they would burn their goods. This situation was incited by Shoprite Managers who decided to use an organisation with Xenophobic tendencies instead of reporting their concerns to the relevant law enforcement. The foreigner street vendors have been operating outside shoprite in Jules street for more than 10 years, selling used clothes, vegetables, African food  to take care of their families. It is alleged that the foreign street vendors are still operating in front of the shoprite premises and Operation Dudula came to collect an amount equivalent to R25 from each vendor.
records.duration: The intimidation lasted a few days
records.response: No, the vendors tried to negotiate with the shoprite managers the very same day but they (foreign street vendors) were turned away.

records.name: Two migrant Uber eat drivers warned to stop working and go back to their home country or else...
records.description: On Saturday 5/8/2023 around 19h30, 2 refugee males were in their car delivering food as one of them, the driver, does that in the evening after work to supplement his income. While driving on Lena Ahrens road in Glenwood, they noticed a white double cabin bakkie behind them. When they approached the red light at intersection with Che Guevara road, the bakkie stopped in front of them and blocked them (the two refugees) from moving. Two boys came out of the bakkie leaving 3 others inside, armed with long knives. They threatened the driver, showing both refugees the long knives and told them that they had been warned several times but do not listen and continue working for Uber, taking their jobs. The perpetrators told the victims to stop working for Uber immediately; otherwise whatever happens to the refugees, they should not turn around and say the were not warned before hand. The perpetrators went and joined the other 3 who were in the bakkie and left without taking anything from the victims nor even attempting to damage their car. The victims were left shaking and traumatised. They subsequently went to Umbilo Police station to report the incident and requested that the police accompany them to the crime scene but the police said they are under staffed and since the victims were not harmed there is nothing they (the police) could do.
records.who_attacked: 2 refugee males who were delivering food for Uber Eats
records.response: No, the matter was reported to Umbilo Police station and a request was made to accompany the victims to the crime scene but the police refused, arguing that they are under staffed.

records.name: A grade 10 learner was brutally attacked and beaten at school by her classmate and a school teacher
records.description:
On Tuesday the 29th of August, a Congolese girl ,who is 17 years old and in grade 10 at a technical school in Krugersdorp was attacked by her classmate and a school teacher who is the mother to the perpetrator's classmate. During the first break the victim was stopped by her classmate; the classmate who is a South African told the victim that she was carrying a school bag that was not hers. The two pupils entered into an argument concerning the school bag, and the argument resulted  in a complete quarrel between the two pupils. 

After the second break, when the learners were changing classes, the victim decided to go to see the principal to report about the incident. On her way to the reception office, the victim  saw her classmate picking up a brick and a stick, accompanied by a school teacher, who is her mother. The classmate was approaching with rage to attack the Congolese pupil. The learners in the school started  screaming while watching the scene. The victim was insulted and beaten up. Other students were watching and took videos of the incident. Others tried to intervene and pull off the teacher on top of  the victim. The victim had braids on her head which were pulled off by the math teacher. 

When the fight ended, the victim was told that she is not going to do anything about the case because she as  is a foreigner. The school teacher involved in the incident informed the victim that her husband is a senior police officer and  that the victim's claim was not going to be heard anyway.  The next day on the 30th of August, the  parents of the victim went to the school. On that day, the victim was in severe pain, her hands were swollen, she could not manage to  attend classes. The parents were surprised to learn that  the principal of the school had not inform the HOD about the incident.

The victim's parents decided to report the case to the police and the victim was taken for check ups at the hospital. The victim missed classes and tests not only because of pain but the principal suspended her because of misconduct. The family was not supported, they felt discriminated against.  The situation became worse after the arrest of the school teacher. She was kept in jail and was released the following day. The victim stopped going to school and was seeking help, calling organisations, going to the education department.  After a few days, the case turned against the  victim. The victim's  family  received a letter from DCSM ( disciplinary committee for serious misconduct ) saying that the victim was the one who hurt the other learner. The principal told the parents of the victim to look for lawyers and a short hearing date notice for one day was given to them. 

The victim's parents were traumatised about this situation, and fearful not having any one to stand for them because there are migrants. It is reported that on the day of the hearing, no one showed up. The videos of the incident went viral on social media and luckily the victim went back to school again but she said that her family is not safe any more.
records.duration: A once off event that escalated to  arrest and threats
records.response: The police intervention was noticed and  Krugersdorp social worker's referred the victim's family to different NGOs.

records.name: Migrant traders live in fear after being threatened by locals who evicted them a year ago
records.description: Two months ago, the Chamber of Informal Economy in Pietermaritzburg, an affiliate or partner of Operation Dudula in evicting migrant informal traders more than a year ago, lost its leader. She was shot and killed in a very mysterious way, and so far, no one knows who killed her. However, considering the role that she played in violently evicting migrant informal traders from their trading spots last year, members of the chamber and indeed many other local informal traders who are anti-migrant informal traders started pointing fingers at migrants, accusing them of being behind the death of their leader. On Tuesday, August 29, 2023, they had a big meeting around a taxi rank situated on Pietermaritz streets, after which they started threatening migrant informal traders, saying that they would be evicted and beaten again very soon. These threats were based on the fact that a significant number of evicted migrant informal traders are back on the streets, trading again The victims, who are now living in fear of another impending violent xenophobic attack, have taken the threats made by the chamber members very seriously.
records.who_attacked: Migrant informal traders in the CBD in general
records.response: No because the matter was not reported to the police

records.name: A Lesotho national strangled to death in Lutzville
records.description: On the 2nd of September 2023 in the middle of the night time in Lutzville near a shebeen. A group of youngest strangled to death a Lesotho national. This was in the informal settlement Mbeki square. According to the station commandant one of the perpetrators was arrested and still in custody.  This kind of incident has happening regularly in that specific area to the foreign nationals as attested by a witness. It is reported that the perpetrators, who are youngsters addicted to drugs single out foreign nationals to rob them. Some of the tactics the perpetrators employ to identify foreign nationals are to ask victims questions in isiXhosa and isiZulu and when an individual is not able to respond they rob them.
records.response: The police did intervene and arrested one of the perpetrators who is currently in custody

records.name: Migrant traders at Soldiers way flea market are once again forced to pay protection fees
records.description: Since late 2021, migrant flea market traders at Soldiers Way have been required to pay protection fees. To put a stop to this, a group of local youth banded together in the guise of "security officers" to protect the market and its traders. They claimed to be willing and capable of protecting all flea market vendors from extortionists. It was then agreed that all market traders, South Africans and migrants alike, would each pay R5 each every Sunday as a fee to those security officers. This was done under the supervision of the market committee. However, only two months later, South African traders began to refuse to pay, claiming that they saw no reason to continue paying because their safety was not jeopardised. The security officers then decided to unilaterally increase the amount to R10 and force all migrant traders to pay so as to compensate for the loss from South African traders. Unfortunately, no one wants to intervene, and most victims believe it is because only migrants are affected. The matter has already been reported to the municipal manager in charge of informal trade in Durban Central, but so far no action has been taken.
records.duration: It has been going on for quite some times now, just that we needed time to establish whether only migrants were targeted.
records.response: So far not yet.

records.name: A Nigerian was beaten to death by police during a raid in Johannesburg CBD
records.description: On the 15th of July, around 10 a.m, a Nigerian man died. The policeman beat him after arresting him. A few hours later, the Nigerian was declared dead at the hands of the South African police. The incident took place at the corner of Kerk and Delvers streets. The victim was estimated to be 40 years old; he was searched, and nothing suspicious or illegal was found. The victim usually came to town to assist his friend, who is a vendor selling cell phone accessories; the victim was supposed to look after his friend's shop while the friend was out looking for stock. On the day of the incident, the victim was still wandering around town after completing his duty when police caught up with him. He then panicked and started running, alerting everyone that they should close their shops. But the police started chasing the victim. The victim ran and was caught, beaten severely for running away. According to the witnesses, the victim was calling for help by telling the police that he was not feeling well, but the police officer ignored him and threw him in the police van. Inside the police van, two migrants from Malawi, who were arrested for being undocumented, witnessed the brutality of the police towards the victim. Apparently, the victim was suffocated inside the police van. The police tightened the victim's hands; the victim could not defend himself, then the police covered the victim's head with plastic. The two Malawians' community leaders shared the incident, as the two men who witnessed everything that happened inside the police van are afraid. Both men are undocumented and are afraid of being detained again.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Malawians families forcibly evicted in houses in Mayfair by Operation
records.description: On September 16th, a number of men surrounded the occupants of two houses on 7th Avenue in Mayfair. The men claimed that they were Operation Dudula. When the migrants asked their motive, the members of Operation Dudula said that they were there as citizens to take back their houses and added that they didn't want to see Malawians and Zimbabweans occupying houses in Mayfair any more. The victim who reported this incident is a 54-year-old man from Malawi. He was living in that house with his three children and wife of more than 15 years. The house had five bedrooms, and the owner is a 60-year-old lady from India. The harassment started a few days before the incident, and the residents did not take it seriously because of the period that they had been in these houses. The residents started to take it seriously when they saw that the perpetrators were increasing in number every day when they came to harass the residents. Operation Dudula returned the following day, September 17th, with a larger group of men and women singing isiZulu songs. The victims called their community leaders, who then called the police around 8 p.m. The police arrived on the scene to mediate peace, but the perpetrators were already inside the houses, beating up the residents. According to reports, seven Malawians were seriously injured and taken to the hospital the same night. On the 18th of September, Operation Dudula members returned in large numbers, apparently around 50 people carrying sticks and stones, and this time, the victims were overpowered and gave up. The perpetrator entered and occupied the houses, burned and stole Malawians' belongings, suits, shoes, and so on. This act is xenophobic because not all residents of those two addresses were evicted. South Africans and Indians remained in the houses, and 56 people were evicted, all Malawians. Families who have been evicted are currently sleeping in Mayfair Station, with a few moving to Gardens City.
records.response: The police responded trying to make peace but failed to protect the migrants

records.name: Police officers in Diepsloot breaking into shops owned by Ethiopians at night  , collecting  money, goods from  shop keepers  and arresting them .
records.description: The Diepsloot neighbourhood was alerted to a concerning noise at approximately 11 p.m. on September 23rd, when police officers broke into stores containing heavy metals. According to the victims, money up to R5,000 was taken from each store. Not only did the police collect money and cigarettes, but they also arrested shopkeepers without documentation and took them to the Lindela Repatriation Centre. It is further reported that out of the nationalities that own or run spaza shops in the areas, Ethiopians are the ones targeted.
records.response: No interventions were reported

records.name: Foreign- owned spaza shops  in Soweto threatened after 5 children died from suspected food poisoning bought from the shops
records.description: On the 3rd of October 2023,  Operation Dudula and community members in  Naledi, Soweto revolted against foreign- owned  spaza shops after suspected food poisoning consumed by 4 children. Community members have called for all foreign shops to be shut down. The tension is  escalating and  spaza shops are targeted and shutdown by the anti- migrant movement.  The investigations are still ongoing  and the cause of the death unknown but  the community blames the shop owners. Currently more than 6 shops are  been closed.
records.response: Police intervened to try and calm the situation

records.name: An Asylum seeker arrested by immigration officers in Vryheid while waiting for th renewal of his document
records.description: An immigration officer detained an Ivorian asylum seeker on Church Street on October 5 on the grounds that he was an unlawful immigrant. The victim then produced his expired permit and the automatic response for his permit renewal from the Department of Home Affairs, but the immigration officer, who seemingly was acting on a tip-off, insisted that the electronic renewal of refugee documents had been discontinued. The victim then called his leader, who additionally assists refugees with document renewals. When the refugee leader attempted to engage with the immigration officer, the officer rudely responded that the refugee leader was undermining him. The victim was then brought to a police station and held there. The following day, the leader went to see the head of immigration in Vryheid, who, after verification, confirmed that the document was genuine. He then sent correspondence to the police station to get the victim released. The victim was only released at 15:00 the following day.
records.response: Yes, the head of immigration in the area was contacted and intervened to get the victim released

records.name: Congolese Community in Zeerust,  in the North West  Province, attacked and severely beaten by  local community members.
records.description:
Non-nationals living in Zeerust, mostly Congolese nationals, experienced significant challenges with their businesses being affected due to xenophobic attacks that commenced on November 5, 2023. This came about as a consequence of Congolese nationals being held accountable for the alleged rape of a young girl by a drug addict from Lekubu village. The individual, who was accused of the rape incident before succumbing to a fatal beating, claimed he acted under the influence of drugs sold by a Congolese individual. This statement triggered an attack on the Congolese, starting with the leaders and extending to others. Fourteen individuals were reported injured, some hospitalised for body injuries, including a pregnant woman. The pregnant woman and her husband were publicly undressed and beaten in front of their children. The situation remains tense, and police intervention in Zeerust has been ineffective in protecting the victims. The Congolese community was instructed to close businesses, posing a challenging situation as many rely on them for their daily income.

On November 7th, the Congolese community attempted to engage with officials and locals, which unfortunately exacerbated the situation. The local community refused dialogue, escalating the violence by invading houses and destroying property. A witness claimed that the locals' acts were motivated by rage, anger, and hatred towards migrants. By November 9th, fearing for their lives, Congolese residents sought refuge in a church, which was subsequently vandalised and destroyed. A 20-year-old boy narrowly escaped being killed; he was undressed, tied to an electrical board, and nearly burned, but was rescued in the nick of time. Those who saved him were also attacked, resulting in three injuries. The Congolese community in Zeerust was appealing for assistance from UNHCR and other NGOs, expressing a profound sense of insecurity. MSF and SAHRC delegates went on the ground to assess the situation and provide medical assistance where it was required. MSF also donated food items, such as packets of maize meal and green vegetables. UNHCR engaged Future Families to carry out evaluations of the most vulnerable individuals in order to provide additional assistance.

records.name: A foreign national vender at  Baragwanath  taxi rank almost got burned alive by  angry Dudula Members  in Soweto
records.description: On October 7, 2023, around 3 pm, nearly 500 Dudula members raided a small market under the Baragwanath taxi rank. An order was issued for all foreign vendors selling shoes to close their stalls and leave. As concerned vendors were packing their stock, a Nigerian vendor caught the attention of the Dudula members. They seized all his bags and began to walk away with them. The victim followed the Dudula members to reclaim his stock but was told he wasn't allowed to sell there or anywhere else in the country as a foreigner. He was also advised to conduct business in his home country, Nigeria, rather than in South Africa. During the victim's attempt to retrieve his bags, which contained his stock, he was pushed, beaten, and doused with petrol in an attempt to set him and his eight bags of shoes on fire. Fortunately, bystanders intervened just in time to prevent the victim from being killed. The victim reported the incident to the Diepkloof police station but never received a case number. His bags, valued at R8500, were stolen that day.
records.response: None, only few vendors around the market .

records.name: Foreign Spaza shops owners in Delmas, Mpumalanga subjected to Extortion
records.description:
Since the reported case of child food poisoning in Soweto in October 2023, locals have targeted foreign spaza shop owners, forced them to close their businesses, and accused them of doing things like selling expired goods, residing in their businesses, not hiring South African citizens, and violating health regulations. This has resulted in foreign spaza shop owners being subject to extortion, looting, intimidation, harassment, and threats from some community members and some municipality officials in various provinces.  As a consequence, it resulted in the closing of spaza shops owned by foreign nationals. In Delmas, more than 121 shops were closed. and 40 shops in town also closed, including one shop confiscated with stock and equipment still inside.  On Saturday, November 11, 2023, a witness reported that the stores opened following the payment. Unfortunately, this didn't last long. After two hours, a group of community members came and attacked the shop owners. According to reports, two vehicles belonging to Ethiopian nationals were damaged, three shops were burned down, and four Ethiopian nationals were brutally assaulted (one was still hospitalised at the time of the report).  According to the Ethiopian community in Delmas, the attacks were not justified as shop owners complied with South African rules and regulations pertaining to business operations, and they believe they were attacked by criminal opportunists residing in the community.

On November 15, 2023, a group of stakeholders convened a meeting with the aim of finding a solution. The stakeholders present during the meeting included the UNHCR, the Department of Home Affairs (DHA), the foreign national shop owners affected by the issue, representatives from the mayor's office, and the Refugee Led Network. 

Some of the resolutions from the meeting were that, following concerns expressed by the department regarding undocumented foreign nationals, the DHA would embark on a paper-marking exercise to authenticate all documents used by foreign nationals. A sticker will be placed on all checked documents used by foreign nationals in the area to verify that they are indeed legal in the country and have the authority to conduct business. It was agreed by stakeholders in the meeting that there should be wider engagements with all stakeholders in the area, including the local community members, traditional leaders, religious leaders, and other relevant departments such as Health, Labour, and Community Safety in an attempt to find an amicable solution to the attacks in the area.  

The situation still remains tense and volatile because just as the meeting was about to adjourn, as stakeholders were discussing a date for the next meeting to facilitate the opening of shops in the area, the ring leader of the group attacking foreign owned shops barged into the meeting and started hurling insults, threatening those who were present in the meeting, especially Ethiopians and accusing them of being illegal in South Africa with no rights to conduct business. The leader further stated that the deadline for foreign shop owners to vacate the area was 20 November 2023. He reinforced that the group is not willing to negotiate with anyone including the Mayors office and the SAPS.  He added that by the said set date, foreigners conducting business in the area will be allowed to depart with all their belongings and and families. Failure to do so will result in more attacks.
records.response: Police arrived but did nothing.

records.name: Non- nationals Spaza Shops Owners fear for their safety if they do not comply with extortion in Zwelihle Hermanus
records.description: In Zwelihle Township, Hermanus, a group of foreign-national spaza shop owners are raising concerns about the extortion that some thugs and some dishonest police officers have imposed on them. In return for their safety and operating freely, a fixed amount of R2000 or R3000 has been asked to be paid each month. According to the victims, if you disobey the request, you risk losing your life or having to close down the business. This is really a nightmare for the victims, as sometimes they have to pay the same amount twice a month, as the first payment will go to the thugs and another one to the corrupt police officers.
records.who_attacked: A group of foreign shop owners
records.response: No

records.name: An asylum seeker assaulted at Jozini Police Station
records.description: On Friday, October 13, 2023, around 14:00, a Congolese asylum seeker accompanied a new asylum seeker to the local police station in Jozini to obtain an affidavit. This affidavit would be used while waiting for an appointment date at the Department of Home Affairs to apply for asylum. Upon arrival, they encountered a police captain who refused to assist them, claiming the new asylum seeker was in the country illegally. The Congolese asylum seeker attempted to persuade the captain to change his mind. During this interaction, the captain asked to see the Congolese asylum seeker's own asylum document, only to discover that it had expired. The asylum seeker presented his application for renewal, explaining that he had fulfilled his part and was awaiting the electronic delivery of his renewed document, as had been the practice since the lockdown. Enraged, the police captain pulled the asylum seeker into the station and physically assaulted him, hurling insults and questioning why he was in the country and when he planned to return to his homeland. Upon learning of the situation, members of the refugee community in Jozini rushed to the police station. They found the captain preparing to leave, as he was scheduled to be off duty for the next three days. Fearing that the asylum seeker would remain in police custody until the captain's return, they negotiated for his release. The asylum seeker was finally released around 21:00 after paying a sum of R2000 to the captain.
records.response: Community members assisted with payment of R2000

records.name: An asylum seeker is wrongfully arrested in Mkuze and only released on bail after spending 10 weeks in custody
records.description: On Saturday, October 14, 2023, around 09:00, a Congolese asylum seeker who was awaiting the renewal of his document was approached by members of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in Mkuze. He presented his expired asylum permit, his application form for renewal, and the automatic response he received as proof that the Department of Home Affairs had received his application. Despite this, the police did not believe him and decided to arrest him, stating they needed to verify the documents with the Department of Home Affairs. After spending two weeks in police cells with five other Congolese asylum seekers, he appeared before a magistrate. He was released on bail on November 27, 2023, after spending more than 10 weeks in detention.
records.duration: The victim spent more than 10 weeks in jail
records.response: Mkhuze is a small and isolated rural town in North of Kwazulu Natal, far from organisations that would have assisted.

records.name: Seven Migrants from Mozambique detained unlawfully for more than 3 months
records.description: In an operation targeting undocumented immigrants in the Umkhanyakude district municipality, seven immigrants from Mozambique were arrested on Saturday, October 14, 2023, in Mkuze. They were asked by police and immigration officers to produce their documents, which they did. Although the visas in their passports were still valid, they were arrested because the officers suspected the visas might be fake or obtained fraudulently. The officers needed to verify the authenticity of the visas. The victims spent two weeks in police cells before appearing before a magistrate. Despite this appearance, they continued to be remanded due to delays in verifying their visas caused by power outages and internet connection issues. The victims were eventually released after three months and were ordered to leave the country because their visas had expired by then.
records.duration: The victims spent more than 3 months in custody
records.response: No. They appeared in Libombo Magistrate court 2 weeks after their arrest but continued being remanded due to power outages or internet connetion problems.

records.name: Community raids foreign owned spaza shops in Vredefort after death of 2 children allegedly by food poisonning.
records.description: On 18th October, in Mokwallo, near Vredefort in Free State, community members raided foreign-owned spaza shops checking the quality of food sold and their expiry dates, after two kids died allegedly after eating snacks from one of foreign-owned spaza shop in the area. Reports received do not indicate the nationality of the shop owner but the person being interviewed by the journalist in the video below appears to be a Somali or Ethiopian national. In the same interview, the owner of the spaza shop from which the kids allegedly bought the snacks is denying the sale of expired snacks in his shop, arguing that even his own children ate the same snacks the same day. The Free State Provincial Police Commissioner urged the community to refrain from jumping to conclusions or presumptions and to take the law into their own hands, which could lead to pointing fingers without tangible evidence. He pleaded with them to be patient and wait for results of their investigation. So far all spaza shops in the area are closed, waiting for instructions from authorities.
records.response: Yes, the Free State Provincial Police Commissioner,appealled to the community to allow the investigators to conduct thorough investigation into the matter and not take the law into their own hands.

records.name: Four Asylum seekers falsely arrested in Kokstad by Immigration officers
records.description:
When traffic and immigration officers stormed a barbershop at 70 Main Street in Kokstad, it was around 17:30. This is a barbershop where about 10 barbers from DR Congo and Burundi work. All barbers in the shop were requested to produce their documents, which they did. But even after producing their documents, they were still arrested and put in the police vans. The police stated that they have to be taken to the nearest police station to verify whether their documents are genuine. The police did not take these victims straight to the police station but rather made many rounds with them before taking them to a road block where traffic officers were stopping and searching cars, and immigration officers were also searching buses for possible illegal immigrants.
These asylum seekers were only released around midnight after verification of their documents, where it was found that the documents were theirs and were genuine.
records.response: Not that we are aware of

records.name: Riots, looting and closing of shops owned by foreign national in Heidelberg
records.description: Around six in the morning on October 27, 2023, over 600 people from the Heidelberg Township neighbourhood arrived and caused chaos on Voldan Road. The offenders began to sing anti-immigrant songs while setting tyres on fire. The first group to be targeted was the community of Ethiopian shop owners. ''Pack out all your groceries outside and evacuate the shop premises'' was the slogan used by the perpetrators against shop owners.  Fridges and groceries were set on fire, and the leftovers were taken.  All foreign nationals residing in Heidelberg are currently impacted by this situation, including those from Ethiopia, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Mozambique.  According to the victims, 119 stores were looted in total, with 7 belonging to Pakistanis, 12 to Mozambicans, 15 to Bangladeshis, and 85 to Ethiopians.  The remaining groceries were burned to dust after the looters arrived in large cars loaded with groceries. The victims had planned to tidy up and replenish the area this week, but a letter was sent to the local landlord requesting that they not rent out their space to foreigners. The victims, who are wailing for aid, claim to have lived in this community for more than eighteen years, and some of them are married to South Africans.  Helderberg's migrants reported that they are hungry and that many of them are unable to pay their rent because they have not received money for the previous three weeks.  The group is reported to have approached the Police Station for assistance with the aim of submitting damages but were informed that a case was already open and they were provided with a case number, although it is unclear who opened the case. The affected group submitted letters to the local municipality as well as the station commander on the 1st of November 2023 but had not received received any response at the time of this report. The affected victims also tried to engage with their landlords and the community but things did not go as planned as the community threatened the landlords that their houses would be burnt if they allowed them back. As such, the landlords are refusing to rent out the houses to foreign nationals which is not affecting their livelihood.
records.who_attacked: shops owned by foreign nationals, their properties like cars as well were damaged

records.name: The Food poisoning saga brought unprecedented extortion toward foreign Spaza shops owners in Witbank Mpumalanga.
records.description: The Operation Dudula group and a few locals took to the streets of Witbank and shut down about 40 foreign spaza shops following the October 2023 food poisoning death of two schoolchildren in Soweto, which was attributed to a nearby spaza shop. The foreign owners of the spaza shops and the mayor's office had a consultation. It was alleged that a request of R120 000 be paid to the mayor's office with the assurance that the office would remain open and operational for a full year. The stores were closed on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday in the week of November 6. After the payment was received on Saturday, the stores reopened.
records.response: Police was on the scene but did nothing to stop the raid.

records.name: South Africa Police Service (SAPS) raids turn into assaults on foreign national business  facilities.
records.description:
On Mowbray Main Road in Cape Town, the Perfect Touch Boutique corporate business of Salon and Car Wash is situated in the same building.  Police stormed the businesses twice in a week without a search warrant. One of the victims from the salon explained that a wall with a door and window is what separates the entrance that connects the two businesses. The salon workers heard some screaming coming from the car wash business on Tuesday, November 7, around the time the business closed at 7 p.m. They noticed three employees from the car wash laying on the ground and a group of police officers inside the building as they walked up to the window to have a look. The police officers searched and inquired about the owner's whereabouts and accused them of drug dealing. When the police couldn't find what they were looking for, they physically assaulted the employees. The police officers then realised that the salon employees had been observing them through a window. Three of the police officers went into the salon. They entered it with the intent to search the phones of the staff members but did not find anything. The police officers went as far as brutally assaulting a barber originally from Burundi .
https://www.groundup.org.za/article/barber-assaulted-by-police-officers-in-full-view-cctv/

records.name: Migrant spaza shop owners forced to close down their shops in  Gqeberha townships
records.description: The situation in East London regarding the alleged consumption of expired food from spaza shops and subsequent raids on shops run by foreign nationals, particularly Ethiopians and Somalis, raises significant concerns about the treatment of foreign-owned businesses and the enforcement of regulations. The actions taken by Nelson Mandela Bay officials, in collaboration with police and immigration authorities, appear to disproportionately target foreign nationals operating spaza shops. During the raids, officials focused on verifying the immigration status of foreign shop owners and checking for business licenses. It is alarming to note that while both foreign-owned and South African-owned shops were found to be operating without proper documentation, only the foreign-owned shops were closed down and instructed not to reopen until they obtained the required licenses, as mandated by a court order. South African shop owners, on the other hand, were merely urged to address their licensing issues and allowed to continue operating their businesses
records.response: The authorities also took the matter to the high court to get an interdict that ensures that affected shop owners do not open their shops and if they do, they should be arrested.

records.name: A number of Zimbabwean and Namibian Nationals were forcibly evicted in Vrederndal Western Cape
records.description: On September 20, 2023, a group of locals and some Eff members evicted a number of foreign nationals from Namibia and Zimbabwe from the plots rented to them by some members of the community of Vredendal Municipality of Matzikama in the Western Cape. The claim of the Eff is that those plots are allocated to the citizens of the country; foreign nationals are not allowed to occupy them.

records.name: A police captain was exposed and arrested for extortion against a foreign national Spaza shop owner In

It didn't end there because the police captain revisited the spaza shop owner in November 2023 for another payment of the protection fee. records.name: Migrant informal traders forcefully evicted from their trading sites
records.description: The Jozini local municipality stormed the Jozini main road on Thursday, November 23, 2023, at around 09:45. Traffic police and SANDF pick-ups were accompanying them. Jozini is a small rural town in the north of Kwazulu Natal, around 100km before the Kosi Bay border with Mozambique. On arrival, they approached non-national street barbers who are predominantly Congolese and Burundians and forced them to close their gazebos and put them in SANDF pick-ups. Out of the 30 street barbers operating in Jozini, only 2 were left, and the reason given was that they are South Africans and have IDs. When asked about the refugee and asylum documents that they have, which give them the right to work, they were told that as foreigners they do not have the right to work in this country and that the documents they are showing are fake. It was reported that the documents of some of them were even confiscated. The barbers were then instructed to go to the municipal offices to look for their gazebos, but no fine was issued or any document to indicate what goods were taken from whom and which were in the hands of the municipality. It should be noted that none of these people are in the country illegally, and most of them are refugees and asylum seekers from the DRC and Burundi. Also, many of them have been living and trading in Jozini for more than 15 years, and the municipality has never issued a licence or trading permit to any informal trader, which suggests that even those 2 South Africans whose gazebos were not confiscated do not have trading permits or any document issued by the municipality for that purpose.
records.response: Not yet

records.name: A Nigerian  was  brutarly beaten by police and died from internal injuries in police custody in Johannesburg.
records.description: The young migrant, originally from Nigeria and still in his early 30s, was single and worked selling clothes around Bree Street in Johannesburg's CBD. The Nigerian Citizen Association in South Africa (NICASA) claimed that the victim had an expired asylum seeker document when he was arrested and taken to John Foster police station. Allegedly, he was asked to pay a bribe of R3000 at the police station, but he didn't have the money. Due to his honest response to the police officers, the victim was subjected to physical abuse and severely beaten. From the police cell, he called a friend, expressing that he was in severe pain due to the abuse he endured at John Foster police station for not paying the requested bribe. The victim's case was transferred to Sun City, a correctional center where detainees await court appearances. On the day he was supposed to appear in court, he was absent. It was announced that he had been hospitalized and couldn't attend court. A few days later, the Nigerian community was informed that the victim had died on December 6, 2023, at Baragwanath Hospital. A murder case was opened.

records.name: Immigration officers wrongfully arrest an asylum seeker in King Williams Town
records.description: Around 10h00 of Friday 8/12/2023, a group of immigration officers accompanied by police officers commonly known as "law enforcement" locally, arrested a Burundian national on Wellington street in King Williams town. They asked for his document, which he showed them, but they refused it saying that it is probably a fake document. They took him to the local police station for verification, which unfortunately did not take place for reasons unknown to the victim. He spent the weekend behind bars and was only released on the following Monday by the captain on duty as he was enraged by the fact that a documented asylum seeker was being kept at the station and no one was bothering to verify whether his document was genuine or not.

records.name: A Congolese barber stabbed multiple times by a local client because he requested a payment for four haircuts done in his salon in Lebowakgomo  complex.
records.description: On December 19, 2023, during the bustling week leading up to Christmas, a local client visited a salon around 5:00 PM with four school-going children. After receiving services, the client refused to pay the barber the agreed-upon fee of R250, claiming the barber made too much money in South Africa and wouldn't receive any payment. An argument ensued, escalating into a physical altercation when the client called in others to join in, threatening to harm the barber. Later, as the barber was closing the salon around 8:00 pm, the same group awaited him outside and viciously stabbed him, stealing R2700 in revenue for the day. They accused him of various wrongdoings, including human trafficking and offering services below market value. Despite a security guard witnessing the attack and calling for an ambulance, the victim faced further discrimination and verbal abuse upon arrival at the hospital, enduring a prolonged wait for treatment. Eventually, the victim underwent surgery without anesthesia due to complications from the stabbing which have resulted in the victims inability to use two of his fingers.
records.who_attacked: A foreign business owned barber shop
records.response: After the victim was stabbed, a security called an ambulance but no one intervened when the victim was attacked.

records.name: Police and South African army officers collecting cell phones, money and arresting documented foreign nationals in primrose.
records.description: On December 21, 2023, near the Primrose squatter camp (Rasta), the South African Army and police officers conducted Operation Shanyela, resulting in the arrest of one hundred and ninety foreign nationals. Documented migrants were also detained during the operation. According to a victim, an Ethiopian conducting business in Primrose near the Rasta squatter camp, he presented a valid asylum seeker document, but the police officers refused to consider it. The police officers informed the victims that they wouldn't be able to leave until the Department of Home Affairs had examined their paperwork. The victim reported having R2000 and a mobile phone with him. When he attempted to take pictures with his cellphone to provide evidence of extortion and violence by the police, he was caught in the act. The police became irritated, threatened the victim at gunpoint, and forced him to delete the pictures taken on the spot. Reports indicate that both police and South African army officers collected money and cell phones from the victims. A significant number of foreign nationals, including Ethiopians, Bangladeshis, Pakistanis, and Malawians, were arrested in Primrose. Only a few were released, while others were taken to face the court of justice.
records.response: Police and SA army officials were present not to protect but to take money and cell phones from foreign nationals.

records.name: Foreign nationals tenants and their families threatened to be evicted and denied access at the gate from the complex in Clayville
records.description: On December 12, 2023, the board of trustees in Clayville Township (Midrand Village Estate) convened a meeting and collectively decided to exclude foreigners from the complex, permitting only South Africans to continue renting there. According to victims, the complex management initiated actions such as refusing foreign tenants to park their trucks. For instance, a Pakistani employee of Sasko was denied parking because Sasko was not a legally registered company in South Africa, as per the complex management, which comprises local community members in the township. Tensions escalated on January 6th, leading to the deletion of all foreign nationals' fingerprints used for gate access in the complex, resulting in a complete lockdown. No one could enter or exit, leaving children outside until late at night. Despite residing in the complex for over 10 years due to its perceived safety, foreign nationals reported feeling threatened. Local children were verbally intimidating migrant children, insisting they move out. Landlords in Clayville asserted no issues with migrant tenants and expressed a desire to retain them. A meeting with landlords' lawyers is scheduled, but complex access remains deactivated. Additionally, the local community within the complex collectively agreed to no longer allow tenants from specific nationalities, including Ethiopians, Bangladeshis, and Pakistanis. Twelve families, each consisting of more than five members, are affected, and there is no accountability for the situation. Disturbingly, foreign nationals were notified of potential firearm use in the eviction process if they resisted.
records.who_attacked: A group of migrants renting in the Midrand Village Estate
records.response: police refused to interfere,

records.name: Congolese school transporters in Durban prevented from taking even refugee children to school
records.description: On 10/01/2024, a crucial meeting of the Durban Central Taxi Association occurred at David Landau Hall in Umbilo/Durban. Among the decisions made, attended by various Law Enforcement Agencies and Leaders, is the prohibition of foreigners, regardless of their residency status, from transporting school children in Durban upon the reopening of the 2024 school year. On 18/01/2024 around 07:30 AM, while dropping off children at Addington Primary School, two Congolese refugees were stopped by taxi drivers representing the Durban Liner Taxi Association. They were instructed to cease transporting school children, with the threat of vehicle arson and physical violence if they continued. It's crucial to note that these Congolese school children transporters are legitimate members of the Durban School Transporters Association and are fully compliant with their membership fees. They've already collected fees from parents for January and are now uncertain how to refund the money. They're hesitant to report the situation to the police due to fear of reprisals from the violent taxi drivers. When questioned, the Chairperson of the school transporters association stated there's nothing he can do as the decision was made by a higher authority.
records.response: Not yet, the victims are scared to report the matter to police

records.name: All foreign-owned shops on King Dinuzulu Road, downtown Durban, are now forced to pay protection fees
records.description: In downtown Durban, King Dinuzulu Road is a hub for foreign nationals running various small businesses like tuckshops, internet cafes, and barber shops. On December 16, 2023, at around 8:00 PM, after closing their tuckshop, the owners were attacked by armed assailants. They were held at gunpoint, one was beaten, and they were robbed of their belongings and earnings. This was the second such incident in four weeks, and the first for the couple who had been operating the tuckshop for over six years. A month later, on January 20, 2024, a group of six individuals in a white Polo offered protection to the shop owners for a monthly fee of R900. They claimed to know all the criminals in the area and would provide a sticker for the shop, indicating their protection. The owners were warned that refusing this offer might lead to consequences. Interestingly, South African-owned shops in the area, like a furniture shop, were not approached for payment or provided with stickers from the Umlilo security company, raising concerns about unequal treatment based on nationality.

records.name: A Somali shopkeeper is killed in Kwalanga, Uitenhage
records.description: A Somali shopkeeper who suspected a local boy of stealing from his store assaulted him on Sunday morning, January 21, in the Kwa Langa township near Uitenhage. The boy went and alerted other boys who went on rampage and looted all foreign-owned shops in the area. records.name: A 42 years Male from Nigerian was unlawfully arrested  in Soweto/ Baragwanath taxi rank
records.description: On the 22nd of January 2024, around 6 pm, a foreign national from Nigeria who sells shoes at the Baragwanath taxi rank in Soweto, was unexpectedly approached by three police officers: one female and two males. Only the female officer was in uniform, while the other two were not. The officers began threatening the victim, pushing him in various directions, and falsely accusing him of selling liquor, despite him solely operating a shoe business (selling sandals, safety boots, children's soccer boots, etc.). According to the victim, after a long day in the sun, he bought a drink and intended to start packing his goods as it was getting late. However, three police officers approached him, questioning and threatening him, stating that he would be arrested. When asked for his passport, the victim provided the document, after which the officers began pushing him without allowing him to pack his goods properly. As a result, his stock of shoes were scattered, leading to a reported loss of almost R 3000. Later that night, when taken to Diepkloof police station, the officers continued to threaten the victim demanding money from him, which he refused to give.  it is alleged that police were requesting the victim to pay R3000 for his release. The victim refused to give a bribe. Consequently, he was harshly treated and told he would be sent to Lindela and repatriated back to Nigeria. After spending a night in police custody, the victim was taken to court the next day and was released after intervention of a local NGO (KAAX).

records.name: Police refuse to assist a Congolese refugee
records.description: This morning, on 13/2/2024 around 07:30, a Congolese refugee went to drop his children off at Addington Primary School. They confiscated his car's disc and threatened him with severe consequences if he continued to transport school children. It's worth noting that this individual used to be a registered school transporter but was prevented from doing so last month by the same group of people. They had decided that from January of this year, foreigners would no longer be allowed to transport school children. Now, it seems they don't even want foreigners to transport their own children to school. Following the incident, the victim went to report the matter to the nearest police station as advised. However, when he explained what happened, the police on duty informed him that they couldn't assist him, suggesting he hire a lawyer as it was deemed a civil matter.
records.who_attacked: A Congolese refugee and his children
records.response: The victim went to  open a case at police station but the police refused to open the case or to assist in any way.

records.name: A documented Burundian Asylum seeker is unlawfully arrested in Empangeni
records.description: On Saturday 13/02/2024, around 10h00, a Burundian asylum seeker was approached by police while cutting hair in his gazebo. They asked him to exhibit his document, instead he showed them the photo of his document that he kept in his phone. They refused to accept it as genuine, arrested him and took him to their police station. He then called a relative and asked him to collect his document at his home and bring it to him at the said police station. When his relative arrived at the police station with the document, the police refused to listen to him or looking at the document. He was subsequently taken to prison while the magistrate was verifying his document with the department of home affairs. He was only released on Friday 1/3/2024 after spending 18 days in prison.
records.duration: The incident lasted for 30 minutes or so but the victim spent 18 days in jail
records.response: Not that we are aware of. The judge released the victim after home affairs confirmed that the document was valid.

records.name: A 33 year old refugee holder from Ethiopia arbitrary detained by police, he was locked in police  van for more than 3 hours without any ventilation
records.description: On Wednesday, the 14th of February 2024, at approximately 11 am, a hair stylist working in the vicinity of Bree Street and Delvers Street in Johannesburg CBD, set out to purchase medication due to feeling unwell. Not far from his workplace, the hairstylist was accosted by nearly 15 police officers. One demanded documents while four others simultaneously began searching the victim's pockets inappropriately, also demanding money.  When the victim refused to comply with the search and didn't possess the R 1500 requested by the officers, all 15 police began physically assaulting him, punching and beating him before forcing him into a police van. According to the victim, he was crammed into the van with nine other foreign nationals from Senegal, Malawi, and Ethiopia. The van was overloaded and tightly sealed in the hot weather, causing the detainees, including the victim, to suffer from suffocation. This brutal treatment by the police persisted for over three hours, during which any attempt by the victim or other detainees to voice complaints about their conditions resulted in further violence or chemical spraying by the officers. Reports indicate that all nine detainees were extorted for money by the police for their release, with Malawians paying R500, Ethiopians R1500, and Senegalese R1000, indicating a fixed price based on nationality. The victim was further threatened with transfer to Sun City correctional center for refusing to pay a bribe. Finally, around 2:30 in the afternoon, the victim was released following intervention by a member of KAAX, a local NGO. Despite possessing valid documentation of his refugee status, the victim expressed feeling unjustly treated, akin to a criminal, throughout the ordeal.
records.response: Kopanang Africa Against Xenophobia (KAAX) intervened to assist the victim

records.name: A refugee in Bloemfontein is harassed and jailed for many days because he was suspected of using a fake document
records.description: A significant number of refugees and asylum seekers have been victimised in Bloemfontein, the latest case is that of a Congolese asylum seeker who was arrested on the morning of Thursday, 15/02/2024 on St. Georges street, downtown Bloemfontein. The victim was waiting for home affairs to send him his renewed asylum document by e-mail, as is the practice now since Covi-19. He showed all the paperwork to the police including the application letter for renewal of documents and the automatic response from Home Affairs. Usually, when an individual shows these documents to police or any other authority, they are left alone. However, this young boy was arrested, jailed and wa released on Monday the 19/02/2024, after the family hired a private lawyer to defend him.
records.duration: The arrest took less than an hour but the victim spent 4 days in jail.
records.response: The court released him on Monday the 19th after spending 4 days in custody.

records.name: A Somali  parent  was assaulted  in  front of his two children buy  Mayfairclinic stuff  and got  arrested because he was asking to be assisted.
records.description:
On the 19th of February 2024, at approximately 9 o'clock, an incident occurred at the Mayfair Clinic involving a Somali parent and his unwell children, aged 7 and 3. The individual, hereafter referred to as the victim, was subjected to discriminatory treatment while awaiting medical attention. Despite queuing like other patients, the victim was consistently relegated to the back of the quee, with  patients attended to ahead of him. This pattern of unfair treatment persisted, leading to the victim's decision to depart from the clinic. Upon requesting the clinic cards for his children to seek private medical assistance, the victim encountered further distress. Allegedly, a male nurse demanded a sum of R200 in exchange for the return of the clinic cards. Despite the victim's persistence in requesting the cards, the situation escalated when the nurse proceeded to tear the cards into pieces and forcibly threw the remains at the victim. This resulted in a physical altercations that ensued between the victim and the nurse. it is reported that the male nurse slapped the victim, and the victim slapped the nurse back. This was the beginning of the tension as the clinic staff came together and started beating the Somali victim. He was assaulted and seriously beaten in front of his children. It is reported that Somali community members who were present at the scene shared the message in Whats App groups, and the victim's wife managed to reach the clinic to take her children. Meanwhile, the clinic staff called the police. The victim was not given a chance to explain what happened and how the problem started. He was arrested and taken to John Foster police station. The victim spent one week in Sun City (a correctional center), and the victim's wife paid R2000 for the victim to sleep for 6 days in a secure cell. The victim's wife paid another R3000 for detective and police fees. She added R1000 for bail and R7000 for a private lawyer. The victim was released on bail on the 26th of February 2024. The family is currently under debt. The nurse who opened the case against the victim is requesting R20000 from the victim to close the case. The family is still traumatized and worried about where to take their children if they fall sick without clinic cards.
few weeks later , the victim and his wife  approached the  closest offices of Lawyers for Human Rights . The family was then referred to SAPS South African Police Station in Mayfair, where by the SAPS went and arrested the Mal nurse in Mayfair clinic.  since the arrest of the perpetrator, the family of  the victim is facing threats,from the clinic stuffs nurses securities and the family member of the perpetrator.
records.who_attacked: A migrant originaly from Somalia a 39 years old
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Lebowakgomo Residents Loot and Burn Foreign-Owned Businesses
records.description: On Thursday, the 22nd of February 2024, around 9 am, residents in Lebowakgomo took to the streets, carrying harmful weapons, and engaging in acts of intimidation, looting, and burning containers used as business premises by foreign nationals. The local community were threating to vandalise houses rented to foreign nationals. According to reports, the social unrest started in mid-February but foreign owned shops were attacked on the 22nd of February 2024. Victims explained that the nationalities that were mostly affected were from DRC, Pakistan, Malawi, Ethiopia and Zimbabwe. It is reported that about 60 Zimbabweans and 30 Congolese/Burundians households are affected. Other nationalities affected are Nigerians and Ethiopians. The victims further emphasised that the attacks seem to have coincided with the upcoming elections in SA. This has seen the emergence of a political party in the area, Defenders of the People which is targeting foreign owned businesses. The victim informed that the political party members started soliciting a “protection fee” bribe of R200 from every foreign owned shop in the area since April 2022. On the day of the actual attacks, the affected communities narrated how a group of about 200 local people targeted foreign-owned containers. They stated that some containers were set alight and vandalised. They added that the attacks were done in full view of the police who did not restrain the marauding group.  A case of public violence was opened at the Police Station: Case number 420/02/2024. The victims also reported the attacks to the South African Human Rights Commission in Polokwane who referred those dispersed in the attacks to a shelter and Future Families in Musina. The affected community members also highlighted that another attack on foreign nationals has been planned for the 14th of March 2024, according to social media posts which are currently circulating. They also stated that the Dudula Movement members are also planning to conduct a door-to-door campaign, rooting out foreign nationals from the area. The affected community members also reported that their livelihoods have been adversely affected as they are now struggling to pay rent, support their families and send their children to school. They also expressed that they are now living in abject fear especially with the impending 14th of March date approaching.
records.response: It was first reported that the police were not helping but at the intervention of SAHRC the police intervened and calm was restored in the area. Migrants have met with UNHCR, IOM, Doctors Without Borders, and Future Families, with further NGO meetings planned next week.

records.name: A Congolese traditional healer stabbed several times and shot twice but survived.
records.description: On Sunday 25 February 2024 around 20h00, a refugee traditional healer from the Democratic republic of Congo (DRC), well known in the area and elsewhere went to buy airtime at a Somali tuck shop, a short distance from where he lived on Demat road, village, near Savannah Park. After loading airtime in his phone, he was approached by 4 guys, armed with knives and a pistol. One of them called his name as a way of confirming it. They then told him that they will kill him because since he arrived in the area, their traditional healers are no longer getting customers. They said he was warned several times to go back to his home country and operate from there but he does not want to listen. Now they will kill him and other foreigners who are in the area will learn from him and leave. He tried to plead with them and even offered them money but they said they didn't need his money. That's when they started stabbing him until he passed out. He was assisted by the tuck shop owner who took him to hospital in his car. It is only on the hospital bed that he realised that he was also shot twice on his thigh and upper chest. He was discharged 2 days later,  but he is now living in hiding fearing for his life.
records.who_attacked: A Congolese asylum seeke who operates as a traditional healerr
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Members of Fiela Organisation raided a foreign national shop in Galeshewe township, Kimberly
records.description: Last Sunday, February 25, 2024, members of an organisation called Fiela took the law into their on hands by entering a shop owned by a Bangladeshi national. They turned everything upside down and destroyed goods on the shelves searching for expired ones. According to a source of the ground, Fiela organisation seized and destroyed some of the goods outside the shop and others were taken away by the members of the organisation.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Extortion of foreign businesses enters Durban Central
records.description: On February 28, 2028, a Congolese internet cafe operating on Magwaza Maphalala Street in Durban central was approached by a group of gangsters who reside at Dalton hostel. They informed the cafe owner that starting from March 2024, he would be required to pay R350 per month, and they would affix their sticker on his door. They warned him that if he did not agree, he should not hold them responsible for any consequences to him or his shop. They also mentioned that all other foreign-owned shops in the vicinity had already complied, and if he followed suit, they would ensure his safety, albeit without assigning anyone to guard his shop. The cafe owner had no choice but to accept this demand and paid the amount the following day for the month of March, intending to continue paying for his own safety.
records.who_attacked: A Congolese man who runs an internet cafe on Magwaza Maphalala street, in Durban.
records.duration: This practice of forcing people to pay protection fees started this month but will continue, unless something is done to stop it.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: A  Somalian lady was insulted at Mayfair clinic in Johannesburg and went back home without her two month baby getting immunized
records.description: On March 1, 2024, a Somali woman took her newborn baby for immunization at the Mayfair clinic. She arrived early, around 5 am, and received ticket number 1. However, when the clinic staff began calling names, she was sent back to the end of the line and given ticket number 6. The woman expressed her concerns, explaining that she had left her other young children alone at home. In response, a nurse told her that no one cared about her children being alone and reminded her that the clinic card was for South Africa, not Somalia. The woman was also told to go back to Somalia and was insulted, being called stupid. The Somali woman felt that the nurses were rude towards her compared to how they treated locals and white patients, whom she perceived as privileged. Since the incident, she has been reluctant to return to the Mayfair clinic and has opted to take her baby to a private doctor for immunization.
records.who_attacked: A Somali lady who was taking her baby for immunization
records.duration: The violence lasted more then 3 hours
records.response: The victim decided to leave the clinic because she was told that she will stay there until night and no one cares.

records.name: Migrant street barbers, who are using municipal pavement are forcefully paying rent fees to hijackers in Thaba Nchu
records.description:
Thaba Nchu used to be part of Bophutatswana, one of 10 former Bantu homelands during apartheid, and as such, there are State buildings that used to belong to the government of Bophutatswana, which were incorporated into the heritage of Mangaung Metropolitan municipality.
At the beginning of this year, many of those buildings were hijacked by a group of people calling themselves "Sthuba Hub". In February, they approached migrant street barbers who have built makeshift structures on municipal pavement on Joseph street, between that building and the taxi rank, and ordered them to pay monthly fees alleging that the building property extends to the whole Joseph street including the pavement used by migrant barbers as trading sites. 
Since the 1st of March, each street barber is paying rent fees between R300 and R500 depending on the size of the area occupied.  
The municipality was informed but was unable to intervened partly because those street barbers do not yet have an agreement with Mangaung municipality but also, and most importantly because the matter regarding the hijacking of buildings is before the courts and they are waiting for the decision of the court on the matter.
records.who_attacked: Migrant street barbers, predominantly from Central Africa
records.duration: The situation has not changed, street barbers are still paying these fees as we speak.
records.response: Not yet.

records.name: Migrant's shops  targeted . looted and vandalized  after a civil attack in Delareyville in  North west
records.description: Tension erupted in Delareyville on February 27th, 2024, following a dispute between a local taxi driver and a street kid caught stealing near the taxi rank. The altercation escalated when the street kid sought revenge with friends, leading to provocations against migrant-owned shops. The situation worsened on March 2nd, resulting in a fatal stabbing among street kids. Subsequent violence, triggered by a murder investigation, spread to the informal settlement. By March 4th, 2024, residents, predominantly Tswana, began vandalizing foreign-owned businesses, resulting in significant property damage estimated at R 25,000. The targeted community comprises Nigerians, Congolese, and Ethiopians, prompting many migrants to flee due to threats. Mafikeng police intervened to assist their Delareyville counterparts, with over 10 migrant-owned containers vandalized. The targeted shops are reportedly now occupied by Delareyville residents. Urgent measures are required to restore peace and security in the community.
records.who_attacked: Foreign owned shops, also the police was attached by the community.
records.response: It is reported that police response were not  focused on migrants but to protect residents.

records.name: Numerous foreign nationals were compelled to leave their homes after allegedly receiving xenophobic threats in the vicinity of Wellington.
records.description: Violence erupted in the New Era Township, situated between Paarl and Wellington, when a local robber was killed by a group of Zimbabwean nationals seeking revenge for an earlier robbery committed by the deceased robber and his accomplices. However, tensions escalated on March 6, 2024, when rumors of the incident spread throughout the community.
