In response, community members took matters into their own hands and launched attacks on the Zimbabwean community. Tragically, five Zimbabwean nationals lost their lives, prompting many others to flee the area in fear for their safety as they became targets of the violence.
records.response: Gift of the givers, Ward 5 Councillor in the Drakenstein Municipality and Taxi drivers intervened.

records.name: Intimidation and  attack on Zimbabweans living in Moshana Village in the North West by the local community members
records.description: On March 8, 2024, around 12 PM, the counselor of Moshana Village and a local school principal held a meeting and informed all Zimbabweans living in the village to pack their belongings and leave within 24 hours. Zimbabweans were accused of cutting electric wires and raping elderly women. A female victim stated that these accusations were false and unfair. She added that the ultimatum to leave was very short, forcing victims to abandon their property for their safety. The intimidation continued throughout the night, and 24 Zimbabweans left Moshana Village. Some went to Tsweletsukhu, while others relocated to Muswedi and Dinoka. The Zimbabwean community in Moshana had been selling clothes door-to-door and working in construction. Victims who had extended credit to local community members said they have not been paid back, as they are not allowed to enter the village.
records.response: no response, as the order was coming from the chef of the village

records.name: Harrassement  and extortion of police officer in Johannesburg led to the death of a migrant from Nigeria
records.description: A foreign-owned beauty salon in Johannesburg's central business district frequently faced visits from police who demanded R1500 from the owner due to document renewal delays. On April 13, 2024, during their usual rounds of extorting migrants for documentation, police began harassing the victim. Feeling threatened, the victim attempted to flee but was shot and killed by police. The victim, who suffered from high blood pressure, panicked during the incident. Despite this, the police did not immediately call for medical assistance. The victim's body was taken to Hillbrow clinic, and the family living in Johannesburg filed a case regarding the incident.
records.duration: The harrassment was constant , apparently every  week police will come in the shop where the victim was working and will ask for R1500.
records.response: The ambulance and paramedics collected the deceased body .

records.name: Attack and Forced eviction of foreign Nationals in Betrams Johannesburg
records.description:
The intimidation began on the 4th of May 2024 on Saturday, around 12 pm and lasted until 4 pm. More than 300 locals reportedly arrived wearing Operation Dudula T-shirts, carrying sticks, guns, stones, and singing, according to the victims. Their slogan was that "kwerekweres cannot stay in buildings where locals have no place to stay." When migrants called the police, law enforcement attempted to calm the situation, and the crowd was dispersed. The following day, on the 5th of May around 10 am, the local community returned in their numbers estimated to have increased to around 400 people. They began shooting and forcibly entered the 6-storey building, breaking in and assaulting tenants. The perpetrators arrived with Quantums and bakkies to loot migrants' properties taking whatever they could seize and have continued to use migrant's belongings after they occupied the building. The building is Rose Hill Court, is located in Bertram’s at number 14 Terrace Road. No one was permitted to retrieve even essential items such as clothing, valuables, appliances, or electronics. Various migrant communities resided in the building, including Malawians, Congolese, Angolans, Burundians, Tanzanians, and South Africans (who were not targeted and remain in the same building).
Families have been severely affected and traumatized, with many still seeking medical treatment for injuries sustained during the attacks. Some families attempted to find alternative accommodation, but unfortunately, there remains a group of migrants who have nowhere else to go. These victims are currently being accommodated by a Zimbabwean single mother, who herself has been threatened with eviction by the perpetrators.  The plight of these families is deeply concerning, as they have been left with nothing and have moved to a more insecure location opposite where they were attacked. Some victims have been unable to resume their daily activities as all their work tools were stolen during the attacks. Locals who are now occupying the victims' rooms are reportedly selling their belongings daily, while the victims feel helpless as the police have informed them that they cannot assist. Despite this, the victims still hold hope that with legal assistance, they may be able to recover some of their stolen property.  Currently the Congolese  affected are estimated to 23 children and 39 adults and the number is said to increase because victims are not together since the incident . The number of other nationalities is yet to be evaluated.
records.response: The first day the police came and tried to intervene, but the next day the perpetrators came back and no police showed up
records.other_text: An organization located next where the incident occured in Bertrams

records.name: A refugee child denied the right to play in local soccer competition
records.description:
A 10 year old, grade 5 asylum seeker from DRC, is a very good and promising soccer player. He has joined a local under 11 soccer team called "Brackenham FC" last year. On Sunday 12/5/2024, he joined his colleagues to prepare for a district soccer league match. Unfortunately, unlike all his teammates, he was not given a "player card" which would allow him to play. When his father went to find out, he was told that he is not allowed to play because he does not have a South African birth certificate. Since then, the boy spent weeks traumatised, could not sleep nor focus on his school work because other children were teasing him. He missed 2 league games because he did not have a player card and only resumed playing when this was issued after interventions from various interested parties including Refugee Social Services and Lawyers for Human Rights.  
This was a clear violation of his rights as a refugee because according to refugee Act of 1998 an asylum seeker enjoys all the rights that are enjoyed by his or her South African counterparts other than the right to vote and the right to stand for election.
After verification with SAFA at national level, it appears that there is no policy at that level that excludes refugees and asylum from playing at any competition. It is therefore the case of SAFA officials at district level acting in bad faith or lacking necessary information on refugee rights in this country
records.who_attacked: A 10 year old refugee school child
records.duration: He missed 2 games until he was issued with the player's card
records.response: Yes, as reported earlier, RSS and LHR intervened and ensured that the child was issued with his player card and joined his teammates in the competition.

records.name: A 43- year-old Nigerian national was beaten to death by SAPS members in his home in Danielskuil.
records.description: A terrible occurrence rocked Danielskuil town, Mgcawu District Municipality in the Northern Cape province on Friday, May 17, 2024, at around eight in the morning. A Nigerian national man was mercilessly beaten to death by the public order police unit. In Danielskuil, the victim was apparently thought to be a narcotics dealer. Eyewitnesses said that after the police unit searched the suspect's residence, there was a violent altercation that resulted in the Nigerian man's unfortunate death. The police unit called the emergency ambulance with hope that the man could survive, but unfortunately, it was too late.
records.response: Ambulance

records.name: Three Ethiopian spaza shops set alight in and around Ulundi
records.description:
On Thursday 16th May 2024, an unsigned notice circulated on social media from local small businesses and addressed to Councillors and traditional leaders. The notice requested permission from those authorities to allow them to go all over Ulundi municipality and close down all foreign-owned spaza shops, because they are now too many of them and are pushing local small businesses out of business. Although it was unclear who wrote and circulated the notice, sources of the ground stated that  the police were able to arrest some of the culprits and released them on a warning. A week later, on Thursday 23 May 2024, it was reported that two Ethiopian owned spaza shops were looted and thereafter set alight in Ulundi C section and in town (Ulundi) essentially by unknown locals who were driving an unregistered Toyota Corolla and had petrol which they used to set alight foreign owned shops. The shop owners were saved by the police but were told not to return to that area. Foreign community leaders in the area told us that the culprits are also mobilising homeless people in Ulundi town so that they can help them to strike at different places.
The good news is that all 9 leaders of this group have been arrested by police, and this has brought some relief to victims and foreign community at large.
records.who_attacked: Ethiopian owned spaza shops in Ulundi
records.response: Yes, the police intervened in some areas but unfortunately in C section, they were not able to save the shops and its contents. They, however managed to arrest 9 among the perpetrators.

records.name: A Burundian refugee is violently evicted from a trading site where he has been operating since 1998
records.description: A refugee from Burundi used to operate as an electronics repairer at shop 52 at Berea station since 1998. He was a subtenant of Mr. Shange, who died in March 2024. He used to repair electronics such as T.V, radio, cellphones, computers and also used to sell parts in that kiosk.  After the death of his landlord in March this year, he started receiving threats that he must leave the kiosk that he was operating from since 1998 because he is a foreigner, until he was forced out early this month. Finally, it was on Monday morning, 3 June 2024, around 09h00 when he was attacked by people he did not know where they were coming from and for reasons he does not understand because he already accepted to leave and was granted until end of June to leave the kiosk. They beat him and stabbed him several times until he lost consciousness. However he remembers them saying that, they can't allow a foreigner to operate there especially now that his protector is no more. He was subsequently admitted at Addington hospital, where he spent 48 hours before he was discharged. He is still under medication and managed to report to police station but no action has been taken so far against his perpetrators.
records.response: A case was opened but no arrest yet and the victim has no way of going back

records.name: Police in Richards Bay refuse a valid asylum visa document and wrongfully arrests an Ethiopian Asylum seeker
records.description:
On Saturday 8/6/2024 around 08h30, an Ethiopian asylum seeker was arrested in Richards Bay by 3 police officers because he was not carrying his asylum visa document and took him to Richards Bay police station. When they arrived there, he called his leader who usually helps them with electronic renewal of their documents, and asked him to please print him a copy of his document because he left his at home, which the leader did. The leader then went to the police station with the document and showed it to the police officers who arrested the Ethiopian asylum seeker. The police then started accusing the Ethiopian leader of forging fake documents for undocumented foreign nationals and asked him for his asylum visa, but when he gave them, they said they wanted his passport. That' when one of them asked his colleagues to compare the documents of both asylum seekers to see if they are similar. When they did that, they found that the asylum visa of the Ethiopian is the old one with COVID-19 watermark while the leader's document is the new one with no water mark but with electronic stamp. That is when they said both documents are fake and decided to lock both of them. They then decided to search his car for anything that would support their allegations that he forges fake documents, but unfortunately they did not find anything. The leader then said to them that, since they are suspecting these documents, they should at least ask an immigration officer to verify them, but they were not interested and proceeded to arrest them telling them that they will spend 2 nights at the police station and appear before court on following Monday.
After few hours, probably after checking with others elsewhere, the 2 victims were called and told to go home. When the leader wanted to know what happened, he was told that he has a big mouth and must be careful because there is a big case that is being built against him.
records.who_attacked: An Ethiopian asylum seeker and a refugee leader in Richards Bay
records.response: No known Interventions reported

records.name: This past Monday, June 10, 2024, at night in Delft, a foreign shop owner was murdered over protection fees.
records.description:
The tragedy took place on Monday, June 10, 2024, in the evening on the corner of Umfuli Road and Umvoti Street in Delft Cape Town, where three-gun men entered the store of a 28-year-old Somalia national man and then shot him dead for failing to pay extortion fees. Police officers have responded to a complaint about that shooting; unfortunately, on their arrival, they found the victim dead, and the suspects fled the scene.
https://www.son.co.za/dieson/nuus/kaapsenuus/buitelander-afgemaai-oor-beweerde-protection-fees-20240611
records.response: Police but they arrived to find the victim already dead

records.name: An innocent Nigerian is assaulted and wrongfully arrested in Makhanda
records.description: On 20 June morning, around 7h00, a group of police officers, who are not from the local police station, stormed the house rented by the victim situated at 15 George street in Makhanda. They accused the victim, who is a Nigerian national, of selling drugs. They searched everywhere in and around the house but found nothing. They then started beating him on his head using the back of a gun among other tools. They even covered his head with a plastic while holding his hands, to an extent where he almost died  of suffocation. They then took his money, around R7500 and left him bleeding from injuries caused by the back of a gun. He subsequently went to the local police station and opened a case against those police officers but so far, he has no knowledge of anything happening to those police officers.
records.response: No, a case was opened but nothing happened so far to perpetrators

records.name: Forced eviction and occupation of houses rented and build by migrants in Alexandra Township
records.description: Migrants in Alexandra, specifically in Rasta Village, Extension 8, were attacked on Saturday, June 22, 2024. The intimidation and threats against these migrants had been ongoing for many months, worsening when the victims reported the incidents to the local police station. The perpetrators of this xenophobic movement were well known to the victims, but the more the victims reported them, the more the threats and harassment intensified. On June 22nd, around 11 a.m., over 300 people, reportedly from the surrounding Madala hostels and mixed with the local community, targeted houses belonging to migrants in Rasta Village. These houses, built by migrants, were specifically identified, and all migrants, including those renting to South Africans, were instructed to vacate. It became clear that the eviction was solely targeting migrants. Rasta Village was home to approximately 300 migrants, including Zimbabweans, Malawians, Mozambicans, and other foreign nationals. While the police attempted to intervene, chaos ensued after they left. The perpetrators forcibly broke into homes and removed the migrants. Many who were not present that day returned to find their houses locked with new locks, their belongings and furniture outside, and their homes occupied by others. Rasta Village is now occupied entirely by South African citizens, with no migrants allowed to stay there. Only a few migrants, not more than two, remain in the camp and have decided to rent rooms. Others have relocated far away, to places like Diepsloot, or have left the country due to the danger to their lives.
records.who_attacked: Migrants living in Rasta Village Camp
records.response: The police tried to confront the perpetrators on the first day of the incident but that mad things to be worse as every one who reported  to the police was attacked.

records.name: Asylum seekers are unlawfully arrested by Metro Police in Isipingo rail, South of Durban
records.description: From Tuesday, 25 June 2024, Metro Police conducted raids throughout Isipingo Rail, south of Durban, targeting foreign-owned shops and undocumented immigrants. During these raids, they arrested many asylum seekers, who were released only after spending around 12 hours in police cells while waiting for verification to be finalized. Between 25 and 26 June, six asylum seekers and newcomers with appointments at the Durban Refugee Reception Centre to apply for asylum were also arrested. This operation was carried out by Durban Metro Police officers, whose powers are limited to enforcing efficient traffic management, bylaw adherence, crime policing, and ensuring the protection of Council's assets and personnel. Therefore, they did not have the mandate to arrest immigrants, whether undocumented or not, unless supporting immigration officers. One particular asylum seeker spent the weekend in jail because the police officers misspelled his asylum file number during verification, causing his file number to not be found in the Home Affairs system. As a result, he was falsely accused of using a fake document. Some arrested asylum seekers have appeared in Amanzimtoti Magistrate court but they are all remanded in custody. They will go back to the same court next week for bail application.
records.who_attacked: Asylum seekers from Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo
records.duration: It started on Tuesday 25/6/2024 and continue until today Friday the 28/6/2024
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Two Congolese asylum seekers are spending the weekend behind bars because the police was unable to verify their documents
records.description: As part of a Metro police operation which started on Tuesday 25 June 2024, two Congolese asylum seekers were arrested on Friday 28 June 2024 in their shared shop because  the police suspected that their documents may not be genuine and needed to be verified. The two asuylum seekers were taken to Isipingo metro police station so that their documents could be verified. Unfortunately, the systems were allegedly down which means the verification could not be concluded.  They were then forced to spend the weekend behind bars until next week Monday, with the hope that the system will be up and running and the verification will take place. It is unclear what will happen if the system continues to pose problem even tomorrow Monday.
records.duration: The victims are still behind bars, 2 days after their arrest
records.response: No response so far.

records.name: A Somali man shop owner was denied service at Camel police station in Upington as he went to report crime with evidence.
records.description:
On Thursday, July 4, 2024, at around 3:30 PM, a thief entered the store of a Somali shop owner, stole an outfit from the shelf, and ran off. A witness outside the shop alerted the owner, but it was too late. The shop owner went to the Camel police station in Upington, Northern Cape province, to report the theft, as he had footage of the incident and knew the thief. However, the officer told him it was unnecessary to open a case since the thief was a street person. This was the third time the same person had stolen from him. 
While conducting research visits in the area for the Xenowatch project, our research assistant received a call from the victim seeking intervention. The research assistant escorted the store owner to the Camel police station and requested the captain on duty to open a case of shoplifting, given the proof the victim had. The captain promised to visit the shop the next day, Friday, July 5, 2024, to see the footage and take the victim's statement. However, since we left the station on July 4, no police officer has visited the shop to take a statement. It was clear from the Research Assistant's assessment of the situation that this was a case of denied service as the victim did not receive help because of his nationality.
records.response: No response from Police

records.name: Second Round of Forced Evictions and Occupation of Houses Rented and Built by Migrants in Alexandra Township
records.description: On July 4, the same perpetrators who had attacked migrants in Rasta Village moved to Extension 7 in Alexandra township and attacked migrants there. The victims stated that returning to their homes is no longer an option, believing that the only way the city or municipality can assist them is by compensating them or allowing them to sell their homes and recover their money.
records.who_attacked: Migrants living in Extension 7, Alexandra Township
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Three police officers allegedly beat up a Burundi National in Rosedale, Upington, Northern Cape province.
records.description: On Wednesday, July 10, 2024, around 4:30 PM, a Burundi national was on his way home from work on his motorbike when he heard police sirens behind him. As he tried to give way, an officer instructed him to stop. He stopped, and three officers emerged from the van and began searching him while he was still on his motorbike. When he pleaded to be allowed to get off the bike for a proper search, the officers became furious, told him not to tell them how to do their job, and began beating him. After the assault, they abandoned him at the scene and drove away. The incident occurred in Rosedale, Upington, Northern Cape province.
records.response: Witnesses helped him to get to the hospital

records.name: Migrants arrested in Pretoria west  and police took phones and money when searching in their rooms.
records.description: On the 11th of July around 6am, police officers accompanied by unknown men in green uniform raided in Hagen Street in Pretoria West.  The area is occupied mostly by migrants from Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Malawi, because the migrants claim rent is affordable there, around R1500pm. The police raid happened while other migrants were asleep. Some migrants were detained when they failed to present valid permits or passports.  A  five month pregnant woman from Zimbabwe reported that police broke into her house around 6 am  asking for her passport,  two police officers kept the victim outside  while the other four were busy searching inside the house, turning everything up side down. The  victim  said  that  police officers were using  xenophobic language  saying "you foreigners we want  you to go".  and the victim added that police were asking her about the validity of her documents. After the operation ended and the victim was released, she entered her room and found that her money, equivalent to R2000 was taken by the police. The victim said that the money was inside her toiletry bag.  The raid took an hour and other migrants reported that their phones were stolen.   It was also reported that migrants were injured while jumping and running from the police. While the migrants who were detained and taken to  police station in Pretoria West, paid money to be released. Others paid  R1500 and some R2000 as reported by a witness from  Malawi who was selling in a shop in  Marabastad.
records.who_attacked: Migrants from Malawi, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Foreign owned shops looted and trashed after a service delivery protest in Delareyville township in the North west province.
records.description: On July 16, 2024, at around 10 am, the local community in Delareyville organized a march to protest against the municipality for poor service delivery and other issues, including the need for a new clinic. It was alleged that jobs were given to people who did not apply. The march was planned to be peaceful, but two days later, on July 18, around 10 am, a group of approximately 500 protesters disrupted schools, taking primary and secondary students out of classes. The protesters split into two groups: one group blocked roads, while the other group protested, shouting that they didn't want shops in the location (Masera Pata, Sinthomole, RDP). The protesters started vandalizing shops run by foreign nationals (Bangladeshi and Pakistani). Six shops were reported looted. Fortunately, police from Mafikeng dispersed the protesters using pepper spray. Currently, migrants are leaving Delareyville township due to the violence, relocating to Frieburg, Tau, Free State, and Kanyesa.
records.response: Yes , the police came from Mafikeng to disperse  protestors by spraying pepper spray.

records.name: A delivery driver from Somalia survived three murder attempts in Tekwane township, Mombela Nelspruit.
records.description: This incident happened on July 21, 2024, around 4 o'clock p.m. A Somali national driver and his assistant were driving around Tekwane township delivering stock to different Tuck and Spaza shops. Suddenly, they were ambushed by two-gun men who shot them randomly. They lost control of the vehicle and knocked on a wall. A week after the incident on July 29, 2024, around 3 p.m, a Xenowatch research assistant was in the area for research visits. He went physically to visit the victim to try to understand the cause of the shootings. The victim revealed that he had received several threats before the incident from local citizens who threatened to kill him because he was making money in their country.  The victim was seriously injured from the shooting and as a result, he cannot walk anymore due to injuries received from the bullets.
records.who_attacked: A Somali driver and his assistant
records.response: Police

records.name: Extortionists impose law on protection fees on poor migrant informal traders
records.description:
Migrant street barbers, mostly from the DRC and Burundi, who use eight containers and gazebos as places of work on Wellington Street in Qonce (King Williams Town), have been paying protection fees to gangsters since early last year. They were paying between R600 and R750 per month in weekly installments, but the extortionists were not providing any protection.

On Saturday, 21 July 2024, around midday, five members of one of the three extortionist groups active in the area approached the barbers and demanded that they now pay R1000 per month in a single payment. The barbers explained that they couldn't gather such an amount all at once and reported that two other groups were also demanding protection fees. They then stood their ground and said they would not pay until all the groups agreed to a single extortionist group.

After making several threats, the extortionists left, saying they would "see." Early Monday morning, around 5:00 AM, the barbers received calls that their containers were on fire, though fire trucks were on the scene to extinguish it. All their work equipment in the containers was destroyed, and it took them more than a week to rebuild and buy new equipment for those who could afford it.
records.duration: Several hours until fire extinguisher truck came
records.response: Yes, fire department was alerted by neighbours, they responded many hours later but managed to extinguish the fire.

records.name: 1 Immigrant killed and another still fighting for his life, after an armed attack targeting Immigrant informal traders at Mandeni flea market
records.description:
Immigrant and refugee informal traders, mostly from Durban but also from other small towns, travel every weekend to Mandeni flea market on Fridays. They trade there and then wait until early Saturday morning to proceed to Esikhaleni flea market before returning to their respective towns. Friday, July 26, 2024, was no different, especially as it was the end of the month and many workers had received their salaries.

Around 6 PM, while packing their trading goods to head to a nearby petrol station where they usually spend the night, they heard gunshots. At that time, the market was nearly empty, with only immigrant traders left packing their goods. After the gunshots, they realized that two immigrant males from Mozambique were lying in pools of blood and not moving. They were rushed to a nearby hospital, where one was declared dead on arrival. Their vehicle was missing, and goods belonging to many immigrants and refugees were stolen by locals during the chaos created by the shooting.

The police were alerted and arrived later to take the 16 stranded and terrified women refugees to the local police station for their safety until they could leave this morning.
records.who_attacked: Immigrant informal traders who were trading at Mandeni flea market
records.duration: Until he police intervened late at night
records.response: Yes, the police intervened to protect the 16 women after 2 traders were shot, one fatally and another one still fighting for his life in hospital

records.name: Police at Pietermaritzburg Police station refuse to certify an asylum document
records.description: On Saturday, July 27, 2024, around 10:00 AM, a couple from Burundi went to the Pietermaritzburg Police Station to get their asylum documents certified. The police officer on duty claimed the document was fake because a genuine home affairs document couldn't be on normal A4 paper and lacked a signature. The woman tried to explain that since the lockdown, home affairs renews documents online and recipients print them themselves, but the officer was not interested. They spoke to his supervisor, who supported the officer. Despite seeking intervention from community leaders, they were unable to get the service they needed and had to leave without their documents being certified.
records.duration: They left the police station around 11h00, an hour later.
records.response: There were various unsuccessful interventions, but in the end the victim gave up and left.

records.name: Angry Tsakane  residents looting and vandalizing foreign-owned shops after the death of a grade 1 learner
records.description: On 06/02/2024, a 6-year-old pupil died at school, and four other learners were hospitalized after consuming biscuits (cookies) purchased from a local spaza shop. The death of the young learner has ignited the local community in Tsakane against foreign-owned shops, blaming them for selling poisonous foods. Tension in Tsakane is high and has resulted in looting, damaging, and shutting down most local shops in the township. The actual number of vandalized and targeted shops in Tsakane is still unknown as residents remain out of control. On the other hand, the family of the deceased has blamed the emergency services for a late response. Following the recent incident, the Gauteng Department of Education announced plans to regulate spaza shops around schools. It has been a challenging time for shop owners in Tsakane.
records.duration: The tension still intense in Tsakane.
records.response: So far no intervention have been  reported to be in Tsakane

records.name: A Congolese Pastor is a unlawfully arrested and spend the weekend behind bars
records.description:
On Friday,  August 2, 2024, around midday, a Congolese pastor and one of his congregants were approached by the South African Police Service (SAPS) near RK Khans Hospital in Unit 5, Chatsworth. The police requested that they produce their documents, which they did. The congregant had not renewed his document for a long time, while the pastor's document was valid. However, the police claimed that the pastor's document appeared suspicious and proceeded to arrest them. The pastor was detained for document verification, while his congregant was arrested for allegedly living in the country illegally.

The police were unable to contact the Department of Home Affairs to verify the pastor's document on the spot. Instead, they decided to take him to court for verification purposes. This type of discriminatory practice is increasingly being used by the police, leading to documented refugees and asylum seekers being victimised in the process. This action also goes against the instructions of the Minister of Home Affairs, who stated that the police are equipped to verify documents on the spot using the necessary equipment.
records.duration: The victim stayed behind bars and appeared in Court on Monday 5/8/2024
records.response: Victim was waiting for decision from the court at the time of the report.

records.name: A 39-year-old migrant worker from Zimbabwe was severely assaulted by law enforcement officers, including immigration officials and police in Fourways (Johannesburg)
records.description: On August 10th, at approximately 5:30 p.m., a Zimbabwean national employed at a local restaurant went out to buy airtime. He was stopped by two men in green uniforms, who were part of a joint operation involving immigration police and the Expanded Public Works Program, known as the Green Army. This operation was targeting illegal immigrants working at Cedar Square in Fourways. As the victim approached the shop, he noticed people running from the immigration officers and joined them, fearing repercussions for not having his documents on him. The victim was intercepted by a white officer in a green uniform wearing a mask. The officers demanded to see his documents. The victim explained that he had left them at home and requested to retrieve them, but the officers refused. The officers then ordered that the victim be restrained. When the victim resisted, noticing that others were not being handcuffed, the officers began to assault him, kicking him in his private parts. Unable to restrain him with traditional means, they used a cable to tie him up and dragged him away. The victim experienced severe pain and felt a wet sensation in his pants, realizing he was injured and bleeding. He was placed in a police van with 15 other detainees. Despite his pleas for help due to the pain, the officers dismissed his concerns, suggesting he might have been injured prior to his detention. Eventually, the van door was opened, and the victim was allowed to walk slowly to a bathroom, where he discovered the extent of his injuries and collapsed from trauma. A cleaner called for an ambulance, which arrived an hour later. The victim was transported to Johannesburg Hospital, where he was unconscious upon arrival and remained so until the following day. Medical interventions included pipes, oxygen, drainage, and drips. He was discharged but continued to rely on a pipe supply. On August 22nd, he was readmitted to Edenvale Hospital due to shortness of breath and required oxygen. The victim, a father of two, is seeking justice and reports that he nearly died from the injuries. He has not yet filed a formal complaint due to fear and ongoing trauma from the encounter with the police and law enforcement.
records.response: An ambulance taking the victim to hospital arrived an hour after the incident

records.name: closure of spaza shops operated by foreign nationals in Soweto(White City) by Operation Dudula after a shooting of a 21 years old resident.
records.description:
21-year-old, along with his friends, went to buy something in a shop while holding a bottle of liquor. The shop owner, a foreign national from Somalia, did not allow the young customers to enter the shop with the liquor bottle. An argument ensued, and the local 21-year-old was shot in the stomach. Since then, Operation Dudula has decided to shut down all shops owned by foreign nationals in Soweto, with the support of law enforcement. The shops in Soweto are operated by Somalians, Ethiopians, and some Bangladeshis. The agenda to shut down foreign national shops in Soweto began on August 12th of August 2024 following a press conference by Operation Dudula on the same day. Operation Dudula members (OD) requested all shop owners to remove their stock and leave the townships, with only a few hours given to comply.


 Few days after the closure of 21 shops in Soweto, the local community began to oppose Operation Dudula, resisting the closure of additional shops. Although Operation Dudula still hopes that local community members will join the movement against foreign nationals in Soweto Township, they plan to continue their activities on Monday, August 19, 2024. However, the local community has started to disengage from Operation Dudula.
records.response: The police was accompanied the operation Dudula members.

records.name: In Cofimvaba, 2 Ethiopian shopkeepers shot dead and one is fighting for his life in hospital
records.description: On the evening of August 13, 2024, three Ethiopian shopkeepers, aged between 32 and 35, were working in their spaza shop when two gunmen entered and opened fire. The attack resulted in the fatal wounding of two shopkeepers, while the third is in serious condition and receiving hospital treatment. The police have launched investigations into two murder cases and one attempted murder case. The motive behind the shooting remains unclear and is still under investigation. However, many in the Ethiopian community suspect that the attack was carried out by a new extortion group. They believe the shooting was an act of retaliation because the victims had refused to pay protection fees to this group, as they were already paying another extortion group.
records.response: The police opened 2 counts of murder and 1 count of attempted murder, but no arrest made so far

records.name: A call by Operation Dudula and the local community in Etwatwa to remove foreign shop owners from Ekurhuleni.
records.description: Conflicts arose between a foreign shop owner and a local young man who was intoxicated. The young man had previously dropped a court case against the shop owner for assault. Although the shop owner was fined, when the young man later demanded the money that the Somali shop owner had promised, he was assaulted again and died from his injuries on August 14, 2024. This incident sparked significant tension in the township, leading to the launch of Operation Dudula, which mobilized the local community in Etwatwa. The operation aimed to close down and remove all foreign-owned shops across the Ekurhuleni area, including Daveyton. Social media plans circulated among the community on how to handle the situation, and residents armed themselves with weapons, steel pipes, and other dangerous objects. Fortunately, the police responded quickly and effectively, preventing any property damage. Despite this, threats continued. Some foreign shop owners chose to close their shops and leave due to the threats, while others remained, believing they were not involved in the incident. A march against foreign shop owners was planned for August 23, 2024, just before the deceased’s funeral. However, the Etwatwa police intervened and aborted the march to prevent potential looting. In Etwatwa township, shops are operated by foreign nationals from Tanzania, Ethiopia, Somalia, and Pakistan.
records.response: The police in Etwatwa did a very good job and did not allow any damage or looting

records.name: Three Somali shopkeepers were gunned down and six others wounded in the informal settlement of Imizamo Yethu Hout Bay.
records.description: The evening of Friday, August 16, 2024, was marked by a horrific incident. Around 8 p.m., three Somali nationals were gunned down, and six others were wounded in three different spaza shops on Molokwane Street in Imizamo Yethu, Hout Bay, Cape Town. Each shop was attacked simultaneously by three armed men in what appeared to be a well-coordinated assault. The police arrived at the scene shortly after the attack, but the nine perpetrators had already fled. The six wounded Somali nationals are receiving treatment in the hospital. The motive behind the shooting remains unclear, but local residents speculate that it may be related to the Somali nationals' refusal to pay a protection fee to local gangs.
records.response: Police

records.name: An Ethiopian shop keeper of Mandlazini near Richards Bay is fighting for his life in ICU at Ngwelezana hospital following the shooting by extortionists
records.description: On Saturday, August 17, 2024, at around 8:30 PM, an Ethiopian shopkeeper was targeted by armed extortionists. They found him inside his shop on Koninga Road/Mandlazini near Richards Bay, shot him, and left him for dead. According to the Zululand Observer, which reported the incident, three men had visited the shop earlier that day. They demanded R1000 per month from each Ethiopian-owned spaza shop in Mandlazini as a protection fee. The shopkeeper gave them his employer's contact number, and they left in a white Toyota Hilux bakkie. They returned later at around 8:30 PM, fired shots at the shopkeeper through the window, and left him seriously injured without taking any valuables. The victim was taken to Nseleni Clinic and later transferred to Ngwelezana Hospital, where he is currently fighting for his life in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).
records.response: Not really. There are talks underway led by the district police management following that attack.

records.name: A Service Delivery Protest turned into Looting  of Shops and Damage to Properties owned by Foreign Nationals in Potchefstroom, North West
records.description: A notice of protest was issued to the residents of Ikageng Township on Friday, August 16, 2024. The protest, driven by grievances over water and electricity costs, called for shutting down schools and all public facilities, and instructed everyone to stay home. By Sunday, August 18, 2024, all roads in Ikageng and Promoda were blocked. The following day, August 19, around 11 a.m., taxi drivers and local community members began demonstrating by burning tires. The protests continued until the afternoon of August 20, when the local community began vandalizing shops owned by foreign nationals, including Somalians, Ethiopians, and Bangladeshis. Approximately 100 shops were damaged on that day. The situation remains volatile, with protesters threatening to return in two weeks if the municipality fails to address their concerns. This has caused significant fear among the migrant community in Potchefstroom. Many have started repairing their damaged shops, focusing on rebuilding from the roof. The police have advised migrant business owners to take measures to protect themselves.
records.response: The police intervened later, after the damage had been done.

records.name: Threats of Violence Against Foreign Shop Owners is about to break out in Thubalethu Township, near Melmoth
records.description: Violence is imminent in Thubalethu Township, where local shop owners are preparing to forcibly evict foreign spaza shop owners. On August 22, 2024, local business owners posted a notice on Facebook, which was then shared via WhatsApp, demanding the immediate removal of foreign-owned spaza shops in Thubalethu Township, Melmoth. The foreign spaza shop owners are operating legally, with valid trading licenses issued by the Mthonjaneni local municipality. This has angered local small business owners, who accuse the municipality of fraudulently issuing these licenses. They claim to have met with municipal officials, demanding the removal of the individual responsible for issuing the licenses, referred to as "O my friend." They allege that "O my friend" is a woman employed by Mthonjaneni municipality, but they are frustrated because the municipality is hiding her and claiming she is not at work. Local shop owners are now threatening to take matters into their own hands, planning to forcibly remove all foreign spaza shop owners from the township, regardless of their licensing status. They accuse these shop owners of selling expired goods and items that are allegedly not permitted for sale in South Africa. Additionally, local shop owners have accused law enforcement agencies of corruption for failing to arrest "O my friend" despite evidence suggesting that an arrest is warranted. The foreign spaza shop owners and operators are living in fear of an impending attack but are waiting anxiously as tensions continue to rise.
records.duration: The threat is still on at the time of recording this incident
records.response: The municipality is trying to intervene but so far they have not been successful

records.name: An Ethiopian businessman was stabbed, killed, and dumped on Jules Street (Malvern) in Johannesburg because he didn't pay protection fees.
records.description: Two brothers from Ethiopia, who had recently started a business partnership, were operating a car wash, parking service, and shop rentals at the corner of Bree and Nugget Streets in Johannesburg CBD. Their business began in February 2024, opening daily around 7 a.m. and closing between 8 and 9 p.m. In early July 2024, five months after opening, the brothers started receiving visits from three unknown local individuals demanding protection fees. On their first visit, the men demanded R500, which the brothers paid without any formal documentation. On July 24, 2024, the same individuals returned, this time armed. One of them was stationed at the gate to monitor it, while the other two entered the car wash premises. They demanded more money, insisting that everyone else had already paid their protection fees and that the brothers needed to do the same. The victim, one of the brothers, explained that the business was new and not yet making substantial profits. He requested to pay the protection fee the following month, in August 2024. The perpetrators began threatening him, and since his brother was not present at the time, the situation escalated. This incident occurred around 6 p.m. The female cleaner present was also pushed against the wall with her hands up. When the victim couldn’t pay, the perpetrators kidnapped him and drove him to Malvern, as tracked by his car's GPS. There, the victim was tortured and killed that same night. After the kidnapping, people in the area alerted the victim’s brother, advising him to contact the police. The brother went to John Foster Police Station, but the police were reluctant to go to Malvern, as the car tracker indicated Jules Street, a dangerous area. They advised the brother not to go there. Later, the victim was found with fatal injuries—his throat cut and multiple stab wounds. He was taken to Helen Joseph Hospital but did not survive. Following this tragic event, the entire family was traumatized and decided to leave the business premises.
records.response: The police were afraid to go to malvern as the car tracker indicated it as a dangerous location

records.name: More than 15 Immigrants Assaulted during early Morning Raid in Pietermaritzburg
records.description: In the early hours of Friday, from around 1:00 AM to 8:00 AM, a joint operation was conducted in Pietermaritzburg by the Department of Home Affairs and the South African Police Service (SAPS). The operation, which officially targeted hijacked buildings and undocumented foreign nationals, led to several arrests. Authorities focused on removing occupants from hijacked buildings and arresting undocumented individuals in areas such as Church Street, East Street, and Pietermaritz Street. On Church Street, the operation targeted Nooran Flat, a building housing hundreds of immigrants, both documented and undocumented. During the early morning hours, many people were arrested, including their children. According to SAPS, this operation is part of a larger initiative aimed at "sweeping KZN clean" of undocumented foreign nationals. It is estimated that over 200 people were arrested. Of these, more than 20 had valid documents and were later released. However, they reported being assaulted—some severely—by police officers. They claimed that their delays in opening their doors led to the assaults. Additionally, the victims alleged that their cellphones and laptops were stolen by the police, who remained in their flats searching for drugs and other items, while the residents were taken to the police station for verification.
records.who_attacked: Immigrants living in 4 targeted flats in central Pietermaritzburg
records.duration: The operation started around 01h00 and lasted up to 8h00
records.response: This was a joint operation, so no response was possible

records.name: The police beat and break the leg of the Malawian supervisor of Nooran Flat, during a raid.
records.description:
In the early hours of Saturday, September 7, 2024, at around 1 AM, police and immigration officers raided several buildings known to house immigrants in downtown Pietermaritzburg, primarily targeting Nooran Flat at 503 Church Street. This building is home to hundreds of immigrants, both documented and undocumented. One victim, a documented Malawian national and supervisor of the building, was severely beaten, resulting in a broken leg and the theft of an undisclosed amount of money by the police. In a video sent to us by the victim, he recounts hearing women and children crying and the sound of heavy boots in the building at around 1 AM. As the supervisor, he confronted the police, asking to see their search warrant. In response, they began to beat him and insult him, telling him to return to his home country and ask those questions there. The assault was so severe that he lost consciousness and fell, breaking his leg in the process.

While he lay unconscious, some officers broke into his flat, forcibly opened his cupboard, and took his savings—approximately R5,700—along with his cellphone. Despite the visible swelling in his leg, the police took him to Loop Street Police Station along with other immigrants, both documented and undocumented. It was not until around 10 AM that they transported him to a hospital, where he received treatment and was eventually released three days later.
records.response: The only response is the treatment he received from the hospital

records.name: 2 Burundian asylum seekers jailed before they could apply for asylum at home affairs
records.description: At 161 Vusi Mzimela Road in Mayville, Durban, opposite Bassas Hardware, there are two converted containers serving as barber shops, operated by a Burundian permanent resident in South Africa. Most of the employees are young Burundian male asylum seekers, some of whom are still waiting to apply for asylum at the local refugee reception center in Durban. On Saturday, September 7, 2024, around 10:00 AM, a police van stopped in front of the barber shops and entered the containers, demanding that all workers produce documentation proving their legal status in the country. Those with asylum documents presented them, but two individuals who did not have any documentation were arrested. Despite their attempts to explain their ongoing efforts to apply for asylum at Home Affairs, the police were uninterested and took them to the local police station, where they were held until their court appearance the following Monday. The owner of the barber shops was called and rushed to the police station to inquire about the arrests. He was subsequently arrested for employing "illegal foreigners" but was later released after paying a R5,000 fine, which he is currently appealing. The two detained individuals have appeared in court twice but remain in Westville Prison. Being new to the country, they lack the resources to hire a private lawyer and have not yet found a pro bono lawyer to represent them. These arrests of asylum seekers, along with their potential deportation before they have a chance to apply for asylum at Home Affairs, violate the principle of "non-refoulement" outlined in the 1951 UN Refugee Convention, to which South Africa is a signatory without reservation.
records.duration: The victims are still in Westville prison
records.response: They have since appeared twice before the magistrate court.

records.name: A Refugee podcaster is agressed for covering an extortion incident in Empangeni
records.description:
An asylum seeker based in Empangeni, calls himself an investigative journalist who runs an online podcast that focuses on social cohesion and issues affecting asylum seekers and refugees. On Thursday 12 September 2024 around 16h00, he went to Ngwelezana road and interviewed a Pakistani cellphone trader who have just been extorted an undisclosed sum of money by people who were wearing police uniform.  On his way back, he stopped at his studio, located near the train station. As soon as he stopped, while still seated in his car, 5 guys erupted from nowhere and surrounded his car. They were masked up but were wearing what looked like uMkontho weSizwe Party (MKP) regalia with no logo, so it was difficult to properly identify or recognise them.
They smashed his windscreen and back window and started intimidating him, telling him "auzwe wena inja" meaning, you don't listen you dog. They then took his equipment from the back seat, which included 2 cameras, boom microphone and a report ring light and then left. The victim said that he panicked, lost control and only recovered when they had already left.
He is still considering to report the matter to police, considering that in previous  occasions, they took no action against the perpetrators.
records.who_attacked: A podcaster who runs a podcast on refugees and social cohesion
records.response: No response

records.name: A Pakistani shop owner extorted by people wearing police uniform in Empangeni, Northern KZN
records.description:
A Pakistani man who has a cellphone repair shop in Ngwelezane B, near Empangeni is used to paying protection fees to a local gang but what happened to him and his shop on Thursday 12 September around 16h00 was different. He was busy working in his shop when 3 men wearing police uniform knocked at the gate of his shop. Although he did not see their van, he believed they were police officers, so he opened the gate. 
When they entered his shop, they did not have badges and did not show their service cards; instead they started asking him questions about his business and whether he is documented or not. Later on they became aggressive in the way they were speaking to an extent where they served themselves with expensive cellphones that he was selling and an undisclosed amount of money, which was in the shop. They then left and went after a podcaster who came to interview the shop owner for something else. When asked whether he did report the incident to the police, the shop owner said he did not want to endanger his life as he thought his extortionists were probably police officers. He said, in any case he reported a few incidents in the past, and even opened cases but nothing was done. It is a waste of time and energy, he said.
records.response: No, the victim did not call the police for fear of retaliation

records.name: A rejected asylum seeker is forced to pay R3000 to immigration officers
records.description: A Congolese asylum seeker received a communication from Home Affairs regarding the renewal of his asylum visa. He was informed that a final decision had been made, and he should go to collect this decision on Friday, September 20, 2024. Typically, this notice indicates that an appeal has been unsuccessful, meaning he would receive a final rejection letter instructing him to leave the country within 14 days. Many asylum seekers face arrest at Home Affairs' refugee reception offices immediately after receiving such letters. Concerned about potential arrest, he reported to Lawyers for Human Rights before his appointment. Upon arrival, he received the final rejection letter, which confirmed he must leave the country within 14 days. However, shortly after receiving the letter, two immigration officers arrested him, placed him in their van, and stated they were taking him to an undisclosed police station. Instead of heading to a police station, the officers drove around Durban for several hours, demanding R3,000 for his release. When he explained he didn’t have the money, they instructed him to call his relatives to arrange the funds, which he did. He was finally released around 6:00 PM after his cousin delivered the R3,000. The officers let him go without providing any documentation. This incident highlights a troubling trend for newcomers and rejected asylum seekers in South Africa, where victims are unlawfully arrested and pressured to pay a fee—an act that resembles extortion.
records.duration: The whole day, about 5 hours, the victims' relatives brought him money later in the afternoon
records.response: Not that we are aware of at the moment

records.name: Burundian barbers are attacked again in Mayville, Durban
records.description: This is the third incident involving young Burundian barbers working in two converted container shops at 161 Vusi Mzimela Road in Mayville, Durban, across from Bassas Hardware. Previously, in April of last year, three barbers were shot and injured but survived. Following that attack, they refused to return, forcing the owner to find replacements. Three weeks ago, police targeted the shops again, arresting two undocumented newcomers who could not secure appointments at Home Affairs' refugee reception center. On Saturday, September 21, a mob of over 30 locals from a nearby informal settlement gathered outside the shops, chanting xenophobic slogans such as "nina amakwerekwere hambeni Kini, asinifuni la," which translates to "you foreigners, go back to your countries, we don't want you here." Their anger escalated when they did not see the shop owner, who is also Burundian, and they began throwing stones and beating the barbers with sjamboks. They eventually took three barbers hostage to pressure the owner to come forward, while others shouted "mabahambe," meaning "let them go." Instead of confronting the mob, the owner reported the incident to the police and filed a case. The police escorted him to the scene, stating they needed to review the CCTV footage before taking action. When the mob learned that the police were present, they released the beaten barbers. Currently, both shops remain closed, and none of the barbers are willing to return to work there. It’s also important to note that the owner had been paying a monthly protection fee of R500 to a local gang, two members of which were shot and killed two months ago.
records.response: The police responded late. The injured were also treated at King Edward VIII hospital.

records.name: A Congolese refugee woman is arrested and handcuffed by police even after exhibiting her valid ID
records.description: A Congolese refugee woman operates a registered beauty salon at 57 Alan Paton Avenue in Scottsville, Pietermaritzburg. She has a business account with First National Bank. On Friday, September 20, 2024, two police officers (one male, one female) visited her salon, inquiring about nail prices before leaving. The next day, Saturday, September 21, around 1:30 PM, four officers returned, including the previous ones, and demanded to see the passports of all employees. The owner explained that she, as a refugee, does not possess a passport but has a valid refugee ID. When she presented her valid maroon ID, the officers questioned its legitimacy and insisted on taking her to the police station for ID verification. Despite her attempts to explain that her business is registered with SARS and her ID was used to open her business account, the officers became aggressive. They insulted her, suggesting South Africans could do their own hair and accused her of arrogance. Their hostility escalated when they noticed she was recording them; one officer attempted to smash her phone, causing it to fall along with her wallet. Ultimately, they handcuffed her and placed her in the back of their vehicle. Instead of taking her to the police station, they drove around for three hours. As her hands swelled and became painful, she pleaded for her handcuffs to be removed so she could breastfeed her baby. Hearing this, the officers released her from the cuffs but demanded R1,000 for her release. She refused and insisted on going to the police station instead. Around 6:00 PM, she was taken to Alexandra Police Station, where she found over 20 others arrested for lacking proper documentation. Fortunately, an immigration officer confirmed her documents were valid, and she was released. That night, she sought medical treatment at a local clinic, and the following day, she reported the incident to the police station management, who promised to investigate.
records.response: She reported her ordeal to the police management and they promised to investigate.

records.name: A Burundian Refugee is seriously assaulted, arrested and had to spend 10 days in prison, even though his document was valid
records.description: On the morning of Tuesday, September 24, 2024, it was unusually quiet for barbers along Charlotte Maxeke Street. A Burundian refugee stood in front of his shop, observing the street. Around 10:00 a.m., a police van stopped nearby, and officers called him over, asking for his documents. He explained that his documents were in his bag inside the shop. As he went to retrieve them, the officers followed him and began assaulting him, leaving him bleeding. They claimed his body language had offended them. Despite the assault, he managed to show them his documents, but they threw them to the ground and continued beating him. They then handcuffed him, placed him in the back of their van, and accused him of being an illegal immigrant with fake papers. Later, two more individuals were added to the van, accused of stealing a cellphone. While in the van, the police continued to assault the Burundian refugee, using derogatory language and threatening that they could shoot him without consequences. He questioned why they were assaulting him over his documents while not touching the two locals accused of theft, asking whether it was because he was a foreigner. After spending the weekend in custody, the verification process confirmed that his documents were valid. However, the police then added a new charge, accusing him of stealing a cellphone, just like the other two detainees. This accusation was baseless, as he does not use smartphones, and no phone was found on him when they searched him at the time of his arrest. After 10 days in prison, he was released on Friday, October 4, 2024, on R2000 bail.
records.duration: He was released on R2000 bail on Friday 4 October 2024
records.response: He was released 10 days later on R2000 bail.

records.name: Two police officers assaulted an Ethiopian national in his spaza shop in Mangaung Vredendal, North Western Cape
records.description: On Monday morning, 29 September 2024, in Mangaung Vredendal North, an Ethiopian national spaza shop owner was operating his daily business when suddenly, around 9.30, he spotted a 13-year-old boy speedily enter his shop and went behind the shelves and walked out promptly. The shop owner didn't pay attention to what the boy was doing, as he was occupied serving customers. Then, after five minutes, when the boy left, a local man walked to the shop and asked him to give the stuff that the boy dropped there. The shop owner retorted to the man what stuff he was talking about because the boy walked in and out quickly from the shop. The local man didn't want to believe the shop owner when he told him that he was not aware of the stuff that the boy brought, and there is no description about the stuff, so their discussion turned into a huge argument. At that moment, a police van with two officers was patrolling the street. The local man halted the van and explained the issue to the officers in Afrikaans, while the shop owner doesn't speak or understand Afrikaans. After listening to the local man, the two officers entered the shop and asked the owner to give the stuff without hearing his side of the story. The Ethiopian national repeated the same thing to the officers, but they insisted up until they lost their temper and started to beat the shop owner. He suffered serious wounds and was taken to the hospital by two community members to be treated. Fortunately, there are cameras inside the shop, and the incident was recorded.
records.response: Community members

records.name: A Burundian asylum seeker is arrested by police and asked to pay R1000 before they could release him
records.description: A Burundian asylum seeker applied to renew his asylum document in June 2024. Instead of receiving the renewed document, on June 10, he received a notice directing him to report to the Cape Town Refugee Reception Office (RRO) on October 24, 2024, for processing. In the meantime, he had been using this notice to explain his situation to anyone who asked for his documentation. On Friday, October 4, 2024, around 7:30 a.m., while returning from a nearby store, he was stopped by the police. When they asked for his documents, he presented his expired asylum paper along with the notice summoning him to the Cape Town RRO on October 24. The police refused to accept his explanation, detained him, and placed him in the back of their van. For the next five hours, the police drove around, repeatedly demanding R1000 for his release. Despite his constant pleas that he did not have such money, they pressured him to call friends or relatives to deliver the amount. When he told them that no one could help him, they eventually abandoned him around 1:00 p.m. in an unknown location, forcing him to spend R50 on transport back to town. This incident reflects a growing trend in which police, whether acting within or outside the law, arrest immigrants with the sole purpose of extorting money from them.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: A Somali shop owner is accused of injecting poison into snacks in Phomolong township, near Hennenman.
records.description: At around 1:00 am on Tuesday, October 8, 2024, a group of residents from Phomolong township, near Hennenman in the Free State, confronted a Somali shop owner, accusing him of injecting poison into snacks sold at his spaza shop. The group mobilized more community members, who forced the shop to close indefinitely. Police were called to the scene and collected the allegedly poisoned snacks for pathological testing. Two days later, the test results confirmed that there was no evidence of poisoning. Following the findings, the police ordered the shop to reopen.
records.duration: The shop was closed for 4 days
records.response: Yes, the police ordered the shop to close until the results of the pathological report was available.

records.name: Migrants residing at Elwyin court are under siege by elements of Umkontho weSizwe Party
records.description: Elwyin Court, located at 362 Mahatma Gandhi Road in Durban, is a large building with many flats, primarily occupied by immigrants, mostly refugees and asylum seekers from Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo. On Sunday, October 6, 2024, several individuals wearing military uniforms of the MKP (Umkhonto weSizwe Party) entered the building, walked around silently, and then left without speaking to the tenants. However, on Wednesday, October 9, 2024, around 1:00 p.m., buses arrived and dropped off a large group of people in MKP uniforms carrying bags and other belongings. These individuals stormed the building. When questioned, some said they had been sent to occupy all flats currently rented by immigrants, though they refused to reveal who had sent them. This caused panic among the tenants, who locked themselves inside their flats, fearing they would lose their homes if they stepped out. The MKP members stationed themselves across all eight levels of the building and the stairwells, as if waiting for further instructions. Later, it was revealed that the group was led by a Zulu princess, who moved around the building on crutches. She demanded documents from the immigrant tenants, claiming she was acting on behalf of dissatisfied African flat owners. In response, the building's supervisor filed a case with the local police station for intimidation, harassment, and trespassing. The police intervened the following day, around 11:00 a.m., evicting all those in the MKP uniforms, including the princess. The police operation concluded around 1:00 p.m.
records.who_attacked: Elwyin court, a building occupied predominantly by immigrants from DRC and Burundi
records.duration: The situation remained the same until the following day (Thursday), when the police evicted the perpetrators.
records.response: Yes, the police came on Wednesday night to assist the supervisor to open a case and then came back the following day, to evicts the perpetrators.

records.name: Angry Soweto residents in Naledi closed foreign-owned shops after the alleged deaths of five children, believed to be due to food poisoning.
records.description: Over the first weekend of October 2024, tragedy struck Naledi Township in Soweto when five children, all friends, lost their lives. This sparked outrage in the local community, which began to mobilize, targeting landlords who rent spaces to foreign nationals and demanding the removal of all spaza shops in the area. According to the community, when they operated these shops themselves, there were no deaths from food poisoning, but since foreign nationals took over, such incidents have reportedly increased. On Monday, October 7, 2024, the local community gave all spaza shop owners a one-day deadline to leave Naledi. Amid rising tensions, the police urged the community to remain law-abiding and assisted some foreign shop owners in removing their stock. However, on October 9, 2024, the shops that had not been emptied were vandalized and looted. The following day, October 10, the police arrived to monitor the situation and disperse the looters as looting continued. Environmental health practitioners cited the failure of these spaza shops to meet public food safety standards, further fueling calls to shut down all spaza shops across the country. By Monday, October 14, 2024, Operation Dudula arrived in Naledi, but they found that most of the shops had already been closed by the local community. The exact number of shops closed in Naledi has not yet been determined, and the situation remains ongoing.
records.who_attacked: Shops owned by foreign nationals in Naledi
records.response: The police presence was effective .

records.name: A Somali pregnant refugee woman was forced to pay R 1500 before being attended at Rob Ferrara Hospital.
records.description: On Thursday, October 11, 2024, at around 6 a.m., a pregnant Somali woman was rushed to Rob Ferrara Hospital in Nelspruit, Mpumalanga, to give birth. Upon arrival, the hospital clerks and nurses on duty refused to assist her, demanding a payment of R1500 before providing any care. The person accompanying her made several phone calls in a desperate attempt to gather the money, while the woman, in severe pain and ready to deliver, pleaded for help. Despite her condition, the nurses insisted that no assistance would be given without the payment. After hours of distress, a family member arrived around 10 a.m. and paid the required amount. Only then did the nurses begin to attend to her. It is important to note that the woman is legally in South Africa, holding refugee status for the past four years.
records.response: Victim was assisted family paid the amount demanded by the nurses

records.name: Looting and Closure of Migrant-Owned Spaza Shops After Local Business was Killed
records.description: On October 12, 2024, spaza shops predominantly owned by Ethiopians in Sharpeville were targeted for shutdown by vigilantes posing as local community members. This followed the Naledi food poisoning incident, which allegedly claimed the lives of six children. Tensions escalated further after reports emerged of a local business owner's alleged killing, which was falsely attributed to migrants. On October 14, the Sharpeville police station commandant ordered the closure of all spaza shops after Ethiopian community leaders reported threats from a group wielding machetes and chanting hate songs. The violence quickly escalated, with looting beginning at shops directly opposite the Sharpeville police station, raising concerns about police inaction. Approximately 200 Ethiopian-owned spaza shops were looted, and shopkeepers were locked inside for three days before being forced to flee as attackers broke in. Many Ethiopian shopkeepers were beaten and injured while escaping. The affected areas included Vooker I, Sepiso Phase 1 and 2, Pala Ndaba, Bencher, Phase 3, and Phase 5. Despite the looting and destruction, the shops have since been rebuilt and rented out to local tenants, with Ethiopian shopkeepers barred from resuming their businesses. It is alleged that landlords are now renting the premises to locals. Ethiopian community leaders were in discussions with district officials to find a resolution at the time of conducting verification
records.response: Police

records.name: Community members of Masthula township in Nelspruit shut down fifteen foreign national spaza shops.
records.description: A group of community members in Matshulu township Nelspruit has closed down fifteen foreign national spaza shops on Thursday, October 24, 2024, around 10 o'clock after twenty-four pupils allegedly ate food poisoned and were rushed to hospitals. The reason for closing foreign spaza shops is that they have been accused of selling expired and poisoned foods. Those shops closed down belong to Somali, Ethiopian, and Pakistani nationals.
records.response: No

records.name: Foreign owned shops looted in Rockland/Bloemfontein
records.description:
On Thursday night 7 November, around 21h00, spaza shops operated by immigrants were looted in various parts of Rockland location in Bloemfontein, after 47 learners were admitted at Pelomoni Regional Hospital from suspected food poisoning. The number of spaza shops looted so far is still unknown but safe to say that one of those looted shops was operated by a Congolese national and another one by 3 Bangladeshis. 

It is alleged that those learners consumed expired biscuits and chocolates bought from one of foreign-owned spaza shop, situated on Moshoeshoe street. The owners of all those spaza shops are in hiding, fearing for their lives while looters and other locals vow that, from now onward, no foreigner will be allowed to operate spaza shops in their respective areas. Instead they want citizen to take over. 
So far, 29 looters have been arrested for public violence
records.who_attacked: Various foreigners who operate spaza shops in Rockland/Bloemfontein
records.duration: The looting continued until Friday morning when the police intervened.
records.response: Yes, so far the police has arrested 29 looters for public violence

records.name: Daveyton residents says no to foreign owned spaza shop.
records.description: On November 11, 2024, a wave of xenophobic violence forced foreign spaza shop owners in Dayveton, Etwatwa, to shut down their businesses. The attacks targeted shops across several streets, including Turton, Eiselen, Kheswa, Gumede, and Emahlobo, with an estimated 65 spaza shops affected. Most of the shopkeepers, who are migrants from other African countries, faced intimidation, threats, verbal abuse, and violence despite their role in serving the local community. This incident followed a mass gathering at Sinaba Stadium on November 10, where local residents called for the expulsion of foreign traders from the Etwatwa community. The unrest was reportedly linked to an alleged food poisoning incident in Naledi, Soweto, which claimed the lives of six children. Shopkeepers in Dayveton were given an ultimatum: close their businesses and leave or face physical harm. The police were present but remained passive, failing to intervene as residents vandalized and looted the shops. This escalated the already volatile situation, leaving the community deeply divided and the affected shopkeepers displaced.
records.response: It is reported that the Police were present but did not intervene

records.name: Four Somali national spaza shops stormed by a group of community members in Nelspruit, Mpumalanga province.
records.description: On Monday evening, November 11, 2024, at around 8 pm, a group of community members in Nelspruit, Mpumalanga province, targeted four spaza shops owned by Somali nationals. They removed all the snacks from the shelves, took some with them, and burned others outside the shops. The attack was allegedly prompted by reports that 21 pupils had been hospitalized after consuming food, suspected to be poisonous, purchased from local vendors and spaza shops. The looters accused the shop owners of trying to harm their children. Despite the severity of the situation, there was no response from law enforcement or police.
records.response: No

records.name: Foreign nationals in Umlazi J section threatened and forced to close their Spaza shops amid fears of poisoned food
records.description: On Saturday, November 16, 2024, a group of individuals went door-to-door in uMlazi's J Section, ordering spaza shop owners to close amid allegations of contaminated goods. The group specifically targeted foreign nationals, warning them to shut down their shops or face severe consequences. Tensions rose in the area following claims that children had fallen ill after consuming food purchased from these shops. Many foreign shop owners, fearing for their safety, quickly closed their shops as the group used aggressive language, saying, "Shut down, or we will deal with you." The group also threatened to return and take action if the shops reopened. Some shop owners expressed uncertainty and fear about reopening, stating they were unsure how long the closures would last. They emphasized that reopening under current conditions would put their lives at risk. For now, the shops will remain closed until the situation stabilizes, although there is no clear timeline for when that might happen.
records.response: Not that we are aware of

records.name: An Ethiopian shop owner is forced to keep his shop closed on false pretences
records.description: On Sunday, November 17, 2024, at around 7:30 am, four intoxicated community members forced the closure of a spaza shop run by an Ethiopian asylum seeker. They claimed that a 9-year-old boy had been hospitalised the previous night after consuming an allegedly expired snack from the shop, located at House No. 2608, Khwebula Road, Welbedach West, Chatsworth. Although the child was reportedly discharged from the hospital, community members prevented us from speaking to him or his parents during our visit. The police were called to the scene, inspected the shop, and found no expired snacks. They took samples for testing and advised the shop owner to keep the shop closed until tensions eased. On Monday, November 18, the shop's landlady applied for a protection order against the four instigators.
