She alleged that their actions were driven by jealousy over the income she earns from renting the property to the Ethiopian shopkeeper. According to her, one of the instigators, a former Transnet employee, plans to open his own spaza shop in the area and orchestrated the food poisoning allegations to eliminate competition. He allegedly bribed and bought alcohol for some community members to support his efforts. The community remains divided: some support reopening the shop, others prefer to wait for the laboratory test results, and some demand the shop's permanent closure regardless of the findings.
records.duration: The spaza shop is still closed as we submit this report
records.response: Police attended the scene and the landlord is applying for protection order at Chatsworth Magistrate court.

records.name: Foreign spaza shop owners face uphill battle to register their spaza shops in Gauteng
records.description: Members of the Patriotic Alliance (PA) and government officials are actively obstructing migrant spaza shop owners from registering their businesses in Soweto. The PA has targeted spaza shops owned by Somali, Ethiopian, and Bangladeshi nationals, using xenophobic and hate-filled rhetoric to threaten migrants. They have also been closing shops, contacting landlords to enforce disputes, and demanding the immediate closure of foreign-owned businesses. While the government has initiated efforts to formalize the informal retail sector, many foreign entrepreneurs face significant challenges during the registration process. The PA has mobilised the local community in Soweto to oppose the registration of migrant-owned businesses, arguing that such shops are illegal and that local businesses should be reserved for South Africans. Foreign spaza shop owners report numerous hurdles, including being met with hostility at registration offices, having their applications repeatedly rejected for incomplete or additional documentation, and even facing threats or physical attacks from local community members. This growing hostility, fueled by the Patriotic Alliance and some local community members, has created a hostile environment for migrant business owners, making it increasingly difficult for them to operate or formalise their businesses.
records.response: Police were called to assist

records.name: Six foreign owned spaza shops looted in full view of the police at Ntuzuma B Section
records.description: On Wednesday, November 20, 2024, at around 11:00 am, several spaza shops owned by foreign nationals in Soweto Road, Ntuzuma B, were looted in broad daylight while police officers were present but failed to intervene. According to a witness, the police arrived at one shop and demanded the shopkeeper’s documentation to verify their legal status in South Africa. The shopkeeper complied and handed over the documents. However, the police decided to detain the shopkeeper in a van while conducting a verification process. As the shopkeeper remained in custody, a crowd gathered outside the shop, growing increasingly aggressive. In full view of the police, the crowd broke into the shop, ransacked it, and looted its contents. The police, accompanied by the crowd, then moved to five additional Ethiopian-owned spaza shops in the area. At each location, they arrested the shopkeepers for document verification—three of whom had valid documents, while two were undocumented newcomers. At every shop where arrests were made, the crowd looted and destroyed property using the same method, again with the police taking no action to stop them. The looting and destruction continued until approximately 8:00 pm. By then, the four shopkeepers who had valid documents were released, while the two undocumented individuals remained in police custody.
records.who_attacked: 6 Ethiopian owned spaza shops and their shopkeepers
records.duration: It only ended around 20h00 at night
records.response: Yes the police responded late and arrested 6 of the perpetrators

records.name: 2 Ethiopian shopkeepers severely assaulted and their shop looted in full view of the police in Ntuzuma B
records.description: On Wednesday, November 20, 2024, these inspections took place in Ntuzuma B Section. What set Ntuzuma apart was the presence of a crowd of locals following the police, leading to the looting of six Ethiopian-owned spaza shops. At one shop on Soweto Road, the two Ethiopian shopkeepers, aware of the operation, removed certain food items from their shelves and hid them in their landlord's house, leaving the shop half-stocked. When law enforcement arrived, the unusual state of the shop raised suspicion among the crowd, who demanded to search the landlord's house. The shopkeepers resisted, but the crowd assaulted them severely, forcing entry into the house, retrieving the hidden food, and looting it. The shopkeepers were badly injured in the attack and were later taken to Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital for treatment. One was hospitalized and discharged two days later. According to one of the victims, the police were present in significant numbers but failed to intervene or stop the assault and looting.
records.who_attacked: Ethiopian shopkeepers and their spaza shop
records.response: The victims were taken to hospital where they were treated.

records.name: Foreign owned spaza shops looted in Villa Liza (Boksburg)
records.description: On November 20, 2024, tensions escalated in Villa Liza, near Ekurhuleni, as community members forced foreign shop owners to leave the township. The shop owners, mostly Somali and Ethiopian nationals, were waiting for police escorts to collect their belongings from rented premises due to local opposition to migrants operating businesses in the area. While waiting for police assistance, the situation worsened when some residents began looting the shops. This incident underscores the rising hostility between local residents and foreign business owners, fueled by accusations that migrants were selling expired food. The violence and looting have left the shop owners not only intimidated but also without livelihoods, as their shops remain closed, stock is damaged or stolen, and safety concerns persist. The local community has declared that no migrant-owned shop should reopen in Villa Liza, further heightening the uncertainty and fear faced by these business owners.
records.who_attacked: Spaza shops and their owners  who are Somalians and Ethiopians
records.response: police came to help foreign owned spaza shops to remove their stock

records.name: Operation Dudula members  blocking and monitoring the registration   process of foreign owned shops in Soweto
records.description: On November 20, 2024, Operation Dudula members pledged to block foreign-owned spaza shops from registering their businesses in Soweto. This followed President Cyril Ramaphosa’s announcement requiring all spaza shops, especially in Gauteng Province, to register and comply within 21 days. Operation Dudula mobilized in Soweto, gathering at the Jabulani Civic Center (JCC) to rally local community members. They claimed to be defending the township economy and alleged that landlords were dissatisfied with Somali and Pakistani tenants, who reportedly abandoned shops they had built after moving out. On November 21, 2024, Operation Dudula members conducted raids across Soweto, monitoring the registration process. During these raids, locals assisting migrants with registration were harassed, cornered, and publicly humiliated. The tension escalated into chaos, forcing the Soweto municipality to suspend the registration process. Operation Dudula members and some locals actively chased away migrants, accusing them of being responsible for the deaths of South African children and asserting that township businesses should be reserved exclusively for South Africans.
records.response: The civil center in Jabulani  suspended the registration process,

records.name: Diepkloof residents in Soweto on Spaza shop owners after the death of a 5 years old.
records.description: Tensions are high in Diepkloof following the death of a 5-year-old child, allegedly from food poisoning after consuming snacks bought from a spaza shop. Anger has erupted, with the local community demanding the closure of all spaza shops, particularly foreign-owned ones, which were already under scrutiny after last month’s Naledi food poisoning incident. Community members have called on landlords to prevent any spaza shops from reopening. Shop owners have been instructed to remove their stock, shut down their businesses, and leave the area. In addition to the food poisoning allegations, migrants are also being accused of selling drugs, further fueling hostility. The shop where the child reportedly bought the snacks became the focal point of the unrest. The owner was surrounded by an angry crowd for hours, with police providing protection while awaiting inspectors to investigate the matter. The shopkeeper had expressed willingness to cover the child’s hospital expenses, but tragically, the child did not survive. The shop has since been closed. The community has vowed to take matters into their own hands, stating they will ensure no spaza shop in Diepkloof reopens, regardless of any government intervention.
records.response: Yes, the police arrived and protected the shop owner and the shop, preventing it from being vandalised

records.name: A large, angry community member in Delmas burnt, looted, and closed down foreign spaza shops.
records.description: On Thursday, November 28, 2024, at around 8 p.m., an angry crowd in Delmas, Mpumalanga, took to the streets, targeting foreign-owned spaza shops. The mob set fire to three shops, looted seven others, and forced the closure of more than twenty businesses, primarily owned by Ethiopians and Somalis. The unrest was triggered by allegations linking foreign spaza shops to the tragic deaths of six children in Naledi, Soweto, reportedly due to food poisoning. The Delmas community accused the shop owners of selling expired and harmful food products to children. Police arrived late to the scene to restore order, but tensions remain high, with many residents demanding the permanent closure of all foreign-owned spaza shops in the area.
records.response: Police responded late

records.name: Spaza shop in K section, uMlazi torched aftershop owner was unable to pay protection fees of R5000 demanded by extortionists
records.description: In a tragic incident highlighting the growing trend of extortion targeting foreign-owned spaza shops, an Ethiopian shop owner lost everything when his business was set on fire by a group of men in uMlazi, K section, on Saturday, 7 December. The shop owner described the ordeal, saying, “I narrowly escaped when five men ransacked and set my shop ablaze, threatening to kill me if I didn’t pay.” The Ethiopian national has been operating his shop since arriving in Durban in 2006, but now he has lost all his hard work and is left with nothing. He lives in constant fear and has decided not to reopen his shop in the area for the safety of his wife and two children, as he fears the same thing could happen again. While the government and spaza shop owners are focused on meeting the 13 December deadline to register spaza shops in an attempt to regulate the sector, the increasing violence and extortion against foreign spaza shop owners, like this Ethiopian man, are creating even greater threats to the livelihoods of informal businesses in townships, particularly those run by foreign nationals.
records.response: No because the shop owner was still considering to open a case but was worried about his safety if he goes ahead.

records.name: Arson Attack on Salon in Delft
records.description: A woman who owns a salon in Delft became the victim of an arson attack by a group of men, suspected of wanting to prevent her from operating in the area. The men set fire to her salon, destroying the property and forcing her out of business. This incident is believed to be part of a larger pattern of intimidation against foreign-owned businesses in the region. Authorities are investigating the case.
records.who_attacked: A congolese Woman who owns a salon
records.response: No intervention reported

records.name: 50-Year-Old Man Dies After Alleged Police Torture During Search
records.description: A 50-year-old man died after allegedly being tortured by police officers during a search operation. According to reports, the victim was stopped by police on the road and complied when officers requested to search him. He was then taken to his home, where officers conducted further searches. It is alleged that during this process, the police tortured the victim, covering his head with a plastic bag until he suffocated and died. Only after his death did the police reportedly open a case, accusing him of possession and sale of drugs.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Man Killed, Another Injured in Extortion-Related Shooting in Cape Town
records.description: A man was fatally shot, and another seriously injured in an extortion-related attack in Samora Machel, Cape Town. According to reports, the victim had just returned from  the Mosque and was heading to a barbershop where he worked when a group of extortionists approached him and his colleague. The assailants demanded money, but the victims did not have any cash on them at the time. Refusing to accept their explanation, the extortionists opened fire. The victim was shot seven times in the chest, while his colleague sustained a gunshot wound to the stomach. Both were rushed to the hospital, but the victim succumbed to his injuries upon arrival. His colleague survived and was discharged a week later. Police arrived at the scene and took statements, but no further action has reportedly been taken since the incident.
records.response: Police attended to the crime scene but no further interventions afterwards

records.name: Barbershop Owner Killed in Philippi for Refusing to Pay Extortion Fees
records.description: A Congolese national was shot and killed in Philippi after refusing to pay protection fees to extortionists. According to witnesses, the victim, a barbershop owner, was closing his shop when a group of extortionists demanded money. He refused, explaining that he had already made payments to two other individuals earlier in the month. Despite promising to pay them the following day, the assailants ignored his plea and shot him on the spot. The victim was declared dead at the scene. He is survived by his wife and four children.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Malawian Detainee Allegedly Abused in Custody, Parents Fear Taking Legal Action
records.description: A Malawian national was reportedly held in police custody instead of being taken to court for a magistrate’s decision, exposing him to severe abuse by fellow inmates. According to reports, the detainee was bullied and assaulted by other inmates, who demanded payment of R300  per day and threatened to kill him if he did not comply. He was beaten and subjected to degrading treatment, including being urinated on. The victim’s parents, fearing repercussions due to their documentation status, hesitated to open a case. The matter was reported to the Chairperson of the African Migration, who raised concerns with the Kokstad police station commander. Following this intervention, the officer in charge was instructed to transfer the victim to Francis Prison while awaiting trial. By law, the court is required to see the detainee within 48 hours before determining deportation; however, delays in the process have prolonged his detention.
records.response: Captain of the police intervened after the case was reported to him

records.name: Foreign-Owned Shops Attacked and Burned in Delft
records.description: A group of unidentified individuals attacked and set fire to three business containers owned by foreign nationals in Delft. The targeted shops belonged to Cameroonian, Congolese, and Burundian business owners. According to reports, the attackers do not want foreign nationals operating in the area. During the incident, one of the shop owners was physically assaulted. Among the items destroyed in the fire were televisions and microwaves. Police were present at the scene and encouraged the victims to open a case. However, no arrests have been reported.
records.response: Police attended the scene and encouraged victims to open a case

records.name: A 40-year-old Nigerian reportedly died while in South African police custody.
records.description:
A Nigerian national has died after allegedly being tortured and assaulted by police officers during a search operation. According to reports, the victim and his brother were stopped and searched by police officers before being taken to their residence for further inspection. Despite finding no incriminating evidence, the officers allegedly proceeded to torture and brutally assault both men. The victim succumbed to his injuries, falling into a coma before passing away. His brother survived the attack and later reported the incident to the Nigerian Citizens Association in South Africa (NICASA).
https://www.naijanews.com/2025/02/09/40-year-old-nigerian-benjamin-okoli-reportedly-tortured-and-beaten-to-death-at-south-african-police-custody/
records.who_attacked: A Nigerian National and his brother
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Sotho Man Murdered in Lutzville, Suspects Arrested
records.description: A Sotho man was robbed and fatally stabbed in the early hours of Saturday morning in Lutzville (Mbeki square). According to reports, the perpetrators attacked the victim during a robbery, resulting in his death. Police managed to apprehend the suspects following the incident. It is further alleged that a group of individuals regularly breaks into shacks belonging to foreign nationals, stealing cellphones, food, and clothing. The stolen goods are then resold to other foreign nationals, who later become targets of further theft. The perpetrators allegedly rob foreigners because they believe they are in South Africa illegally.
records.response: Police were able to apprehend the suspects

records.name: DRC National Assaulted and Detained by Police in Johannesburg
records.description: A man from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) was reportedly assaulted and verbally abused by police officers in Mafikeng on Saturday, 22 February. According to the victim, he was waiting outside a salon for his wife to finish having her hair done when two police vehicles arrived. He was with five other Congolese nationals. Officers questioned why he was standing outside instead of entering the salon and proceeded to demand his identification documents. After confirming that he had the necessary documentation, the officers allegedly began to assault him, beating him until he bled. When the victim asked why he was being attacked, the officers reportedly responded that they did so "because they wanted to. and that South Africa is their own country and they can do whatever they want" They also hurled derogatory insults at him, including calling him "Mokwerekwe," a xenophobic slur. The police then took the victim into custody, allegedly as a form of punishment. He was held in a cell until around 1 am, when he was released while being subjected to further verbal abuse. The officers allegedly told him, "If you think this is the DRC, go back to your home country and fight with M23. Following his release, the victim reported severe swelling on his head and required medical attention at a hospital.
records.response: No response reported

records.name: Violent Attack on Foreign-Owned Barber Shop in Delft: Third Incident
records.description:
At approximately 9:00 AM on 21st February 2025, a violent incident occurred at a foreign-owned barber shop and salon in Delft. Five gunmen, described as black South African males, entered the premises and confronted the individuals inside. Upon entering, the assailants asked the following questions:
"Why is this barber shop still here?"
"Today is the last day, and you will never operate here again."
While the gunmen were speaking, they opened fire. Two foreign nationals were shot and they are hospital and in a critical condition, and one South African male also died within the shop. This marks the third such violent incident at this location. The motive behind the attack appears to be linked to targeted intimidation of foreign-owned businesses in the area. Authorities are investigating the case.
records.response: Police came but nothing has been done so far

records.name: Denial of Medical Assistance and Delayed Care
records.description: A pregnant woman was denied immediate medical care at a hospital due to a demand for R1500 before any assistance could be provided. The woman arrived at the hospital without her husband, and upon presenting her case to the nursing staff, she was told that she could not receive care unless she paid the specified amount upfront. As a result of this delay, the woman’s delivery was severely impacted. The baby was born under distress, struggling to breathe, and was at risk of dying due to the delayed medical intervention. The life-threatening situation was only addressed once the payment issue was resolved, but the baby’s health had already been compromised due to the delay.
records.response: Payment of the fee demanded was made for the victim to receive assistance

records.name: Foreign Shops Forced to Close after an Ethiopian is Accused of Raping a 6 year old
records.description: An Ethiopian national, aged 26, was arrested in connection with the alleged rape of a 6-year-old girl in the Hendrina area. The incident reportedly occurred last Thursday (03 April), and the suspect was apprehended two days later. The alleged crime has sparked significant outrage within the local community, which has led to xenophobic actions targeting foreign nationals living and working in the area. As a direct result of the incident, local community members took to shutting down all shops owned by foreign nationals in Hendrina. The shops, which were largely run by migrants, were forcibly closed, with only South African shop owners permitted to continue operating their businesses. This action appears to be a direct response to the arrest of the Ethiopian national, who had been running a tuckshop in the area at the time of the alleged incident.
records.who_attacked: Shops owned by foreign nationals were forced to close
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Two Somali Nationals Fatally Shot in Mfuleni
records.description: Two foreign nationals of Somali nationality were shot and killed in Mfuleni, in what authorities suspect may be an extortion-related ambush. The incident took place at a spaza shop in the Wallacedene neighbourhood around 9:45 PM. According to reports, four armed men approached the shop and opened fire before fleeing the scene. One of the victims died at the scene, while the second was rushed to a nearby hospital but was later pronounced dead. Initial investigations suggest that the shooting may be linked to extortion, and authorities are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack.
records.response: SAPS are investigating the killings

records.name: Pregnant Zimbabwean Woman Harassed in Hospital
records.description: A pregnant Zimbabwean woman was publicly humiliated and denied medical care at Kalafong Hospital by members of the so-called Progressive Forces of South Africa. The woman, visibly pregnant and demonstrating remarkable calmness and dignity, was rejected from receiving medical assistance solely because of her foreign national status. In a distressing incident captured on video, she is seen walking away from the hospital, visibly upset.  She sought refuge on the street, she was confronted by a group of  South African women who mocked her and told her to go and give birth in her country. Despite the cruel treatment, the woman remained composed.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Extortion and Illegal Detention of Somali Refugee
records.description: A Somali refugee had their papers seized by the police, and they were subsequently taken into custody. The victim was held without legal justification, and it was only after the payment of R2000 to the police that they were released. The victim, who holds refugee status, was subjected to illegal detention and extortion by police officers. The demand for payment before releasing the individual is a violation of legal procedures and demonstrates the ongoing abuse of power faced by refugees and migrants in South Africa.
records.response: Payment was made for the victim to be released

records.name: Xenophobic Remarks by Healthcare Professional in  Local Clinic
records.description: A healthcare professional at a local clinic caught on camera making openly xenophobic remarks regarding the treatment of foreign nationals in South Africa. The nurse informed patients that starting from May 16th, the clinic would prioritise South African citizens over foreign nationals. She stated that even if non-South African patients arrived early in the morning to queue, they would be sent to the back in favour of South African patients. She justified this by claiming that South Africans are tired of being ill-treated in their own country and that foreign nationals, particularly those without proper documentation, should return to their countries. The healthcare professional further expressed her belief that foreign nationals owning property in South Africa was unacceptable, especially when they did not own property in their own countries. She also referred to an incident in which a foreign national was allegedly chased away from a hospital, claiming to be one of the individuals who had done so. The nurse emphasised that foreign nationals would not be allowed to give birth in South African hospitals and should instead return to their countries to do so. In her comments, the nurse also mentioned that children of foreign nationals attending South African schools should be removed, as they were not entitled to be in the country. She made it clear that South African citizens were now being treated as "foreign nationals" in their own country. Additionally, the healthcare professional distributed her personal phone number and informed the patients present that they were recruiting people to join a movement aimed at "taking back South Africa." She announced a meeting scheduled for May 24th at Rotunda Park in Tuffontain, where they would discuss and develop plans related to this movement.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Xenophobic Looting and Forced Eviction
records.description: On 15 May 2025, a Somali shop owner who resides in Mayfair and operates a small business in Roodepoort was violently attacked. The incident began when the property owner/landlord informed the shop owner that he no longer wished to rent to a foreign national, despite the tenant having paid three months' rent in advance. The landlord refused to engage in further discussion and instead brought a group of individuals to forcibly evict the shop owner. The group proceeded to loot the shop, stealing goods estimated to be worth R250,000. Two employees of the shop were physically assaulted and fled the scene. The victim contacted the police; however, by the time they arrived, the perpetrators had already looted the premises and left. The incident has had a devastating impact on the victim’s livelihood. He has lost his stock, place of business, and sense of security. The case was referred to Future Families for social and psychosocial assistance.
records.who_attacked: A Somali Shop Owner and his employees
records.response: The SAPS were called but arrived when the damage had already been done

records.name: Fatal Shooting of Two Nigerian Nationals Outside Hotel in Pretoria
records.description: A tragic shooting occurred outside the Capitol Hill Hotel in Pretoria, resulting in the deaths of two Nigerian nationals. According to eyewitness accounts and video surveillance footage reviewed by investigators, the first victim was a street vendor operating outside the hotel, selling cigarettes, sweets, and gizzards. A man exiting the hotel walked past him but soon returned, alleging that his phone had been stolen. When the vendor denied any knowledge of the phone, the man accused him of being responsible. He then went back into the hotel, retrieved a firearm from his room, and returned to the entrance where the vendor stood. Without warning, he shot the vendor five times at close range. One of the victim’s brothers, who was nearby, witnessed the attack and shouted in shock. The shooter then turned on him and fired four rounds, fatally wounding him as well. CCTV footage from the Capitol Hill Hotel confirmed the sequence of events. The assailant was arrested shortly after the incident and taken into custody. However, reports indicate that he appeared in court and was released on bail on 23 May 2025, sparking public outrage and renewed calls for justice from the Nigerian community. The killings have heightened concerns about the safety of Nigerians and other foreign nationals in South Africa, particularly in light of ongoing xenophobic tensions and a perceived lack of consistent accountability for violent crimes against migrants. The victims’ families and Nigerian community leaders have demanded a transparent and expedited investigation, and for the South African justice system to ensure that the perpetrator is held fully accountable.
records.response: Police arrested the Perpetrator who is currently out on bail pending further investigations

records.name: Xenophobic Violence in (Valencia) Addo, Eastern Cape (24–29 May 2025)
records.description:
Between 24 and 29 May 2025, a wave of xenophobic violence erupted in Addo, a town in the Sundays River Valley Municipality, Sarah Baartman District, Eastern Cape. The violence was triggered by the death of a South African man on 24 May during an altercation at a local tavern, allegedly involving a foreign national. In retaliation, members of the community launched coordinated attacks targeting foreign nationals, primarily Zimbabwean and Malawian migrant workers. On 25 May the attacks escalated, resulting in the deaths of three foreign nationals, bringing the total to four. The Embassy of Zimbabwe later confirmed that at least 30 Zimbabweans were injured, with 17 requiring hospitalization.

As the violence spread, hundreds of foreign nationals fled their homes. Approximately 300 sought refuge at the Addo Police Station, while around 190 others, including 120 women, 40 children, and 30 men, sheltered at a church near Pier 14 in North End, Gqeberha. Properties belonging to migrants were looted and destroyed, leaving many without belongings. Four of the injured were initially denied treatment at Dora Nginza Hospital, and it was only after advocacy by the Southern African Refugee Organisations Forum (SAROF) and the South African Red Cross Society (SARCS) that they were admitted to Livingstone Hospital. On 27 May, the Red Cross deployed social workers, chaplains, and a disaster management officer to the AFM Church shelter in Gqeberha, where they provided medical and psychosocial support. Humanitarian partners such as Gift of the Givers also distributed food, clothing, and bedding.

Despite these interventions, the state’s response was criticised as inadequate and in some instances harmful. Although police were deployed, they failed to prevent or contain the violence. On 30 May, officials from the Department of Home Affairs carried out immigration operations at both the Addo Police Station and the North End church shelter, screening migrants for documentation. From those at Addo Police Station, 128 individuals were found to be undocumented and were transferred to Humewood Police Station in Gqeberha, where a case was opened against them. They appeared in court on 3 June, where a ruling was issued for their deportation. The remaining 172 foreign nationals who were documented were accepted back by the community and returned to their homes in the Valencia area of Addo without further reports of violence.

The Department of Social Development (DSD) worked with the local Ward Councillor, Mr Jonas, and the migrant leader, Mr Simba, to support reintegration. Both confirmed that the 172 had peacefully returned to their homes and had not faced further intimidation. DSD also engaged with Mr Simba to collect the addresses of those who had returned so that social workers could be dispatched. As a result of these interventions, children were able to return to school and families were reintegrated into the community.

Reconciliation efforts were strengthened by a Mega Memorial Service held in Addo on 22 June 2025, facilitated by community leaders, church representatives, the Sundays River Valley Municipality, and victims. The event was centred on the themes of peace, unity, and forgiveness and marked a significant step towards restoring calm and harmony in the community.
records.who_attacked: Migrant workers in Addo and their families
records.response: Migrant organisations, international organisations and the Department of Social Development intervened to assist the displaced victims and facilitate reintegration.

records.name: Alleged Police Misconduct and Use of Force Against Malawian Woman in Joe Slovo
records.description: On the 27th of May 2025, a video began circulating on social media depicting a disturbing incident involving the South African Police Service (SAPS) and a Malawian woman in the Joe Slovo area of the Western Cape. In the footage, several male police officers are seen forcibly detaining the woman and pushing her into a police van, despite her visible distress and repeated verbal pleas. According to what is seen and heard in the video, the woman repeatedly informs the officers that she possesses valid documentation to be in South Africa, but that her documents are at home. She further explains that she does not have access to a phone and is therefore unable to contact anyone to bring the documents to the scene. Despite her attempts to explain her situation, the officers refuse to engage with her and continue to physically force her into the vehicle. At least two female police officers are present at the scene but appear to take no action to intervene or de-escalate the situation. The video has sparked concern among  migrant rights groups over the apparent disregard for due process, the excessive use of force, and the lack of gender sensitivity displayed during the arrest. The incident also raises questions about the treatment of migrants during routine documentation checks, especially in the context of heightened xenophobic tensions. This incident adds to growing concerns about the conduct of law enforcement during operations involving migrants, particularly women, and underscores the urgent need for training on human rights, gender sensitivity, and non-violent policing methods.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: June 2025, a young Congolese asylum seeker woman and mother of a 2 days old baby was abandoned by nurses. But saved by a doctor who recognized her
records.description:
In June 2025, a young Congolese asylum seeker woman gave birth by caesarean because her BP was high; she was then 38 weeks pregnant. When the doctor saw how high her BP was, she advised her to go for an operation so that they could remove the baby, as the risk of losing one of them or even both was high. Two days later, her BP shot up even more, reaching over 200 or something. That night, she went to the hospital. The way the nurses at Addington Hospital and other people treated her was very frustrating; they literally abandoned her when
they realised that she was not from here. After a while, the Indian doctor who used to consult her at the antenatal clinic passed away; she stopped him and asked if he remembered her. She reminded the doctor that he used to consult her at the antenatal clinic. She told him that she gave birth to a baby girl by C-section two days ago. He told her that he remembered her. He took her where the emergency department, checked her BP and gave her appropriate medication on that day. She remains very indebted to that doctor who saved her life.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A congolese refugee has been denied access to healthcare for the past 6 months
records.description:
A Congolese refugee has been denied access to healthcare since June 2025. For the past 6 months, members of Operation Dudula have prevented him from entering Addington Hospital to seek the medical care he urgently needs. The refugee is living with a communicable disease that requires him to take five pills daily and attend medical check-ups every 3 months. Due to being blocked from the hospital, he has been unable to receive his medication or attend his scheduled check-ups.
As a result, the Congolese refugee has been forced to seek help at a local cathedral that provides limited primary healthcare services to individuals who are denied access to Addington Hospital. However, the cathedral is only able to supply two of the five pills he is required to take each day, leaving his treatment incomplete and his health at risk.
records.response: No interventions regarding this matter have been reported

records.name: Patients Segregated by Nationality Outside Public Health Facility
records.description:
In another recorded incident, a man is seen instructing patients at a public health facility that “if you are not South African, you can leave the premises.” He then proceeds to divide patients based on nationality, directing foreign nationals to one queue and South African citizens to another, stating explicitly that “only South Africans are allowed.”

He further instructs patients from Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Malawi, and other countries to go to Helen Joseph Hospital instead. Another individual, also involved in enforcing this segregation, tells a patient that as of the previous day, they made the decision to deny healthcare access to all non-South Africans.

When one dissatisfied patient questions the enforcement of this rule, asking when it was implemented, the man responds, “We put South Africans first.” When pressed on which political figure authorized the decision, he replies that he does not care about politicians, emphasizing that “this is about putting South Africa first.”

The video ends with the man telling the crowd that if anyone has a problem with the new arrangement, they should speak up immediately so that the matter can be “dealt with.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Patriotic Alliance Members Block Access to Reproductive and Child Health Services for Foreign Nationals
records.description:
Members of the Patriotic Alliance (PA) were seen stationed outside the Rahima Moosa Mother and Child Hospital, actively preventing foreign nationals from entering the facility. The group was reportedly checking identification documents and denying access to individuals without South African IDs or those identified as foreign nationals.

Video footage captures one member declaring, “Permit or no permit, we are not allowing foreign nationals to access healthcare.” Another PA member is seen addressing a group of people outside the clinic, claiming they are enforcing Section 17 of the Constitution. She instructs them to seek assistance from their own governments, stating, “Go get medical care in your own country.”

In a particularly inflammatory moment, she tells several men, “You cannot impregnate your women and expect them to get healthcare here. We don’t want you here.” She further asserts that healthcare services are reserved for South African citizens who pay taxes and advises foreign nationals to obtain medical permits and seek care at private hospitals. One patient was explicitly told to go to Mozambique for medical assistance and denied entry to the clinic.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: An Ethiopian women experiencing labour pains was denied medical attention
records.description: On the 5th of June 2025, an Ethiopian woman who was experiencing labour pains arrived at Hillbrow Clinic in the City of Johannesburg, around 11:00 AM. Upon her arrival, she was confronted by members of Operation Dudula. They demanded that she show them a South African ID and rejected her refugee documentation, subjecting her to verbal abuse and xenophobic slurs like “Makwerekwere.” The group made it clear that foreign nationals were unwelcome at the clinic. This resulted in her waiting outside until 14h00 before leaving for Forsberg Midwife Hospital, where she gave birth. Two days later, she returned to Hillbrow Clinic for a follow-up with her newborn but was again denied care by nurses who insisted on a South African ID. She expressed concern over the risks she faced in giving birth at a private hospital with limited resources.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: Xenophobic Threats Emerge During Service Delivery Protest in Nquthu, KZN
records.description: On Monday, 09 June 2025, what began as a service delivery protest in Nquthu, a rural town in KwaZulu-Natal near Dundee and Vryheid, reportedly escalated into threats against foreign nationals residing in the area. Community members voiced grievances not only about poor service delivery but also accused foreign nationals of taking jobs and business opportunities meant for locals. Audio recordings circulated via WhatsApp capture groups of disgruntled residents declaring that they “do not want foreign nationals” in the community. A source on the ground confirmed that, due to high unemployment rates, many locals have begun entering informal sectors traditionally dominated by migrants—such as tuck shops, barbershops, hair salons, and street trading. Feeling economically displaced, some community members called for the removal of all foreign nationals, regardless of their documentation status or how long they have lived in the area. While no violence or looting occurred, tensions were high. The local mayor reportedly intervened to defuse the situation. However, protestors warned they would return on Friday if their service delivery concerns were not addressed and if action was not taken to remove foreign nationals from the area.
records.response: Yes, the mayor intervened to calm the situation

records.name: Protection fee gang forces shops to close in Khayelitsha
records.description: Several spaza shops in Site C and New Khayelitsha, Cape Town, have been forced to shut down following escalating threats and extortion demands by local gangs. The incident, reported by Daily Sun on 12 June 2025, reflects ongoing violence and intimidation in the area, particularly targeting foreign national traders. According to a Somali businessman, the closures were triggered by traders’ inability to meet increasing demands from multiple gangs. He explained that one group had begun collecting protection fees in December, but in January, another gang led by a man known as Bhara—recently released from jail—also began demanding payments. Traders paid Bhara’s group R85,000, but last month a third group approached them for money. When the traders explained they were already paying two other gangs, the new group responded that they didn’t care and insisted on being paid, allegedly terrorising those who refused. The businessman claimed that four shopkeepers had been shot in the past two weeks, although he could not provide exact locations or dates. These developments have created a climate of fear among informal traders, leading to the closure of essential spaza shops and disrupting local residents’ access to basic goods. The situation further undermines the stability of the informal economy and poses a significant threat to migrant livelihoods. A police spokesperson confirmed that officers have been deployed in the affected areas to curb extortion and called on shop owners to report such incidents.
records.who_attacked: Foreign shop owners in New Section C and Khayelitsha
records.response: Police were deployed to monitor the area

records.name: Denial of Access to Public Healthcare
records.description: On 12 June, a refugee who has lived in South Africa for 20 years was denied access to Rahima Moosa Mother and Child Hospital while attempting to get urgent medical assistance for his 8-year-old autistic son, who had sustained an injury at school. Upon arrival, members of the Patriotic Alliance were reportedly stationed at the hospital entrance, refusing entry to non-South African nationals. Despite his legal entitlement to healthcare as a refugee, the father and son were blocked from accessing the facility. Police were present at the scene but allegedly did not intervene. After waiting for two hours, the victim was advised to seek help from a private doctor. He then attempted to get care at another hospital in Johannesburg but was turned away due to the absence of an existing patient file. The child only received limited assistance after 6 PM and was told to return to Rahima Moosa, where his son had still not been treated at the time of reporting. The victim was referred to Lawyers for Human Rights and Section 27 for further legal and advocacy support.
records.who_attacked: A refugee looking for assistance for his son
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: 3 girls from DRC assaulted by operation Dudula members in Rosettenville, johannesburg
records.description:
On 16 June 2025, at approximately 3:00 pm, a violent attack took place in Rosettenville targeting a Congolese migrant family with nine children. An estimated 600 men and women, identifying themselves as members of Operation Dudula, invaded a residential building comprising 12 units. The perpetrators arrived in large numbers, transported in taxis (“quantums”), singing and carrying weapons such as metal rods and sticks. Their stated objective was to intimidate, harm, and forcibly evict the migrant family.

The attackers forced their way into one of the units, breaking down the door. Inside, a 22-year-old woman, who had just come out of the shower and was wrapped in a towel, was confronted by four Operation Dudula members. She was physically assaulted and narrowly escaped sexual assault. The perpetrators sprayed pepper spray into her eyes to prevent her from identifying them.

At the same time, two of her younger sisters were also attacked. A 16-year-old girl was beaten severely on her chest and had her mobile phone stolen. Their 25-year-old sister was assaulted, fainted during the attack, and was left bleeding from her mouth. The sustained violence forced the children to flee the building around 6:00 pm.

The siblings managed to contact their mother, who had been away doing piece jobs. On her arrival, she immediately took the three victims to Johannesburg Hospital, but the hospital referred them to the police before sending them back with a Form G88 for medical examination. The victims were subsequently admitted to South Rand Hospital, where they remained for three days receiving treatment.

A case of assault was opened with the police. Two perpetrators were arrested but have since been released on bail. The family continues to live in fear and remains deeply traumatized by the incident.
records.response: Police were present but were also telling the victims to leave the country and go back to their country DRC

records.name: A Congolese national was sexually assaulted, physically assaulted and threatened at her place of residence
records.description:
On the 16th of June 2025 in 
Rosettenville Johannesburg, a Congolese national was threatened by members of Operation Dudula, who also assaulted her at her place of residence. This was after the assault; the victim, as well as her family, were told to move immediately and go back to their home country. Operation Dudula continued to tell the victim and her family that they would kill her and they would also burn her and her family in their home.  Members of Operation Dudula continued to pepper-spray the inside of the home and forcibly broke the doors and windows. At the time of the attack, the victim was in the bathroom. She became extremely frightened when she heard male voices shouting. In panic, she ran out of the bathroom, wrapped only in a towel. One of the men attempted to remove the towel from her. As she tried to protect herself, he assaulted her by striking her in the face and beating her with a sjambok. She eventually managed to escape from the house, but the group continued singing and chasing the family while shouting that they must leave the country. The yard was filled with members of the group. Following the incident, she and other affected family members went to the hospital with their mother, where they were charged R430 for medical treatment. They were there to seek help after being assaulted. A case was opened with the authorities following the assault. Only the women who were involved in the assault of the victim’s sister were arrested and subsequently released. The men who had directly assaulted the victim were neither located nor arrested. The family attended court proceedings; however, the case was ultimately dropped.
records.who_attacked: A congolese national and her family
records.response: No response from the police was reported

records.name: Forced Eviction of Refugee Informal Traders by Vigilante Group in Ladysmith, KwaZulu-Natal
records.description:
Between 17 and 20 June 2025, in Ladysmith, KwaZulu-Natal, a group calling themselves the “Concerned Citizens” launched a campaign of forced evictions targeting refugee and foreign-national informal traders. The operation began in Early Road, an area outside the town centre, where non-South African traders were removed from the streets, regardless of whether they had valid documentation or trading permits. The evictions were led by a group known locally as Abadayisi, composed mostly of women. By 20 June, the area had been cleared of all foreign traders, with Malawians and Congolese among the most affected.

On 23 June, the group extended their actions into the town centre, where they continued removing foreign traders. At present, the only non-nationals still operating are Nigerian traders married to South African women, trading under their partners’ names. The group justified their actions by claiming that South Africans should be prioritised for trading opportunities. However, their exclusionary actions were based solely on nationality and did not consider legal status or documentation, amounting to xenophobic discrimination.

Despite the scale and visibility of the evictions, neither the Ladysmith municipality nor the South African Police Service intervened. Foreign traders who attempted to report the incidents received no assistance.
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Foreign Nationals Denied Access to Health Care in Hillbrow Clinic
records.description: On 23rd June 2025, videos circulated on social media showing foreign nationals being denied access to healthcare services at a public facility in Hillbrow, Johannesburg. The footage captured individuals, allegedly affiliated with Operation Dudula, blocking non-South Africans from entering the clinic and demanding identification documents as a condition for receiving care.
records.who_attacked: Foreign Nationals were denied access to public health care
records.response: No interventions

records.name: Foreign Nationals Denied Access to Public Health Care in Diepsloot
records.description: On 24 June 2025, foreign nationals were denied entry into Diepsloot Extension 7 Clinic by members of Operation Dudula, who conducted ID checks at the entrance and barred non-South Africans without documentation from accessing healthcare services. The group prevented individuals from receiving essential treatment, including chronic medication and childhood immunizations. Police officers were reportedly present but failed to intervene meaningfully, and while the Gauteng Department of Health acknowledged the incident, it stated that only one formal complaint had been logged at Hillbrow Clinic. Operation Dudula claimed their actions were aimed at prioritizing South African citizens, although no legal authority had been granted to enforce such exclusion. Health officials and legal experts condemned the blockade as unconstitutional, and migrant rights organisations have since taken legal steps to challenge Operation Dudula’s actions. The incident has raised serious concerns about the growing pattern of health-related xenophobia and the failure of law enforcement to uphold constitutional rights.
records.who_attacked: Foreign nationals prevented from accessing health care
records.response: No interventions reported

records.name: Siblings with chronic sickle cells(anemia) denied medical attention at Johannesburg Hospital.
records.description: In July 2025, a mother from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), who has three children diagnosed with anemia, sought medical treatment for her children at Johannesburg Hospital. Upon arrival, she was informed by hospital staff that she needed to pay R2,000 before her children could be attended to. Because she was unable to afford this amount, she and her children were denied medical care and sent home. Later, the DRC mother was informed that she owed the hospital R22,000, despite not receiving the required treatment. She stated that each time she returned to the hospital without money, the receptionist refused to assist her, repeating that her children would not be treated without payment. When the mother tried to explain her circumstances, saying, “You know me, you know my story,” the receptionist reportedly replied that it was not her problem if the children were chronically ill. Another nurse allegedly made a xenophobic remark, saying, “You people need to go back to your country.” Because she was turned away, one of her children’s health deteriorated severely, eventually leading to a stroke. The child has since been declared unfit for a regular school environment due to long-term medical complications. The DRC mother also reported that even when she previously received care at Johannesburg Hospital, the treatment was often incomplete or inadequate. For example, if a doctor prescribed 30 capsules of Amoxicillin, she would only be given 10 and told to buy the rest at a pharmacy. In other cases, the hospital informed her that certain more expensive medications were unavailable and would need to be purchased privately. Unable to afford the required medical care and prescriptions, the mother resorted to home remedies, giving her children beetroot, Panado, and water in an effort to help them recover. Unfortunately, these measures were insufficient. She eventually had to borrow money to support her children’s medical needs but remains afraid to return to the hospital due to her ongoing financial difficulties and the discriminatory treatment she experienced.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Congolese asylum seeker, father of an autistic boy, is denied to get medication for his 8 years old son.
records.description: A Democratic Republic of Congo national, living in Durban, he has been prevented from getting medication for his 8-year-old autistic son; medication that he desperately needs to manage his sleep problems, aggression and other behaviours associated with his autistic condition. His son is now dependent on the leftover from the last appointment and is trying to consider reducing the dose so that it can last a bit longer. His first denial was on 2nd July, when he took a taxi with his autistic son from home to Addington hospital, for a routine doctor’s visit, only to be greeted by march and march members who demanded to see his documentation. He took his asylum seeker permit out and showed it to them, only to be told that foreigners are not allowed in, whether documented or not. He tried to reason with them to look at his child’s condition and show some empathy, but they didn’t care. They told him to go back to his home country, not understanding that, as an asylum seeker, he is not allowed to go back to his country of origin. When he insisted, they aggressively pushed him and threatened to beat him up. He left the hospital but went back the following day and the third day, but it was worse. Since then, he has been going there every day to this day.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A heavily pregnant Ethiopian women was left unattended at Addington hospital
records.description: On the 3rd of July 2025, at Addington Hospital in the eThekwini district, a heavily pregnant Ethiopian asylum seeker was left unattended.  This was after the lady was transferred from Gateway Clinic to Addington Hospital.  Upon her arrival at Addington Hospital, she was stopped by the March and March people, who denied her access to the hospital. She sought assistance, but that resulted in increased tension between refugees and the March and March people. This resulted in the police being called as the heavily pregnant Ethiopian asylum seeker needed assistance getting into the hospital. The heavily pregnant Ethiopian woman remained unattended the whole day. Shifts changed, but the lady remained unattended as the people from the new shift did not know who she was and thus resulting in her not getting the assistance she required.  After waiting the whole day, the pregnant Ethiopian lady was not only tired but in pain and had no other option but to leave the hospital and go back home.
records.who_attacked: A heavily pregnant Ethiopian Asylum seeker
records.response: The police were called and intervened and helped her get through the hospital

records.name: A refugee mother from the DRC was denied access to health care at Rosettenville Clinic
records.description: A 57-year-old refugee mother from the Democratic Republic of Congo has been attempting to access healthcare for her five-year-old child in South Africa since the 3rd of  July 2025. The child suffers from a severe respiratory infection requiring surgery. Despite holding valid asylum documentation, the mother was repeatedly denied entry to Rosettenville Clinic. On 12 September 2025, she arrived at the clinic at 08h00 but was blocked by vigilantes and left at 13:00 without receiving medical assistance, even as her child’s condition worsened.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: An Asylum seeker from DRC was denied access to health care services at Rosettenville clinic
records.description: On the 3rd of July 2025, an asylum seeker from the DRC was trying to get medical attention for her 5-year-old child, but she was denied access to health care services at Rosettenville clinic. The asylum seeker's child had a respiratory infection, which made it difficult for the child to breathe easily; the child required surgery. The mother tried to gain access to healthcare services on the 12th of September 2025, but vigilantes were denied access once again, even though she had her asylum documentation with her.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Permanent resident mother of an autistic teenager denied to collect his medication at Addington hospital
records.description:
The 3rd of July 2025 was an appointment day for this Congolese permanent mother of an
autistic South African teenager at Addington Hospital. She went to collect medication for her son and was denied entry by a group of 4 people claiming to be from March and March. She arrived
there around 8h00, not anticipating anything, and she went straight through, only to be
violently intercepted by march and march people. She showed them her ID and the birth
certificate of her son and argued that she is a permanent resident and that her son was
born here and is a citizen of this country. In response, they told her that only native South
Africans, born here, can be allowed to go through. While she was waiting to figure out
what she could do next, a group of migrants, predominantly Ethiopian refugees, came to
support their 9-months-pregnant sister who was denied access, whereas she was due.
Altercations followed between them and March and March people, which led to police
intervention. She used police presence to ask for intervention from Metro Police, only to
be asked by one of them where she bought her ID from. This said to her that even the
police are in agreement with what March and March are doing at hospitals and clinics.
records.response: Police were present, but instead insinuated that the accused bought her ID

records.name: A Burundian refugee is teargassed by public order police and thereafter arrested by SAPS after being denied access at Addington hospital
records.description:
A leader in the Burundian community was due for eye medication collection on 3rd July in 2025. He normally collects at the pharmacy of Addington Hospital. So, when he got there, he found many refugees and migrants facing hospital officials and members of March and March, who were blocking people from access, and then, he joined the negotiation team which called the police, expecting that they will intervene and to do their job of enforcing the laws of the country and solve the problem, so that the people can be able to proceed with whatever they are doing. But as soon as they arrived, migrants were asked to evacuate, to stay away from the hospital entrance. Then they went across the hospital from where they were asked to move away as well. Before they knew it, a quantum full of police officers was called and started shooting them with rubber bullets and teargas. And then after that, he got arrested alongside five other refugee patients. They were accused of being involved in public violence in front of a
public entity, and then. They were subsequently taken to a nearby Home Affairs office to verify their documents, which were found to be in order. Thereafter, they were taken to The Point Police station were to be charged with public violence, but the commander in charge refused to press charges because he had no evidence that they were involved in public violence. They spent unnecessarily eight hours in detention while March and March are left to continue violating the constitution and the laws of this country. It should be noted that March and March continued to demand IDs from patients, in violation of the Constitution and the laws of this country, even while the police were there, but no action was taken against them.
records.response: A quantum full of police officers were called and started shooting them with rubber bullets and teargas.

records.name: A Somali refugee woman was denied access into Addington hospital after attempting to enter on several occasions and once at Beatrice Street clinic.
records.description: In July of 2025 a Somali refugee attempted to seek assistance at Addington hospital, in the eThekwini district. The Somali refugee was stopped by March and March people who insisted on denying her access into the hospital as she is not South African. The March and March people continued to inform her that she cannot have access into the hospital as she does not have a green ID card. The Somali Refugee continued to try get access into the hospital as she required to collect chronic medication from the hospital for herself, her husband and their child. The Somali refugee's attempts to enter the hospital were met with aggression, but on the 26th of August her interaction with the March-on-March people was just verbal. The Somali Refugee also attempted to see medical assistance at the Beatrice hospital but was also denied access into the hospital. The Somali Refugee and her family have been denied medication and medical attention for 2 months.
records.response: There was no response to this incident

records.name: An undocumented Zimbabwean national has been trying to access immunisation services for her 20-month-old child
records.description: An undocumented Zimbabwean national has been trying to access immunisation services for her 20-month-old child since 7 July 2025. Despite multiple attempts, she has been repeatedly denied entry to the Rosettenville Clinic by vigilantes. On 12 September 2025, she arrived at the clinic gate at 08:00 but was again blocked by the same individuals. She waited until 13h00 but ultimately had to leave without receiving the necessary healthcare for her child.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A 37-year-old undocumented Zimbabwean national was denied access to health care
records.description: A 37-year-old undocumented Zimbabwean national has been trying to get her 20-month-old child immunised since the 7th of July 2025. On the 12th of September, the Zimbabwean national was denied access to the Yeoville clinic by vigilantes and had to leave without obtaining the immunisation her child needed.
records.response: No response regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Somali lady was denied medical care at a Rahima Moosa clinic due to the presence of Operation Dudula members
records.description:
On 5 July 2025, a Somali lady was denied medical care at a Rahima Moosa clinic due to the presence of Operation Dudula members. When she arrived just by the gate with other migrants, they were chased by more than 100 Operation Dudula members.  Operation Dudula blocked access to the clinic, preventing the victim from seeking treatment for her sick child who was vomiting and had a high fever. 
Operation Dudula members cited reasons such as being "tired of foreigners," claiming the hospital is "for South Africans only," and accusing foreigners of taking their jobs and businesses. They added that they are tired of Somalians. The Somali woman seeking help tried going back again on the eve of the 16th  of July. The Somali mother was taking her child to the hospital, who had a sinus infection and had difficulty breathing due to sinus growth.  She found Operation Dudula members at the hospital again, but their leader wasn’t there. The Somali national was told to go to a private hospital. She was pushed with the child. She said that the Operation Dudula members made her feel unsafe and traumatised. She couldn’t even access the inside as she was blocked from the gate of the hospital.
 Her child's condition was not improving as quickly as it should have due to a lack of proper medication. The child was also scared by the experience. While the Somali national had experienced verbal abuse from nurses in the past, this was the first time she was completely denied access to healthcare. The Somali national is now scared to seek medical care, fearing she will be denied again. No one intervened to help the Somali national, including hospital staff, police, or the press who were present. The Somali national ended up buying medicine from a pharmacy after borrowing money from a neighbour.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded. It is worth noting that hospital staff, police, or the press were present.

records.name: An epileptic Congolese youngster is denied access to critical medication by March and March at Addington Hospital
records.description: The 7th July 2025, was the appointment date of a Congolese national who needed to collect the medication for his epilepsy that he contracted in 2019.  As usual, at 7 o’clock, he was already there. Unfortunately, when he was about to enter, about 4 men and women, wearing plain clothes, stopped him at the outer gate. He asked the reasons why they were stopping him as he regularly goes there to collect his medication, then they told him, “You have to give us your green ID”. He asked them in English what for, and they responded angrily in isiZulu and told him that things have changed now; if you are not a South African citizen born in South Africa, you will not have access to anything from this hospital or any other public hospital, for that matter. They told him to go to a private hospital or go back to his home country to seek treatment there. What surprised him more was the inaction of the hospital security guards and of police officers who were patrolling the beachfront. They watched what was happening but could not intervene. Then they started insulting him, calling him names and ordered him to leave immediately before they hurt him; and he left because he could see that, indeed, they were prepared to hurt him. Since that date, he has unsuccessfully tried to go there countless times. Now, he can’t leave home alone, because the side effects of not taking medication are serious; he is more forgetful, and he is highly likely to get fits.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: Burundian refugee, mother of four and regular patient at Addington hospital, was shocked to be denied access
records.description:
On 10th July, 4 guys and one white woman wearing March and March t-shirts and caps denied a Burundian refugee woman access to Addington Hospital. When she arrived at the first gate, she saw them standing. They stopped her and asked her to produce her green ID before letting her in. This was the first time that anyone had asked her for an ID before that; the security guards used to ask for appointment cards only. When she showed them her refugee ID, they said it was fake, and they only wanted a green ID. I told them that I had an appointment and desperately needed to be seen by a doctor, but they would not listen. Finally, they started pushing and insulting her, telling her that public
hospitals were only for South Africans. She persistently explained to them how serious her condition was, but they said no, it is only for citizens, not refugees. She told them that she had been receiving treatment from that hospital for the last 5 years, but instead, they became aggressive and told her to go back to her home country. That is when she became emotional and cried because they were very offensive in the way they were talking and acting, not even worrying about those who were very sick. She went to the Point Police station to report, but was told there was nothing they could do. Since she was on a resettlement programme and was in contact with IOM, she called them to report, but they also said there was nothing they could do because the American process was suspended. She called UNHCR, and they said she should go to the LHR offices, but when she went there, they also told her that there was nothing they could do other than the court process that they are preparing. She received the same response from her social worker at RSS, and that made her even more sick and frustrated. After that, she went again to try 4 times, the last one being on 1st August, and she gave up.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Burundian refugee woman uses ambulance to gain access to Addington hospital after being denied access by march and march
records.description:
A Burundian refugee woman was involved in an accident on 13 July, around 09h00. I was
Then taken to King George Hospital, where she was scanned, and the doctor decided to transfer her to Addington Hospital for an operation, because she had a fracture around her knee. She went to Addington Hospital the following day in morning. Upon arrival, she met dudula people at the gate, who asked her to produce her ID. She had a refugee ID, so she gave it to them, but they refused and said they wanted a South African ID. She said to them that even hers was issued by the South African government, but they were not interested and told her to go back home. So, she went back to King George's hospital and
requested to be transported by ambulance, which they did. When she arrived at Addington Hospital, the doctor told her that she would undergo a knee operation, which took place 4 days later. Before and after the operation, she noticed, for the first time, even doctors were asking for her ID before they could attend to her, and they were only asking the ID to her ID, not for all other patients who were in that ward, as she was the only refugee in that ward. She said that she has 4 children, all born at that hospital, and this
has never happened to her before. After that operation, she was given a check-up appointment for 29 July to go back to Addington Hospital. When she went there on that day, they (dudulas) stopped her, then she decided to go to the Denis Hurley Centre clinic, where she was given a referral letter to
King Edward, where she was almost sent, told me back on the ground that they don’t accept referrals from clinics, only hospitals, until the orthopaedic doctor intervened. He attended to her and sent her to physiotherapy, and from there, she was sent back to her nearest hospital, which is King George's.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded.

records.name: A 12-year old Congolese asylum seeker is denied to see his doctor at Addington hospital for check-up, after a heart operation
records.description: On 17th July, 2025, a 12-year-old boy and her mother went to Addington hospital for a checkup after he had undergone heart surgery at Albert Luthuli hospital, a while ago. When they arrived at the gate, they were asked by march and march whether they were citizen or migrants. They said they were refugees from the DRC. When they heard that, they became agitated and said, “If you are not a citizen, you will not go through here. However, citizen who did not have their IDs were asked for their surnames and clans’ names, and were subsequently allowed to go through. The 12-year-old’s mother then tried to plead with them, showing them that the boy had operated of heart condition and needed to see the doctor, but they replied that they don’t care, if he dies, so be it; they are at work and have to do what they are paid to do. Since then, they have gone there several times, with no success.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were recored

records.name: A Congolese woman was stopped from getting her gallbladder operation
records.description: On the 21st of July 2025, A Congolese woman was scheduled for a gallbladder operation at Addington Hospital in the eThekwini district.  She was blocked from entering the hospital by a group of March and March people. After explaining the incident to the hospital, she was given a new appointment for the 18th of September, but missed it out of fear of encountering the same group. She was then asked to report to Ward 2B before 7:30 AM on the 9th of October and assured there would be no issue. Upon her arrival, she was again stopped by March and March people, who did not care about her appointment and hospital call, claiming they were fighting against such practices. They became hostile, insulted her, and called her names, leaving her distressed and unable to access the medical care she needed. The March-on-March people told her. They told her to ask to call Ramaphosa to come and get her into the hospital, or tell the hospital to send her file by e-mail so that she can go to a private hospital.
records.response: No response was reported regarding this incident

records.name: A pregnant Zimbabwean asylum seeker was denied medical attention at Tswelopele Clinic in Vosloorus Johanessburg
records.description: On the morning of the 22nd of July 2025, a 28-year-old pregnant asylum seeker from Zimbabwe arrived at Tswelopele Clinic in Vosloorus for a scheduled prenatal check-up at 07:45 AM. Despite showing visible signs of distress, including swelling, nausea, and difficulty walking, she was told by a security guard to wait outside while several local patients were allowed in before her. After nearly an hour in the cold, she approached reception, and this is when staff reportedly made xenophobic remarks, saying foreigners should pay or return to their countries. Her cramps got worse, but the Zimbabwean Asylum seeker was dismissed by the staff; she was told the clinic could not prioritise people who were not South African. No medical assessment was done, and she left without receiving care, which resulted in her feeling humiliated and fearful for her unborn child. She later stated that such discrimination against foreign nationals, especially pregnant women, was common at the clinic.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were reported

records.name: A diabetic Congolese older person is denied access to Beatrice Street Clinic, to collect his medication
records.description: On 22 July 2025, an old refugee from DRC was denied access to Beatrice Street clinic, where he went on an appointment to collect his Diabetes and blood pressure medication. When he arrived at the gate, he was stopped by 2 women wearing t-shirts on which you could read “march and march”. They asked him to produce his ID, and he gave them his refugee status, but they refused to take it. They want only citizens who have a green ID. If you are a citizen but you don’t have an ID, they would ask you to explain your ID numbers, and then they would allow you to get through. That is what he explained. They told him that they don't want foreigners in their public health facilities; only South Africans should be treated at public healthcare facilities. He did not say anything; he immediately went back because he didn't want anything bad to happen to him as an old and weak person.
records.response: No response regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Burundian refugee on chronic medication is denied access at Lancers’ Road Clinic
records.description:
A Burundian refugee woman collects her chronic medication from Lancers’ Road clinic for
the past year and a half or two. However, on 22 nd July, she went to collect her medication
from that clinic, but she felt that her sugar levels were quite high. When she arrived, she
was stopped by three people; two ladies and one gentleman, who were wearing March
and March t-shirts. They told her that, unless she produces her green South African ID,
unless she is a South Africa citizen, she cannot be assisted. So, she insisted, saying that
she has been getting medication from there for a long time and she is not feeling well,
she needs to be helped, but they refused. They said, no, you are not a citizen, you cannot
come here and use our medication. All this happened in front of the security guards of
the clinic who are always at the gate, to let people in. After that, she called her husband
because he is the one who dropped her at that clinic. A few minutes later, he arrived and
found her crying and very depressed, very sad because she was very scared that, with
high blood sugar levels anything could happen to her if she does not get her medication.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was recorded

records.name: A diabetic Congolese asylum seeker is denied access to Addington hospital for checkup, after spending 10 days of admission at the same hospital
records.description:
On 24 July 2025, a diabetic Congolese refugee was denied access to Addington Hospital by
people wearing march and march regalia.
