They have been trying throughout July and even later to gain access, but have been unsuccessful, and every time they were told that they don’t have the right to use their public health facilities, that they are a threat to South Africans’ rights and privileges and must go back home and fight for their countries. However, on this day, they had the support of an academic and activist who went there to protest against what March and March are doing, which is to blatantly violate Section 27 of the Constitution of South Africa. On that day, they went earlier before these march and march people arrived, and managed to go through. But as soon as march and march people arrived, they were alerted by an old lady who sells food outside the hospital that there are foreigners who
are already inside, and they went in, asked everyone who was in the waiting area to produce their IDs, and forced them out, in collaboration with security guards, while calling them names like amakwerekwere, ama zai-zai. In fact, while march and march were forcing them out, nurses and admin staff were mumbling that “lawa amazai-zai angene kanjani la ngaphakati?”, which means, these amazai-zai, how did they get in here?
It is alleged that even the admin clerk refused to register them because they had already
called the march and the march people. Then, when they arrived, they violently pulled and
pushed them like animals, holding them by their clothes and dragging them outside. After
that, the academic, who was already outside, took them to King Edward's hospital. He
spoke to hospital staff, and they agreed to attend to them, but as soon as he left, the
hospital staff took them out, saying they couldn’t help them.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A 2 months old baby is denied vaccination by March and March
records.description:
On 24 July 2025, a Congolese asylum seeker took her 2-month-old to the vaccination at the Gateway clinic. Around 6 o’clock, she was already in the queue. March and March people went through the queue, asking everyone to produce his or her ID. When they reached her, she showed them her asylum papers. They saw that she was not a South African and told her to stay outside because foreigners are not allowed to access healthcare there, as public hospitals are only for citizens. They came to the queue and said, Whoever is not South African must get out of the queue. She subsequently became emotional and started crying, and even her BP went up. In addition to immunisation, the baby was also
suffering from a rash as if hot water had been poured on him. When they saw her crying, they
started insulting, calling her names and telling her to go back to her country.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Congolese woman  died after being denied access to health care at Addington hospital
records.description: On the 25th of July 2025, a Congolese month of a 19 Month old, Ubered to Addington hospital. This was after she complained about a headache and migraine. She took painkillers, but had no luck; this led to her being in a critical condition, which resulted in her going to the hospital. Upon her arrival at Addington Hospital, March and March people denied her access to the hospital. Her husband tried to intervene and tried to get her into the hospital, but they were denied access to the hospital and forced to leave. The  Congolese woman was forced to go back home. The next day, the Congolese lady was admitted to King Edward Hospital. She spent 3 days in King Edward Hospital without being attended to and was discharged. Upon enquiring about his wife's health conditions, the Congolese woman's husband was told that the tests that they ran on his wife all came back negative, which justified the hospital's discharge of her, even though the husband did not think that they were being truthful. 3 days after being discharged from the hospital, the Congolese lady passed away at home.
records.response: No people responded to the incident

records.name: A Zimbabwean Refugee was denied access to health care at Tembisa Health Clinic
records.description: On the 25th of July 2025, a 34-year-old Zimbabwean refugee, seeking urgent medical care at Tembisa Health Clinic in Extension 9, was denied treatment. The Zimbabwean Refugee had a high fever, persistent cough, and severe body aches. Despite arriving shortly after 08:00 AM and presenting his refugee documentation, he was denied treatment by the receptionist at the Tembisa health clinic. The staff told the refugee that the clinic only served South African citizens. The Zimbabwean Refugee cited his legal right to healthcare, but was told to go to his country for help. Witnesses confirmed staff made xenophobic remarks, including accusations that foreigners were draining resources. The Zimbabwean Refugee was not given medical attention and was forced to leave. The Zimbabwean refugee emphasised that this incident reflects a broader pattern of discrimination against foreign nationals in public health facilities.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were reported

records.name: A Congolese refugee on chronic medication is denied access at Gateway clinic
records.description:
A Congolese refugee went to the Gateway clinic on his appointment, which was on 28th July. It was the first time since he was diagnosed with high BP at Addington Hospital, and from there, he was given another appointment and was advised to go to his local clinic. When he arrived at the gate, he found two women who were wearing march and march regalia and who asked him what he was going there for. He replied that he was there for his appointment. Then, they asked whether he had an ID. He said, No because he is not a South African; he is an asylum seeker. Then they said to him, No, you can’t go inside,
You must go back; public healthcare is only for South African citizens.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A child died after been denied access to Alexandra Clinic and Charlotte Maxeke Hospital
records.description: On the 31st of July 2025, a Malawian national urgently sought medical help for her one-year-old child suffering from severe vomiting and diarrhea at the Masakhane Health Clinic in Alexandra. The Malawian national was blocked at the gate of the hospital by two individuals identified as Operation Dudula members. The Operation Dudula members refused to grant her access to the hospital because she failed to show them a South African ID. Clinic security did not intervene. The Malawian national then walked to 8th Avenue Clinic. Upon her arrival, a security guard there reportedly followed staff instructions and physically stopped her from entering. The Malawian national proceeded to show the security her child’s clinic card and pleaded for help, but she was ignored.  The Malawian national then went to Johannesburg Clinic, where she was left waiting for hours without assistance. With no other options, the Malawian national paid for private care on 1 August, but her child’s condition had worsened beyond recovery, and her child proceeded to pass away that evening.
records.who_attacked: A Malawian mother's child was denied access to health care
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded. The security at Masakhane Health Clinic in Alexandra security did not intervene. At 8th Avenue Clinic a security guard there reportedly following staff instructions physically stopped her from entering

records.name: Mozambican National was denied access to health care after suffering a serious arm injury
records.description: On 1st of August 2025, a 34-year-old Mozambican construction worker who suffered a serious arm injury while on site in Germiston urgently sought help at Geba Clinic in the Ekurhuleni municipality.  The Mozambican national was visibly wounded and in pain, but was denied medical attention after presenting his Mozambican passport and a valid work permit. The staff at Geba Clinic insisted they only assist South African citizens with proper Identification Documents. Security did not remove him but ignored his repeated requests for help, leaving him waiting over an hour without care. With no medical attention provided, he was forced to leave the hospital. A local church group later stepped in to offer basic care and comfort. The Mozambican national described the ordeal as deeply humiliating and dehumanising. The Mozambican national furthermore highlighted a pattern of xenophobic exclusion faced by foreign nationals at the Geba clinic.
records.response: No responses regarding the incident were reported. The security at the clinic were present, but ignored the Mozambican nationals' pleas for help

records.name: Two 54-year-old Malawian passport holders were denied access to medical attention at Rosettenville Clinic.
records.description: Two 54-year-old Malawian passport holders were denied access to medical attention at Rosettenville Clinic. The 2 Malawian nationals have been trying to get their chronic medication since August 2025. The 2 attempted to seek medical help on the 12th of September, but were stopped by vigilantes.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were recorded

records.name: A Somali refugee, mother of two, is deceived by a march and march person who pretend to be a security guard.
records.description:
A Somali refugee went to Addington hospital on her appointment. She was transferred to
that hospital from Eastern Cape. She initially went there on 23rd June and opened her file
for her and her 2 children. But, since July, she is not getting the needed assistance. She
has gone there several times for her and/or for one of her children and every time they
refuse her entry, saying that she does not a South African ID and she was not born in
South Africa. They kept on telling her to go to private hospitals, which she I can’t afford.
She went there on 4th and 11 July and then again on 1st August, and each time she was
stopped by people wearing clothes where it is written march and march. Before that, she
went there on the 19th with her unwell son. She was very early; at three o'clock,
early in the morning. She found one of them sitting there, wearing security clothes. She
spoke to her about my problem and how these march and march people were not
allowing her in. She asked for her help, which she offered to do, but only from 5h00. Only
to find later that she was not a security guard but a march and march person. She was
wearing a security jacket, but inside, she was wearing the March and March T-shirt. Then,
after five o'clock, I was standing there waiting to go in, she approached and saw that the lady
was asking everyone for their IDs. Then, when she asked, that lady replied, “Why are you asking
me a question. She said, You told me you would open for me at 5h00, what is happening
now? Then she took off her jacket and showed her the march and march t-shirt, and told
her, if you don't want to fight, you have a small kid, please go home and find your way to
get a private doctor, this hospital is only for South Africans.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: March and March is preventing a Somali refugee, mother of two, to get her children vaccinated
records.description:
A Somali National in need of help at Beatrice Street clinic, was denied access to health care. 
She saw a board where it is written “if you don't have an ID, you are not allowed”. So, she found them there as well. She said to them “I want to go in, they said, no, no, no, did others like you tell you that you are not allowed to go in?”. They said to her, foreigners are not allowed here, only South Africans. She was there for her baby’s 6 months immunisation, which she could not get. Early September, she went back to Beatrice Street to try and get her 6 years old boy vaccinated. This is also because at school, they are saying all six years old children must got for vaccination. When she arrived there, she was greeted by yet another march and march guy who said to her “I've told you that day not come here anymore, here is not for foreigners, if you want injection, you can go buy or go and get it at a private clinic or hospital”. While this is happening, at school, they keep on sending her letters asking her to take her for immunisation. Now, she does not know where to take him for that immunisation as she can’t afford private healthcare.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded.

records.name: March and March denies vaccination of a 6 months old Congolese baby at Lancers’ Road Clinic
records.description: On 1st August 2025, a Congolese mother of a 6-month-old boy took him to Lancers’ road clinic for his scheduled immunisation. When she arrived there, she was asked by the 3 people who were in front of the gate, who were wearing March and March, to give them her ID. She said to them that she does not have an ID and that she only has an Asylum seeker permit. They said to her that, in that case, she would not be allowed to go inside because only those with an ID can go inside the clinic. They said, “This clinic and other public healthcare facilities are not for foreigners; they are for South Africans only”. She tried to plead with them that she is only coming for her baby’s immunisation injection, but they said no, she must go to a private clinic, and if she wants, they can show her a private hospital where she can go. She told them that she can’t afford private healthcare because she is not working and her husband is not working, but they were not interested, and she went back home.
records.response: No response regarding this matter were recorded

records.name: A Malawian woman was denied health care at Klipspruit Clinic in Soweto even after she fainted.
records.description: On the 5th of August 2025, a 34-year-old Malawian woman and long-term resident of Johannesburg sought urgent medical attention at Klipspruit Clinic in Soweto. The Malawian woman was suffering from severe flu-like symptoms, chest pain, and shortness of breath. Despite her critical condition, the clinic staff refused to assist her after she presented a valid Malawian passport. The staff at Klipspruit clinic insisted that only South African citizens or those with medical aid could be treated at the clinic. The Malawian woman expressed that she lacked funds for private care, but the staff at the clinic ignored her. While waiting outside for medical assistance, she collapsed near the entrance of the clinic.  Her fainting resulted in the clinic security briefly checking on her, but the security failed to seek medical assistance. A community member eventually escorted her home, and no emergency support or follow-up was provided.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was reported. Clinic security was present at the scene ,but refused to assist the Malawian woman

records.name: A Congolese woman who is on regular chronic medication is denied access for the third time.
records.description:
On 5 August 2025, a Congolese woman who is on regular chronic medication attempted
again to go to Addington Hospital. This was the third time, after being denied access on the 3rd
and on 8th July. Like the previous times, she met people who she believes were from
Operation Dudula at the gate, before reaching where security guards are, who asked her
to produce her ID. They were doing that to anyone who was going there before letting
you in. When she showed them her refugee ID, they asked for the green one and said
they only want people who have South African citizenship and who have a green South
African ID. But after her, someone who had a green ID was also denied entry, because he
was not born outside South Africa.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: The Commander of Nquthu Police station refuse to assist refugees in need pf protection
records.description: In the afternoon of the 08/07/2025, refugees and migrants were invited at the Nquthu police station to discuss the antimigrant violence in Nquthu. They met there with the March and March group which is forcibly evicting them. They were called there to discuss a way forward with perpetrators, who ordered them to close their businesses for 2 days for peace. Unfortunately, when they reopened after those 2 days, they were again attacked and ordered to close. That is when they run to the police station for assistance and asked to speak to the station commander. As a result, the station commander told them that he can't do nothing for them, they must go to the municipality because they are the ones who allowed them to operate in Nquthu in the first place. He said to them, for them to trade in this county, they should obtain a special permit from home affairs. He blamed the municipality for allowing them to trade in Nquthu in the first place. This shocked the traders because they know that as refugees and asylum seekers, they are allowed to work (including self-employment) and study. The following day they run to the municipality, where they were told to just leave the area because what is happening is a popular uprising against foreign nationals.
records.who_attacked: Refugees and other immigrants trading in Nquthu
records.response: Not that we are aware of

records.name: A KZN provincial children’s hospital hides a Congolese asylum seeker woman in her car, to get her treated at Addington hospital
records.description:
On the 7th of August, A Congolese asylum seeker, mother of 3, went to Addington hospital as she was feeling very sick, as she was passing blood. She had dysentery. She was blocked by so-called operation dudula (march and march), who asked her to produce her ID. When she said she did not have it, as she is an asylum seeker, they told her to go to a private hospital or go back to her home country. They were asking everyone, not only her to take out their IDs, and everyone was doing so. But when she showed them her Asylum Seeker documents, they said she was illegal in South Africa. So, she tried to wait a bit with other refugees and asylum seekers, to see if they could change their minds, but instead they became more offensive and started chasing them. They said “hamba Makwerekwere”, you must go to private hospitals. Since she goes regularly to the KZN provincial children's hospital for her autistic child, she decided to go there to ask for help, considering her condition. One of the doctors there hid her in her car and took her to Addington Hospital through the staff parking lot. That doctor made sure the patient’s file was in her hands, and then they put a drip on her before leaving. She was discharged the following day, and they gave her medication to continue taking at home. That doctor from the children’s hospital saved
her life.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: March and March denies vaccination of a 6 months old Congolese baby at Overport Clinic
records.description: After being denied the opportunity to get her 6-month-old baby vaccinated at Lancers’ Road clinic, this Congolese mother of a 6-month-old boy took him to Overport clinic on 8th August 2025. This is a different clinic situated around 5km from the Lancers’ Road clinic, where she first went on 1st August. When she arrived there, she was intercepted by 2 ladies wearing March and March t-shirts who asked to see her South African ID. She told them that she does not have an ID and that she only has an Asylum seeker permit. They said to her that the clinic is only for South African citizens and repeated the same things that those she met at Lancers’ road clinic the previous week told her: that “this clinic and other public healthcare facilities are not for foreigners; they are for South Africans only”. She tried to plead with them as well that she is not going there for her treatment but for the baby’s immunisation, but they were not interested. They told her to either go to a private hospital or go back to her home country. However, a month later, she was called by a friend of hers, who told her that she should go back to Overport clinic because they are no longer there. She rushed there, and indeed they were seen, and her baby was vaccinated.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Congolese Asylum seeker fought March and March people as they would not grant her access into Addington  hospital
records.description: On the 12th of August 2025, at around 05h00, a Congolese asylum seeker was refused access to Addington hospital in the eThekwini municipality. The Congolese asylum seeker went to Addington Hospital seeking help for her dying baby. Upon her arrival, the Congolese asylum seeker was stopped by 2 March and March ladies who denied her access to the hospital. The asylum seeker then informed the March and March ladies that her baby was dying. The March and March people then replied by informing the Congolese mother that they were okay with her dying and that the death of the Congolese asylum seeker's child was no problem. Furthermore, the March and March people encouraged her to go to a private hospital or to go back to Congo. This angered the mother, which then prompted her to fight the March and March ladies. This ordeal led to the police being called, and upon the arrival of the police, the police encouraged the Congolese asylum seeker to take her dying child to another hospital, as the March and March people who denied her access into the hospital were doing their work by denying her access into the hospital. The Congolese asylum seeker then went to Prince Mshiyeni Hospital where her dying baby was attended to on the same day.
records.response: Police were called

records.name: A desperate Congolese asylum seeker fights with March and March to see if her very sick child can be attended to.
records.description:
On Monday 12 August 2025 around 05h00 a.m., a Congolese woman took her child to Addington Hospital. The baby was very sick and could not breath properly. On arrival, she was stopped by 2 March and March ladies. She begged them to let her through as her baby was dying, but instead one of them replied that he can die no problem, she does not care because this hospital is for South Africans only. She told her to either go to private hospital or take her baby back to Congo. This angered the Congolese mother who reacted with anger and fought with both ladies. The police was then called and in few minutes a van arrived and told the Congolese mother to take her baby to another hospital because
her baby is very sick, she may end up losing her. The police also added that these March and March people are doing their work, let them do their work. She then took her baby to another hospital in Umlazi called Prince Mshiyeni Hospital. There, she was well received and assisted by everyone and the same day the baby was admitted.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was recorded

records.name: A nurse at Clare Estate clinic, joined march and march protestors in denying a heavily  pregnant woman access to primary health care
records.description: On the 15th of August 2025, at Clare Estate Clinic in the eThekwini municipality, a heavily pregnant Burundian asylum seeker was denied access to an antenatal class, which she had been frequenting. Upon her arrival, she was informed by the nurses that they were reluctant to let her attend her last appointment before birth, as Operation Dudula and the March and March people would arrive at any time. One of the nurses went as far as informing her that her presence might attract the likes of Operation Dudula and encouraged her to leave, as they do not want to attract Operation Dudula.
records.response: No police intervened

records.name: A heavily pregnant asylum seeker from Burundi, is denied access twice at Addington hospital
records.description:
On 5th August, A pregnant Burundian asylum seeker went to Addington hospital for a check-up-
up. Since falling pregnant in February, after being operated on in December, she was required to go there every month for a checkup. When she arrived there, dressed in her Muslim women's attire, the marchers and marchers who were at the gate. Suspected already that she was a foreigner, before even talking to her. They asked her for her ID, which she didn’t have, and instead she showed them her asylum seeker visa. They told her that she must go to a private hospital because public hospitals and clinics are for
South Africans only. She went back home on that day, but she went again on 23rd August and both times they denied her entry. On both occasions, when she tried to reason with them, they got very angry and pushed her outside, saying all amakwerekwere must go back to their home countries; they must leave South Africa. She felt belittled, insulted, and her heart started beating very fast. She said, An African can’t chase away a heavily pregnant woman like that. She was seven months pregnant.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Nigerian man was denied access into Addington hospital as he was trying to visit his South African child who was hospitalised at Addington
records.description: On the 15th of August 2025, at Addington Hospital in the eThekwini district. A Nigerian father was denied the opportunity to visit his South African child, who was hospitalised at Addington Hospital. The Nigerian father was travelling with his child's caregiver, who also happened to be a non-national, when the two were stopped at the hospital entrance by March and March people. The Father and the caregiver were asked to present their Identification documents. The father presented his valid passport and informed the March and March people that he was there to visit his child, who had been admitted to the hospital.  The March and March people informed the 2 non-nationals that they were not allowed into the hospital; they specifically said that no foreigners can go into the hospital. The March and March people furthermore said that the child can stay in the hospital and die without having seen their father. The father and the caregiver also had snacks for the hospitalized child, and the March and March people told the non-nationals that a South African child does not have to eat snacks from foreign nationals. The Nigerian man called his wife who happened to be a South African, to inform her about the situation at hand. The Nigerian man's wife managed to go see their child but was not permitted to enter with the snacks that her husband had brought for their son.
records.who_attacked: A Nigerian father who wanted to visit his South African child
records.response: No response was recorded regarding this incident

records.name: A Zimbabwean National was denied access to healthcare at Dresser Clinic in Thokoza
records.description: On the 22nd of August 2025, a 41-year-old Zimbabwean national, who urgently needed treatment for a recurring asthma attack at Dresser Clinic in Thokoza, was refused medical attention. The Zimbabwean National was said to have arrived at the hospital at 10h15. The Zimbabwean national had shortness of breath and was in distress. Furthermore, the Zimbabwean national requested immediate access to an inhaler or nebuliser. His requests were met with the clinic staff refusing to assist the Zimbabwean national. The staff explained that the clinic has a policy against treating non-South African nationals without local documentation. The Zimbabwean national presented his valid Zimbabwean passport, but the clinic staff's response remained the same; they furthermore called security, who physically escorted him off the premises. Shortly after returning home, the Zimbabwean national collapsed outside his gate and was temporarily stabilised by neighbours using a borrowed inhaler. No ambulance or medical follow-up was provided.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was reported , but the security at the clinic escorted the sickly Zimbabwean national out the hospital

records.name: An Ethiopian permanent resident was denied to opportunity to accompany his South African child into Addington Hospital
records.description: On the 25th of August 2025, an Ethiopian permanent resident was denied the opportunity to accompany his 14-year-old South African son to Addington Hospital in the eThekwini district. The boy was South African as his late mother was a Zulu local. Upon the father and son's entrance to Addington hospital, they were stopped by the March and March people, who allowed the son to enter but denied his Ethiopian permanent resident father entrance into the hospital. The father informed the March and March people that his son is a minor and therefore needs to be accompanied, as the son will not be attended to if they are not travelling with a guardian or a parent. The March and March people were not only disinterested but told the Ethiopian father that he should go back to his home country and get treatment there because South African public Hospitals are for South Africans.
records.response: No response to this incident was recorded

records.name: A Somali refugee woman has attempted 10 times to access Addington hospital and Beatrice Street clinic, unsuccessfully
records.description:
A refugee woman from Somalia has attempted for the last time to enter Addington Hospital on 26 August 2025. She has been attempting to access the hospital regularly since the beginning of July, when March and March started blocking migrants from accessing healthcare, to collect medication for her husband, her son and herself. They said they can’t allow refugees; they only allow native South Africans. They said public hospitals are for South Africans; they can’t allow foreigners to access public healthcare,
and only those with green IDs can go in. On 26 August, she went there early in the morning for her son’s appointment. They stopped her and told her that she was a foreigner, and she couldn’t go inside. If she has a green ID, she must show it to them, and then they will allow her to go inside. On other days, they were very aggressive, but on 26 August, they only talked but didn’t do anything else. She is from Somalia, a country at war since 1991, so she can’t go back there. She can’t count the number of times that she attempted to access both Addington Hospital and Beatrice Street clinic, but when she went for the last time to Beatrice Street clinic on 07/08/2025 to collect her medication, she was denied access again. It has been 2 months now that 3 of them have not been able to see the doctor and get medication for their different chronic illnesses.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A naturalised South African father struggled to get medical attention for his child
records.description: On the 27th of August at the Gateway clinic, in the eThekwini district, a naturalised South African father tried to get his son immunization but was stopped by 2 ladies wearing March and March tops. The naturalised father asked why he was being stopped, seeing that he is a South African Citizen. The ladies replied by informing him that he could proceed into that specific section of the hospital, but the child could not see that his child was not born in South Africa. Which is incorrect, as the father mentioned that the child was born in South Africa. One of the people wearing a March-on-March top attempted to assist the father when her colleague was not looking.
records.response: No responses were recorded regarding this incident

records.name: A Somali refugee is forced to pay R268 to open a file because he is a foreign national
records.description: On the 31st of August 2025, A Somali Businessman was shot after leaving the mosque in downtown Durban. The Somali Asylum seeker, who was in a very critical state, was then rushed to Addington Hospital in the eThekwini. The Somali Asylum seeker was accompanied to the hospital by fellow Somali community members. Upon their arrival at the hospital, the community members were advised to open a file for the shot victim, as the victim was in a critical state. When the Somali community members conversed with the admin clerk, they were told that they needed to pay R268, as the person for whom they were opening a file was a foreign national.  The community member responded to this by informing the admin clerk that the victim was an asylum seeker, thus giving him the same rights as a South African citizen. This information was not well received, as the admin clerk continued to inform them that they would not help them or even open a file. The Somali nationals had to borrow R100 before the clerk was willing to open a file. After borrowing R100 to open a file, the community members learnt that the person they were accompanying had passed away and was taken to the mortuary.
records.who_attacked: A group of Somali community members
records.response: No responses were recorded regarding this incident

records.name: A Burundian refugee was denied the opportunity to attend his doctor's appointment
records.description: A Burundian refugee who underwent six surgeries at Addington Hospital in the eThekwini district for appendicitis and a hernia, he was told by his physicians not to do excessive labour, as this might lead to him needing another operation soon. This conversation with his doctor led to him submitting a SASSA application. The SASSA application required a few of his documents to be signed and filled in by the district surgeon. The Burundian Refugee had a check-up appointment with his physician on the 9th of September 2025, and also wanted to ask the Physician to sign his documentation.  Upon his arrival on the 9th of September 2025, the Burundian Refugee was halted by people in March and March regalia who proceeded to inform him that he should go to a private hospital.  An option which is not realistic for the Burundian refugee, as he cannot afford to go to a private hospital.  The Burundian Refugee tried going back on the 17th of September 2025 and tried to explain to the March-on-March people that he cannot afford private health care, along with the fact that Addington hospital has his file. The march and march people did not care.
records.response: No responses were reported regarding this incidents

records.name: A DRC national was denied medical assistance from Johannesburg hospital
records.description: On the 8th of September 2025, a chronically ill woman from the DRC, suffering from a heart condition and high blood pressure, sought medical attention from Johannesburg Hospital (Charlotte Maxeke), but was denied access to the hospital. Around 08h00 AM, the DRC national went to collect her medication from Johannesburg hospital. The DRC national was confronted at the hospital entrance by four individuals in white T-shirts, identified as Operation Dudula members. Operation Dudula then demanded that she present a South African ID. Upon presenting her refugee ID, she was told to leave and seek care at a private hospital, as public facilities were “only for South Africans.” Similar treatment was given to other foreign patients. DRC National then travelled to Alexandra Clinic, where she again encountered Operation Dudula hindering her entrance into the hospital. Her condition worsened, with difficulty breathing and dangerously low blood pressure, yet no medical staff intervened. In the afternoon, the DRC national left and sought help from a private doctor in Yeoville. She was subjected to paying R500 for emergency treatment that stabilised her condition. Shocked and disappointed, she reported the incident to the local police, who said they could not assist.
records.response: This incident was reported to the local police who said they could not assist.

records.name: A DRC national and her child were denied  the opportunity to get urgent medical care at Rosettenville Clinic in Johannesburg
records.description: On the 12th of September 2025, a 57-year-old refugee from the DRC attempted to access urgent medical care at Rosettenville Clinic in Johannesburg for her child. The DRC national's child was suffering from a severe respiratory condition and was scheduled for surgery due to worsening symptoms. The two arrived at 8h00 with valid asylum documentation. The DRC national was denied entry by Operation Dudula vigilantes. Despite her child’s critical condition, she was told, alongside other migrant patients, that only South Africans could use the clinic and that foreigners should seek private care. She remained outside until 13h00  before leaving without receiving any assistance.
records.who_attacked: A DRC national and her child
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: 2 documented asylum seekers from DRC were denied access to medical serivices at  Rosettenville Clinic
records.description: On 12th of September 2025, 2 documented asylum seekers from the DRC, attempted to access medical care at Rosettenville Clinic in Johannesburg for their seriously ill children, but were denied access to medical services. The one DRC asylum seeker's child was suffering from continuous vomiting and high fever, while the other DRC asylum seeker's child had a persistent dry cough, sore throat, vomiting, and fever. While queuing with other patients, Operation Dudula members ordered all non-South Africans to exit the queue. Despite presenting valid asylum documents, both DRC asylum seekers were forced out of the queue. One of the DRC asylum seekers pleaded for help. The DRC asylum seeker insisted that her child needed urgent help, but this plea was met with the Vigilante group telling her to seek private care and also forcing her to leave the queue.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: An undocumented Zimbabwean national  was denied access to health care
records.description: On 12th of  September 2025, an undocumented mother from Zimbabwe, tried again to get her 20-month-old child vaccinated at Rosettenville Clinic in Johanesburg. The undocumented Zimbabwean nation had been trying to get her child vaccinated since the 7th of July 2025 but was repeatedly blocked by vigilantes at the clinic gate. On the 12th of September 2025, the undocumented Zimbabwean asylum seeker arrived at 08h00 but was denied entry by the same group of vigilantes. Despite waiting until 13h00, the undocumented Zimbabwean national was never allowed inside the hospital and had to leave without the immunization her child urgently needed.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was documented

records.name: A Malawian national was denied healthcare services at Rosettenville Clinic in the Johannesburg
records.description: A Malawian national was denied healthcare services at Rosettenville Clinic in the Johannesburg municipality. This has been an ongoing matter since August 2025. This comes after the Malawian national had been persistently seeking an opportunity to get her chronic medication from the  Rosettenville Clinic. On the 12th of September 2025, at 08h00 until about 09h00, the Malawian national was once again denied access to the hospital by vigilantes and ultimately left without receiving her chronic medication.
records.response: No responses were recorded regarding this incident

records.name: 17-year-old from Zimbabwean undocumented mother was denied access into a hospital.
records.description: A 17-year-old from an undocumented Zimbabwean mother was denied access to a hospital. The Zimbabwean National had frequented Charlotte Maxeke Hospital. The Zimbabwean was scheduled to bring her child in for vaccination and a routine examination. On September 12, she attempted to visit the Yeoville clinic for services, and upon her arrival, at around 08h00, she was restricted from accessing the clinic. The Zimbabwean national mentioned that three unknown women stopped her from entering the hospital. She stayed at the clinic until 13h00 and then left without receiving assistance.  The Zimbabwean National then returned to  Yeoville clinic on the 15th of September, at 08h00, and the same women who had disrupted her days previously were present and denied her access into the clinic once again. She stayed outdoors and decided to leave at 13h00.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Burundian refugee, who have gone through 6 operations, is stopped from seeing the Doctor on his check-up date
records.description:
A Burundian refugee, who was operated 6 operations of hernia and appendicitis at Addington hospital, was advised by his doctors not to do hard work anymore and that another operation may be needed soon. For that reason, he was forced to go to SASSA to apply for He went to SASSA to apply for a grant, where he was given forms that were to be filled out and signed by the district surgeon. He also had a check-up appointment with his doctor on the day. He first went there on 9/9/2025. He was stopped by those people wearing march and march regalia, who told him to go to a private hospital. He went back on

records.name: A mother from the DRC and her children discriminated and rejected at a free mobile clinic by organizers at the Hills Recreation Centre.
records.description:
The Meals on Wheels Caregiver Program hosted a free medical clinic at the South Hills Recreation Centre on 18 October 2025. The program aimed to offer free counselling, medical consultations, HIV testing, ECG testing, and optometry services.
After being denied healthcare services multiple times at local clinics and hospitals, the DRC mother was hopeful that she and her children would finally receive assistance through this free community healthcare event. As a mother, she took her children with her because they also needed medical attention. The event poster, issued by Meals on Wheels Community Services, stated that the clinic was open to everyone in the community. Encouraged by this, the respondent attended the event expecting to be assisted. However, upon arrival at the reception, she presented her refugee identification document and was told, “No, we are so sorry. We are only taking citizens.” The respondent asked, “Why didn’t you mention on the poster that you are only helping citizens? It says you are helping the community.” She expressed her disappointment, saying she did not know that “community” referred only to citizens and not to foreigners. The organisers repeatedly apologised but maintained their stance. Eventually, the person in charge came to explain that they could not assist her because she was a foreign national. The organiser admitted that she was afraid of Operation Dudula and said, “Those citizens who are here might fund the Dudula people to come and cause trouble. They might start harassing and assaulting people here.” For that reason, she said, they would only assist citizens to avoid any conflict.
The respondent said her heart was broken once again. Her children, who had been hopeful, were deeply disappointed. It was yet another experience of rejection, the same painful words repeated: “You are a foreigner. We can’t help you.” After wasting both time and transport money, they returned home feeling defeated. The respondent said the experience affected her children emotionally and morally. They asked their mother, “Why is this happening to us? Weren’t we born here in South Africa?”
She concluded by saying that her children felt discriminated against, rejected, and heartbroken.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were recorded

records.name: A mother and her children discriminated and rejected at a free mobile clinic by organizers at the Hills Recreation Centre.
records.description:
On the 29th of October 2025, a Congolese national went to Edenvale hospital. She arrived at 07h00.  After waiting for a long time, she eventually gave her card, but the staff continued to call other people, even people who came after her. At 11h00, the Congolese national went to ask the staff why she was not being assisted. The nurses proceeded to tell the Congolese national that they were still busy looking for your file.  Around 10, 11 more people came, and all of them were passing her.  The Congolese national stood and went to ask again.  Upon her arrival at the front desk, she saw her file isolated; the file was on the side. She notified them that the file is there, and they were not calling me here.  She then she was then told to go back and sit.  They eventually called her, and she was told that she needed to pay out the money at the counter.   They checked her papers and discovered that she was Congolese with an H1.  The admin said," How come? How did you get this? How did you get this paper? How come you can be an H1 and you are not a South African? You were born here. You are not a South African. You don't have the right to have H1, you are coming to play here!!"  And then she told them that she had been using a status (section 24). She proceeded to show them the document, which will expire in 2027. The document was still up-to-date and valid. She even insisted that she has been coming to Edenvale Hospital since. And that she was an H1 patient all along.  She added that even when she goes to Johannesburg, she is qualified to be H1 because she has a status. The admin proceeded to tell her that she cannot use the H1, and she did not deserve to be an H1 because she is not a South African. 
 They asked her who put her under H1, and finally told her that she needs to change her documentation to pay like a private foreigner. The Congolese national refused and proceeded to tell them, “No, I am not a private foreigner because I have an H1 status from South Africa." The nurse proceeded to shout at her, saying, "You are the refugees, you are supposed to stay in the camp, but you even got the opportunity to go everywhere that you like, in a way you want, even to town, to shops, you are supposed to be somewhere else, not with us. You must pay. If you don't have that money, you must go away”. The Congolese national was surprised and very confused about the attitude given to her, verbally abusing her with strong words. She left the hospital crying as she wasn’t feeling well, having a heart condition.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was recorded

records.name: A chronic patient was denied health care at Edenvale hospital after been ignored on the queue for many hours.
records.description: On 29 October 2025, a Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) national arrived at Edenvale Hospital around 7:00 a.m. for medical attention. She presented her hospital card, as she had been receiving treatment there since 2003 and was registered as an H1 patient (a category for patients who receive free or subsidized care). Despite arriving early, the DRC national noticed that other patients who came after her were being called and assisted before her. When she asked the staff why she had not been helped, she was told that they were “still looking for her file.” Later, she saw her file set aside on the counter and pointed it out to the staff, but was told to sit and wait again. Eventually, when she was called, she was directed to the payment counter. The administrative staff questioned her H1 status after noticing she was not South African. They asked how she obtained H1 classification and told her she was not entitled to it because she was “not born in South Africa.” The DRC national explained that she holds Section 24 refugee status, valid until 2027, which grants her legal stay and access to public services in South Africa. Despite her explanation, the staff insisted that she should be classified as a “private foreign patient” and therefore must pay for services. When she objected, one staff member reportedly shouted at her, making xenophobic remarks  saying that refugees should “stay in camps,” “not come to town,” and that she should “pay or leave.” Feeling humiliated, verbally abused, and unwell due to her heart condition, the DRC national left the hospital in tears without receiving medical care.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A patient experiencing Kidney problem and visiting Mayfair clinic for treatment and blood test was mistreated and chased, by the clinic phlebotomist.
records.description:
On the 30th of October 2025, A Somali national who was experiencing kidney problems was denied access to healthcare services at Mayfair Clinic. The Somali National who had frequented Mayfair was denied access to healthcare. The Somali national initially sought help for kidney issues and received medication and injections. Her condition seemed to be getting worse. The doctor gave her three months to check her progress, and she was given medication for three days. The doctor told her, “After three days, check how you’re responding. If you don’t feel better, come back for a blood test.” An appointment date was issued. However, the appointment for her blood test was too early in the morning for her because she had to drop her children off at school. She had difficulty making an early morning appointment. The appointment date was the 30th. The nurse told her to come at 7:30 a.m., but she said she couldn’t make it at that time because she had to drop children at school and would only be able to come around 8 or past 8:00 a.m. The next day, which was the 30th, she went to the clinic around 8 in the morning. When she arrived, she met the male staff member, who was unhelpful, rude, and accused her of arriving whenever she wanted. The phlebotomist started by telling the patient to go back and stand in the queue properly. Another staff member came out and asked everyone, “Are you here for chronic medication or for an injection?” The Somali national responded and told him that she was there for a blood test. The man then said she had to come back another day.  The patient went back outside and waited, but when she was called again, they sent her back once more.
Later, she was told that she needed to come back next month or in two months for the blood test; otherwise, she would not be attended to again. The Somali national tried to explain that her appointment time was changed because of her children’s school schedule, but the phlebotomist said, “No, they must give you the time you want? You foreigners are getting free service here” He even reported her to the other nurses, saying that she comes whenever she wants. The Somali national explained, “It’s my health; it’s my priority. She also told them that she doesn’t enjoy going to the clinic every week that she goes because she is sick. The phlebotomist then told her not to come back to Mayfair Clinic again and threatened to call the police to arrest her. He chased her away. Somali National said that the staff member in question lacks empathy and is not effectively communicating with the patient, leading to misunderstandings and frustration. She felt misunderstood and unfairly accused of causing problems. 
Now, the patient is afraid to return to the clinic because she needs to go back for the blood test and will have to face the same man again. She emphasises that she has been a patient at the clinic for 16 years and has never had issues before.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: A Congolese patient in pain was denied health care at Hillbrow clinic because of his nationality.
records.description:
A 41-year-old woman from Congo living in Berea was chased while accompanying her husband, who was in severe pain due to a shooting by police officers a few years back. The Congolese national and her husband have been repeatedly denied healthcare at Johannesburg Hospital since the husband was shot by a police officer. At Johannesburg hospital, she was told not to return there again. Staff stated it was a police case and they couldn't help. Her husband was shot in January 2023 and still has a bullet in his body. They sought medical attention for pain related to this. In August 2025, the Congolese national took her husband, who was having pain, to Hillbrow clinic. They arrived there around 06h00, when nurses came in, they started checking who was South African and who wasn’t South African. The nurses started calling only South Africans and told all migrants that they only wanted South African faces in that clinic. They were told that the hospital's medicine was only for South African patients.  While Operation Dudula members were present, the nurses were the ones who chased migrants away. Hospital staff used offensive language (Zulu and other languages) and told them to go back to their country, she said. Shouting at migrants, and they were forced to go out. The Congolese national expresses feeling scared, helpless, and restricted in South Africa. This denial of care is not an isolated incident for this couple. They have faced similar issues since the shooting. Lawyers helped after the initial shooting, but not recently.
These experiences have affected the couple's ability to work. The Congolese national is now afraid to go to hospitals, fearing for her safety. No organisations have intervened to help them at the hospital recently. Her husband still didn’t find a solution.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded.

records.name: Police in Brixton extort a group of foreign nationals
records.description: On Thursday, 15 January 2026, nine foreign nationals, three women and six men from Zimbabwe and Malawi, were stopped by SAPS members while waiting for taxis. The officers were in uniform, but did not have badges. One member of the group later provided an account of the events as a witness. The group was informed they were being arrested for not carrying their passports and was taken to Brixton Police Station. According to the witness, no personal details were recorded, no charges were explained, no case docket was opened, and no formal booking occurred. The group was not placed in official police cells, but what appeared to be a back room of some sort. The SAPS members involved refused to provide their names and had removed their name badges. During the detention, the individuals were informed they would only be released upon payment of money. The victims called the witness for financial assistance, but the witness could not provide it. The witness offered to bring the victims their passports, but the police were not fond of this idea. An initial demand of approximately R3 000 per person was made, regardless of whether valid passports could later be produced. No receipts, fines, or written documentation were issued. On Friday, 16 January 2026, the witness contacted Colonel Mkhwanazi, Station Commander of Brixton SAPS. He confirmed that the individuals had not been booked, that one member of the group was not recorded as being in the police cells, and that he had no knowledge of the detention at that time. At approximately 11:00 on 16 January 2026, all nine individuals paid money and were released. One woman negotiated the amount to R1 400 and paid in cash. No receipt or official acknowledgement of payment was provided.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter have been recorded

records.name: A congolese refugee father struggled to fetch his children from school due to Operation Dudula
records.description: On the 19th January 2026, a Congolese Refugee father struggled to fetch his children from school because they are Congolese. The Congolese father of 2 children enrolled at Addington Primary School was met by Operation Dudula members who were advocating for the removal of foreign national students from the school and for foreign national students to be denied access to the school. The father shared that xenophobic slurs such as "Kwerekwere" were shared, and he was on his way to fetch his children from school.  The protestors were not on school property, but as soon as the foreign national parents left the school property, they were pelted with stones. The Congolese father of 2 also experienced being thrown with a stone. The police struggled to intervene, but later the police opened fire and tried to help foreign nationals to safety, but Operation Dudula continued to throw stones. The Congolese father further shared that his children did not go to school for the rest of the week out of fear.
records.response: The police assisted in getting the people to safety

The protesters continued to tell parents who are foreign nationals that their children should not be enrolled at Addington Primary School. The police were present and attempted to escort foreign nationals to safety, but struggled to control the situation and were forced to open fire in the school vicinity. The Congolese father later reported that, due to fear of further attacks, his child did not return to school for the remainder of the week.

records.name: Community Tensions Erupt After Murder, Leaving Migrants Displaced Near Winterton
records.description: In Winterton, Bergville, a Zimbabwean national allegedly killed his South African girlfriend, with whom he had a child. After committing the crime, he reportedly dumped her body near a river. He then contacted her family, informed them of the incident, and told them where the body could be found. On 11 February, the family went to the location and recovered her body. The incident sparked outrage in the community. Tensions quickly escalated, and community members began calling for the removal of all migrants from the area. Violence and unrest followed, and several foreign nationals were reportedly threatened. Police intervened to prevent further harm. As a result, many foreign nationals were displaced. Some are still being sheltered at the police station and in local church halls. A local church near Winterton Police Station is currently housing many of the displaced migrants. Most of those affected are Congolese and Burundian refugees and asylum seekers, although there are also Eritrean, Malawian, and Zimbabwean nationals among them. Over 100 adults were left displaced.

records.name: Eastern Cape march against Nigerian 'king' turns violent
records.description: Traffic was brought to a stop in KuGompo City as the group March and March, together with others, protested against the crowning of a Nigerian king. The protest started after videos and photos spread on social media showing Chief Solomon Ogbonna Eziko being crowned “Igwe Ndigbo” of the city. Government officials and cultural leaders said the coronation was not legal and did not follow local traditions. The protest later became violent. Some protesters, including people from KwaZulu-Natal, forced foreign-owned shops belonging to Somali and Ethiopian nationals in the city centre to close and burned vehicles. Police used rubber bullets to control the crowd. The march began in Windmill and moved to City Hall, where protesters wanted to share their concerns. One protester said the coronation was disrespectful and went against local customs. Another said they wanted to show that illegal foreigners are not welcome.

records.name: A woman was killed zimbabwean asylum seeker was shot and killed by the unknown zulu vigilantes in her home
records.description:
On 29 April 2026, a Zimbabwean asylum seeker was selling food at a musical event in Hillbrow, Johannesburg, alongside her pregnant daughter. In the early hours of the morning, between approximately 02:00 and 03:00, the daughter returned to their residence to collect additional food supplies.

While attempting to leave the apartment, she was confronted and obstructed by a group of individuals described as Zulu vigilantes, who refused to allow her to exit the building. Feeling threatened, she contacted her mother to inform her of the situation.

The mother immediately left the event and went to the residence to intervene. Upon confronting the group, she was shot in the head and chest. During the incident, the perpetrators allegedly made xenophobic remarks, stating: “You makwerekwere want to rule this whole area.”

The suspects fled the scene and were not apprehended. The police later arrived and assisted in transporting the victim’s body to the mortuary.

records.name: Anti-Immigrant Confrontation Raises Questions Over Documentation and Migrant Integration

During the confrontation, the individuals she was travelling with asked he Ghanian National to produce his passport and was accused of bribing police officers to obtain immigration stamps and certified documentation. The individuals continued to tell the Ghanaian national that immigrants were not permitted to certify official documents while residing in a foreign country and then accused him of paying a police officer to certify his documents. records.name: March on March targets immigrants
records.description: On 29 April 2026, members of the March and March movement held a protest in Johannesburg. During the demonstration, a Cameroonian migrant was beaten with a knobkierrie after being identified as a foreigner, while protesters shouted xenophobic slurs. In addition to this identified case, other foreign nationals in the Braamfontein–Hillbrow area , specifically Twist Street, past the Wanderers taxi rank towards the Ethiopian Quarter on Rahima Moosa Street in Jeppe, where most of the shops were already shuttered. were reportedly attacked and intimidated. These included incidents where individuals were accosted and struck by members of the group, as well as repeated cases of people being chased, harassed, and threatened after being identified as “foreigners” by protesters. The protest was also characterised by narratives portraying foreign nationals as undocumented migrants and associating them with crime, drug activity, and social disorder. Some protesters were reportedly armed and engaged in vigilante-style behaviour, including stopping individuals in the street, issuing threats, and acting outside formal law enforcement procedures. The Johannesburg Metro Police Department said the protest deviated from its approved route due to crowd size and safety-related “unpredictable factors.” They explained that when large groups change direction, officers often prioritise managing public safety and traffic rather than trying to force the crowd back, as this could escalate tensions. They also noted that carrying weapons during protests is prohibited, but acknowledged that confiscating them in a volatile situation is difficult.

records.name: Anti-Immigrant Protest in Johannesburg Escalates After March Deviates From Approved Route
records.description: An anti-immigrant protest organised by “March and March” took place in Johannesburg on 30 April 2026, beginning at Mary Fitzgerald Square and initially proceeding toward the Gauteng Legislature.  Ground up showed that approximately 1,000 protesters participated, including supporters linked to ActionSA and the MK Party. The protest diverted from its approved route and moved through Braamfontein and Hillbrow. The marchers shouted insults at anyone they thought was an immigrant. GroundUp showed that a man was assaulted with a weapon and left bleeding during the unrest, while some protesters carried sticks and shields.  Businesses owned by foreign nationals closed temporarily due to fears of violence and looting. A protester smashed his stick against closed shops in a largely immigrant neighbourhood in Johannesburg.  An Ethiopian shopkeeper stated that businesses closed because owners were uncertain whether police could guarantee their safety. The South African Police Service (SAPS) later stated that “no incidents were recorded” and described the protest as peaceful, despite eyewitness reports of violence. Protestors called for all non skilled jobs in South Africa to be reserved for South Africans and advocated for general working environments to be filled with South Africans only

records.name: Zambian National faced with retrenchment after admin issues
records.description: Since 2023, a Zambian national employed as a teacher in South Africa has experienced ongoing difficulties in obtaining and renewing the documentation required for registration with the relevant teaching council. Throughout this period, the requirements and procedures appeared to change frequently, making compliance increasingly difficult. It was reported that the process was significantly more complicated for foreign nationals than for South African citizens. Numerous attempts were made to resolve the documentation issues. Assistance was sought through online platforms; however, the systems were often unavailable or offline. When visits were made to the relevant offices in person, discriminatory treatment was allegedly experienced. Xenophobic remarks were reportedly directed at her, including being told to return to her country of origin. Accusations were also made that she was a criminal and that her documents were fraudulent, despite no evidence being provided to support these claims. In 2024, an application was successfully submitted online. However, inconsistencies were allegedly encountered within the system. At certain times, the system indicated that all documentation was in order, while at other times it suggested that requirements had not been met. Screenshots were retained showing instances where the system reflected that her documentation status was compliant. Thereafter, employment was secured at Benoni Christian School. During the course of her employment, inspectors were reportedly contacted by the school to verify her documentation. Following this verification process, it was indicated that her paperwork was not up to date, despite the screenshots showing that her documentation had previously been accepted by the system. On 23 May, she was contacted by a manager from the documentation office after the inspectors had made enquiries regarding her status. During this interaction, she was allegedly accused of committing fraud and was referred to as a criminal without any explanation or evidence being provided. It was further alleged that xenophobic remarks were made, that she was shouted at, and that she was instructed to leave, while being accused of engaging in criminal activity. Subsequently, her employer instructed her to attend the teaching council's offices in Pretoria to prove that her documentation was valid and in order. However, transport assistance was not provided. Due to financial constraints, she was unable to travel to Pretoria to attend to the matter. On 25 May, her employment at Benoni Christian School was terminated after she was unable to travel to verify her documentation. Although she remained willing to continue with the process of resolving the documentation issues, the inability to attend the council offices resulted in the loss of her employment. She is currently unemployed and does not have the financial means to travel to Pretoria to address the outstanding documentation concerns. A case has since been referred to the CCMA for assistance and resolution.
records.response: A case has been opened with the CCMA

records.description:
On the 28th of May 2026, Violent protests with anti-immigrant sentiments took place involving around 700 pupils in Kraaifontein, Cape Town. The protests disrupted normally busy streets and created fear among informal traders, particularly foreign nationals. The sudden protest action, amid reports about a national shutdown planned for
30 June 2026 by anti-illegal immigration group March and March, has worsened already
heightened fears for vendors in the area. Vendors reported that learners threw stones at moving cars and people, looted stalls, and made threats, forcing many traders to stop working and leaving them unable to earn an income. Police were alerted by a member of the public and deployed officers to escort the pupils back to their schools. Authorities said the unrest appeared to have started at Masibambane Secondary School before spreading to nearby schools, although investigations suggest outside groups may have played a role in encouraging the protests.
records.response: Police were alerted by a member of the public and deployed officers to escort the pupils back to their schools.

records.name: Smash-and-Grab Incident During March & March Activities in Marabastad, Pretoria
records.description: On 28 May 2026, at approximately 9:20 AM, a Zimbabwean national was a victim of a smash-and-grab incident that was reported in Marabastad, Pretoria. The incident occurred during the activities of the March & March campaign, during which the complainant's vehicle was targeted. It was further reported that members of the South African Police Service (SAPS) responded swiftly to the incident and provided immediate assistance.
records.response: South African Police Service responded swiftly to the incident and provided immediate assistance.

records.name: Police investigate as two Mozambican nationals and SA teen killed in Mossel Bay
records.description: In the early hours of Saturday, 30 May 2026, police were called to a scene in Asla Park informal settlement where the body of a 27-year-old man was discovered with multiple injuries. Shortly afterwards, another man, aged 43, was taken to a local hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival after sustaining assault-related injuries. It was later established that the two deceased men were of Mozambican descent. Investigations are ongoing, and no arrests have been made at this stage. No arrests have been affected yet
records.response: No arrests have been affected yet however the police were present at the scene.

records.name: Mossel Bay protests clash over Tsonga teen's murder
records.description: A fatal stabbing was reported in KwaNonqaba, Mossel Bay, on 31 May, after a 19-year-old man sustained a chest wound and was declared dead at the scene. An investigation has been launched by the police, although no suspect has been arrested and no motive has been officially confirmed. It has been said by the victim's family that the attack occurred during anti-foreigner unrest and that the victim was mistakenly identified as a foreign national because he spoke Xitsonga, despite being a South African citizen. Further claims have been made that he was removed from a house where he had been sleeping before the attack took place.
records.response: Officers attended the scene in Kwa Nonqaba after receiving a complaint and found the victim with a stab wound to the chest. Emergency medical personnel declared him dead at the scene. A murder investigation was subsequently opened, and efforts to identify and arrest the suspect were initiated.

records.name: A Burundian delivery driver was assaulted in Durban
records.description: On Tuesday, 2 June 2026, a documented Burundian delivery driver was allegedly assaulted after completing the delivery of a bed to a customer who had requested his services. Following the delivery, he was reportedly subjected to verbal abuse and was told to return to his country of origin. The incident is alleged to have been motivated, at least in part, by his nationality.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident have been recorded

records.name: Thousands of displaced Malawians seek refuge at Durban park
records.description: On the 14th of June 2026, approximately 4,000 Malawian nationals were displaced and forced to seek refuge at Sherwood Hall Park and nearby facilities in Durban after threats were issued by anti-illegal immigration groups demanding that undocumented migrants leave the country. In some informal settlements, foreign nationals were subjected to intimidation, with armed individuals said to have conducted door-to-door visits during which threats were made, and instructions were given for migrants to leave South Africa before the 30 June deadline set by the groups. As a result of the attacks and intimidation, a voluntary repatriation programme for affected Malawian nationals was initiated by the Malawian government.
records.response: A voluntary repatriation programme was initiated by the Malawian government for those seeking to return home. A task team was deployed under the coordination of the Malawi High Commission in South Africa, while documentation was processed by South African Department of Home Affairs officials to facilitate the return of affected individuals.

records.name: 4 people looting resulted in the killing of a Malawian national
records.description: On 18 June 2026, members of 4 March and March members looted shops foreign own shops in Thembelihle, during which a Malawian national was shot. An additional Malawian national was stabbed with a knife during the lootings.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident have been recorded

records.name: Malawian National stoned
records.description: On 19 June 2026, a Malawian national was stoned to death in the Jika Joe informal settlement in KwaZulu-Natal. The killing is linked to anti-migrant protests taking place in the community. Foreign nationals living in nearby settlements were attacked after some members of the protest broke away from the main group. A murder case has been opened by the police, and investigations are ongoing.
records.response: Police have opened a murder case and investigations are ongoing

records.name: Foreign national beaten to death, others assaulted in Pietermaritzburg
records.description: On the 20th of June 2026, Dozens of foreign nationals, most of them Malawian, were forced to flee their homes after a Malawian man was stoned to death by a group of people armed with sticks at Sable Flats Manor. The incident occurred after a protest in Pietermaritzburg's city centre, which had been organised by March and March. As the attacks unfolded, many foreign nationals were left with no time to collect their shoes or personal belongings while escaping. Temporary accommodation was later provided to those who had fled.
records.response: The police have started investigating the murder and the foreign nationals who fled have been given temporary housing.

records.name: Unidentified individual was stoned to death by a mob that though that they were a foreign national
records.description: On the 20th of June 2026, an individual suspected of being a foreign national was stoned to death by community members
records.response: No police intervention was reported

records.name: Police probe killing of Malawian national in Pietermaritzburg
records.description: A 29-year-old Malawian national was stoned to death during a march against undocumented migrants. Two other individuals were also injured during the violence. The march, which was organised in opposition to illegal immigration, escalated into violence when foreign nationals were targeted and assaulted with sticks and sjamboks. Following the attack, fears for the safety of migrants intensified, resulting in the displacement of foreign nationals who sought refuge at the Mayor's Walk grounds. KwaZulu-Natal Premier condemned the attack; security measures were strengthened at the temporary shelter site, while arrangements were made for affected Malawian nationals to be transported to the Lindela Repatriation Centre as part of ongoing voluntary repatriation efforts.
records.who_attacked: Police probe killing of Malawian national in Pietermaritzburg
records.response: KwaZulu-Natal Premier condemned the attack, and the Malawian nationals were also provided with temporary shelter surrounded by protection

records.name: Xenophobic Intimidation of Foreign Nationals in Boksburg
records.description: Foreign nationals and businesses owned or operated by migrants were targeted during anti-foreigner marches in Boksburg on 23 June 2026. Properties were vandalised and marked with anti-foreigner slogans, while threats and intimidation were directed at foreign nationals. Several businesses were closed due to fears of violence and property damage. In response, warnings were issued by authorities that acts of intimidation, violence and vandalism would not be tolerated, and increased law-enforcement deployments were implemented ahead of further planned demonstrations.
records.response: warnings were issued by authorities that acts of intimidation, violence and vandalism would not be tolerated, and increased law-enforcement deployments were implemented ahead of further planned demonstrations.

records.name: A Somali national residing in Gugulethu Cape Town was displaced
records.description: A Somali national residing in Gugulethu, Cape Town, was displaced after the shop in which accommodation had been provided by a family member was destroyed by fire on 24 June. As a result, shelter was lost and relocation became necessary. At present, no legal documentation is held in South Africa. A return to Somalia is considered unsafe because of the ongoing conflict and the country's unstable security situation.
records.response: No police response has been recorded
