records.description: In Durban a Somali national's supermarket was looted on the 30th of June 2026. He suffered losses exceeding R5 million after looters emptied his store. Another store near the Kwa Dabeka police station was looted leaving people who work in the shop without work, people who were locals. A shop owner who is in South Africa legally and has been for 7 years expressed hurt after his shop was looted.
records.response: No interventions were recorded

records.name: Anti Migrant protests take place In Katlehong
records.description: In Katlehong in Ekurhuleni on the 30th of June 2026 a group of young people looted foreign owned shops after a peaceful march that day.  A shop being rented by a Mozambican national was looted on the 30th of June and everything was taken. The owner of the shop proceeded to say that she had no choice but to open for protestors as they were already on the roof attempting to break in
records.response: No responses were recorded

records.name: Evicted Malawians shelter in Robertson community hall
records.description: More than 300 Malawian immigrants were displaced and accommodated at the Callie de Wet Community Hall in Robertson following xenophobic threats, intimidation, and forced evictions in surrounding communities. Individuals were evicted by landlords or compelled to leave their homes after threats were made against foreign nationals, resulting in widespread displacement across Robertson, Ashton, Swellendam, Klapmuts and nearby areas. Xenophobic intimidation included night-time attacks on dwellings, removal of personal belongings, and repeated threats, which contributed to a climate of fear and insecurity. As a result, many individuals fled their residences and sought refuge at the designated shelter. Police raids targeting undocumented immigrants were conducted; however, the South African Police Service (SAPS) stated that no official record of such operations existed. Despite this, the incidents contributed to heightened fear within migrant communities. The displacement resulted in significant humanitarian consequences, including loss of employment, loss of accommodation, and depletion of financial resources among affected individuals. Women and children were among those accommodated at the shelter, where emergency assistance was provided.  The majority of those affected sought refuge due to threats experienced in their communities, and ongoing safety concerns contributed to the decision for voluntary repatriation, with transportation arrangements made for Malawian nationals to return via Musina.
records.response: South African Police Service (SAPS) stated that no official record of such operations existed

records.name: Destruction and Looting of Foreign Nationals' Homes in Alexandra
records.description: On the 1st of July 2026, In Alexandra, an unidentified woman led a group of armed youths who damaged and destroyed homes belonging to foreign nationals. Several properties were targeted, including the residence of a Malawian national. During the incident, property was damaged, and personal belongings were looted, including items such as fridges and winter blankets.
records.response: No responses regarding the incident were reported.

records.name: Harassment and Attacks on Foreign Vendors at Taxi Ranks in Bellville, Western Cape
records.description: From 1 July 2026, incidents of harassment targeting foreign national vendors were reported at taxi ranks in Bellville and across parts of the Cape Flats in the Western Cape. A group of Xhosa women stationed at the taxi ranks were said to have confronted foreign vendors, instructing them to stop trading in these areas. Foreign nationals who were present at the taxi ranks were subsequently attacked. The number of affected individuals could not be determined. Those targeted included foreign nationals from Zimbabwe, Malawi, Mozambique, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania who were engaged in informal trading at the taxi ranks.
records.who_attacked: Foreign nationals who also happen to be vendors
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were reported

records.name: Anti-immigration Protesters illegally detained two foreign national
records.description: In KuGompo city in the Eastern Cape, Anti-immigration Protesters illegally detained two foreign nationals on the 1st of July 2026, and at the same time, they were calling on authorities to investigate whether a Pakistani-born man who had become a citizen had entered into a fraudulent marriage. Police warned against lawlessness during protests
records.response: Police warned against lawlessness during protests

records.name: Anti-migrant protestors demanded that a Ghanaian national closes his store.
records.description: In KuGompo City on the1st of July 2026, Anti-migrant protestors demanded that a Ghanaian national close his store. While closing the store, he was asked to present an ID. The ID seemed to be South African and it was new, the protestors then told the Ghanaian man that he would have to go to the police station with them to verify the ID. The Ghanaian national kept denying that he was in South Africa illegally. On their way to the police station they bumped into a Malawian man and asked him to produce identification, this is when the Anti migrant protestors took him with them to the police station. On the same day in KuGompo, a Pakistani furniture outlet owner married to a South African national was asked by anti migrant protestors to produce an ID. They did not take him to the police station however released a statement that said that they would request that the police go to the shop and investigate how he got married to a South African national. They continued to express that their actions are helping the government because has limited resources.
records.who_attacked: A Ghanaian shop owner, A Malawian national and  a Pakistani man
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were recorded

records.name: Anti migrant protests in Greenfields Ekurhuleni
records.description: In Greenfields in Ekurhuleni, on the 1st of July 2026, the homes of foreign nationals were broken into, and foreign nationals were told to leave. On the same day, anti-migrant protestors gave the owner of a shop 20 minutes to pack up his stock and leave.  The Ethiopian national mentioned that he had been a shop owner for 9 years and he mentioned that he had relocated to what he thought was a safer location . The  shop owner managed to get private security to stand by while he packed up his shop . The protestors then went to a backroom shack and insisted that a Mozambican national leave. The protestors began to remove his belongings from the property and placed his belongings on the street. The protestors then went down to several different shops and requested that the ones owned by foreign nationals be closed off. Police arrived on the scene and liaised with community leaders
records.response: The police arrived and were seen talking to community leaders

records.name: Refusal of Access and Harassment of Zimbabwean Vendors at Bellville Taxi Rank
records.description: On 2 July, at a taxi rank in Bellville on the Cape Flats, Zimbabwean nationals were refused access to the taxi rank and told by Xhosa people and Operation Dudula that they were not allowed to sell goods there. Members of the group patrolled the taxi rank to ensure that no foreign nationals were selling. Police were present at the scene but did not intervene, while the Xhosa people continued to harass vendors who attempted to enter the taxi rank.
records.response: Police were present at the scene

records.name: Assault and Theft of a South African Citizen at a Shell Garage in Mpumalanga
records.description: On 6 July 2026, a South African citizen travelling by taxi to Mozambique stopped at a Shell garage in Mpumalanga, where she was harassed by a Mozambican foreign national in relation to the March and March protests. Xenophobic remarks were directed at her, and the following statements were made: "We are beating them now. When I visit their country, they hit me. What am I going to do?" It was further stated, "We caught you. The witch doctor serves you." The South African citizen responded by stating, "I have never hit anyone." Following her response, she was physically assaulted. The assault continued, and during the incident, her personal belongings, including her passport and driver's licence, went missing.
records.response: No response from the police was indicated

records.name: Police seen assisting Limpopo residents to round up and evict immigrants
records.description: Approximately 200 foreign nationals were removed from Vleifontein and surrounding villages, including Maila and Kanana, and taken to the Louis Trichardt Showgrounds after being identified by community members and handed over to police. The individuals were processed by the Department of Home Affairs and later transported to Musina, where they joined other foreign nationals awaiting repatriation. During the operation, foreign nationals stated that community members entered their residences, instructed them to leave, and that some were transported in police vehicles while further individuals were collected from surrounding homes. Concerns were raised regarding the removal of personal belongings, with some individuals stating they were not given sufficient opportunity to collect their possessions before being taken away. The campaign was organised by community members who stated that the intention was to address undocumented immigration while preventing possible attacks against foreign-owned businesses. It was stated that some foreign nationals voluntarily surrendered after learning that repatriation arrangements would be made. Police indicated that their role was to maintain public order and ensure the safety of all individuals involved, while Home Affairs managed the processing and repatriation procedures.
records.response: Police vehicles were used to transport some foreign nationals to the Louis Trichardt Showgrounds. SAPS stated that their role was to maintain public order and ensure safety, but the information provided does not establish that police officers participated in forced removals or home entries. Department of Home Affairs processed the individuals at the showgrounds and facilitated their movement to Musina for repatriation procedures.

records.name: Residents demand landlords stop renting to undocumented immigrants
records.description: On the 8th of July 2026, Residents in several Soweto neighbourhoods, including Naledi, Emndeni, and Zola, intensified a campaign against undocumented foreign nationals by marching through the communities and calling on landlords to stop renting properties, backrooms, and business premises to undocumented migrants. Following a march to the Naledi Police Station, businesses, including spaza shops and hair salons operated by foreign nationals, were targeted and closed during the demonstrations. The campaign formed part of broader anti-illegal immigration protests aimed at reclaiming the local spaza shop economy for South African citizens.
records.response: Police presence or intervention during the Soweto campaign was not confirmed.

records.name: Community Actions Targeting Foreign Nationals in  Thembelihle
records.description: On Thursday, 9 July 2026, concerns were raised by community members in Thembelihle, regarding the presence of foreign nationals in the community. It was stated that the deadline of 30 June 2026 had long passed and that foreign nationals had become too comfortable and too familiar within the community. Calls over Whatsapp were made for the community to unite and force foreign nationals out by making their living conditions unbearable. It was further stated that the township had been ruined by foreign nationals, who were described as lawless and as doing whatever they wanted. Demands were made for the remaining foreign nationals to be forcibly evicted, and landlords who accommodated foreign nationals were urged to remove them from their properties, with the view that they had been given too much freedom. The community was also described as having become "Malawi" because of the presence of foreign nationals. Community members further stated that the community needed to unite and "clean" the area. On Saturday, 11 July 2026, an unknown foreign national from the same community pleaded with community members to allow her and other foreign nationals to leave peacefully. During the incident, the homes of foreign nationals including the one unknown foreign national mentioned prior, were forcibly entered, property was damaged, and belongings were moved in an effort to compel them to leave. Acts of rape, theft, and the looting of personal possessions were also committed against some of the foreign nationals.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were received

records.name: Malawian residents face assault and get robbed
records.description: On 29 June, the home of a long-term Malawian resident was broken into, and the occupant was assaulted while personal belongings were stolen. Subsequently, on the night of 16 July, at least four households belonging to Malawian nationals were targeted in coordinated robberies. During these attacks, victims were instructed to return to their country of origin, indicating that the incidents were motivated by xenophobic hostility rather than ordinary criminal activity.
records.response: No police response has been recorded

records.name: Malawian nationals robbed
records.description: On the 16th of July in Thembilihle, Johannesburg, five men kicked down a Malawian national was, beaten when he said he had no money. His eyes filled with tears as he recounted how the gang took his fridge, TV and mobile phone.
records.response: No response regarding this incident was recorded

records.name: Malawian nationals were robbed
records.description: On the 16th of July , several migrant households were targeted in a series of coordinated robberies. During one of the attacks, savings amounting to approximately R4,000, which had been set aside to finance a return journey to Malawi, were stolen. Xenophobic remarks were made during the robbery, with the victims being told that, as foreigners, they should leave South Africa. As the night progressed, at least two additional migrant households were robbed by the same group of attackers. The loss of their savings left many victims unable to afford their planned return to Malawi, further compounding the financial and emotional impact of the attacks.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: Xenophobic Violence and Forced Displacement in Alexandra Township
records.description: On 16 July, a protest involving approximately 50 individuals took place in Alexandra Township, Johannesburg. The demonstrators, some of whom were carrying sticks, clubs, and other objects, marched through the area while chanting slogans. Although the protest was initially presented as peaceful, the situation escalated later in the day. As the demonstration progressed, doors to several homes were forcibly broken down while police officers were reportedly present. Both South African citizens and foreign nationals were affected, suggesting that the attacks were not limited to undocumented migrants. Residents repeated damage to their homes, and families described experiencing fear and psychological distress as the violence unfolded. During the protest, individuals suspected by the demonstrators of being undocumented migrants were removed from their homes and taken away by police. In addition, two women, one of whom was holding a baby while another showed signs of severe distress, were transported in a police vehicle after officers stated that this was being done for their safety.
records.response: No responses were recorded

records.name: Jeffrey’s Bay quiet but tense after spaza shop looting and 69 arrests
records.description: On 17 July 2026, foreign-owned spaza shops in the township areas of Jeffrey's Bay were forced to remain closed following violent protests that targeted migrant-owned businesses. At least 23 spaza shops were looted, and 69 individuals were arrested on charges of public violence. Public order was restored through the deployment of Public Order Policing and Visible Policing units, while a high police presence was maintained to prevent further unrest. Search-and-seizure operations were intensified to recover looted property, and investigations into the violence, including the role of the protest organisers, are ongoing. The incidents reflected a pattern of xenophobic violence directed at foreign-owned businesses in the area.
records.response: Public order was restored through the deployment of Public Order Policing and Visible Policing units. Search-and-seizure operations were intensified to recover looted property, and investigations into the violence,

records.name: Incident Involving Threats Against Mozambican Nationals
records.description: On 19 July 2026, at approximately 20h00, in Thembelihle, Lenasia, a Mozambican national who was visiting his family was informed by a South African national, who had entered the family home, that he and his family should leave the country. It was further noted that the South African national threatened that she can organise someone to rob them, burn their property, and kill them
records.response: No police intervention was recorded

records.name: Vereeniging residents clash with foreign business owners
records.description: Foreign business owners in Vereeniging, in the Vaal, came under xenophobic attack after a group of South African nationals targeted their businesses and demanded that foreign nationals leave the town and return to their countries. Police intervention was carried out after the violence escalated. Roads were blockaded with burning tyres and rocks, while businesses and vehicles belonging to foreign nationals were vandalised, with windows smashed during the attacks. Some foreign nationals responded by confronting the protesters, with both groups pelting each other with stones in the town's CBD. The attacks unfolded as some protesters insisted that foreign nationals should not be operating businesses in the area. One of the protesters said: "Immigrants are not supposed to be running businesses in our areas when there is so much poverty. This is such an impoverished area in the whole of Gauteng, and we cannot look on as foreigners take the money and ship it to their countries. The people of the Vaal are saying enough is enough. It's not going to be Thursday. It's going to be every day. We need economic restoration."
records.response: Police intervention was carried out after the violence escalated

records.name: A South African student whose father is Nigerian has stated that they experienced discrimination at St Ursula's School
records.description:
A South African student whose father is Nigerian has stated that they experienced discrimination at St Ursula's School. According to the student, a classmate made derogatory remarks about Zimbabweans, including mocking them by imitating a Zimbabwean accent. The same classmate  went on to mock Nigerians by speaking in a Nigerian accent, despite being asked to stop. The student says this continued for approximately 30 minutes. The incident took place during a lesson on entrepreneurship in less fortunate communities. During the lesson, the classmate claimed that Nigeria is a "less fortunate" country, suggested that people there probably live in huts, and further said that Nigerians are trying to poison South Africans. The student says these comments were offensive, discriminatory, and targeted their Nigerian heritage.
The principal did not help.
records.response: The principal did not help much

records.name: Ethiopian shop owner dies weeks after Willowfontein arson attack
records.description: An Ethiopian shop owner in Willowfontein, Pietermaritzburg, has died after being seriously injured in a xenophobic attack on 28 July 2026. The 38-year-old shop owner was trapped inside his business when paraffin was thrown into the premises and the shop was set alight. With only one door and no windows, his escape was prevented as the fire rapidly spread. Community members and a local security company responded to the fire and eventually broke through a wall to rescue him. He was rushed to hospital, where he spent two weeks being treated for severe burns before succumbing to his injuries.  A case has been opened.
records.response: A case has been opened

records.name: Bertrams and Bedford Centre attacks
records.description: During a March and March protest on 29 July, protesters entered a clothing shop in Bertrams and attacked. Congolese employees. One Congolese employee was beaten and sustained an injury to the forehead. Despite the incident, the employee returned to work after several days due to the family's financial circumstances. On 15 July, March and March members also arrived at the workplace of another Congolese worker at Bedford Centre and demanded that the individual produce their documentation. The group subsequently demanded that the employer pay R10,000 for employing workers without proper documentation. The employee was subsequently dismissed. During the same period, March and March protesters attempted to forcibly enter a residence in Bertrams where Congolese residents** were living. The incidents contributed to heightened fear and insecurity among Congolese residents and other immigrant communities in the area, with concerns also raised about the lack of safe and accessible mechanisms through which refugees and asylum seekers could report xenophobic attacks.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were highlighted

records.name: Foreign Nationals Injured During Anti-Illegal Foreign Nationals March
records.description: At least three foreign nationals were injured during an anti-illegal foreign nationals march in Kranskop, KwaZulu-Natal, after the protest turned violent. Several shops were looted during the unrest, and one of the injured foreign nationals was robbed. Two of the injured people were receiving treatment in hospital, while the whereabouts of the third remained unknown. At least 80 people who participated in the march were detained for questioning after a bus carrying the group was intercepted on the R74 road towards Greytown. Police investigations indicated that the injured foreign nationals were legally in South Africa, although their immigration status was to be verified by the Department of Home Affairs. Investigations into the violence, looting and reported robbery were continuing.
records.response: anti-foreigner protests

records.name: A Zimbabwean national evicted
records.description: A Zimbabwean woman was in her flat in Hillbrow in mid-August when a group of men, supporters of March and March, barged in and ordered her to leave. She was seven months pregnant. She begged to stay until after the birth, but her landlord who said he was put under pressure  told her to leave.
records.response: No police intervention was reported

records.name: Bellville Anti-Immigration Protest Turns Violent
records.description:
On 19 August 2026, violence broke out in Bellville, Cape Town, during an anti-illegal immigration demonstration involving March and March and Operation Dudula.

Several shops were looted during the protest, and clashes occurred between protesters and foreign nationals. Public Order Police were deployed to the area.

 One foreign national was arrested for discharging a firearm in a municipal area, while a South African man was arrested on an attempted-murder charge following an assault on a foreign national with a metal object. 
Police also opened a case of public violence, while investigations into the incidents continued.
records.response: Police also opened a case of public violence, while investigations into the incidents continued.

records.name: A self-employed carpenter was left homeless
records.description: A Zimbabwean self-employed carpenter based in Sebokeng, who made cupboards, beds and sofas, left his backyard shack on 15 August to work in the Free State. Upon returning on 19 August, he found that the shack had been burnt down, with all his belongings destroyed, including a television, radio, sofas, bed, cellphone and R1,500 in cash that had been kept under the carpet. There had been no previous threats of xenophobic violence in the area. However, tensions increased after messages began circulating that foreigners should leave the area, while neighbours played the Abahambe song. Following the incident, money was borrowed to travel to the consulate. He arrived with only the slippers and clothes he was wearing and was subsequently provided with donated clothing.
records.response: No responses regarding this matter were found

records.name: Attacks and Unrest in Bellville
records.description:
On 20 August 2026, demonstrations linked to the March and March movement and Operation Dudula took place in Bellville, Cape Town, amid calls for action against undocumented foreign nationals.

During the unrest, foreign-owned informal trading stalls were dismantled, and businesses were disrupted. Confrontations also took place between groups, while property was damaged in parts of the area.

The demonstrations were focused on undocumented immigration and foreign nationals operating informal businesses. Protesters called for undocumented migrants to leave South Africa and for stricter enforcement of immigration laws and municipal bylaws.

Police were deployed to the area to manage the unrest and prevent further violence.
records.response: Police were deployed to the area to manage the unrest and prevent further violence.

records.name: A foreign national living in Tembisa and specialising forced to leave work and his home.
records.description: A Zimbabwean foreign national living in Tembisa and specialising in tree felling was forced to leave his employment and accommodation following anti-immigrant mobilisation in the area. March and March protesters went to his workplace and demanded that all immigrants leave. His employer subsequently dismissed him because he did not have documentation. He was also instructed by his landlord to vacate the property immediately. A request for several additional days was refused, with the landlord stating that a local tenant had already been found. After losing his employment and accommodation, he expressed a preference not to remain in South Africa due to the hostility he had experienced. He had been a tenant for more than five years and had been employed in skilled work. For three weeks, consulate officials had not provided information on when repatriation would take place.
records.response: No interventions were recorded

records.name: Raid on Refugee Camp in Durban
records.description: A refugee camp outside the Department of Home Affairs on Che Guevara Road in Durban was raided by members of the March and March vigilante group. The camp had been occupied for more than three months by hundreds of refugees, mainly from the DRC, Burundi and Rwanda, who had been verified by Home Affairs as being legally in South Africa. During the raid, refugees’ belongings were moved into the road, and a police line was breached. Several people were injured, including two refugees who sustained head injuries after being assaulted. A seven-year-old girl was also injured after being stepped on during the dispersal of the crowd. A woman was taken away by ambulance after fainting. Police intervention followed, with rubber bullets and stun grenades being used to disperse the crowd. The incident occurred amid calls for refugees to be removed from the country, including statements that their legal status should not prevent them from being sent back to their countries of origin.
records.response: Police intervention followed, with rubber bullets and stun grenades being used to disperse the crowd.

records.name: Renewed Violence at Durban Refugee Camp
records.description: A group of March and March supporters, joined by members of Operation Dudula, marched to a refugee camp outside the Department of Home Affairs in Durban. The refugees, who had been staying at the site for more than three months while seeking protection from xenophobic attacks, were forced to move away as the protesters approached. Some protesters were seen carrying sjamboks, golf clubs and bats. Refugees’ blankets and other belongings were subsequently set alight. Several people were injured during the confrontation, while police and private security personnel were deployed to contain the situation. The incident followed violent clashes at the same site the previous week, during which several people were injured and police used rubber bullets and stun grenades.
records.response: Police and private security guards were deployed. They were seen trying to extinguish one of the fires with five-litre water bottles

records.name: Durban March and March’s protests
records.description: During a March and March protest in central Durban, a man was assaulted after being mistaken for an immigrant. Protesters carrying sticks, batons, sjamboks and knobkerries also targeted immigrant-run shops, where people were threatened. Several businesses were subsequently closed for the day. The march was billed as part of a national day of action against gender-based violence (GBV) and femicide in response to the murder of 12 women in Ekurhuleni in recent weeks. The poster advertising Wednesday’s march only mentioned GBV. But it was clear to reporters that many of the people who joined were also there for issues surrounding immigration. Leaders shouted, “Abahambe”, with some attendees holding up posters with the same slogan.
records.who_attacked: A person suspected to be a foreign national
records.response: No responses were recorded

records.name: Xenophobic attacks in Durban
records.description: A Congolese asylum seeker who arrived in South Africa in 2025 after fleeing ongoing conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo experienced xenophobia while trying to establish herself in the country. She was chased away from work and told to return to her home country. Before seeking asylum, she worked as a shop teller and used her skills to make clothes for people, but without documentation she struggled to secure stable employment. The xenophobic treatment occurred amid tensions surrounding access to the asylum system in Durban, where March and March members shut down the Refugee Reception Centre on Che Guevara Road, disrupting access to asylum services for people seeking protection.
records.response: No responses regarding this incident were recorded

records.name: Protests obstructed access to asylum-related services
records.description: Protests outside the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) Refugee Reception Centre on Che Guevara Road in Durban disrupted access to asylum services. The centre was closed, and asylum seekers were instructed to leave the area amid a strong police presence. This occurred while asylum seekers had been invited by the Refugee Appeals Authority to attend hearings to finalise their outstanding asylum appeals. As a result of the protests, several asylum seekers who arrived at the centre on Thursday morning turned back and left after encountering the protesters, preventing them from accessing the services they had come to receive.
records.response: The police were present and the asylum seekers were told to leave for their own protection

records.name: Protests break out in Soweto, several vehicles torched
records.description: On the 8th of October 2026, foreign shop owners and local residents in Soweto clashed, and this resulted in several vehicles being set alight. The violence occurred amid protests in which community members marched to the Department of Home Affairs offices in Orlando, demanding that the premises be closed. The demonstrations followed the reopening of South Africa’s asylum system to new applicants by the Department of Home Affairs, in compliance with a Constitutional Court judgment. The clashes and protests disrupted movement in the affected areas, with the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department warning of active road closures and advising motorists to avoid certain areas. Eight vehicles were believed to have been set alight.
records.who_attacked: Cars torched as Soweto residents clash with foreign nationals
records.response: Shots were fired in the direction of protestors this resulted in vehicles being set alight. The police stayed present at the scene

records.name: Protesters set scrapyard alight and march into Durban CBD
records.description: On the  8th of October 2026, a scrapyard in Berea close to the Home Affairs refugee centre was set alight. It is said that protestors set tyres and debris behind the offices, prompting police and fire services to respond. 100 protestors armed with sticks and sjamboks accosted asylum seekers who were queuing outside the office on Che Guevara Road for the third day running.  Police were deployed to the scene; the police used pepper spray due to how unruly the protestors were. Asylum seekers were asked to leave. The protestors moved from the home affairs to the Durban CBD where they were joined by other members including IFP who were originally there for a GBV protests
records.response: The police and firefighters were present at the scene

records.name: Lootings in Durban CBD
records.description:
On the 8th of October, Violence continued in Durban’s central business district (CBD), where shops were looted, foreign nationals were attacked, and a building on Joseph Nduli Street, formerly known as Russel Street, was set alight. Groups of men moved through nearby side streets, damaging shops and destroying property.

Amid the violence, activist Nkosinathi Ndabandaba called for calm and urged the crowd not to break the law despite their frustrations. However, the appeal came after shops had already been looted and foreign nationals attacked. Foreign nationals were targeted and businesses damaged. Despite calls for calm, looting, attacks and property destruction had already taken place.
records.who_attacked: Foreign nationals and shops owned by foreign nationals
records.response: An activist called for people calm down
